Philippines Drug War: 32 Killed in Single Day of Police Operations in Bulacan Province MANILA, Philippines — At least 32 people were killed during a 24-hour police operation in Bulacan province, north of the capital Manila, marking one of the deadliest days in President Rodrigo Duterte's ongoing war on drugs. Police officials said those killed were suspected drug offenders who were armed and resisted arrest during the raids that took place throughout Tuesday. The operation, which ran from midnight to midnight, comprised dozens of coordinated raids across Bulacan province, according to local reports. More than 100 people were arrested during the operation, and officers seized illegal drugs and weapons throughout the raids. The deadly operation serves as a stark reminder that President Duterte's controversial anti-drug campaign, launched in 2016, continues unabated despite fading from international headlines. Thousands have been killed since the campaign began, attracting intense international criticism over the scale of deaths. Mr Duterte has previously sanctioned extrajudicial killings in pursuit of his stated goal of wiping out the drug trade. In a strongly worded public address last month, the president warned drug users that he would hound them to the "gates of hell." Human rights groups have accused Philippine police of planning extrajudicial killings and, in some cases, profiting from them. One mother recently described how her son was shot and killed by masked vigilantes during a late-evening raid, insisting he wasn't a dealer and had declared his marijuana use to authorities three months before his death. Police have consistently maintained that suspects are only killed when they offer armed resistance, a claim that has been highly disputed by rights organizations. Despite such accounts, many Filipinos support the drug war, citing reduced street crime and improved public safety. Taxi drivers report decreased bag snatching, while Manila residents say streets feel safer. Mr Duterte briefly suspended the campaign in January, promising to "clean up" the police and reorganize anti-drug units. The campaign resumed in March.

Woman Hospitalised After Assault in Derry A woman was taken to Altnagelvin Hospital following an assault on Creggan Road in the early hours of Wednesday morning. The incident occurred shortly before 05:00 GMT. The victim sustained wounds to her abdomen and facial bruising, though her injuries are not considered life-threatening. Police arrested a 36-year-old man in connection with the assault. He has since been released on bail pending further enquiries.

New Ultrasound Treatment Shows Promise for Pancreatic Cancer Patients Researchers at a UK university have announced a groundbreaking treatment for pancreatic cancer that could significantly improve survival rates for patients with one of the deadliest forms of the disease. The innovative therapy involves injecting tumours with oxygen-filled micro bubbles coated with cancer-fighting drugs, which are then activated using ultrasound technology. Early results suggest the treatment could reduce tumour size by up to five times, potentially making previously inoperable cancers suitable for surgical removal. Pancreatic surgeon Mark Taylor described the development as "very exciting," telling BBC Northern Ireland's Good Morning Ulster that the breakthrough could transform treatment options. "If this local treatment can actually allow us to operate, then we have a five-fold increase in survival," he explained. Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most challenging cancers to detect and treat, with fewer than 9,000 people diagnosed annually in the UK. It has the lowest five-year survival rate of any common cancer, a statistic that has shown minimal improvement over the past four decades. Mr Taylor attributed these poor outcomes to the disease's typically late presentation and vague symptoms, including heartburn, indigestion, and unexplained weight loss, which often make early diagnosis difficult for medical professionals. Currently, approximately 80% of pancreatic cancer patients have tumours deemed unresectable, meaning they cannot be surgically removed. The new treatment offers hope by potentially shrinking these tumours sufficiently to make surgery viable. "If you are able to give a targeted treatment without the side effects of that treatment in the rest of the body, then that helps prolong survival and that is an excellent chance," Mr Taylor said. Professor John Callan, who led the research at the university's biomedical laboratories in Coleraine, emphasised the treatment's precision. "We can selectively target the tumour and spare healthy tissue making this a highly targeted therapy with reduced side-effects," he stated. The university described the development as "a major breakthrough that can open up more treatment options, even for advanced forms of the disease." Prof Callan called it "one of the most promising advances in pancreatic cancer research for decades," expressing optimism that clinical trials could begin within one to two years, offering new hope to patients facing this devastating diagnosis.

Dragons Secure Bonus Point Win Over Enisei-STM in European Challenge Cup Newport Gwent Dragons left it late but secured a crucial bonus-point victory, defeating Russian side Enisei-STM 34-10 at home in their European Challenge Cup Pool 3 encounter. The Welsh side had to dig deep to overcome stubborn resistance from the enterprising Russian visitors, with young replacement Harri Keddie scoring the vital bonus-point try late in the match – his second of the evening. Dragons opened strongly with tries from hooker T Rhys Thomas and replacement Rhys Buckley, while fly-half Dorian Jones contributed eight points with the boot. Replacement Angus O'Brien converted Buckley's try and both of Keddie's scores to help seal the comprehensive victory. However, the hosts faced a stern test from Enisei, who showed plenty of enterprise throughout. Wings Denis Simplekevich and Igor Kurashov both crossed for tries at either end of the second half, threatening to disrupt Dragons' bonus-point aspirations. At 13-5, the Russians looked capable of staging a comeback before the home side finally wore down their resistance in the final quarter. The standout performance came from 20-year-old Keddie, whose dynamic display as a replacement number eight earned him the man-of-the-match award. His two tries proved crucial in securing the bonus point that keeps Dragons firmly in contention in Pool 3. The victory maintains Dragons' perfect home record in this season's competition, having won all their matches at Rodney Parade. This continues an impressive tradition for Kingsley Jones' side, who have reached the semi-finals in successive seasons. Dragons head coach Jones, who previously coached the Russian national team, praised his side's resilience. "I know they're a stubborn team," he told BBC Radio Wales. "It's never going to be 25-0 in five minutes. The way we went about our business in the second half particularly was excellent. The biggest positive is that we went on and achieved what we set out to do when they got back in the game." The result leaves Dragons level on points with Pool 3 leaders Brive heading into the final round of group matches. Dragons travel to face Brive in France on Saturday, 21 January, while the French side host bottom-placed Worcester. Referee Frank Murphy oversaw the contest, with the bonus-point victory keeping Dragons' European ambitions firmly on track.

**Police Commissioner Katy Bourne Investigation Passed to CPS** The Independent Police Complaints Commission has concluded its investigation into allegations against Sussex Police and Crime Commissioner Katy Bourne and forwarded its findings to the Crown Prosecution Service. The probe centred on claims that Ms Bourne made false statements about her expenses during the 2016 PCC election campaign. Ms Bourne's office declined to comment while the matter remains under review, stating it would be "inappropriate" to discuss the case until concluded. An IPCC spokesperson clarified that referrals to the CPS occur when investigations suggest a potential criminal offence may have occurred, but emphasised this does not guarantee charges will be brought. The CPS will now review the evidence to determine whether prosecution is warranted. Ms Bourne continues in her role as Police and Crime Commissioner pending the outcome.

Rugby Charity to Support Paralysed Dragons Player Ed Jackson's Rehabilitation Former Newport Gwent Dragons player Ed Jackson will receive financial support from rugby's injury charity following a devastating accident that left him paralysed. Jackson, 28, suffered the injury when he dived into a swimming pool. Restart Rugby, the official charity of the Rugby Players' Association (RPA), says it will "assist Ed with the significant cost of the intensive rehabilitation that will be required". Jackson is currently receiving treatment at the Royal United Hospital in Bath. RPA chief executive Damian Hopley told BBC Wales Sport: "The trustees agreed to make a sizeable donation to look after the rehab and physiotherapy cost that Ed will undergo. Ed has made some very encouraging progress in the first month post his accident." He added: "Clearly you can see the huge support he has across the game and we're lucky in the rugby perspective that the game rallies around situations like this." Jackson had emergency surgery at Southmead Hospital in Bristol after the accident at a friend's barbecue on 8 April. The former Bath, Wasps, London Welsh and Doncaster Knights player has recovered some movement and is updating his friends and supporters on his progress on his Facebook page. Hopley emphasised the importance of the support: "It's important we're there to support Ed and his family and give them some peace of mind around what is to come because they are in uncharted territory. Recognising the humour and spirit that Ed is renowned for on his social media account, it's fantastic to chart his progress." Bath-born Jackson made 36 appearances for the Dragons after joining from Wasps in 2015 and signed a contract extension with the region in December 2016.

**Campbell-Ryce Joins Barnet on Free Transfer** Barnet have completed the signing of experienced winger Jamal Campbell-Ryce on a free transfer. The 33-year-old, who departed Sheffield United this summer, becomes the club's fourth signing of the current transfer window. Campbell-Ryce netted seven goals in 53 appearances during his two-year stint with the Blades, spending last season on loan at Chesterfield. The former Charlton trainee brings extensive experience, having previously represented Rotherham, Southend, Barnsley, Bristol City and Notts County. The Bees have not revealed contract details for their new recruit at The Hive.

Funeral held for BBC Wales editor who died in Laos boat tragedy A funeral service is being held today for BBC Wales picture editor Johanna Powell, who died in a boat accident in Laos last month. The 37-year-old from Cardiff was on holiday with three friends when their cruise boat capsized on the Mekong River on 11 April. Nine other tourists, including six Britons, and three crew members survived the incident. The funeral takes place at Glyntaff Crematorium in Pontypridd at 12:45 BST. A coroner's investigation was opened and adjourned in Aberdare on Tuesday, with a pre-inquest review scheduled for August.

Racing Legends Gather in Scottish Borders to Honor Jim Clark's Historic Achievement Motor racing legends Sir Jackie Stewart and Allan McNish traveled to the Scottish Borders over the weekend to celebrate one of the sport's most remarkable achievements by local hero Jim Clark. The event in Duns, Berwickshire, marked the 50th anniversary of Clark's extraordinary 1965 season when he became the only driver in history to win both the Formula One World Championship and the Indianapolis 500 in the same year. Sir Jackie Stewart, himself a three-time F1 world champion, spoke movingly about his friendship with Clark, revealing the depth of their bond. "He was a very, very good friend," Stewart said. "We shared an apartment in London together - two fellow Scots - in 1965, my first year in Formula One." Stewart explained that Clark would have been godfather to his second son had tragedy not intervened when the Berwickshire farmer died in a racing crash in 1968 at the age of just 32. Recalling their time racing together, Stewart said: "I was on the podium with Jimmy three times, I think, the Belgian, the French and the Dutch grand prix. We were, in those days, called Batman and Robin and there was no doubt who was Batman and who was Robin. It was a great period in my life." Bob Dance, former chief mechanic for Team Lotus, Clark's racing team, remembered him as exceptionally gifted yet humble. "He was sympathetic to the car and just a high quality driver - quite calm and collected and easy to get on with," Dance recalled. "He just used to get on with the job." Modern-day racing star Allan McNish suggested Clark's dual championship achievement would be almost impossible to replicate today. "The world of motorsport has definitely changed and that is probably what makes so many people here today remember him," McNish said. "He was a Borders farmer that went on and dominated the world of motorsport." The weekend celebration also served to promote plans for a new Jim Clark Museum in Duns, scheduled to open by 2018. Sir Jackie enthusiastically endorsed the project, saying: "It would be a good thing for Scotland, a great thing for the Borders and fantastic for Duns. We don't have that many great Scots but Jim Clark was a great Scot."

Nuclear Plant Developer Nugen in Talks with Banks and Foreign Firms Joint venture group Nugen has announced it is in discussions with banks and foreign nuclear companies regarding funding for its ambitious Moorside nuclear power plant, which is designed to supply electricity to six million homes. The company stated that "there is a universe of options open to us" as it explores various financing routes for the major infrastructure project. ## Potential Investors and Timeline "We are talking to potential investors familiar with the nuclear industry, including banks, credit-export agencies and nuclear companies in countries interested in nuclear new build projects," a Nugen spokesperson told the BBC. According to the Financial Times, among those expressing interest is Korea Electric Power Corporation (Kepco), South Korea's state-controlled energy company. The firm is reportedly considering taking a stake in Nugen and assisting with construction of the facility, which is scheduled to be built near the Sellafield nuclear complex in Cumbria. A final investment decision on the site is expected in 2018. ## Project Scale and Significance The Moorside project is substantial in scope, designed to provide up to 3.8 gigawatts of power - exceeding the 3.2 gigawatts planned for the rival Hinkley Point project. When operational in the mid-2020s, it aims to supply approximately 7% of the UK's electricity requirements. The project is expected to employ up to 21,000 workers over its lifetime, with three reactors to be provided by Westinghouse, the US subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate Toshiba, which supplies around half of the world's operating nuclear plants. ## Strategic Advantages Nugen, currently owned by Toshiba of Japan and Engie of France, hopes to leverage existing infrastructure at nearby Sellafield, which employs more than 10,000 staff and claims to house the largest concentration of nuclear expertise in Europe. The developments come as questions surround the Hinkley Point project, with Prime Minister Theresa May expected to make a final decision this month on whether to proceed with that facility.

Valdes Set for January Exit from Manchester United Victor Valdes is poised to leave Manchester United during the January transfer window, according to his agent Gines Carvajal. The 33-year-old goalkeeper has endured a difficult spell at Old Trafford, making only two appearances since his free transfer arrival 10 months ago. His tenure has been marred by a public dispute with manager Louis van Gaal in July, followed by a failed move to Turkish side Besiktas in August. Speaking to Radio Marca, Carvajal confirmed: "He'll have a chance in January, wherever he goes. Victor won't be coming to Spain, unless he decides otherwise. He needs to go to a place he feels is right for him." The World Cup 2010 and Euro 2012 winner's contract expires at season's end. Valdes enjoyed a distinguished 12-year career at Barcelona, collecting six La Liga titles, three Champions League trophies, and two Copa del Rey medals between 2002 and 2014.

Putin Dismisses Panama Papers as Western Plot to Destabilize Russia Russian President Vladimir Putin has dismissed the Panama Papers revelations as a Western-orchestrated campaign to undermine Russia, speaking publicly for the first time since the massive leak of confidential documents from Panama-based law firm Mossack Fonseca. The leaked papers exposed a network of offshore companies owned by close associates of Mr Putin, raising questions about potential money laundering activities. However, the Russian leader characterised the revelations as a calculated attack designed to weaken his country. "Russia's Western opponents are worried by the unity and solidarity of the Russian nation, and that is why they are attempting to rock us from within, to make us more obedient," Mr Putin said during a live television appearance. The President suggested that because investigators could not directly implicate him in the Panama Papers, "they've made an information product". He added: "They've found a few of my acquaintances and friends, and scraped up something from there and stuck it together." Mr Putin pointed to Wikileaks tweets that accused the US international development agency USAID and the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) - an independent journalistic consortium - of producing and funding what was described as "the #PanamaPapers attack on Putin". The OCCRP was part of a network of 107 organisations, including the BBC, that received documents from the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists. Among those named in the papers is Sergei Roldugin, a cellist who has been Mr Putin's long-time friend and is godfather to his daughter. The documents identify Mr Roldugin as owner of two offshore firms, International Media Overseas and Sonnette Overseas, allegedly involved in suspicious financial transactions. One particularly questionable deal involved International Media Overseas receiving a $6 million loan in 2007 that was written off just three months later for only $1. Mr Roldugin has not publicly addressed these allegations. While Mr Putin avoided discussing specific allegations against Mr Roldugin or other Russian offshore interests, he offered praise for his friend, saying he was proud of people like Mr Roldugin. He claimed the cellist had spent nearly all his earnings on musical instruments and donated money to state institutions. The Panama Papers leak has prompted investigations into possible financial crimes by wealthy and powerful individuals across multiple countries. Iceland's prime minister resigned earlier this week after revelations that he owned an undeclared offshore company with his wife, though he denies wrongdoing. Mossack Fonseca, the firm at the centre of the leak, has denied wrongdoing and claims the information has been presented out of context. In response to the scandal, Panama announced Thursday it would create an international panel to improve transparency in its offshore financial industry.

Three Men Arrested After Stabbing in Belfast Police are investigating a stabbing in the Hatfield Street area of Belfast that occurred around 07:45 BST on Saturday morning. Three men in their twenties have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder following the attack, according to Detective Sergeant Moffett. The male victim sustained injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening, though his exact condition remains unclear. Authorities have issued an appeal for witnesses or anyone with information about the incident to come forward.

Carwyn Jones Warns Immigration Caps Could Harm Welsh NHS Recruitment Welsh First Minister Carwyn Jones has raised concerns that Conservative plans to cap immigration could severely impact the recruitment of doctors and nurses in Wales, potentially damaging the country's healthcare system. Mr Jones was referring to proposals in the Conservative manifesto that net migration should be reduced to less than 100,000 a year. He warned a cap could result in fewer doctors and nurses being recruited in Wales. But UKIP said caps were designed to prevent oversupply not undersupply. Speaking on BBC Wales's Sunday Supplement programme, Mr Jones said: "Now, if we introduce a cap and that cap means we can't recruit the doctors we need in Wales, then surely that doesn't make any sense at all." In the past Mr Jones has criticised Labour's UK leader, Jeremy Corbyn, for not taking a tough enough stance on immigration. Mr Jones said he favours a system which would allow migrants to come to the UK if they have a job, or to give them three months to look for work. But he said he did not see how having a cap on the numbers could work. "What kind of cap are we looking at?" he asked. "Are we looking at a cap where there's a certain number of people for every sector? My suspicion then would be that what a Tory government would do was to look after the city of London and forget about everybody else." The Liberal Democrats said the Conservatives' plan to bring immigration down to the tens of thousands was "a perfect example of chasing headlines". "In Wales, we have benefited enormously from the free movement of people across the EU, and Theresa May's plans to end freedom of movement will be bad news for our NHS, our businesses, and tourism in Wales," a spokesman added. "We must have a fair and sensible approach to immigration, but scapegoating immigrants and fuelling division in our communities will do nothing to address people's concerns." But a UKIP spokesman accused Mr Jones of "constructing a straw position to attack". "Sector caps are not arbitrary numbers; they are designed to prevent oversupply based on estimates for a given period, not create an undersupply," they said. "Further, these limits can be used to stimulate domestic skill creation and help lower the skills shortfall going forward." Other parties have been asked to comment. Net migration is the difference between people coming to the UK for more than a year, and the number of people leaving the UK for a year or more. It was estimated to be 248,000 in 2016 - a fall of 84,000 from 2015. The Office for National Statistics estimated immigration at 588,000, with emigration of 339,000. The difference between the two gives the total for net migration. In 2016, the total number of people moving to the UK was made up of 264,000 non-EU citizens, 250,000 EU citizens and 74,000 British citizens.

Stephen Hawking Stalker Arrested in Tenerife, Banned from Contact A 37-year-old woman has been arrested in Tenerife for stalking renowned physicist Professor Stephen Hawking and threatening to kill him. The woman has been banned from approaching within 500 meters of the scientist or communicating with him via social media for eight months. The suspect was apprehended at a hotel in Tenerife, where Prof Hawking was attending the prestigious Starmus Festival. The event brought together Nobel laureates, musicians including Brian May, Brian Eno, and Hans Zimmer, as well as celebrated astronauts. According to Spanish News Today, Prof Hawking's daughter alerted police after threatening messages began flooding the scientist's social media profiles and email account on Tuesday. The woman, identified in Spanish media as Jenny Theresa C., had been stalking Prof Hawking online before following him to the island. She allegedly sent messages threatening to kill him during the festival. Police arrested the woman on Wednesday and discovered she was carrying a map detailing Prof Hawking's itinerary on the island. Following her detention, she claimed to be in love with the scientist and insisted she would never have harmed him. Authorities indicated that all evidence suggested the woman was mentally unstable. This marks the first time Prof Hawking has received such serious threats, prompting Spanish police to provide enhanced security throughout his visit. During his lecture at the festival, titled "A brief history of mine," Prof Hawking discussed his forecast that humans would not survive another thousand years on Earth due to the planet's fragility.

Motherwell Sign Striker George Newell on One-Year Deal Motherwell have completed the signing of 20-year-old striker George Newell on a one-year contract, with manager Stephen Robinson expressing high hopes for the young forward's development. Newell, son of former Blackburn Rovers and Everton striker Mike Newell, will initially join the Scottish Premiership club's development squad but is expected to compete for first-team opportunities. "Although he'll form part of that group initially, I fully expect to see him push for a spot," said Robinson. "We are really excited with what we have seen from George already." The young Englishman progressed through Everton's youth academy, following in his father's footsteps at Goodison Park, before moving to Bolton Wanderers two years ago. However, his time at Bolton yielded limited first-team action, with just two substitute appearances for the side that earned promotion to the Championship. He spent the first half of last season on loan at National League side AFC Fylde, making 11 appearances. Robinson has been impressed with Newell's early performances in training and youth matches. "He's played a couple of games for our under-20s and has really shone, scoring a couple of goals," the manager told the club website. "He's young, hungry and is one of those busy, never-say-die strikers that football fans love." The signing comes as Motherwell continue their strong start to the League Cup campaign, having scored nine goals in their opening two ties, including a 4-0 victory over Morton featuring seven summer signings. Robinson remained cautious about expectations despite the positive start. "You don't bring so many players in and have instant success, that's not going to happen, but you can see the makings of what we are trying to do." Newell expressed his enthusiasm about the move, saying: "For me, this is the next step because Motherwell presented the best opportunity for me as a player. I hope to push myself as much as I can and hopefully contest for a place in the first team."

Boxer Nick Blackwell Remains Sedated After Brain Bleed Following Title Fight British boxer Nick Blackwell remains in a serious condition after suffering a small bleed on the brain during Saturday night's British middleweight title fight against Chris Eubank Jr. The 25-year-old fighter was stopped in the tenth round at Wembley Arena and immediately stretchered from the ring while receiving oxygen. A family spokesman confirmed to BBC Sport that Blackwell is currently "heavily sedated" in hospital, with doctors potentially bringing him round on Tuesday. Referee Victor Loughlin halted the contest on advice from the ringside doctor, citing severe swelling over Blackwell's left eye that prevented him from continuing safely. The British Board of Boxing Control has defended the handling of the bout, despite suggestions from Eubank Jr's camp and boxing analysts that the fight should have been stopped earlier. Notably, at the end of round eight, Chris Eubank Sr—himself a former world champion—instructed his son to target Blackwell's body rather than his head, though it remains unclear whether this was tactical advice or concern for his opponent's welfare. Following the fight, Eubank Jr acknowledged the severity of his punches, stating: "I hit him with some big shots. Maybe the referee should have stopped the fight earlier." The incident has drawn comparisons to the tragic 1991 bout between Chris Eubank Sr and Michael Watson, who suffered life-changing brain damage. Watson, now 51, told the Telegraph he experienced "a real sense of deja vu" watching Saturday's fight.

Bayern Munich's Title Celebration Put on Hold by Gladbach Draw Bayern Munich's coronation as Bundesliga champions for the 26th time was postponed after they were held to a draw by Borussia Monchengladbach, with Andre Hahn's equaliser 18 minutes from time denying the Bavarian giants the title. Thomas Muller had given Bayern the lead with his 20th league goal of the season, heading home what looked set to be the championship-clinching strike. However, Hahn drove his shot low into the net to secure a point for Gladbach and force Bayern to wait at least another week. The result came as Bayern coach Pep Guardiola made eight changes to his starting lineup following their 1-0 Champions League semi-final first leg defeat to Atletico Madrid. With the crucial return leg at home approaching next Tuesday, squad rotation was inevitable. Muller was one of those recalled, but his goal couldn't maintain Bayern's remarkable record of 51 consecutive league victories when the Germany international found the net. Hahn's fifth goal of the season ended that impressive run. Meanwhile, Borussia Dortmund kept their mathematical hopes alive with a commanding 5-1 victory over Wolfsburg, moving to within five points of Bayern with just two games remaining. Bayern now face a local derby at Ingolstadt next weekend before hosting Hannover in their final league fixture, needing just a point to secure the title. Guardiola acknowledged the disappointment: "Of course we had wanted to win today, for our fans and for ourselves. We need just a point now, a draw, or a win to secure the title. But now there's time to concentrate on Atletico Madrid." Bayern chairman Karl-Heinz Rummenigge added: "We would have liked to be champions today, I won't lie. But we'll try to seal the deal against Ingolstadt next weekend. Now we switch all our focus towards Tuesday." For Gladbach, the result was significant beyond denying Bayern, as they moved above Hertha Berlin into fourth place on goal difference, enhancing their Champions League qualification hopes while ending a four-match away losing streak. Bayern still have the German Cup final against Dortmund on 21 May as they pursue a treble before Guardiola's summer departure to Manchester City.

Motorcyclist Dies in Collision on A696 Near Kirkwhelpington A motorcyclist has died following a collision with a car in Northumberland. The crash involving a blue Ford S Max and a red Honda CBR motorcycle happened at approximately 09:10 BST on the A696 near Kirkwhelpington, Northumbria Police said. The male motorcyclist was pronounced dead at the scene. He has not yet been named. The male driver of the car was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries and is in a stable condition. Police have launched an investigation and are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Welsh Refugees Face'Two-Tier System' as Syrians Get Priority Support Refugees arriving in Wales through different routes face vastly different levels of support, creating a "two-tier system" that leaves non-Syrian asylum seekers struggling with basic paperwork while Syrian refugees receive comprehensive assistance, charity workers have warned. Tracey Sherlock of the Welsh Refugee Council told assembly members that other migrants were "still struggling" to obtain the documentation necessary to settle and find work, whilst those arriving through the Syrian resettlement scheme received swift, well-resourced support. The stark disparity in resources was highlighted by Ms Sherlock, the charity's policy manager, who revealed that four caseworkers were supporting 700 people who arrived through the regular asylum route over the last quarter. In contrast, two caseworkers were assigned to just 46 Syrian refugees - approximately ten families - who arrived through the special resettlement scheme over the past year. "All of the administrative things that people when they get refugee status through the asylum route find very problematic, they're not issues for people coming through that Syrian resettlement scheme," Ms Sherlock told the assembly's equalities committee on Wednesday. She explained that Syrian refugees very quickly received support around employment and education opportunities, whereas those arriving spontaneously continued to struggle even after gaining refugee status to access basic necessities such as National Insurance numbers and the paperwork required for employment and integration. The UK government has pledged to settle 20,000 Syrians in the UK by 2020 under its Syrian resettlement scheme. Latest figures for July to September show that 294 Syrians have been resettled in Wales since the scheme launched in October 2015. Hayley Richards of Oxfam Cymru acknowledged the severity of the Syrian crisis but warned that the special arrangements sent a troubling message. "It does send out a message to other asylum seekers and refugees in Wales..... there's a real sense that Syrian refugees are good and all other refugees and asylum seekers are not as worthy," she said. Ms Richards noted that the disparity even affected Syrians themselves, with those who arrived spontaneously not receiving the same welcome as those coming through the official scheme. Neil McKittrick, refugee operations support officer for the British Red Cross, confirmed the two-tier system existed throughout the UK, not just Wales. He contrasted the reception of Syrian refugees, who were "met by dignitaries," with those arriving through normal asylum routes, whose first contact with officials was characterised by distrust. "From the very first contact that people have, that kind of sets the tone," Mr McKittrick said. A Home Office spokesman responded by stating that all those granted refugee status or humanitarian protection in the UK were entitled to unrestricted access to the labour market and had broadly the same rights as British nationals and other lawful residents.

Highland and Islands Airports Reports Strong Passenger Growth Highland and Islands Airports Limited (Hial) has announced a significant increase in passenger numbers during the first half of the 2016-17 financial year. Between April and September 2016, 908,116 passengers travelled through Hial airports, representing a rise of 111,750 compared to the 796,366 recorded during the same period in 2015. The airport operator, which manages facilities across the Highlands, islands, Argyll, and Dundee, highlighted particularly strong performances at Inverness Airport. New airline services connecting Inverness to London and Amsterdam have delivered "outstanding performances," contributing significantly to the overall growth figures.

Man Jailed for Minimum 31 Years for Machete Murder in Bolton Street Attack A man has been sentenced to serve at least 31 years in prison for the murder of Sebastian Zuchlinski, who was brutally attacked with machetes and knives in a Bolton street. Mr Zuchlinski was found injured on Davenport Street on 6 February and was pronounced dead at the scene. The 39-year-old victim, known to friends as Seba, had been planning a night out with his girlfriend and her sister when the attack occurred. Bolton Crown Court heard that Tomasz Bubrowski, 39, of Cavendish Gardens, Bolton, was part of a group of three armed men who carried out the "savage and unprovoked attack." The victim was with his girlfriend's sister, who was driving him home to change his footwear, when their vehicle was blocked by a Honda Civic. Bubrowski and two accomplices jumped from the Honda and dragged Mr Zuchlinski from the car before launching a sustained assault as he lay on the ground. Police said the attack would have continued had it not been for the intervention of a brave passing witness. A fourth man drove the attackers away from the scene. Detective Inspector John Mulvihill described it as an attack on "an unarmed man, who had made plans for a fun evening out." He added that Mr Zuchlinski's loved ones "still feel the impact of his death and miss him dearly." Greater Manchester Police confirmed they are continuing to search for the other men involved in the fatal attack.

Dimitrov Overcomes Raonic to Set Up Brisbane Final with Nishikori Bulgaria's Grigor Dimitrov advanced to the Brisbane International final after defeating Canada's Milos Raonic in a hard-fought semi-final encounter. The seventh seed saved a crucial set point in the opening set before prevailing 7-6 (9-7) 6-2 over the world number three. Dimitrov, currently ranked 17th in the world, will face Japan's third seed Kei Nishikori in Sunday's final. The world number five reached the championship match by defeating US Open champion Stan Wawrinka 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 in the first semi-final. "Nishikori is one of the trickiest players out there," Dimitrov said. "He has a tremendous fighting spirit and quite a few weapons." The Brisbane tournament serves as a key warm-up for the Australian Open, commencing 16 January.

Edinburgh Council Approves Compensation Scheme for Mortonhall Crematorium Scandal Families Edinburgh's local authority has decided to proceed with a proposed settlement scheme for families affected by the Mortonhall Crematorium scandal, offering compensation payments ranging from £1,000 to £4,000, plus legal expenses. The scandal, which first emerged at Mortonhall Crematorium in Edinburgh, affected more than 250 families whose children's remains were disposed of without their knowledge or consent. Staff at the crematorium secretly buried baby ashes and falsely informed grieving parents that no ashes remained after the cremation of young babies. This deeply troubling practice is believed to have been in place from the crematorium's opening in 1967 until a change of management in 2011, spanning more than four decades. The Mortonhall Settlement report, which details the compensation scheme, will be presented to the council on 5 February for approval. Thompsons Solicitors, representing 129 affected clients, played a key role in developing the proposed scheme. Sue Bruce, Chief Executive of the City of Edinburgh Council, acknowledged the distress caused to families: "The events of the past two years have understandably been distressing for families affected by the events at Mortonhall Crematorium. The council is taking forward all the recommendations made by Dame Elish Angiolini in her report, and will ensure nothing like this happens ever again." In addition to financial compensation, draft designs for permanent memorials have been revealed. Following consultation with parents, two memorial sites are being proposed: one within the grounds of Mortonhall Crematorium and another at a location yet to be determined in the city. The Meadows and the Botanic Gardens are among locations under consideration, recognizing that some families expressed strong reluctance to return to Mortonhall. Parents will have the final say on which designs are selected, with completion targeted for autumn. Patrick McGuire from Thompsons Solicitors praised the families' courage: "In addition to the grief they face over the loss of their children, the families also have to bear the deep upset caused by practices at the crematorium. Despite this they have shown remarkable courage and resolve to make the Scottish public aware about what had gone on." He added that the families' solidarity and tenacity have led to wider investigations into crematorium practices throughout Scotland, ensuring that "no other families will have to suffer distress due to unacceptable practices at our crematoria."

Glamorgan Sign South Africa's Jacques Rudolph on Two-Year Deal Glamorgan have secured the services of experienced South African batsman Jacques Rudolph on a two-year contract for the upcoming seasons. The 32-year-old will replace Australian Marcus North, who has been with Glamorgan for the last two seasons. "I'm delighted to be joining Glamorgan on a two-year deal," Rudolph said. "I enjoyed my time playing for Yorkshire so I'm looking forward to the challenge at Glamorgan." Rudolph has previously played county cricket for Surrey and Yorkshire and is currently playing Champions League cricket in India for the Titans. The left-hander has played 48 Tests for South Africa at an average of 35.43 runs and also has a slightly higher average in one-day internationals. Hugh Morris, who will join Glamorgan as chief executive and director of cricket, said: "Signing a player of Jacques Rudolph's undoubted capabilities and experience is a great boost ahead of the new season. With an increasingly heavy first-class schedule it will be a huge advantage to have a world-class opening batsman available to us. I look forward to welcoming Jacques to Glamorgan." Glamorgan say they are also close to agreeing new contracts with this season's leading run scorer Murray Goodwin and spinner Dean Cosker for the 2014 season, plus ex-England bowler Simon Jones on a deal to play just limited-overs cricket. The Welsh county are currently playing Essex in County Championship Division Two and will contest the YB40 final against Nottinghamshire on Saturday - Glamorgan's first Lord's appearance for 13 years.

Hundreds Evacuated as Floods Hit Scotland, Government Activates Emergency Support Hundreds of people were forced to flee their homes following severe flooding across Scotland over the weekend, prompting urgent calls to accelerate the implementation of flood prevention schemes. The Scottish government has activated the Bellwin Scheme, which provides financial assistance to local councils dealing with costs arising from natural emergencies. The decision comes as communities, particularly in the Scottish Borders, continue to deal with the aftermath of heavy rainfall and widespread flooding. The Scottish Borders emerged as one of the hardest-hit regions, with homes evacuated, numerous roads closed, and at least one school forced to remain shut on Monday. While conditions are gradually improving, forecasters have issued another yellow weather warning for rain covering parts of southern Scotland on Wednesday and Thursday. During a visit to the flood-damaged town of Hawick, Ms McLeod witnessed firsthand the extensive destruction caused by the extreme weather. She expressed gratitude to emergency responders "who have been working round the clock to help those most in need." Ms McLeod also praised local volunteers who demonstrated remarkable community spirit by providing food, transportation, and support to affected neighbours, describing it as something "all of Scotland can be proud of." With additional rainfall predicted, authorities expect continued disruption to traffic and services. "The Scottish government will continue to work closely with SEPA and Transport Scotland to monitor the latest updates so that we ensure our local authorities and the emergency services get the support that they need," Ms McLeod stated. On a positive note, she emphasized that "all of Scotland's existing flood defences worked over the weekend," validating the government's ongoing commitment to investing in flood protection infrastructure. "It is also important we recognise the impact of our significant investment in protecting people's homes and livelihoods from such extreme conditions," she added.

**Saracens Secure Bonus-Point Victory Over Scarlets in European Challenge Cup** Saracens dominated early proceedings against Scarlets, racing to an 18-0 half-time lead through tries from Nick Tompkins and Matt Gallagher in their European Challenge Cup encounter. The hosts attempted a fightback when Morgan Allen crossed the line, but Mike Ellery's try kept Saracens firmly in control. Scarlets showed resilience as substitute Billy McBryde scored to threaten a comeback, but Tom Whiteley sealed the bonus-point victory with the visitors' fourth try. The result saw Saracens climb to the top of Pool One, whilst Scarlets remained in third place in Pool Four. Saracens captain Tim Streather led a strong performance, with Matt Gallagher, Max Malins, and Henry Taylor proving influential. For Scarlets, captain Emyr Phillips marshalled his side valiantly, with Josh Macleod and Morgan Allen providing the most resistance. The bonus-point victory strengthens Saracens' position in the competition, while Scarlets will need to regroup quickly to improve their standing in Pool Four.

MP Alistair Carmichael Loses Legal Costs Claim After Election Court Battle Liberal Democrat MP Alistair Carmichael has lost his bid to recover legal expenses following a court case that challenged his election victory in Orkney and Shetland. The case centred on allegations that Mr Carmichael misled voters during the 2015 general election campaign over a leaked government memo. Four constituents brought the action under the Representation of the People Act 1983, seeking to have his election declared void. In December, judges ruled that it had not been proven beyond reasonable doubt that Mr Carmichael had committed an "illegal practice" under the Act. However, in a subsequent hearing at the Court of Session in Edinburgh to determine responsibility for costs, Mr Carmichael has now lost his claim to have his legal expenses paid. His legal expenses have been estimated at approximately £150,000, a substantial sum that the MP will now have to bear himself. ## Legal Arguments During the costs hearing, Roddy Dunlop QC, representing Mr Carmichael, argued it would be "frankly inconceivable" that the four petitioners would not have sought expenses against the MP had they won their case. He emphasised that "Mr Carmichael is not a rich man" and that forcing him to endure the distressing process without redress after successfully defending himself would not be "in the interests of justice" or fair. Mr Dunlop added that "Mr Carmichael has already suffered very publicly the consequences of this court's rebuke." Jonathan Mitchell QC, representing the petitioners, countered that there had been a public interest in bringing the case and noted that the petitioners had successfully argued several points during the proceedings. ## Court Decision After hearing submissions from both sides, Lady Paton delivered the court's decision: "In all the circumstances, exercising our discretion, we consider this to be in effect a case with divided success. Accordingly, we find no expenses due to or by any party." ## Background to the Case The controversy arose from a leaked memo published in the Daily Telegraph at the start of the 2015 election campaign in April. The document claimed that SNP leader and Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon would secretly prefer Conservative leader David Cameron as prime minister rather than Labour's Ed Miliband, allegedly undermining her claims of wanting to build a "progressive alliance" with left-wing parties. Mr Carmichael initially claimed in a Channel 4 television interview that the first he knew of the memo was when contacted by a reporter. However, he later admitted, days after being re-elected, that he had actually authorised his special advisor to leak the document. ## Original Ruling In their December ruling, the judges found that Mr Carmichael had told a "blatant lie" in the Channel 4 interview. However, they concluded that section 106 of the Representation of the People Act did not apply to lies in general. The judges said they had a "reasonable doubt" about whether the lie constituted a false statement of fact "in relation to [his] personal character or conduct," and therefore held that his election was not void. At the time, Mr Carmichael said he was "absolutely delighted" with the decision, while acknowledging there had been a lapse in his conduct. He described the case as "highly politically-motivated."

Welsh NHS Shows Best Performance Since 2015 Target Introduction The Welsh ambulance service has recorded its best performance since new targets were introduced in October 2015, with the latest monthly figures showing improvements across multiple areas of healthcare delivery. The statistics reveal better waiting times in accident and emergency departments, as well as reduced delays for patients awaiting planned treatment, diagnostic tests and cancer care. While improved performance in spring is not uncommon as winter pressures ease, Health Secretary Vaughan Gething described the figures as painting "a very positive picture for Wales." However, the NHS in Wales continues to fall short of meeting most of its key targets. ## Ambulance Service Improvements Response times to immediately life-threatening "red" calls showed significant improvement between March and April. The service responded within eight minutes to 80.5% of red calls in April, up from 77.9% in March, comfortably exceeding the 65% target. The median response time for red calls reached its lowest level since the new target began, at four minutes and 17 seconds, compared to five minutes 30 seconds in April 2016. ## A&E Performance Emergency care units saw 82.8% of patients spending less than four hours in A&E in April, an improvement from 80.9% in March. However, this remains well below the 95% target, which has never been achieved. The number of patients waiting over 12 hours before being admitted, transferred or discharged fell to 2,269 last month, a reduction of 922 from March. Current targets stipulate that no patient should wait this long. ## Waiting Times for Treatment Diagnostic test waiting times improved significantly, with patients waiting over eight weeks reducing from 6,625 in February to 4,741 in March, continuing an upward trend since January 2014. Therapy waiting times remained relatively stable, with a slight increase in patients waiting over 14 weeks, rising from 2,445 to 2,477. Mr Gething thanked NHS staff for their efforts, stating: "We will continue to work to improve performance for patients."

Rachel and Nyomi Fee Murder Trial: Jury Sent Home for Weekend A jury has been sent home for the weekend to consider verdicts in the trial of two women accused of murdering a two-year-old boy. Rachel and Nyomi Fee deny murdering the child at a house near Glenrothes on 22 March 2014 and blaming his death on another child. Jurors at the High Court in Livingston retired to consider their verdicts on Friday morning before being sent home that afternoon. Judge Lord Burns instructed them to consider the evidence dispassionately and without speculation. Rachel Fee, 31, and Nyomi Fee, 29, both originally from Ryton, Tyne and Wear, deny all charges against them in the seven-week trial.

Speeding Driver Given Suspended Sentence After Pedestrian Left with Life-Changing Injuries A teenage driver who struck a pedestrian while speeding through a residential area, leaving her with permanent injuries and severe psychological trauma, has been handed a suspended jail sentence. Henry Rigby, 19, was travelling at 40 mph in a 30 mph zone when his Vauxhall Corsa hit Beverley Finney and another pedestrian on Haresfinch Road in St Helens, Merseyside, in May 2016. Liverpool Crown Court heard that the collision left both victims with life-threatening injuries. Ms Finney suffered extensive facial injuries and continues to experience severe health problems. In a victim impact statement, she described ongoing "bad headaches", "a lot of back pain" and "numbness to the side of the face". She has visible scars around her eye socket and hairline and said she "may consider" plastic surgery in the future. The psychological impact has been equally devastating. Ms Finney revealed she has been forced to relocate from her home because living near a busy road triggered severe panic attacks. "I just couldn't relax with the noise of traffic," she told the court. "I would get so distressed with the noise of skidding cars or revving engines." CCTV footage captured the moment Rigby, of Harris Street in Dentons Green, struck the pedestrians. He was found guilty of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. Rigby received a 15-month suspended jail term, a three-year driving ban, and was ordered to complete 240 hours of unpaid work. He must also pay £750 compensation to each victim and £500 in court costs. Inspector Mike McFall of Merseyside Police said the incident was "totally avoidable and shows the very real consequences of motorists who exceed the speed limit".

Dubai Police Crack Down on Illegal Street Racing, Seize 81 Luxury Vehicles Dubai authorities have launched a major crackdown on illegal street racing, confiscating 81 high-performance vehicles from drivers engaged in dangerous racing activities across the wealthy Gulf emirate. The seized cars, many of them luxury models, had their number plates removed to evade identification during illegal races. Dubai police chief Maj Gen Khamis Al Mazinah announced that traffic patrols tracked down reckless drivers who were either using their vehicles for illegal races or preparing to do so. "Other cars were caught in dangerous performances and reckless driving that endangered road users," Al Mazinah stated. Some drivers reportedly reached speeds of 196mph while attempting to flee from police patrols. The penalties are severe: drivers face fines of 100,000 dirham ($27,000; £19,000), while vehicle owners must pay 50,000 dirham. If owners fail to pay within three months, police have the authority to sell the confiscated vehicles. Luxury cars are extremely popular in Dubai, where even the police force operates Lamborghinis, Porsches and Aston Martins. Transport officials reported last year that Dubai's vehicle numbers had doubled in eight years, giving the city more cars per person than New York or London. The crackdown signals authorities' determination to eliminate the dangerous street racing culture that has flourished among the emirate's wealthy residents.

Sheffield's Hidden Beer Scene Revealed: City Boasts 23 Breweries in Brewing Renaissance Sheffield has emerged as one of Britain's most significant brewing cities, with a comprehensive study revealing a thriving beer industry that locals have quietly enjoyed for years, according to research by beer writer Pete Brown. The steel city now boasts 23 breweries—one for every 24,000 residents—making it almost five times more brewery-dense per capita than greater London. However, this "beery brilliance" has remained something of a well-kept secret among Sheffield's discerning drinking community. Kate Major, chairman of Sheffield's Campaign for Real Ale (CAMRA) branch and landlady of The Three Tuns pub, attributes the city's brewing success to its knowledgeable beer enthusiasts. "The report is very exciting but it is nothing we didn't know already in Sheffield," she explained. "Many of our breweries are tiny and we like the beer they produce too much to let a lot of it out." The study, commissioned by the University of Sheffield, found that nearly nine out of ten city breweries qualify as "microbreweries"—those producing below the beer duty threshold. These small-scale operations maintain a distinctly local focus, keeping three-quarters of their production within city limits. What truly distinguishes Sheffield's beer scene is its diversity: the city produces approximately 400 different beers, many exclusive to the region and difficult to find elsewhere. Sheffield's brewing heritage stretches back to 1758 with its first brewery foundation. The following century saw 30 brewers establish operations, establishing the steel city as a significant brewing centre. However, consolidation reduced this number to around 16 by World War One, with continued decline in subsequent decades. The 1980s marked a turning point. A grassroots brewing movement positioned Sheffield as a pioneer of what would become the national "craft beer" explosion. Dave Wickett, a polytechnic lecturer and real ale enthusiast, catalysed this renaissance in 1981 by purchasing a dilapidated pub in a derelict Sheffield neighbourhood and transforming it into the Fat Cat. Wickett's establishment stocked diverse, interesting beers, and his decision to start brewing helped ignite the city's beer revival. "The general trend for Sheffield's new beer all started with the Fat Cat and the Kelham Island area," Major noted. Wickett passed away in 2012. Professor Vanessa Toulmin from Sheffield University described beer and pubs as the "cultural glue that holds the city together." She added: "Sheffield has always been a city of makers and it's no surprise that this extends to beer too." While the report acknowledges that London, Manchester and Leeds enjoy greater recognition as beer destinations, Sheffield's secret may finally be revealed. Major welcomes the attention: "We have room in Sheffield for a lot more people to come and drink our beer and as a city we need to be telling everybody."

**Aston Martin Returns to Profit After Six Years of Losses** Aston Martin has swung back into the black after six consecutive years of losses, reporting a pre-tax profit of £5.9m for the first quarter ending in March. The luxury British carmaker's turnaround was driven by strong sales of its new DB11 model, which launched late last year. Revenues more than doubled to £188m in the three-month period. Chief financial officer Mark Wilson said customer demand had doubled year-on-year. "We're now in an area and an environment where we are generating demand in excess of supply," he said. Aston Martin sold 3,687 cars last year but expects its latest models to boost sales by over 30% in 2017. The company, which was sold by Ford to Italian and Kuwaiti investment firms in 2007, has endured a turbulent history, going bankrupt seven times. Looking ahead, Aston Martin confirmed plans to enter the electric vehicle market following last year's partnership with LeEco, the Chinese backer of electric car start-up Faraday Future.

Linfield Thrash Dungannon 6-0 to Keep Pressure on League Leaders Media playback is not supported on this device. David Healy's Linfield produced a dominant first-half display to secure a comprehensive 6-0 victory over Dungannon Swifts at Windsor Park, maintaining their pursuit of Premiership leaders Crusaders. The Blues had effectively sealed the three points before the break, with Andrew Waterworth opening the scoring in the 15th minute with a powerful drive. Paul Smyth added a second after breaking through the Swifts' defence, before defender Mark Stafford bundled home from close range on 38 minutes to give Linfield a commanding 3-0 half-time lead. The home side continued their dominance after the interval, with Stafford grabbing his second goal of the evening. Aaron Burns and Michael McLellan also found the net to complete the rout. The victory extends Linfield's winning streak to six consecutive matches, though they remain six points behind league leaders Crusaders. Dungannon stay 10th in the table, just three points clear of bottom-placed Warrenpoint Town. Linfield manager David Healy acknowledged his side's performance: "Six goals maybe flattered us a bit, but it was another clean sheet for us too. We are on a decent run and will just focus on doing our jobs." Dungannon boss Rodney McAree was disappointed with his team's showing, particularly their defending at set pieces and lack of belief during the match.

Tilda Swinton Stars in David Bowie's Latest Music Video "The Stars (Are Out Tonight)" Oscar-winning actress Tilda Swinton has reunited with music legend David Bowie for his latest music video, "The Stars (Are Out Tonight)," marking a rare appearance by the acclaimed actress in a music video format. Swinton, who won the best supporting actress Oscar in 2007 for her role in the George Clooney thriller "Michael Clayton," appears alongside Bowie in domestic scenes, including shopping excursions and watching television. This marks only her second music video appearance, following Orbital's "The Box" in 1997, which received a nomination for best video at the Brits. The video was directed by Floria Sigismondi, who has an extensive history with Bowie, having previously collaborated on "Little Wonder" (1996) and "Dead Man Walking" (1997). Sigismondi's impressive portfolio includes work with Muse, Katy Perry, The White Stripes, The Cure, Bjork, Leonard Cohen, and Marilyn Manson. The video features androgynous models Andrej Pejic and Saskia De Brauw, with Norwegian model Iselin Steiro portraying a young Bowie. According to a statement on Bowie's website, the video "captures a twenty first century moment in its convergence of age, gender and the normal/celebrity divide." "The Stars (Are Out Tonight)" is Bowie's second single from his forthcoming album "The Next Day," his first new material in a decade. The Daily Telegraph's Neil McCormick praised the release, calling it "the return of the master, showing every other rock and roll star, old or young, how things should be done." Swinton recently appeared in Wes Anderson's "Moonrise Kingdom" at Cannes and received critical acclaim for 2011's "We Need to Talk About Kevin."

Orient Sign Colchester Forward Massey on Three-Year Deal Leyton Orient have completed the signing of striker Gavin Massey from Colchester United on a three-year contract. The 23-year-old scored four goals in 47 appearances last season as Colchester were relegated from League One. Former Watford trainee Massey netted 21 goals in 178 games for the U's after initially joining on loan in January 2012 before making the move permanent. Massey becomes Orient's third summer signing as they prepare for the upcoming campaign.

Nashville Predators Beat Pittsburgh Penguins to Take 3-1 Stanley Cup Final Lead The Nashville Predators moved within one win of their first Stanley Cup title after beating the Pittsburgh Penguins 4-1 in game four at Bridgestone Arena. Calle Jarnkrok opened the scoring for the hosts before Sidney Crosby equalised for the defending champions. Frederick Gaudreau and Viktor Arvidsson then struck for Nashville in the second period, before Filip Forsberg fired into an empty net late on to seal the victory. Predators goaltender Pekka Rinne made 23 saves to secure back-to-back victories over Pittsburgh. Nashville, playing in their first Stanley Cup final since their inception in 1998, now lead the best-of-seven series 3-1. Game five takes place in Pittsburgh on Thursday (01:00 BST on Friday), where the Predators will have their first opportunity to clinch the championship. Prior to the game, Predators coach Peter Laviolette asked fans to stop throwing dead catfish onto the ice - a tradition dating back to 2003. However, fans defied the request, with a catfish adorned with Predators paraphernalia thrown before the game. Staff had to clear multiple catfish during play, continuing a trend from previous games in the series.

Federal Reserve Maintains Interest Rates and Bond-Buying Programme The Federal Reserve has announced it will continue its current monetary policy, keeping interest rates near zero and maintaining its bond-buying programme as the US economy shows mixed signals of recovery. The central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee kept its key interest rate at zero to 0.25%, citing persistently high unemployment as the primary reason for maintaining its quantitative easing policy. The decision comes despite the US economy rebounding to grow by 2.5% in the first quarter, a figure that still fell short of expectations. Quantitative easing, a policy whereby the Federal Reserve purchases bonds to increase the money supply and improve liquidity in the financial system, aims to spark economic growth and support employment. The current programme, known as QE3, had been expected by many analysts to be reduced in the second half of this year, but recent economic data has cast doubt on that timeline. "Expectations for tapering off of the Fed's outcome-based purchases have been pushed back due to recent softening in the economic data," stated the private sector Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee on Wednesday. Paul Ashworth, chief US economist at Capital Economics, suggested the Federal Reserve's language indicates flexibility in either direction. "The fact that the Fed felt it necessary to point out that the pace of purchases can be adjusted in both directions presumably means that, at the very least, it is less inclined to slow the rate of purchases any time soon," he said. Employment figures remain a concern, with US private sector employers adding only 88,000 jobs in March—less than half the 200,000 needed to maintain employment levels given population growth. The economy presents a mixed picture: whilst the housing sector shows positive signs with buoyant house prices, manufacturing data reveals factory activity barely grew in April. Analysts now expect any reduction in quantitative easing to occur closer to year-end, if at all.

Police Appeal for Community Help in Wester Hailes Murder Investigation Police are intensifying efforts to solve the murder of Robbie Morrison, who was fatally attacked in Dumbryden Gardens, Wester Hailes, at approximately 4:30 PM on August 22nd. The 31-year-old's death has prompted a significant police response in the area. Detective Chief Inspector Gary Cunningham emphasized the crucial role the community could play in solving the case. "It is clear from our inquiries that the community holds vital information," he stated. One week after the horrific attack, investigators are conducting high-visibility patrols and door-to-door inquiries with local residents. Officers will be questioning witnesses about suspicious activity or individuals seen in Dumbryden Gardens on the Friday afternoon of the incident. "While our officers are making progress with the investigation, we would urge anyone with any information to come forward," DCI Cunningham said. "We will also ask if they have heard something which may prove key to our investigation." Chief Inspector Mark Rennie reassured the public that inquiries suggest Mr. Morrison's murder was an isolated incident. "Our officers are doing everything they can to trace the person who carried out this murder," he added. Witnesses can provide information confidentially by calling 01506 445 620 or texting 07769 239 691.

UK Troops in Estonia Given Guide to Strip Clubs During NATO Exercise British troops deployed to Estonia for a major NATO military exercise were issued with an official guide that included detailed recommendations for strip clubs in the capital Tallinn, the BBC has learned. The advice was featured in a booklet titled "Tallinn guide for friendly forces", given to troops taking part in a NATO Steadfast Javelin training operation. The operation took place in May 2015. The Ministry of Defence would not comment on the guide but said advice on "staying safe" was routinely given to troops while abroad. The BBC requested copies of various documents concerning the operation, also known as Exercise Hedgehog. In its response, the department provided the guide, which includes a section detailing three strip clubs in Tallinn. Lasso Baar was said to be a "big strip bar with one of the prettiest dancers" and Soho was identified as the "biggest strip club in Estonia". X Club was billed as "the most professional strip club with various elements". The guide also gave British troops further advice on what to expect at Estonian strip clubs. Troops were informed that "all strip clubs offer private rooms for individual dances", and that "the average level of rolling tips to girls is 5 to 20 euros". They were also advised "to use cash in such places". Asked if it was appropriate for the government to provide such material, a spokeswoman for the Ministry of Defence said: "As you would expect, we routinely provide guidance to our people about staying safe while on deployment." The department would not comment on who had produced the guide, how it had been distributed to troops, or whether it would be issued to troops serving in Estonia in future. The guide included other nightlife tips, such as pubs Mad Murphy's and Hell Hunt, or visiting the city's historic Old Town for a dash of Baltic culture. It also offered a warning on public drinking, saying that to avoid a police fine, "when you want to drink spirits in the street it is wise to cover the bottles". And it includes gift ideas for British troops. It suggests a visit to a shop called Bonbon Lingerie as a good place to pick up something special for wives and girlfriends. In terms of a bottle of something to bring home, it suggests Vana Tallinn or Old Tallinn liquor. A spokesperson for the Estonian embassy in London said the Estonian government had not produced the guide. "According to the information received from the Estonian Defence Forces this is not an official document produced by or for the Government of Estonia." Operation Steadfast Javelin was a major NATO training exercise, in which 13,000 troops and reserves defended positions against a simulated attack by land and air.

Elton John Leads Boycott Against Dolce & Gabbana Over "Synthetic Children" Comments Sir Elton John has sparked a celebrity-led boycott of fashion house Dolce & Gabbana after the designers made controversial comments about same-sex families and children born through surrogacy. The music icon, who has two sons with husband David Furnish via a surrogate, took to Instagram urging fans to boycott the Italian brand. The #BoycottDolceGabbana hashtag quickly trended on Twitter, with numerous celebrities and supporters joining the protest. The controversy erupted following an interview with Italian magazine Panorama, where designer Domenico Dolce stated: "You are born to a mother and a father - or at least that's how it should be." He referred to children born through assisted reproduction as "children of chemistry, synthetic children" and criticized "rented uterus, semen chosen from a catalogue." Singer Ricky Martin, father to six-year-old twins born via surrogate, also condemned the remarks. The backlash extended beyond celebrities, with parents of IVF-conceived children sharing family photos across social media platforms in solidarity. Following the intense criticism, designer Stefano Gabbana issued a statement clarifying "it was never our intention to judge other people's choice," adding "We do believe in freedom and love." The incident has reignited debates about family diversity and reproductive rights in the fashion industry.

Pair Remanded Over Death of Pembrokeshire Woman Betty Guy of Johnstown, Pembrokeshire, died in November 2011. Her daughter Penelope John, 50, of St Dogmaels and grandson Barry Rogers, 32, of Fishguard, were arrested earlier this month. The pair appeared at Swansea Crown Court on Friday and were remanded in custody ahead of the next hearing in October. While pleas were not entered, a date of January 2018 was laid down for the start of a three-week trial.

Scottish Rivals Higgins and McManus to Meet at Glasgow Masters Scottish snooker stars John Higgins and Alan McManus will clash on Monday 12 December at Glasgow's Emirates Arena in their 23rd career meeting. Four-time world champion Higgins, 41, arrives in impressive form, having secured consecutive titles at the China Championship and Champion of Champions this season. The world number four recently reached the UK Championship quarter-finals before losing to eventual winner Mark Selby. McManus, 45, the 1994 Masters champion, comes into the match after a second-round exit at the UK Championship, falling to Jamie Jones. The pair last met at the World Championship in April, where McManus emerged victorious 13-11. Despite that result, Higgins maintains a 12-10 advantage in their overall head-to-head record. Elsewhere in the draw, fellow Scot Stephen Maguire faces China's Zhou Yuelong on Tuesday, whilst Judd Trump opens against Zhang Yong and Ronnie O'Sullivan meets Matthew Selt.

Manila Apec Summit: Police and Protesters Clash as Leaders Address Terror Threat Hundreds of protesters clashed with police in Manila on Thursday as world leaders gathered for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, with officers deploying water cannons to control crowds demonstrating against globalization. Anti-globalisation protesters gathered in the Manila Bay area, where Apec meetings have been held, demanding the trade bloc be dismantled. Protest leader Renato Reyes told the Associated Press: "Apec and imperialist globalisation have only benefited the rich countries while further impoverishing developing countries like the Philippines." Demonstrators carrying large placards chanted anti-Apec and anti-US slogans including "down with Apec, down with America" under intense sun. Hundreds of police officers equipped with batons, truncheons and shields blocked protesters from approaching the venue, while trucks with water cannons stood ready to disperse crowds. Police reportedly played loud dance music in an attempt to drown out the unified voices of demonstrators. The summit has been overshadowed by escalating tensions over territorial disputes in the South China Sea, where China's land reclamation activities have alarmed neighbouring nations. US President Barack Obama called for China to halt its construction work on disputed reefs and signed defence agreements with the Philippines, one of several countries locked in territorial disputes with Beijing. "There is a need for bold steps to lower tensions" in the region, Mr Obama stated. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also attending the conference, has not yet publicly addressed the issue. China maintains its activities are legal and insists it has no plans to militarise the newly constructed artificial islands. The Paris terror attacks have also cast a shadow over proceedings, with leaders calling for enhanced global anti-terror cooperation. A draft declaration expected to be released later today indicates summit leaders will "strongly condemn" all acts of terrorism and emphasize the "urgent need for increased international co-operation and solidarity in the fight against terrorism." Tens of thousands of soldiers and police officers have been deployed across Manila to guard against disruptions and potential terrorist threats during the high-profile gathering. World leaders have also discussed climate change and regional economic cooperation during the summit sessions.

Woman Who Stabbed Partner to Death in'Flash of Temper' Jailed for Life A woman who stabbed her partner to death with a kitchen knife in a sudden outburst of anger has been sentenced to life in prison. Michelle Spencer, 48, drove a four inch (11cm) kitchen knife into David Butterfield, 43, at their home in Gomersal, West Yorkshire in January. She initially claimed not to know the attacker's identity but later accepted responsibility for the killing. Spencer, who admitted murder, was sentenced to life at Leeds Crown Court. Mr Justice Michael Soole said the stabbing had taken place in "a flash of temper with fatal consequences". "This was an utterly unprovoked assault with a knife on your innocent partner," he said. "In a sudden outburst of unreasoned anger you deliberately stabbed him once and with very considerable force, causing him almost immediate death." ## Pattern of Violence Uncovered Prosecutor Simon Waley told the court the couple had been together for about 16 months at the time of the killing. He said witnesses claimed they had a "close relationship" but had seen injuries to Mr Butterfield on more than one occasion. West Yorkshire Police said they had also uncovered evidence "of unreported violence which Spencer had inflicted on Mr Butterfield and her previous partners". On the night of the murder Mr Butterfield had come back from the shops at about 18:25 GMT to find Spencer preparing a meal. When Mr Butterfield entered the room, Spencer had asked him whether he was going to cheer up, the court heard. "She described him coming towards her for a kiss and a cuddle," Mr Waley told the court. "She said that after they had come together she saw an injury to his chest and she called for an ambulance. "During that call she said'He's been stabbed in the chest'. She was asked'By whom?' and at that stage she said she didn't know and was indicating that it had happened when he was out." The court heard Spencer later told police she accepted stabbing Mr Butterfield but it had been an accident. ##'Deeply Remorseful' Michelle Colborne QC defending said her client had struggled to come to terms with "the fact she could have done this to the person she loved most in the world". "This momentary loss of temper, fatal action, is not something that would ever have been pre-meditated or even contemplated in the mind of the defendant," she said. "It's clear that the meal had been prepared, the knife was being used to cut potatoes, and, within a matter of moments a minor disturbance resulted in this shocking act. She is deeply remorseful and has never tried to suggest that there was any underlying motive." Det Insp Ben McDonald said: "As a result of diligent and meticulous inquiries by the Police investigation team, a violent woman has been brought to justice. "Having originally lied to the police regarding the circumstances, the team have been able to uncover the facts, which has resulted in a guilty plea. "Mr Butterfield had suffered domestic abuse at the hands of his partner and ultimately paid the price for the fact that these incidents were never reported to the police."

Worcestershire's Tom Kohler-Cadmore Signs Contract Extension After Maiden Century Worcestershire batsman Tom Kohler-Cadmore has committed his future to the county after signing a contract extension that will keep him at New Road until 2017. The 21-year-old, who had 12 months remaining on his existing deal, has penned a two-year contract following an impressive end to the season that saw him score his maiden first-class century against Middlesex. "I haven't scored the weight of runs I would have liked but I feel there is a lot more to come," Kohler-Cadmore said. "It was massive to get that first century. The first one is probably the hardest one to get and once you've got one, you have the belief and the confidence that you are going to get a lot more." Director of cricket Steve Rhodes praised the young batsman's development: "Getting that hundred was a big relief to him and thoroughly deserved. The areas we asked him to go away and learn in second-team cricket have certainly paid off and he is scoring good runs." Kohler-Cadmore had lost his place in the County Championship side due to early-season struggles but seized his opportunity when recalled for the final two games, replacing the injured Alex Gidman. He accumulated 257 runs, including an impressive 89 against Durham and a superb unbeaten 130 that helped Worcestershire defeat second-placed Middlesex at New Road. The signing is part of a busy period for the county, with Ross Whiteley committing for four more years, while Brett D'Oliveira, Joe Leach, Tom Fell, Joe Clarke and Ed Barnard have all signed three-year extensions.

School Staff to Issue Parking Tickets in Thurrock Council Pilot Scheme A controversial pilot scheme allowing school staff to issue parking tickets outside a Tilbury primary school will begin on Monday, Thurrock Council has announced. The initiative, first reported by Your Thurrock, comes as the council admits it lacks sufficient traffic wardens to tackle illegal parking outside schools across the borough.
