NHS Borders medical director Dr Cliff Sharp expressed support for the decision, citing "practical, safety and quality of care reasons." Registered patients have been sent letters advising them of the closure and inviting them to discuss concerns with NHS Borders by 21 July. However, Mr Lamont criticized the short notice period. "This is a really disappointing decision which will make it more difficult for some to access GP care," he said. "To announce a closure with only a month's notice is far from ideal and the priority must be to ensure that patients are properly supported during this time." The closure highlights ongoing pressures facing rural healthcare provision in Scotland.

Town Appoints First Official Jester in 700 Years Erwyd le Fol, also known as Russell Erwood, 34, has been officially appointed as town jester in a historic naming ceremony held in the town square. The medieval-themed event featured a birds of prey demonstration, traditional games, and a colourful parade to mark the occasion. Funded by the local chamber of trade, Mr le Fol will represent the town at various functions wearing traditional jester attire, including a distinctive hat with donkey ears. "It's amazing. It's phenomenal. To be the first jester of a town in 700 years feels unreal," he said following the ceremony.

Jobcentre Plus Offices in Glasgow Face Closure Under DWP Review The Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) announced on Wednesday plans to close several Jobcentre Plus offices in Glasgow as part of a comprehensive estate review, prompting concerns from Scottish government officials. Scottish Employability Minister Jamie Hepburn has written to the department seeking clarity on the proposed closures. The DWP has committed to public consultation on any closures that would increase travel distances by more than three miles for claimants. Denise Horsfall, DWP work services director for Scotland, told BBC Radio's Good Morning Scotland programme that three locations – Maryhill, Castlemilk and Bridgton – would see travel distances increase to up to four miles. These offices could remain open depending on consultation outcomes. Meanwhile, Jobcentre Plus offices in Govan, Drumchapel and Laurieston will not be affected by the proposals. Minister Hepburn expressed frustration that discussions had not taken place with the Scottish Government, particularly given ongoing collaboration on transferring new employability support powers. "My first concern is to understand how DWP have assessed the impact of these proposed changes on their customers at a time when they are increasing the level of Jobcentre Plus-based support in favour of reducing funding for devolved employment provision," he said. He also demanded clarification on whether further closures are planned across the wider Jobcentre Plus network. A final decision is expected within six months, with completion scheduled for 31 March 2018.

Parents Mistakenly Believe Tanning is Healthy for Children, Survey Reveals A concerning new survey has revealed that approximately one-third of parents in the UK mistakenly believe that getting a tan is beneficial for their children's health, with a quarter actively encouraging their offspring to develop a suntan. The findings, based on interviews with 1,000 parents of children aged 11 and younger, have raised alarm bells among health professionals, particularly as the UK experiences its hottest June day since the summer of 1976. Perhaps most worryingly, some parents admitted to allowing their children to use sunbeds, despite well-documented health risks. One in ten parents said they had instructed their child to remove their top in the sun specifically "so they don't get tan lines." Additionally, more than one in five parents (21%) stated they would only consider applying sunscreen if their child's skin started to turn red and burn. Medical experts are quick to dispel the myth that tanning is healthy. A tan does not protect against the sun's harmful rays – in fact, it's actually a sign that skin damage has already occurred. When skin is exposed to sunlight, cells called melanocytes produce more dark pigment, known as melanin, in an attempt to absorb further UV radiation. This darkening process is the skin's defensive response to damage, not a sign of health. Repeated sun exposure, particularly during childhood, can significantly increase the risk of developing skin cancer in later life. Children and babies have considerably more sensitive skin than adults, making protection even more critical. Health guidelines recommend that infants under six months should be kept out of direct strong sunlight entirely. From March to October in the UK, children should be protected with appropriate clothing, sunscreen with adequate SPF, and kept in the shade during peak UV hours. Many parents don't realise that UV radiation cannot be felt, making it easy to get sunburnt even on overcast days when temperatures aren't particularly warm. Clare Nasir, Met Office presenter and meteorologist, emphasized that "protecting against skin cancer isn't something parents should leave to chance." She noted that UV levels are typically highest between May and September, and that clouds don't always block harmful UV rays. Parents can check daily UV forecasts on the Met Office website or app. Dr Nigel Acheson from NHS England acknowledged that some sun exposure is beneficial for vitamin D production but cautioned against overdoing it. "We typically recommend that people spend no more than 10 to 15 minutes in the UK summer sun, unprotected, several times a week," he explained. Anyone spending longer than 15 minutes in the sun should apply sun protection factor 15 or higher. Nicola Smith from Cancer Research UK was unequivocal: "There's no such thing as a safe tan, from the sun or sunbeds. A suntan is your skin's way of trying to protect itself from too much sun. And a sunburn is a clear sign that your skin has been damaged." For more guidance on sun safety, parents are encouraged to follow NHS England's skin cancer campaign #CoverUpMate on Twitter.

Venezuelan Woman Killed as Gunmen Attack Symbolic Opposition Vote A woman was shot dead and three others wounded when gunmen on motorcycles opened fire on voters participating in an unofficial referendum in Venezuela on Sunday, escalating tensions in a country already gripped by months of deadly political violence. The victim, identified by prosecutors as Xiomara Soledad Scott, died minutes after arriving at hospital following the attack in Catia, a traditionally pro-government neighbourhood in the capital, Caracas. The opposition quickly blamed "paramilitary" gangs for the shooting. Video footage from the scene captured panicked voters fleeing as gunshots rang out, with many seeking refuge in a nearby church. Opposition spokesman Carlos Ocariz expressed deep sorrow over the incident, saying: "We lament this very much, with great pain." Prosecutors announced they would investigate the deadly attack. The shooting occurred as millions of Venezuelans participated in a symbolic vote organized by opposition politicians to reject President Nicolas Maduro's plans for a new constituent assembly. The unofficial referendum, held at improvised polling stations including theatres, sports grounds and roundabouts across Venezuela and in more than 100 countries worldwide, asked citizens three key questions: whether they opposed the new assembly, wanted early elections before Maduro's term ends in 2018, and whether the armed forces should defend the current constitution. Despite long queues and a generally festive atmosphere at most polling sites, President Maduro dismissed the exercise as "meaningless," calling it an internal opposition consultation conducted "without electoral rulebooks, without prior verification." The violence underscored the deepening crisis in Venezuela, where more than 100 people have died in political clashes since April. In a separate incident on Sunday, journalist Luis Olavarrieta was kidnapped, robbed and beaten by a group of attackers before managing to escape. Images later emerged showing him receiving medical treatment. The opposition organized the unofficial vote to demonstrate public rejection of Maduro's plans for an official election on July 30 to create a new constituent assembly. This body would have sweeping powers to rewrite the constitution and dissolve existing state institutions, leading critics to warn it could pave the way for dictatorship. President Maduro argues the constituent assembly is necessary to resolve Venezuela's severe economic and political crisis. He claims a new constitution would "neutralize" the opposition and defeat "coup-plotters," thereby promoting peace. However, opposition leaders fear the process would delay scheduled regional and presidential elections while further weakening the National Assembly, the country's opposition-controlled legislative body. The BBC's South America correspondent Katy Watson noted that while Sunday's vote was purely symbolic, the opposition hoped a strong turnout would increase pressure on the government to abandon its constituent assembly plans.

Nazi-Era Machine Gun Seized in Australian Traffic Stop CENTRAL COAST, NSW - Police have seized a World War II-era Nazi machine gun during a routine traffic stop on Australia's Central Coast, authorities announced Monday. Officers discovered an MP40 sub-machine gun along with 60 rounds of ammunition while searching a vehicle on Sunday night. The weapon, developed in Nazi Germany with more than a million produced during the war, was found to be missing its barrel, though initial examinations suggest it remained operational. A 40-year-old male passenger was arrested and charged with possessing a prohibited firearm. He was refused bail and appeared at Wyong Local Court on Monday. Police will conduct a forensic examination to determine if the weapon is linked to any shooting incidents. The arrest comes just days after Australia launched a national gun amnesty in response to growing terrorism threats and an influx of illegal weapons. Authorities estimate approximately 260,000 illicit firearms are currently circulating in the country, despite strict gun control laws requiring all firearms to be registered and licensed. Those caught with prohibited weapons during the amnesty period face severe penalties: fines up to A$280,000 ($212,730; £166,480) or imprisonment for up to 14 years. Australia's last major gun amnesty followed the 1996 Port Arthur massacre in Tasmania, where 35 people were killed. That program resulted in the destruction of approximately 650,000 firearms and contributed to a significant decline in gun-related crimes nationwide.

Children Help Clean Cemetery After Vandalism Attack More than 20 schoolchildren rolled up their sleeves to help restore a Welsh cemetery after vandals caused heartbreaking damage to the historic site. Seven graves in Ferndale Cemetery were deliberately toppled in January and rubbish left strewn across the site. The senseless act of vandalism shocked the local community and left grieving families devastated. More than 20 children from nearby Ferndale Community School took part in the litter pick on Tuesday, determined to restore dignity to the resting place. The children collected more than 20 bags of rubbish including a broken bicycle and several traffic cones that had been discarded across the grounds. PC Steve Davies, who organized the community clean-up, said he noticed the rubbish when examining the area. "I have a little son who passed away. I know the price, I know the cost implications and the emotional impact it would have on someone to come and visit a grave and seeing that their headstone has been damaged or destroyed," he told the BBC. "It's just getting people together in response to what's happened to the headstones to build the respect up amongst the community," he added. Among the pupils helping was Rachel, 14, who said she found the experience upsetting. "My ancestors' gravestones haven't been damaged and I'm quite grateful but when I see the others, it makes me wonder how their relatives must feel," she said. "It's upsetting, it's left me quite distraught to be honest." A local stonemason has agreed to repair the headstones and South Wales Police is still investigating.

Police Search for Missing Driver After M6 Crash Police are growing increasingly concerned for a motorist who disappeared after a crash on the M6 motorway. Zahid Mirza, 40, from Chelmsley Wood, crashed on the M6 between junctions 4A and 5 on 15 January. His family has had no contact with him since the incident. Detective Superintendent Tom Chisholm said: "We have now learned that Mr Mirza's family have had no contact with him since then, so we are very concerned for his safety." Officers fear Mr Mirza may have come to harm and are conducting searches near the motorway. "At the time of the collision a search was made of the immediate area, but there was no trace of the driver," Det Supt Chisholm added. Mr Mirza is described as 5ft 9ins tall with a stocky build, short dark hair, and wears glasses. West Midlands Police have urged anyone with information to come forward.

Harris Reflects on Lean Years After Career-Best Match Figures at Lord's Middlesex seamer James Harris has spoken candidly about the struggles he faced following his high-profile move from Glamorgan, after recording career-best match figures against his former county. The 24-year-old, who moved to Lord's from Glamorgan at the end of 2012, took 9-34 in the second innings to finish with match figures of 13-103. "I've had two very lean years which has hurt me," he told BBC London 94.9. "I came here as a fairly big signing and expected to be doing these sort of things from the off. I am there to perform and I wasn't doing it." The right-arm seamer added: "I came on a decent contract and wasn't performing so I was getting some criticism, and rightly so." Harris took 21 wickets at an average of 38.33 in his first season at Middlesex but his second year in north London was more difficult, following a change in his action. He took just 12 wickets at 55.50 in his seven appearances and returned to Glamorgan on loan in order to find form. "We changed last year to be better - you want to be better and you want to improve," he said. "Many things have been said that if I was half a yard quicker I'd be that much closer to hopefully getting an England call-up. That's what we went searching for. "You could argue that we probably found it, but it was at the detriment to what I did naturally. I lost my height, I wasn't hitting the seam and I wasn't causing problems." Harris has now re-modified his bowling action over the winter, culminating in his best bowling figures since his second first-class match for Glamorgan in 2007, aged just 17. "We made a choice to go back. This is the type of bowler I have always been," he said. "I was never going to be express but I'm hopefully bowling at a decent enough pace and doing a bit with it. "I said all the way through the summer so far that I had been bowling quite nicely but there was still something to click. I got in a nice rhythm and I'm thrilled. It has been a long wait to get another 10-for."

Taliban Execute Woman in Public in Afghanistan's Jowzjan Province A video showing the public execution of a woman by the Taliban has emerged on social media, officials confirmed on Wednesday. The footage, filmed one to two months ago in Jowzjan Province, shows a woman in a burqa sitting on the ground as a crowd listens to the verdict being read before she is shot in the back of the head. The Taliban have not issued any statement regarding the incident, though similar killings in previous years have drawn widespread international condemnation. Public executions of women were common practice during Taliban rule in the 1990s, when the group frequently carried out such punishments, typically for alleged adultery, in Kabul's main stadium. These brutal practices have persisted in various forms since then. In 2012, a young woman was stoned to death in central Afghanistan's Ghor province on adultery charges. The previous year, both a woman and the man she had eloped with were stoned to death in Kunduz province's Dashte Archi district. A Taliban spokesman defended the 2011 stoning at the time, stating that such punishment was prescribed in Islamic law and the Koran, dismissing critics as attempting to impose "foreign thinking" on Afghanistan. Extrajudicial killings remain a serious problem throughout Afghanistan. In a high-profile case last March, Farkhunda Malikzada was brutally beaten and burned alive in downtown Kabul after being falsely accused of desecrating the Koran. Her murder sparked nationwide protests and international outrage over violence against Afghan women.

Man Shot Dead in "Cold-Blooded Execution" at West Belfast Home A father of one was killed in what police have described as a "cold-blooded, summary execution" at his home in west Belfast on Thursday evening. Joe Reilly, 43, was shot multiple times in the chest and died at the scene at Glenwood Court in Poleglass. Two other people who were in the house at the time were forced to lie on the kitchen floor while the fatal shooting took place. The incident, reported to police at approximately 20:15 BST on Thursday, marks the second shooting in the area in less than a week. Detective Chief Inspector Peter Montgomery said the killing was almost beyond description. "It's really difficult to know how to describe what happened last night, the adjectives brutal, senseless and barbaric are inadequate," he said. "This was a cold-blooded, summary execution of a man in his own house. At this early stage of my investigation I have no motive for Joe Reilly's murder and I will keep a completely open mind as to why has been killed." DCI Montgomery confirmed that Mr Reilly was known to police and had a criminal record. He appealed for information about three children who were reportedly seen in the area as the gunmen fled the scene. Neighbours who rushed to help on Thursday night described Mr Reilly as a quiet man who rarely left his home. Sinn Féin MLA Jennifer McCann described "distressing scenes" as family members arrived at the police cordon. "This brutal killing has achieved nothing other than plunging another family into grief and despair," she said. "This is a good community and there's no support for this." SDLP MLA Alex Attwood told Good Morning Ulster: "A gunman or gunmen turned up at a house and at least two shots were fired. The result is that one man is dead. His family are in deep distress and the community is tangibly shocked and shaken." He accused those responsible of "brutally undermining the rule of law." Alliance MLA Trevor Lunn offered his "deepest condolences" to the family, adding: "This follows another shooting in the same area last week and has now left a family without a loved one through the evil actions of others." People Before Profit Councillor Matt Collins said he was "deeply disturbed by this senseless and unjustifiable attack." The murder follows a pattern of violence in the area. Last Sunday, a man was shot several times in the leg in a paramilitary-style attack in nearby Glenwood Drive. On Wednesday, another man was shot in the leg in Dungiven, County Londonderry. Police have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

Deadly Green Mamba Snake Euthanised After Discovery on Ship at Scottish Port A highly venomous western green mamba snake discovered on a ship that had docked from west Africa on Wednesday has been destroyed due to health and safety concerns. Workers aboard the vessel discovered the deadly reptile and secured it in a box before contacting animal welfare authorities. The snake was transported under police escort to a Scottish SPCA animal centre in Drumoak, Aberdeenshire. Despite the safe capture, the SSPCA made the difficult decision to euthanise the snake after determining the nearest available anti-venom was located in London, posing significant risk to handlers and the public. The western green mamba, native to coastal tropical rainforests of west Africa, preys on small animals and rodents. According to experts, its venomous bite can prove fatal to humans in as little as 30 minutes.

Motorcyclist Dies After Collision in Penkridge A motorcyclist has died following a collision between a Kawasaki motorbike and a Toyota Land Cruiser in Teddesley Road, Penkridge, at 17:40 BST on Monday. Despite efforts by police officers, paramedics and doctors, the motorcyclist was confirmed dead after arriving at hospital by air ambulance, Staffordshire Police said. The Toyota driver escaped injury in the crash, which closed the road for three hours. Police have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

Blackburn Rovers: Tommie Hoban Set for February Return from Injury Blackburn Rovers manager Owen Coyle is hopeful that on-loan defender Tommie Hoban will return to action later this month. The 22-year-old, who arrived from Watford in August, has been sidelined since mid-October after dislocating his shoulder during a training session, having made just 10 appearances for the club. "He's got a meeting with the surgeon that did his operation and then hopefully he can get the all-clear," Coyle told the club website. "To my mind I would love to have Tommie available from the middle of February towards the end of the month because that would add a real quality player." Rovers currently sit 22nd in the Championship table, one point from safety, making Hoban's return potentially crucial to their survival bid.

Franz Ferdinand to Headline Belladrum Festival in Scottish Highlands Scottish rock band Franz Ferdinand will make their debut performance at the Belladrum Tartan Heart Festival, marking a significant moment for the Highland event. The three-day festival, scheduled for 3-5 August 2017 near Beauly in the Scottish Highlands, has announced an impressive lineup. Franz Ferdinand will headline the closing night, supported by fellow Scottish artist KT Tunstall. Adding to the star-studded bill, disco icons Sister Sledge will headline Thursday's opening night. Festival promoter Joe Gibbs expressed his enthusiasm: "This is the first time Franz Ferdinand has played Bella and we are totally delighted to welcome them to our stage. I couldn't think of a better act to close out the festival." Regarding Tunstall's return, Gibbs noted she previously appeared as an unannounced special guest but is now officially confirmed on the programme.

Amber Heard and Johnny Depp Restraining Order Hearing Delayed A Los Angeles judge has ruled that a hearing regarding actress Amber Heard's restraining order against Johnny Depp will begin on 17 August, two days later than originally scheduled, after determining the proceedings could take up to five days to complete. Heard filed for divorce from Depp on 23 May and subsequently obtained a temporary restraining order after accusing the actor of repeatedly hitting her. If the court rules in her favour, the restraining order could be extended for up to five years. Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Carl H Moor ruled on Tuesday that Heard should sit for a deposition on Friday, with Depp providing sworn testimony on Saturday. The judge determined that Depp—who has denied the abuse allegations through his lawyer—will not be permitted to attend Heard's deposition. The couple met while co-starring in the 2011 film The Rum Diary and married in February 2015. Depp, 53, was ordered to maintain no contact with Heard, 30, and remain 100 yards away from her following her allegations that he struck her and threw a mobile phone during an argument in May. Follow us on Twitter @BBCNewsEnts, on Instagram at bbcnewsents, or email entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

Airports Commission Extends Runway Consultation Over Air Pollution Concerns Sir Howard Davies, chairman of the Airports Commission, has announced an extension to take additional evidence on air pollution issues before finalizing runway expansion recommendations. The decision follows a Supreme Court ruling in April that mandated stronger UK action on air quality improvements. The commission has already shortlisted three runway options: expansion at Heathrow or Gatwick airports. An immediate consultation period will run until Friday, 29 May. The final report, originally scheduled for next month, faces potential delays due to this additional review process. The Airports Commission launched its comprehensive inquiry three years ago, with publication deliberately postponed until after the general election to avoid politicization of the infrastructure decision.

Quitongo Clinches Victory as Morton Edge Past Dunfermline **Morton secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Dunfermline Athletic in a hard-fought Scottish Championship encounter, with Jai Quitongo's spectacular late strike proving to be the decisive moment.** The home side took an early lead through Gary Oliver, who displayed excellent individual skill to skip past a couple of challenges before driving a low shot past the Dunfermline goalkeeper. The opener gave Morton confidence and control in the opening exchanges at Cappielow Park. However, Dunfermline showed their resilience and pulled level on the half-hour mark through somewhat fortunate circumstances. Callum Fordyce's shot was heading towards goal when Nicky Clark's deflection wrong-footed the Morton keeper and found the back of the net, restoring parity to the contest. The match became increasingly fractious in the second half, with referee officials having to reach for their cards on multiple occasions. Ben Richards-Everton, Joe Cardle, Nicky Clark, Jamie McDonagh, Lewis Martin, and match-winner Quitongo all found their names in the book as tensions rose and challenges flew in. Both managers made tactical changes in an attempt to find a winner. Dunfermline boss introduced Kallum Higginbotham and Farid El Alagui from the bench, replacing Michael Paton and Gavin Reilly respectively, while Morton brought on Scott Tiffoney for Aidan Nesbitt before late substitute Thomas Orr replaced the impressive Gary Oliver. The Pars pushed forward in search of a winner, with Lee Ashcroft coming close with a header from a corner that missed the target. Goalkeeper Andy McNeil was also called into action to preserve Morton's chances of claiming all three points. With time running out and a draw looking the likely outcome, Quitongo produced a moment of individual brilliance that settled the contest. Receiving the ball outside the box from Tiffoney, the Morton forward unleashed a powerful right-footed effort that crashed off the underside of the crossbar and into the net, sending the home fans into raptures. Despite late pressure from the visitors, Morton held firm to secure all three points. The victory will provide a significant boost to their league ambitions, while Dunfermline will rue their inability to hold onto their equalizer and their failure to convert chances in the second period. Gary Oliver's late effort that sailed high and wide summed up Morton's desperation to add a third, but Quitongo's stunning strike proved sufficient to seal a memorable victory for the Greenock side.

Woodford Fund Scraps Bonuses in City Pay Shake-up Star fund manager Neil Woodford has abolished bonuses at his investment firm, in an unusual move that challenges the City of London's long-held belief that performance-related pay is essential for motivating staff. The 35 employees at Woodford Investment Management will instead receive increases to their basic salaries and benefits package to compensate for the loss of bonus payments. Mr Woodford, who manages £14bn in assets, earned his reputation as one of Britain's most successful stock-pickers during his time at Invesco Perpetual. After launching his own boutique fund management business in 2014, he rapidly attracted significant investment from those hoping he would continue delivering the above-average returns that marked his Invesco career. Craig Newman, chief executive and co-founder of Woodford Investment Management, explained the rationale behind the decision: "While bonuses are an established feature of the financial sector, Neil and I wanted to take the opportunity to do something different that supports the firm's culture and ethos of challenging the status quo." Mr Newman cited extensive academic research suggesting bonuses fail as motivational tools, with employees coming to expect them as standard. "There is little correlation between bonus and performance," he said. "Many studies conclude that bonuses don't work as a motivator, as expectation is already built in. Behavioural studies also suggest that bonuses can lead to short-term decision making and wrong behaviours." The financial crisis intensified scrutiny of City pay practices, particularly the link between remuneration and performance. Top fund managers can earn millions in performance-related bonuses. However, critics of the no-bonus approach argue such incentives are crucial for retaining talented staff who might otherwise seek opportunities elsewhere. They also note that higher fixed salaries make it more difficult for firms to reduce costs during economic downturns. The firm referenced research from The Journal of Corporation Law, which concluded: "Financial incentives are often counterproductive as they encourage gaming, fraud and other dysfunctional behaviours that damage the reputation and culture of the organisation."

Philip Larkin's Hidden Talent: Poet's Photography Collection on Display at Hull University An exhibition showcasing the photographic work of renowned poet Philip Larkin has opened at the University of Hull's Brynmor Jones Library, where he served as librarian for three decades. The display reveals Larkin as an accomplished amateur photographer who captured nearly 6,000 images throughout his lifetime. The collection includes intimate portraits of female companions, friends, and self-portraits, alongside family photographs from his childhood and portraits of literary contemporaries. The exhibition also features familiar scenes of Hull and the East Riding countryside, as well as various landscapes that inspired the celebrated poet's work. University Librarian Dr Richard Heseltine described the collection as "a unique glimpse into Larkin's life, his interests and even subjects which informed some of his poems." The exhibition, running until 23 December, coincides with the publication of a new book by Richard Bedford examining Larkin's photographic portfolio. "It is an unmissable opportunity to come along to see another side of one of the most celebrated poets of our time," Dr Heseltine added, highlighting Larkin's significance to the university's cultural heritage.

Welsh Drug Services Call for Action as Deaths Rise 50% Drug support services in Wales are calling for urgent action after new figures revealed a dramatic 50% increase in drug-related deaths during 2015, reversing a five-year downward trend. Drugaid Cymru has warned that all agencies involved must "get to grips" with the escalating problem, which comes amid concerns about increased heroin availability and purity on Welsh streets. Ifor Glyn, regional director of Drugaid Cymru covering mid and south Wales, described the situation as a "massive issue" for both service providers and the Welsh Government. "Deaths are likely to go up as there is a lot more heroin around, the purity of heroin has been stronger and there's a lot more people who are not known to the services," Mr Glyn explained. "We weren't able to engage with them. It's something that agencies like ourselves and across Wales have got to get to grips with." Among the solutions proposed, Mr Glyn suggested recruiting drug users as informers to help services reach vulnerable individuals. More controversially, he renewed calls for introducing supervised "fix rooms" where users could take drugs under medical supervision. The proposal follows approval in October for Britain's first such facility in Glasgow. "Allowing people to inject in a room is highly controversial," Mr Glyn acknowledged. "I don't want to see people taking drugs but you've got to be pragmatic. There's tonnes of evidence supporting injecting rooms." The Welsh Government currently allocates £50 million annually to its substance misuse delivery plan and is examining options to address the rising death toll between 2016 and 2018. A government spokesman stated their priority was returning to falling death rates: "We are working closely with partners to evaluate the reasons behind the increase and to take action to address it. "This includes working with the substance misuse area planning boards so that everything possible is done to reach those individuals currently not in touch with substance misuse services."

Ivanka Trump Sparks Controversy After Briefly Sitting in for Father at G20 Summit Ivanka Trump has faced widespread criticism after briefly taking her father's seat at a G20 summit table during a meeting with world leaders. The US president had stepped away for a meeting with the Indonesian leader during the G20 meeting. Ms Trump is an adviser to her father, but a leader's absence is usually covered by high-ranking officials. A BBC correspondent at the summit said he could recall no similar precedent. There has been widespread criticism on social media. ## What Happened? Mr Trump returned a short while later to retake his seat between the British prime minister and the Chinese president. Ms Trump did not seem to make any major contribution to the session on African migration and health during her father's absence. A photograph of her presence was tweeted by a Russian attendee, but later deleted. ## Social Media Backlash Some users highlighted that Ms Trump is unelected, or questioned her credentials - as a fashion brand owner - to sit at such a senior diplomatic meeting. Others lampooned her appearance among the world's most powerful leaders after her claim in an interview two weeks ago that she tries to "stay out of politics". But her brother appeared to suggest there was nothing wrong and asked the "outraged left" if they would rather he sat in instead. ## Earlier G20 Appearance Ms Trump had joined her father for an earlier G20 event on Saturday on women's entrepreneurship and finance, along with German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Christine Lagarde, director of the International Monetary Fund. All three women had previously appeared together on a panel during the G20 women's summit in Berlin in April. At that appearance she defended her father as a "tremendous champion of supporting families and enabling them to thrive". Earlier on Saturday, Donald Trump said having him for a father was the only "bad thing" in Ms Trump's life. "I'm very proud of my daughter, Ivanka - always have been, from day one," he told world leaders at the panel on female entrepreneurs. "If she weren't my daughter, it would be so much easier for her. Might be the only bad thing she has going, if you want to know the truth." ## Background While her siblings, Donald Jr and Eric, took over the family business, Ms Trump put her own fashion brand assets in a trust in order to take an unpaid White House position, a move criticised as nepotism. After a brief modelling career as a teenager, Ms Trump was given a job in her father's company. There, she expanded the Trump hotel brand and became an executive vice-president of development, alongside her siblings. Ms Trump is married to Jared Kushner, who also plays in influential role in Donald Trump's White House.

Monks Fear "Catastrophe" as New A96 Route Threatens Abbey Peace Monks at Pluscarden Abbey near Elgin have expressed alarm over preliminary proposals for a new stretch of the A96 road between Forres and Fochabers, warning that routing the highway close to their centuries-old retreat would be disastrous for their contemplative way of life. Brother Michael de Klerk described the community's shock at discovering the potential route. "We couldn't quite believe it, it seemed extraordinary," he told BBC Scotland. "If we are actually living by it, we would find it hard to absorb it, the noise would be day and night." The monk emphasized the abbey's current tranquility: "The valley is quiet - you can hear a cow lowing. You would just hear a constant whirr of traffic." Father Giles, a resident of over 40 years, cited European examples where transportation infrastructure has damaged monastic communities. "There are a lot of monasteries on the continent where they got railways running through and it has just destroyed the place," he said. "People come here for peace. Why destroy the peace here, it's just daft." Transport Scotland stated it is in the early stages of route assessment and won't finalize the corridor option for two years. The agency plans community engagement throughout the process. The A96 upgrade aims to improve journey times and safety between Aberdeen and Inverness by 2030.

Chisora Fined and Given Suspended Ban After Table-Throwing Incident Dereck Chisora has been fined £25,000 and handed a two-year suspended ban following his shocking actions at Wednesday's press conference, where he threw a table at rival Derick Whyte. The British Boxing Board of Control has imposed strict sanctions on the 32-year-old heavyweight, who must also pay £5,000 in costs. The two-year ban will only be activated if Chisora commits another offence during that period. As a consequence of the violent confrontation, the Board has withdrawn its sanction for the bout being a British heavyweight title fight. Whyte, 28, retains his title and has escaped punishment despite telling Chisora during the press conference that he would attack him after their fight. The Manchester clash remains a WBC world heavyweight title eliminator, but organisers have implemented additional safety measures. The fighters will weigh in separately and there will be no face-off between them. The incident occurred when Chisora, who has lost six of his 32 professional fights, picked up a table and hurled it at Whyte despite promoters and coaches positioned between them. Security personnel immediately intervened. Chisora later claimed he was reacting to what he perceived as a threat on his life. The fight features on Saturday's Manchester Arena card, which is headlined by IBF world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua defending his title against Eric Molina. For Whyte, who has one defeat in 20 fights – against Joshua – this would have been his first British title defence.

Scottish League Cup Final to be Held at Celtic Park The Scottish Professional Football League has confirmed that Celtic Park will host the League Cup final between Aberdeen and Inverness Caledonian Thistle on 16 March, with SPFL chief executive Neil Doncaster citing Rangers' fixture the previous day as the decisive factor in the venue selection. With Hampden Park unavailable due to preparations for the Commonwealth Games, organisers faced a choice between Scotland's two other major stadiums. However, Rangers' scheduled match against Dunfermline at Ibrox on 15 March proved to be the "key determining factor" in ruling out that venue. "That's likely to be a live televised game and, in those circumstances, it just wouldn't have been possible for the broadcasters to de-rig on the Saturday and get rigged up in time for the Sunday," Doncaster explained. The decision followed extensive consultation with both finalists, Police Scotland, and broadcasters before Celtic Park was selected. "We've been left with Celtic Park and are delighted to be coming to Celtic Park, which has a huge tradition of hosting big European games," Doncaster said. "We're absolutely sure it'll provide a great venue for the first final for the Scottish Professional Football League." Despite concerns about potential low attendance at the 60,000-capacity stadium, Doncaster expressed optimism about supporter turnout. "Certainly with it being the first major final that Aberdeen have been in for some years and the first ever in Inverness's history, we're certainly expecting big interest from both teams," he said. "Hopefully, there'll be many thousands of fans travelling from the north to enjoy it," he added. Doncaster acknowledged that Glasgow is "blessed" with three stadia capable of holding over 50,000 spectators, though Hampden's unavailability limited options for this year's final. Celtic Park will also host the Scottish Cup final in May, continuing its role as a major venue for Scottish football's showpiece occasions. In a separate matter, Doncaster confirmed that Hearts are reviewing CCTV footage relating to an incident that led to Celtic manager Neil Lennon leaving Aberdeen's semi-final victory early at Tynecastle Stadium on Saturday.

Abuse Inquiry: Ex-Derry care home resident tells of'Taliban-like' treatment A former resident of a Catholic children's home in Londonderry has described the treatment he received there as equivalent to being "reared by the Taliban". The witness lived at St Joseph's in Termonbacca, Londonderry, in the 1950s. He said he became a zombie, introverted and fearing the next beating. The Historical Abuse Inquiry is investigating abuse claims against children's residential institutions from 1922 to 1995. Termonbacca and another Derry home, Nazareth House, were run by the Sisters of Nazareth. The former Termonbacca resident said he lay soaked in urine at night in an attempt to dissuade any sexual abusers. The man, now 65, said he was never told he had brothers in the same home and sisters in another nearby. He said he witnessed an eight-year-old boy being sexually abused, a 10-year-old boy being raped and that he had been hit on the head with a steel industrial ladle. He said he complained about his treatment to a priest after leaving the home. The response was: "You must never speak about this, you must understand..... you and the other orphans are bastards. You are the product of an evil and satanic relationship. You never had a chance." The witness said: "That was the day I left the Catholic Church." He added: "The truth is setting me free today more than this commission knows. I have come here to tell the truth and as I am reaching out, I am reaching out in healing and trying to forgive, but at this moment I cannot. "I have waited 65 years to say this. When I was reared by the Sisters of the Congregation of Nazareth it was equivalent to being reared by the Taliban, such was their sadism, their lack of empathy, their fundamentalism, their lack of dignity to the little helpless boy." He said he ran away but was brought back time after time. One nun smirked and said: "Welcome back, your majesty," the witness said. "Then the beatings would start." The inquiry, being held in Banbridge, County Down, is chaired by retired judge Sir Anthony Hart and is considering cases in 13 residential institutions. Public hearings are due to finish in June 2015, with the inquiry team to report to the Northern Ireland Executive by the start of 2016.

Kellingley Colliery: Miners Vote for Phased Closure of Yorkshire Pit Miners at Kellingley Colliery have voted overwhelmingly in favour of an 18-month phased closure plan, the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) has announced. The ballot saw 79.9% of workers support the managed closure scheme, which was backed by a £10m government loan to UK Coal. The decision means the North Yorkshire pit will avoid an immediate shutdown that could have happened "within days" had workers rejected the proposal. Chris Kitchen of the NUM acknowledged the difficulty of the decision, saying: "At least the men will not be made a scapegoat for closing Kellingley early. The men had hoped to keep the pit open for a longer term future. It's been a tough decision, it's not a nice thing to vote to put yourself or your workmates on the dole." The ballot results showed 719 papers were issued with 658 returned. Of those, 575 voted for the scheme, 81 against, and two were spoiled. UK Coal counted non-returned and spoiled papers as "No" votes, making the final split approximately 80-20 in favour of closure. The managed closure plan also affects Thoresby Colliery in Nottinghamshire. Business minister Michael Fallon had previously stated that both pits had no long-term future. Andrew Mackintosh of UK Coal welcomed the result, saying: "The vote has been a great hurdle jumped over today, a good result I think. We were nervous before we went into it but the alternative to this was closure within a few days. So, difficult as this has been, it is the best option." UK Coal will now report the ballot outcome to investors, including the government, to seek their acceptance of the result. Mr Mackintosh described it as "a significant vote, that's what the investors were looking for." The phased closure will allow workers time to seek alternative employment and provides a more orderly wind-down than an immediate shutdown.

Sri Lanka Elections: UNP Wins Majority as Rajapaksa's Comeback Bid Fails Sri Lanka's United National Party (UNP) secured a decisive victory in Monday's parliamentary elections, winning 106 seats and effectively blocking former President Mahinda Rajapaksa's attempted political comeback. Mr Rajapaksa's United People Freedom Alliance (UPFA) took 95 seats in the polls, which saw high turnout and were widely interpreted as a referendum on the former president's leadership. The result provides the UNP with sufficient seats to form a coalition government with its allies, consolidating the political changes that began with Mr Rajapaksa's unexpected defeat in January's presidential election. Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe, the UNP leader, celebrated the victory as validation of what he called "the 8 January revolution." He called for national unity, saying: "Now it is no longer necessary to be divided as winners and losers. We need to unite as one family to create a new political culture in this country." While Mr Rajapaksa successfully won his parliamentary seat, the election results confine him to the opposition benches, dashing his hopes of leveraging electoral support to force President Maithripala Sirisena into naming him prime minister. The political dynamic is complicated by the fact that both Mr Rajapaksa and Mr Sirisena belong to the UPFA, though they lead rival factions within the alliance. Mr Sirisena's supporters are expected to join the UNP in forming a national unity government. The UNP is also expected to secure support from smaller parties, including the Tamil National Alliance, which won 16 seats, and the leftist JVP, which secured six seats.

NHS Trust Chief Executive Resigns After Regulatory Criticism Dr Mark Newbold has announced his resignation as chief executive of the Heart of England NHS Foundation Trust, saying "the time was right" to step down after four years in the role. The departure comes just weeks after the trust faced criticism for failing to improve A&E waiting times and death rates. The organization, which operates Good Hope Hospital, Heartlands Hospital and Solihull Hospital, has been under scrutiny from Monitor, the health service regulator. In his resignation letter, Dr Newbold acknowledged that intervention by Monitor had prompted him to reconsider his position. He expressed particular regret at being unable to resolve persistent overcrowding issues across the trust's hospitals. "If I had managed to solve the overcrowding, I do not think I would be writing this letter," Dr Newbold wrote. He also reflected that he wished he had focused earlier on "staff engagement" during his tenure. "However, a chief executive has to know when the time is right to pass the baton on and I believe that time is now," he added. The trust confirmed it had accepted his resignation and said it would be "in a position to announce new arrangements in the near future." A statement noted that Dr Newbold believed new leadership would provide "fresh impetus" for the organization's continued improvement.

Iranians Celebrate Nuclear Deal as Historic Agreement Emerges The Iranian capital experienced an unusual quiet Thursday night as news of a breakthrough nuclear agreement began to surface, according to Thomas Erdbrink of the New York Times. The silence reflected a nation transfixed by state television, which broadcast a live speech by a U.S. president for what is believed to be the first time since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Journalist Pedram Alvandi even took a "selfie with Obama." After midnight, the quiet transformed into jubilation. Videos showed Iranians flooding the streets, chanting, singing, dancing and clapping while waving flags and blaring car horns. Others celebrated privately at home. Despite official bans on social media networks, hundreds of posts appeared online documenting the celebrations. On Friday morning, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif and his negotiating team received a hero's welcome from crowds upon returning to Tehran from Lausanne, where final talks were held. However, reactions on social media were mixed. While largely positive, some users questioned whether Iran could have secured better terms. "@RezaKhonsa wrote, "The removal of the sanctions was good but it eventually ended against our interests." Blogger Reza Parchizadeh commented cynically, "Only Iranians celebrate a failure as a victory." Iranian conservatives expressed outright opposition, using the hashtag "#Lausanne_chay" to compare the framework to the 1828 Treaty of Turkmenchay, in which Iran lost northern territories to Russia. Google+ user SeyedMahdi mocked the agreement, writing that centrifuges at the Fordo nuclear site would now "produce popcorn instead of enriching uranium." Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who holds final authority on state matters, has not yet commented on Twitter.

**Swindon Town Boss Tim Sherwood Charged by FA Over Half-Time Incident** Tim Sherwood faces Football Association charges following an incident during Swindon Town's 1-0 defeat at Bury on Saturday. The FA alleges the 48-year-old manager used "abusive and/or insulting and/or improper words and/or behaviour towards a match official" in the tunnel area at half-time. Sherwood, formerly of Tottenham and Aston Villa, has until 20 February to respond to the charge. Since joining Swindon on 10 November, Sherwood has overseen a difficult period, with just three wins from 18 matches across all competitions. The Robins currently sit 22nd in League One.

British Victim of Tunisia Beach Attack Named as Stuart Cullen A British man killed in the terrorist attack at a Tunisian beach resort has been identified as Stuart Cullen, 52, from the Lowestoft area in Suffolk. Mr Cullen is believed to have died instantly during Friday's attack on a beach near Sousse, carried out by a gunman with links to Islamic State extremists. He was on holiday with his wife, who sustained injuries but has since returned home to the UK, Suffolk Police confirmed. The couple have one grown-up daughter. Lowestoft mayor Stephen Ardley, who was holidaying in Sousse just over a week ago, expressed his condolences. "My heartfelt sympathy goes out to not only the Cullen family, but to all the families and friends that have been affected by this devastating act of cruelty," he said. "I was walking along that very same beach eight days earlier. The wife and I used to go for a walk on it every morning, so it really brings it home." The attack claimed 38 lives and left at least 36 people injured. Among those still hospitalised in Tunisia is Allison Heathcote from Felixstowe, who remains critically injured in an induced coma at a Sousse hospital. Her brother Simon Boon told the BBC she was shot twice and underwent six hours of surgery to rebuild her shoulder. He criticised the response, saying the family had "received very little information from the Foreign Office" and had to "source information" themselves. Mrs Heathcote's husband remains unaccounted for. Since the attack, approximately 3,500 British tourists have been repatriated from Tunisia.

Rochdale to Sign Replacements for Injured Bunney and Moore Rochdale manager Keith Hill has confirmed the club will recruit new players after key injuries on their Tenerife training camp. Joe Bunney, 23, suffered medial knee ligament damage, while Calvin Moore, 25, ruptured ankle ligaments. Hill stated he won't wait or compromise, emphasizing the need for immediate replacements in both positions due to injury severity.

"Black Widow" Serial Killer Sentenced to Death in Japan **SAITAMA, Japan** — A Japanese court has sentenced Kanae Kijima, 37, to death for the murders of three men she met through internet dating sites, in a case that has captivated the nation. The Saitama district court found Kijima guilty of killing men aged 41, 53, and 80 for financial gain. Presiding judge Kazuyuki Okuma declared there was "no room for leniency," citing the defendant's "selfish purposes" and lack of remorse. According to prosecutors, Kijima poisoned her victims with carbon monoxide by burning charcoal briquettes after administering sleeping pills. The murders were allegedly motivated by her desire to avoid repaying money the men had given her. Kijima maintains her innocence and plans to appeal the verdict. Her defense argued that the men either committed suicide after she ended their relationships or died accidentally. The case has been dubbed the "Black Widow" case in Japanese media, referencing the spider species where females sometimes consume their mates. Public interest has been intense, with more than 1,000 people queuing for fewer than 50 courtroom seats to hear the verdict. Two victims were discovered dead in their homes in Chiba prefecture, while the third was found in a rented car in Saitama prefecture. Judge Okuma criticized Kijima for reiterating "irrational excuses" during the trial and showing no remorse for her crimes. The death penalty remains legal in Japan, though executions are carried out infrequently.

Greece Bailout: Confusion Over Start of Creditor Talks Confusion has emerged over when bailout negotiations between Greece and its international creditors officially began, with European and Greek officials offering contradictory accounts. The European Commission said talks had already started, but a Greek government spokeswoman said that high-level talks would not begin until later this week. Olga Gerovasili said that senior negotiating staff would only arrive in Athens on Thursday or later. Negotiators were initially expected to arrive last week. But Ms Gerovasili said there was "no reason" for the delay, adding it was up to Greece's creditors as to when talks began. European Commission spokeswoman Mina Andreeva told a news briefing: "Teams from the institutions are already on the ground in Athens and work is starting immediately as we speak. Work has started, meaning that the institutions are talking to the Greek authorities." ## Varoufakis Reveals Contingency Plans The talks come as it emerged former finance minister Yanis Varoufakis told a group of investors in London that a five-man team under his leadership worked on a contingency plan to create euro liquidity if the European Central Bank (ECB) cut off emergency funding to the Greek financial system. Greek newspaper Kathimerini reported Mr Varoufakis as saying in a phone call that a small team in the governing Syriza party had prepared plans to secretly copy online tax codes. It said the "Plan B" was devised to allow the government to introduce a parallel payment system if the banking system was closed down, which would have seen the return of the drachma. Mr Varoufakis said passwords used by Greeks to access their online tax accounts were to have been copied secretly and used to issue new Pin numbers for every taxpayer to be used in transactions with the state. "This would have created a parallel banking system, which would have given us some breathing space, while the banks would have been shut due to the ECB's aggressive policy," Mr Varoufakis was quoted as saying. In the same phone call, Mr Varoufakis accused German Finance Minister Wolfgang Schaeuble of being "hell-bent" on ensuring Greece left the eurozone. He added that while the government had a Plan B, the difficulty was "to go from the five people who were planning it to the 1,000 people that would have to implement it". "For that I would have to receive another authorisation which never came," he said. Mr Varoufakis told the Daily Telegraph the quotes were accurate but accused the Greek press of trying to make it look as if he planned a return to the drachma from the start. "The context of all this is that they want to present me as a rogue finance minister, and have me indicted for treason. It is all part of an attempt to annul the first five months of this government and put it in the dustbin of history," he told the paper.

**Bath Hold Off Sale Fightback to Secure Home Victory** Bath secured a hard-fought victory over Sale Sharks at the Recreation Ground, withstanding a spirited second-half comeback to claim a crucial win. The hosts dominated the opening 40 minutes, racing to a commanding 17-0 lead through tries from Ollie Devoto and Charlie Ewels. Bath's forwards controlled possession while their backs exploited gaps in Sale's defensive line. However, Sale emerged from the interval with renewed determination. Quickfire tries from Johnny Leota and Andrei Ostrikov brought the visitors back into contention, narrowing the deficit to just three points and setting up a tense finale. Bath responded emphatically with tries from Semesa Rokoduguni and Will Homer, which appeared to have sealed the result. But Sale refused to surrender, with late scores from TJ Ioane and Leota's second earning them a losing bonus point. The two points keeps Sale's top-six ambitions alive, moving them above Northampton into fifth place, six points behind fourth-placed Leicester. For Bath, playing without suspended back row Alafoti Faosiliva, the victory avenged last weekend's 29-17 defeat at Sale and keeps their season alive. Bath remain ninth, three points behind eighth-placed Gloucester with two matches remaining.

Oxford United's Lundstram Relishes Second Chance at Wembley Glory Oxford United midfielder John Lundstram is determined to make amends for last season's heartbreak as the U's prepare for another Wembley appearance. The 23-year-old was forced to watch from the stands during last year's final defeat to Barnsley due to suspension. However, following Wednesday's thrilling 3-2 victory at Luton Town, Oxford have secured their place in this year's final against Coventry City on 2 April. "I am just over the moon that I can finally get the chance to go and put it right this year," Lundstram told BBC Radio Oxford. "Last year was disappointing for us, even me in the stands, so if we can go there this year and do one better than that would be perfect." Oxford have enjoyed an impressive season, also reaching the FA Cup fifth round before falling to Premier League side Middlesbrough. Head coach Michael Appleton emphasized the rarity of such opportunities: "You do not play at Wembley often, so to get the opportunity again twice in two seasons, we want to try and make sure that we do it this time around."

Former FBI Director James Comey to Publish Tell-All Book Former FBI Director James Comey is set to release a book next spring that promises to reveal "previously unheard of anecdotes" from his controversial tenure, publisher Flatiron Books announced. Mr. Comey was dramatically dismissed by President Trump in May while overseeing the FBI's investigation into alleged connections between the Trump campaign and Russia. His firing sparked widespread criticism and led to conflicting accounts between him and the president regarding their private discussions. President Trump later acknowledged that "this Russia thing" influenced his decision to terminate Comey. The former FBI chief has remained a prominent figure in recent political controversies. Hillary Clinton has publicly blamed her 2016 election loss on Comey's decision to reopen the FBI investigation into her private email server use just days before the vote. The untitled book is expected to be completed by spring 2018. On Tuesday, the Senate confirmed Christopher Wray as Comey's replacement to lead the FBI.

Liam Smith Eyes Miguel Cotto Showdown After Landing Kelly Defence Liverpool's world champion Liam Smith has set his sights on a blockbuster fight with boxing legend Miguel Cotto as he prepares to defend his WBO light-middleweight title against Jimmy Kelly. Smith became the first of Liverpool's four fighting Smith brothers to capture a world title when he stopped American John Thompson in October, claiming the WBO crown in impressive fashion. Now the 27-year-old faces a significant challenge from Kelly, who despite competing in only his 17th professional fight, will carry home advantage into their clash at the Manchester Arena. "Miguel Cotto is up there as one of the names I want to face," said Smith, looking beyond his immediate challenge. "Cotto's been a great champion and to beat him will take me to that next level. I definitely believe I have what it takes to overcome him because my style would cause him some big problems." The Puerto Rican veteran Cotto is a former four-weight world champion who most recently lost to Mexico's Saul Alvarez in November. Having campaigned as a middleweight for the past three years, Cotto remains one of boxing's biggest names. However, Smith is refusing to look past Kelly, acknowledging the threat posed by the Manchester fighter. "I know Kelly is going to go into the ring thinking this is his big chance but I'm not going to give him an inch," Smith warned. "I have big ambitions and I'm not going to be foolish and overlook the threat he will bring." The unbeaten champion, who boasts a perfect 21-0 record, is also targeting unification bouts with WBA champion Erislandy Lara and IBF titleholder Jermall Charlo. Kelly's trainer, former British champion Ensley Bingham, believes his fighter is boxing's best-kept secret. "While we've been able to study tapes of all of Liam's fights, there's very little footage available of Jimmy," Bingham explained. "That's hugely to our advantage." The 23-year-old Kelly brings a wrestling background that Bingham believes gives him exceptional core strength and durability. "A Jimmy Kelly victory would be an upset in most eyes, but not mine," Bingham insisted. "He's got the better skills."

**Patrick Vieira Appointed Head Coach of New York City FC** Former Arsenal captain Patrick Vieira has been named head coach of Major League Soccer side New York City FC, leaving his position with Manchester City's Under-21 team to embark on a new challenge in the United States. The 39-year-old French football legend has signed a three-year contract and will officially begin his role on 1 January 2016. New York City FC, part of the City Football Group owned by Manchester City's Sheik Mansour, has assembled a star-studded roster including former Chelsea midfielder Frank Lampard, World Cup-winning Italian midfielder Andrea Pirlo, and ex-Barcelona striker David Villa. "I am delighted to take up the role of head coach of New York City FC," Vieira said. "It is an exciting prospect for any coach." The club has just completed its inaugural MLS season, which ended with elimination from the play-offs despite impressive attendance figures averaging around 29,000 at Yankee Stadium, including 20,000 season ticket holders. Reports suggest the club is exploring a potential move to Columbia University's Baker Athletics Complex in northern Manhattan. Vieira enjoyed a distinguished playing career, winning seven major honours during nine years at Arsenal (1996-2005) and claiming the 1998 World Cup with France. He also won titles with Juventus and Inter Milan before joining Manchester City in 2010, where he captured the FA Cup before retiring in 2011.

Syrian Refugees Stranded at Jordan Border with Limited Aid Access, Rights Group Reports AMMAN — Hundreds of Syrian refugees remain trapped in makeshift camps just inside Jordan's border with severely restricted access to food, water, and medical assistance, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW). The international rights organization acknowledged that Jordan has made significant efforts to assist Syrians fleeing their country's brutal civil war, but emphasized that "this is no excuse to abandon newer arrivals" in remote border locations. The Jordanian government has maintained that it "continues to adopt an open-border policy," even as it hosts approximately 630,000 of the nearly four million Syrians registered as refugees with the United Nations. Jordanian officials say the actual number of Syrians in the country totals 1.4 million, including those who arrived before the 2011 uprising against President Bashar al-Assad. According to HRW, Jordanian authorities have progressively tightened entry restrictions over the past two years. Two informal desert crossings in eastern Jordan—Rukban and Hadalat—have become the primary entry points for most Syrian refugees. However, Jordan has heavily restricted access at these crossings since July 2014. Recent satellite imagery analyzed by HRW revealed approximately 175 makeshift tent shelters at Rukban and 68 at Hadalat, suggesting the presence of hundreds of refugees. Aid agencies estimated that roughly 2,500 people were stranded at these locations in mid-April, though an international aid worker reported this number had decreased to about 1,000 by late May after Jordanian border guards permitted some to leave the border zone. "Jordan has gone to great lengths to meet the needs of Syrian refugees," said Nadim Houry, HRW's deputy Middle East and North Africa director. "But that is no excuse to abandon newer arrivals in remote border areas for weeks without effective protection and regular aid access." The report also documented at least one case of immediate deportation, with a Syrian taken to the Raba Sarhan registration center and returned to Syria without being registered. HRW warned that such summary returns could constitute refoulement, violating international law prohibiting the return of individuals to areas where they face persecution risks. A Jordanian government spokesman responded by reaffirming the country's commitment to maintaining open-border procedures coordinated with international organizations.

**Aston Villa Sign Reading Midfielder Dominic Tshibola** Aston Villa have completed the signing of 21-year-old midfielder Dominic Tshibola from Reading. The youth product made 17 appearances for the Royals since making his Football League debut in a 4-0 defeat at Nottingham Forest in August 2014. Tshibola gained valuable experience during a loan spell with Hartlepool United in 2014-15, making 23 league appearances for the League Two side. He will now link up with former Reading manager Steve Clarke, who serves as Villa's assistant manager. Villa boss Roberto di Matteo expressed his enthusiasm about the acquisition, telling the club website: "He's a highly-rated and well respected young player who will provide us with plenty of energy, courage and determination in the middle of the park. I am confident he will be a tremendous addition to our squad for the very important new season - and beyond."

Newtonmore's Remarkable Winning Streak Ends in Shock Defeat to Oban Camanachd **Shinty's dominant force suffers first league loss in nearly three years as championship race opens up** Newtonmore's extraordinary 56-game unbeaten run in the Marine Harvest Premiership came to a stunning end on Saturday as they fell 2-1 to Oban Camanachd at Mossfield Park. The seven-time reigning champions had not tasted defeat since the third week of the 2015 season, when Inveraray—who would eventually be relegated that year—last managed to beat them. The loss marks a significant shift in the shinty landscape, with Newtonmore's aura of invincibility finally broken. Andrew McCuish opened the scoring for Oban Camanachd after just 18 minutes, before Lorn Dickie doubled their advantage before the half-hour mark. The hosts maintained their 2-0 cushion until midway through the second half when Newtonmore talisman Glen MacKintosh pulled one back, giving the champions hope of salvaging at least a point. However, More's comeback hopes were dealt a severe blow when Andy MacKintosh received a red card, reducing them to ten men. Despite their numerical disadvantage, the champions pressed for an equalizer but could not find a way through Oban's resolute defence. The defeat leaves Newtonmore with only a 50% record after three games, sitting in fourth place—a position virtually unthinkable given their dominance in recent years. During the previous two complete seasons, they dropped just four points in total; they have now lost three points in their opening three fixtures alone. Meanwhile, local rivals Kingussie capitalized on Newtonmore's slip-up, moving to the top of the table with a 2-0 home victory over Glenurquhart. The match remained goalless until its final quarter before Ryan Borthwick and Roddy Young struck to secure all three points. Remarkably, Kingussie were involved in a relegation play-off just two seasons ago and now sit two points ahead of the dethroned champions. In the day's other Premiership action, Lovat recorded their first points of the season with an impressive 4-2 comeback victory over newly-promoted Kilmallie at Balgate. In the National Division, Skye ascended to the top of the table thanks to Iain MacLellan's hat-trick in their 3-1 away win over Oban Celtic.

**Northern Ireland Call Up Uncapped Duo Smith and Washington for Wales and Slovenia Clashes** Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill has named his 24-man squad for upcoming friendlies against Wales and Slovenia, with uncapped pair Michael Smith and Conor Washington earning their first international call-ups. Peterborough United defender Smith, 27, and 23-year-old Queen's Park Rangers striker Washington will be hoping to make their debuts as Northern Ireland continue preparations for this summer's European Championship finals in France. However, Derby County defender Chris Baird, currently on loan at Fulham, has been ruled out through injury and will miss both matches. Northern Ireland face Wales at Cardiff City Stadium on Thursday, 24 March, before hosting Slovenia in Belfast on Monday, 28 March. The fixtures form part of the nation's build-up to Euro 2016, with further matches against Belarus and Slovakia scheduled for late May and early June. Smith, who previously played for Ballyclare Comrades and Ballymena United, spent three years at Bristol Rovers before joining Peterborough in 2014. Washington, qualifying through the grandparent rule, recently signed for QPR in January after an impressive spell at Peterborough, where he scored 27 goals in 82 appearances. Particular attention will focus on the left-back position following West Bromwich Albion's Chris Brunt's devastating anterior cruciate ligament injury, which has ruled him out of Euro 2016. O'Neill will use these matches to assess potential replacements ahead of the tournament. Northern Ireland will make their first appearance at a major finals in 30 years this summer, having been drawn in Group C alongside Poland, Ukraine, and Germany. They face Poland on 12 June in their opening match, followed by Ukraine on 16 June and Germany on 21 June. The squad announcement follows confirmation that O'Neill has signed a new four-year contract to remain as national team manager.

Ding Junhui Makes 147 Break Despite Loss to Neil Robertson Chinese snooker star Ding Junhui produced a magnificent maximum 147 break during his quarter-final defeat to Neil Robertson at a ranking event, setting a new personal milestone despite ultimately losing the match 5-2. The world-class clearance came at a crucial moment when Ding was trailing 4-1 in the best-of-nine-frames contest against the world number three Australian. However, the perfect break wasn't enough to turn the tide, as Robertson recovered to close out the victory. "The reds were looking good so I went for it," Ding told BBC Radio 5 live after the match. "It's just a 147, a new record for me. I like to beat the records every time I play in the tournaments." Robertson, who himself compiled an impressive 140 break in the third frame, was full of praise for his opponent's achievement. "What a wonderful break," he said. "He was clearly determined because he went for a risky shot in the forties." The maximum break comes just days after Ronnie O'Sullivan made headlines by deliberately avoiding a 147 in the first round, citing the £10,000 prize money as "too cheap." Instead, O'Sullivan opted for the pink ball over the black, finishing with a 146 break. The prize fund, which includes an additional £2,000 for the tournament's highest break, is a rolling amount at ranking events. O'Sullivan, who demolished world number one Mark Selby 5-1 in his own quarter-final on Friday, responded to Ding's achievement with characteristic humour. "I thought'he's let the lads down, hasn't he?'" O'Sullivan joked. "Ding got it. Fantastic, at least they've had a 147 this week - and a 146. But I was going for it, 100%. There's obviously pressure and I twitched on the black." The four-time world champion was unrepentant about the publicity his earlier decision generated. "I think I've done brilliant for this tournament," O'Sullivan said. "Most people are saying they didn't actually know this event was on. I've created such good headlines - if you had to go and buy them headlines, it would probably cost you a few quid." Looking ahead to his semi-final against compatriot Joe Perry, who beat Ben Woollaston 5-1, O'Sullivan said he was in the mood to entertain. "If you start to think of it like a match you can start to not enjoy it," he explained. Robertson will face Northern Ireland's Mark Allen, who defeated Michael White 5-0, in the other semi-final.

Cavendish Balances Tour de France Glory with Olympic Dream Mark Cavendish admits he faces an unprecedented challenge as he attempts to juggle Tour de France ambitions with Olympic glory in Rio this summer, describing the ambitious double as something that "could be the best thing I've done, it could be the worst thing I've done." The 31-year-old sprint specialist will compete for Team Dimension Data at cycling's most prestigious race before switching to track cycling for Team GB at the Rio Olympics, where he hopes to finally claim an Olympic medal to add to his impressive palmares. With 26 Tour de France stage victories to his name, Cavendish sits third on the all-time list, just two wins behind legends Bernard Hinault and Eddy Merckx, who leads with 34 stage victories. The Isle of Man rider could make history at Saturday's opening stage from Mont Saint-Michel to Utah Beach in Normandy, where victory would also see him don the race leader's yellow jersey for the first time in his career. However, Cavendish downplayed the significance of wearing yellow, insisting it has never been "a career target, it is just something I haven't done." The sprinter has spent much of the year training on the track in preparation for Rio, raising questions about whether he might leave the Tour early to focus on his Olympic preparations. But Cavendish firmly dismissed such speculation. "I'm not coming to the Tour de France planning to stop," he said. "This is my 10th Tour de France. Every time I stopped, it's been for different circumstances." Cavendish referenced his illness after last year's race, which left him bedridden for a week, acknowledging he cannot afford a similar situation this year. "The biggest stage in the world is the Champs-Elysees for a sprinter," he added. "I know that my eight team-mates are going to do their best to get to Paris and I'm going to try to do my best to get to Paris." Meanwhile, defending champion Chris Froome will also compete at both the Tour and Rio Olympics, though his Olympic focus will be the road and time trial events. The Team Sky rider is targeting his third Tour de France victory in four years and has adjusted his season schedule to maintain peak form through to Rio. "In previous seasons I'd been in that shape and then basically tried to hang on to it whereas now I feel as if I've only just got there," Froome explained. The three-week, 21-stage race concludes in Paris on July 24.

Barnsley FC Celebrate Promotion with Victory Parade Barnsley FC fans turned out in force on Monday to celebrate their team's promotion to the Championship following a triumphant weekend at Wembley. The Tykes secured a 3-1 victory over Millwall in the League One play-off final on Sunday, sparking celebrations across the South Yorkshire town. An open-top bus parade commenced from Oakwell Stadium at 16:15 BST, winding through the town centre before culminating in a celebration at Barnsley Town Hall. Up to 6,000 supporters lined the streets wearing team colours and waving flags. Mayor Linda Burgess said: "We're really proud to be able to welcome our home team on to the town hall balcony for the second time this season." This marks Barnsley's second Wembley triumph in 2016, having previously defeated Oxford United 3-2 in the Johnstone's Paint Trophy final.

Mother with Terminal Cancer Raises £50,000 for Children's Future Care A Derbyshire mother diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer has been overwhelmed by public generosity after raising more than £50,000 to secure care for her three young children. Lisa Foster, 36, received the devastating diagnosis just three weeks ago and immediately launched an online fundraising campaign to hire a nanny who could support her family during her treatment and potentially care for her children if she doesn't survive. The funds will provide care for seven-year-old Ruby, four-year-old Zach, and seven-and-a-half-month-old baby Scarlett, whilst also offering additional support to Mrs Foster's husband. "I just can't believe the generosity of this world and I will be forever grateful to all of those hundreds who have donated," Mrs Foster said. "They really have helped me. I want to enjoy every single minute, of every single day, of every single month now of what I've got left." More than a thousand donors contributed through her online fundraising page, exceeding her original £50,000 target. Many supporters cited their own similar circumstances—being of comparable age with three children—as motivation for donating. Mrs Foster's primary goal is to create lasting memories with her youngest daughter. "My biggest motivation for fighting cancer is to live long enough so that Scarlett might remember me," she explained. She hopes to witness significant milestones: Scarlett's first steps and words, Zach's first day at school, and Ruby beginning secondary school. To ensure her presence during future celebrations, Mrs Foster is recording videos for each child to watch at key moments, including their 18th birthdays. "If I can get a year, that means I can see Zack's first day at school, I can see Scarlett maybe start walking or saying her first word, and that's what's going to keep me going," she said.

Everton Boss Roberto Martinez Stands Firm on John Stones Amid Chelsea Interest Everton manager Roberto Martinez has declared that the club will not be swayed by money as Chelsea continue their pursuit of defender John Stones, with reports suggesting a £40m bid is imminent. The 21-year-old England international submitted a transfer request on Tuesday following Everton's rejection of three previous Chelsea offers: £20m, £26m, and £30m.
