Security camera footage from Hanover station captured the moment she approached two police officers. When they asked to see her identification, she lunged at the 34-year-old policeman with a knife. In a related case, 20-year-old Mohamad Hasan K was sentenced to two and a half years in prison on Thursday for failing to alert authorities about the planned attack despite having knowledge of it. The teenager later apologised to the wounded officer both in writing and during the trial. Her defence team had called for acquittal on some charges and a reduced sentence. They have announced plans to appeal the verdict. Her lawyer, Mutlu Guenal, argued that authorities bore responsibility, noting that Safia S's family had warned police about her radicalisation. "The real failure lay with police," he stated. The trial was held behind closed doors due to the defendant's age. Under German privacy laws, only surnames' initials are released publicly. This case comes amid heightened security concerns in Germany, with Hanover police also investigating a suspected jihadist plot targeting an international football friendly match.

Birmingham City's Gianfranco Zola Under Pressure After Heavy Home Defeat Birmingham City manager Gianfranco Zola admits he needs to discuss his future with the club's owners following a humiliating 4-1 home defeat to Queens Park Rangers on Saturday. The loss at St Andrew's was the heaviest of nine defeats Blues have suffered in 14 games since Zola replaced Gary Rowett as manager in December. It also represented their worst home performance since an 8-0 thrashing by Bournemouth in October 2014. "Obviously I need to have a chat with the owners," said Zola. "As long as they trust me I am willing to try and do my best at St Andrew's." Since the Italian's appointment, Birmingham have collected just six points from a possible 36 in the Championship, plummeting to 14th in the table and now sitting 18 points adrift of the play-off places. The decline has been stark. When Rowett's side won their final match under his stewardship - a 2-1 victory over Ipswich Town on 13 December - Blues were seventh and level on points with sixth-placed Sheffield Wednesday. Rowett was controversially dismissed the following day by Trillion Trophy Asia Ltd, owned by Hong Kong businessman Paul Suen Cho Hung, who had already secured Zola as his replacement. "At the moment, I am feeling very low," admitted Zola. "But I take full responsibility. I am probably not giving enough and it is making me upset. I have committed myself to the club and I am doing it with a lot of passion. We do not like where we are at the present time, but I really care about this club and I want to help them." QPR manager Ian Holloway was sympathetic but direct about his counterpart's predicament: "Birmingham have got to get on with it. The fans do not know what to think. I do not know where Zola will go after this game. It is up to him to work out."

GAA Unveils Scaled-Back Plans for Casement Park Stadium in Belfast The GAA has announced revised plans for Casement Park stadium in west Belfast, reducing its proposed capacity to 34,500 - a decrease of 3,500 seats from the original design. The organization stated it aims to complete the project within the initial £76 million budget, with the stadium expected to open by 2019 ahead of the 2020 Ulster finals. The GAA emphasized the revised plan demonstrates its willingness to "engage and listen" to community concerns. The new design features reduced height, scale, and capacity compared to the previous proposal, addressing issues raised by local residents and safety experts. Tom Daly, chairman of the Casement Park Project Board, highlighted the GAA's commitment to delivering a "travel culture change." The updated plans incorporate coach travel options, park and ride facilities, and integrated travel arrangements linked to ticket sales. "This strategy is good for ease of access to and from the stadium, is cognisant of the needs and views of the local community and is good for the wider environment," Daly said. Ulster GAA president Michael Hasson expressed optimism about the project's future: "GAA members and supporters, as well as people across the local community, are looking forward to an exciting new beginning for Antrim and a provincial stadium for Ulster." He added: "We want to create a positive sporting legacy and iconic stadium that will be a beacon to inspire young GAA players throughout west Belfast, Antrim and across Ulster." The multi-million pound project has faced significant challenges since its inception. Planning permission was overturned in 2014 following objections from local residents. Additionally, safety expert Paul Scott claimed he experienced bullying after raising concerns about emergency evacuation procedures under the initial stadium plans.

Italy Edge Zambia in Dramatic Extra-Time Thriller to Reach U-20 World Cup Semi-Finals **Suwon, South Korea** - Italy survived a dramatic quarter-final encounter against Zambia at the U-20 World Cup, prevailing 3-2 in extra-time after a pulsating match at the Suwon World Cup Stadium. Luca Vido emerged as Italy's hero, scoring the decisive goal in the second period of extra-time after being afforded far too much space in the Zambian penalty area. The strike completed a remarkable comeback for the Italians, who spent more than half the match playing with ten men. Zambia will rue their missed opportunity after Giuseppe Pezzella received a straight red card for a professional foul on Edward Chilufya just before half-time. In a dramatic twist, the referee initially awarded a penalty before reversing the decision following a video assistant referee consultation, though the dismissal stood. The African champions had started perfectly when Patson Daka fired them ahead after just three minutes, converting Emmanuel Banda's exquisite pass from close range. Zambia should have extended their lead when Banda's 14th-minute free-kick was saved, but both Chilufya and Fashion Sakala failed to capitalize on the rebound. Italy equalized early in the second half through Riccardo Orsolini's header - his fourth tournament goal. Fashion Sakala appeared to have sealed victory for Zambia with his fourth goal of the campaign six minutes from time, but Federico Dimarco's brilliant free-kick four minutes later forced extra-time. With penalties seemingly inevitable, Vido's late intervention broke Zambian hearts and secured Italy's place in the semi-finals, where they will face England, who defeated Mexico 1-0 in their quarter-final clash. The defeat ends Zambia's hopes of adding the world title to their African crown in what was an unforgettable encounter.

Suge Knight Sues Kanye West Over 2005 Nightclub Shooting Hip hop mogul Marion "Suge" Knight is taking legal action against rapper Kanye West following a shooting incident that left him seriously injured at a Miami nightclub in 2005. Knight was shot in the leg by an unknown gunman at Miami's Shore Club where West was holding a pre-MTV Awards celebration. At least six shots were fired, but few witnesses came forward and no-one has been ever arrested over what happened. Celebrities like Jessica Alba and the Black Eyed Peas were all at the event. Marion "Suge" Knight, a controversial figure in the hip hop community, helped launch the careers of rappers like Tupac Shakur and Snoop Dogg. The 44-year-old is claiming that Kanye West and the club's owners didn't provide enough security to keep people with weapons out of the venue. Knight's lawyer, Marc Brumer, said: "He had an expectation of security there. How someone came with a gun into a very VIP party, that just doesn't meet the smell test in life." Knight is also seeking more than £650,000 in damages, which includes compensation for a 15-carat diamond earring he says was lost in the chaos. He also claims that he had to pay £130,000 in medical bills due to a shot that shattered his femur. Kanye West and the Shore Club's owners have denied the claims and a trial has been scheduled for 6 December in Miami. The former Death Row boss went bankrupt in 2006, so if he wins the case he'll have to share the payout with the tax man and his bankruptcy trustee.

Nicklas Bendtner: Nottingham Forest sign former Arsenal striker Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of former Arsenal striker Nicklas Bendtner on a two-year deal, BBC Radio Nottingham has confirmed. BBC Radio Nottingham reported on Tuesday that the 28-year-old, who was a free agent after leaving German club Wolfsburg, was discussing terms and he has now agreed a two-year contract. The Denmark international told BBC Nottingham Sport: "My main goal was to come back to England. "What happened in Wolfsburg was a sad situation. I have made mistakes in the past, but I am looking to the future." Bendtner had an unhappy spell in Germany and left the club after several disciplinary issues. He said the move to a club with a "big history", and the chance to work with Forest manager Philippe Montanier, was the ideal way to make a "new start". "It is important to prove myself and get back to scoring goals," said Bendtner. "The coach has given me a great impression of the club and how he wants to do things. "He cares a lot about football. He wants to play football, he is a nice man and I look forward to working with him." Forest face Aston Villa on Sunday and Bendtner, who has scored 29 goals in 72 appearances for his country, said he was not quite ready to play. "I need a little bit of time to settle and adjust but it won't be long," he added. Bendtner scored 45 goals for Arsenal in 171 games between 2005 and 2014 and also had loan spells at Sunderland, Birmingham and Juventus during that period. ## BBC Radio Nottingham's Nottingham Forest correspondent Colin Fray "Nicklas Bendtner is certainly a controversial figure and has his detractors, but Forest will be hoping that their marquee signing can combine with Britt Assombalonga up front and fire the club into top-six contention. "He's a player who's proved he's capable of scoring goals in his career - including in the Championship during his loan spell with Birmingham, when he was only 18 and was sent out by Arsenal to gain first-team experience. That spell apart, his entire career has been spent in the top flights in England, Italy and Germany, and he has a wealth of international experience with Denmark, too. "So, as a free agent, you can see why Forest would be prepared to offer him a deal. At 6ft 4ins tall, he's likely to be handful for Championship defenders, and is the highest-profile signing of 12 this summer." Find all the latest football transfers on our dedicated page.

Cardiff City Face Must-Win Battle at Hillsborough to Keep Play-Off Dreams Alive Cardiff City manager Russell Slade has described Saturday's Championship clash against Sheffield Wednesday as "huge" as the Bluebirds fight to keep their play-off hopes alive. The Welsh side travel to Hillsborough knowing only a victory will realistically maintain their pursuit of a top-six finish, sitting one place and four points behind their opponents with just two games remaining. "It's a huge game isn't it," said Slade. "We still have a wonderful opportunity to deliver something special so it's a huge game for both football clubs." Cardiff's inferior goal difference means they must win both remaining fixtures to have any chance of claiming sixth place. Despite the challenging situation, Slade remains optimistic about his team's prospects. "We're almost at the finishing line and we've got ourselves in a position still where we can put ourselves in a realistic situation of getting to a play-off final and ultimately to the Premier League," the manager added. "That's what we all chase in this division isn't it? Lots of teams below us would swap." The Bluebirds kept their hopes alive with a dramatic 2-1 victory over Bolton, secured by Peter Whittingham's last-minute penalty. Slade has cautioned his players may need similar patience against Wednesday. Despite Wednesday only requiring a point to secure their play-off place, Slade expects an attacking approach from the hosts. "They won't play for a draw," he said. "I think they'll play to their normal strengths and strategy that they have had over recent months." The Cardiff boss emphasised the importance of staying competitive throughout the match. "The game is not going to be won and lost in the first 20 minutes. It's important you stay in the game - that's massive." Wednesday manager Carlos Carvalhal insists his team feels no pressure, already guaranteed sixth position regardless of the result. "Whatever happens we'll be in sixth position. That's a fact and it's a good fact," he said. "We don't feel any pressure and we are not under pressure. "We will fight a lot, run a lot and battle for the three points."

Aberdeen have secured Celtic midfielder Ryan Christie on loan for the entire 2017-18 season, offering a bright spot amid a turbulent summer of departures at Pittodrie. The 22-year-old attacking midfielder made an immediate impact after joining the Dons on loan in January, netting seven goals in just 15 appearances. His impressive form culminated in five goals across his final five matches of the campaign. Christie's return comes as Aberdeen lose winger Jonny Hayes to Celtic for a reported £1.3 million. The retention of Christie, alongside manager Derek McInnes, provides some consolation for supporters facing a significant summer exodus. The Dons have already bid farewell to Niall McGinn, Ryan Jack, Peter Pawlett, and Ash Taylor. However, they've begun rebuilding by signing midfielder Greg Tansey from Inverness, with additional reinforcements expected. Christie originally joined Celtic from Inverness for approximately £500,000 in September 2015 but managed only seven appearances for the champions last season before his successful Aberdeen stint.

Ukraine Removes Journalists from Security Threat List After International Pressure Ukraine's President Petro Poroshenko has removed several international journalists, including BBC staff, from a controversial security threat list following diplomatic intervention. On Wednesday, Mr Poroshenko signed a decree designating nearly 400 individuals and 90 legal entities as security threats. Among those listed were three Moscow-based BBC journalists, whose names were removed after British Ambassador Judith Gough visited the Ukrainian president. The ambassador described the reversal as a "welcome move." Mr Poroshenko's press secretary confirmed that journalists from Spain and Germany were also struck from the list. According to the AP news agency, two Spanish journalists had vanished in Syria in July and were suspected to have been abducted by Islamic State militants. The sanctions were connected to the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine, which began last year. The decision drew immediate criticism from press freedom organizations. Reporters Without Borders condemned the move as "an absurd, counter-productive breach of freedom of information." The Committee to Protect Journalists, noting that 41 journalists and bloggers appeared on the list, stated: "While the government may not like or agree with the coverage, labelling journalists a potential threat to national security is not an appropriate response." President Poroshenko emphasized that the sanctions were implemented "in co-ordination with our partners from the European Union, the United States of America and other countries." The conflict in eastern Ukraine has claimed nearly 8,000 lives since fighting began in April 2014, one month after Russia's annexation of Crimea. Ukraine and Western nations accuse Russia of providing arms to separatists and deploying regular troops, allegations Moscow denies while acknowledging Russian "volunteers" fight alongside rebels. A recent ceasefire has largely held for two weeks, though sporadic shelling continues.

A 27-year-old woman has died following a motorbike crash on a major Welsh road. Sarah Jayne Jones, from the Tredegar area of Blaenau Gwent, was a pillion passenger on the bike involved in Thursday evening's collision on the A465 Heads of the Valleys road between Brynmawr and Ebbw Vale. The 56-year-old male rider sustained serious injuries in the incident. The road remained closed on Friday morning as police continued their investigation work at the scene.

Rangers Boss Warburton Warns Against Complacency Despite Old Firm Victory Mark Warburton savoured his first taste of Old Firm glory but issued a cautionary note to Rangers supporters, insisting Sunday's penalty shootout victory over Celtic cannot be viewed as a true measure of where his side stands ahead of their return to the Scottish Premiership. The Rangers manager watched his team emerge victorious in a thrilling Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden Park, which finished 2-2 after extra time before the Ibrox side prevailed on penalties. However, Warburton was quick to temper expectations for next season's championship challenge, acknowledging the gulf in quality that still exists between the newly-crowned Championship winners and their Glasgow rivals. "Again, there's a gap, don't be fooled, but the better team won on the day," said Warburton. "Celtic are a team packed with international players and we've got to work hard to close the gap. What today showed is that the gap is nowhere near as big as certain people have made out." The match itself provided plenty of drama. Kenny Miller opened the scoring for Rangers in the first half before Erik Sviatchenko equalised five minutes into the second period. Barrie McKay's unstoppable strike early in extra time looked to have settled matters, but Celtic substitute Tom Rogic levelled in the dying moments. Cruelly for the Australian midfielder, he then missed the decisive penalty in the shootout. Warburton stressed that maintaining Rangers' momentum is paramount. "We've made dramatic strides but we've got to keep moving forward. Rangers can't afford to stand still," he said. "We can't be satisfied going into next season being second, third or fourth. We've got to be highly competitive." Rangers' attention now turns to the Scottish Cup final against Hibernian on 21 May. The Easter Road outfit also progressed via penalties after a goalless draw with Dundee United. "That will be a tough test," acknowledged the former Brentford boss. "Hibs have got a strong squad and they'll be keen to end the season on a high." Victory would secure European football at Ibrox, which Warburton admitted "would impact our recruitment" and necessitate additional squad depth. Operating with just five substitutes due to injuries to Martyn Waghorn and Harry Forrester, plus Michael O'Halloran's cup-tied status, Warburton praised his squad's resilience. "You saw we were down to the bare numbers today so all credit to them," he said. "No one hid from the occasion."

Dundee United Apologise to Ross County After Fan Misconduct Mars Cup Victory Dundee United have issued a formal apology to Ross County following incidents of vandalism and antisocial behaviour during Saturday's Scottish Cup quarter-final at Dingwall. Despite a successful result on the pitch, the club was forced to address reports of damaged seating, graffiti, and stickers splashed across the County stand. Seven fans were arrested during the match. In a strongly-worded statement, United expressed disappointment that such an apology was necessary: "After an excellent Scottish Cup quarter-final victory and tremendous backing from the vast majority of the 1,413 Dundee United fans who made the trip to Dingwall, it is extremely disappointing that such an apology has had to be made." The club confirmed it had received "clear evidence of damage to seats in the North Stand" and pledged to take action against those responsible. However, United were keen to praise the majority of their support: "Most of our fans on Saturday behaved in entirely the proper manner, showed superb support and played a large part in helping secure victory." The club vowed to continue efforts to prevent such behaviour, stating: "We simply cannot allow the inappropriate behaviour of a few individuals to stain that reputation."

Carl Frampton Parts Ways with Manager Barry McGuigan After Eight-Year Partnership Belfast boxer Carl Frampton has split from his long-time manager Barry McGuigan, bringing an end to a highly successful eight-year partnership that saw the fighter become a two-weight world champion. Frampton, who has been managed by McGuigan since turning professional in 2009, announced the separation on Monday, stating he was "confident now is the right time to move forward and take my career into my own hands." The 30-year-old's departure from Cyclone Promotions comes amid mounting tension following the controversial cancellation of his scheduled fight against Mexican Andres Gutierrez on 29 July. The bout was postponed at the 11th hour in bizarre circumstances that saw Frampton come in one pound overweight, before Gutierrez ultimately withdrew after injuring himself by slipping in the shower. Although both Frampton and McGuigan apologised to the public following the fiasco, BBC Sport NI understands their relationship was already beginning to unravel behind the scenes. Less than 10 days before the scheduled contest, Frampton had resigned as a director of Cyclone Promotions, a significant indication of the growing rift. "I would like to thank Barry, the McGuigan family and Cyclone Promotions for our time together," read Frampton's statement. "I still believe that I'm the best featherweight in the world and I promise my fans that I am continuing with my efforts to get my homecoming fight rescheduled in the very near future." Cyclone Promotions confirmed they would not be making any immediate statement regarding Frampton's departure. The split marks a dramatic turn in what had appeared to be an exceptionally close relationship. Frampton was trained by McGuigan's son Shane, while McGuigan's wife Sandra and their other sons, Blain and Jake, are also heavily involved in the promotional company. The tight-knit nature of their partnership was showcased earlier this year in a three-part BBC documentary series, Fight Game: The McGuigans, which followed Frampton's preparations for his world title bouts with Leo Santa Cruz. The Frampton-McGuigan partnership had produced remarkable success. After claiming the European belt by defeating Kiko Martinez in February 2013, Frampton won his first world title by beating the same opponent in September 2014 to claim the IBF super-bantamweight crown. He added the WBA belt with a points victory over Scott Quigg in February 2016, before making history by defeating Santa Cruz in New York to win the WBA featherweight title in July of that year. The victory made Frampton Northern Ireland's first two-weight world champion and earned him boxer of the year honours from both Ring Magazine and ESPN. However, Santa Cruz gained revenge in Las Vegas last January, regaining the WBA featherweight title and handing Frampton his first professional defeat. The planned homecoming fight against Gutierrez was meant to mark Frampton's return to action after six months out of the ring, but its cancellation has proved to be the final straw in an increasingly strained relationship. Frampton looked visibly uncomfortable during a joint interview with McGuigan following the Gutierrez fight cancellation, with sources indicating the postponement added significant pressure to an already fragile partnership.

Syrian Army Announces Major Offensive on Rebel-Held Eastern Aleppo The Syrian army has announced the start of a new offensive to retake rebel-held areas of the divided city of Aleppo, escalating a devastating conflict that has already claimed thousands of lives. Army officials said civilians there should avoid areas where "terrorists" were operating, state media reported. It comes after jets pounded rebel positions in the city on Wednesday night as a week-old truce collapsed, reportedly killing at least 13 people. It is unclear whether the new offensive will involve ground troops. Meanwhile, talks between the US and Russia on reviving the collapsed ceasefire have broken up without progress in New York. Russia supports the Syrian government, while the US backs the opposition. ## Diplomatic Efforts Falter US Secretary of State John Kerry said Washington could not be the only one trying to hold open the door to peace. The US wants Russia to press the Syrian government to ground its warplanes. Mr Kerry added that he would hold further consultations with the Russian team on Friday. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said that would amount to a "unilateral pause". Some had attempted to present the ceasefire as if only the Syrian government should be taking steps, he said, but the opposition also needed to stop fighting. The UN envoy for Syria, Staffan de Mistura, described the meeting as "long, painful and disappointing". This feels like a very serious breakdown, with little obvious room left for dialogue until the major powers find new space for compromise, the BBC's diplomatic correspondent, James Robbins, reports from New York. The week in New York is heading towards disastrous diplomatic failure, he adds. ## Devastating Air Strikes Continue Announcing the new offensive, Syrian state media quoted army officials as saying there were exit points for anyone, including rebels, who wanted to flee eastern Aleppo. Women and children are believed to be among those killed in the latest bombing. Some reports put the death toll as high as 45. An AFP news agency journalist reports that his entire street in the southern Bustan al-Qasr district was left burning after warplanes dropped incendiary bombs. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR), a UK-based group which documents casualties in the conflict, said 14 air strikes had hit Bustan al-Qasr and the neighbouring Kallasa district, starting "massive fires", as rebels and troops clashed. SOHR director Rami Abdul Rahman described them as "the most intense strikes in months" on the two areas, with three women and three children among the dead. The pro-rebel Aleppo Media Centre said the fires had been caused by "incendiary phosphorus bombs". Video footage posted by it and another pro-opposition activist group, Thiqa, showed intense blazes lighting up the night sky. Aleppo, once Syria's commercial and industrial hub, has been divided roughly in two since 2012, with the government controlling the west and rebels the east.

Tom Smith Named Lancashire Cricket Captain After Successful 2014 Season Lancashire Cricket Club has appointed 29-year-old Tom Smith as their new captain, replacing Glen Chapple, who transitions to a player-coach role under cricket director Ashley Giles' backroom staff. The Liverpool-born all-rounder, who earned the club's player of the year award in 2014, expressed his excitement about leading his boyhood team. "I was lucky enough to have a meeting with Ashley and he offered the job," Smith told BBC Radio Lancashire. "I was over the moon. It's not every day you get to captain your boyhood club that you've grown up with and it's a truly great honour." Despite Lancashire's relegation to Division Two last summer, Smith delivered impressive personal performances, taking over 50 wickets in the County Championship for the first time whilst scoring 773 runs, including seven half-centuries. Lancashire also confirmed that all-rounder Steven Croft will serve as vice-captain for the upcoming season.

Robot Wars: Team Cherub Beats Experienced Behemoth in Controversial Battle In a dramatic Robot Wars showdown on 13 March 2017, young Team Cherub triumphed over veteran competitors Team Behemoth in a closely-fought battle that required a judges' decision to determine the winner. Team Cherub, a family outfit led by 12-year-old captain Sarah and 13-year-old driver Toby, along with teammates Rosie, 12, and Mark, 26, secured their place in the final after the tense encounter. The match sparked controversy when Team Behemoth captain Ant appeared visibly upset following the defeat, with video footage of his reaction being widely shared on social media. Many viewers initially speculated he was frustrated at losing to children. However, Ant later clarified that his emotional response stemmed from disagreements within his own team about design changes made to their robot, which he believed contributed to their loss. Team Behemoth, despite being one of the most experienced teams in the competition, has developed a reputation for unfortunate luck on the show. Robot Wars' official Twitter account defended Ant's reaction, describing it as demonstrating his "passion and care" for the competition.

Royal London Group to Close Liverpool Office, 220 Jobs Lost The Royal London Group has announced plans to close its Liverpool office, resulting in the loss of 220 jobs in the city. Approximately half of the affected staff members are expected to be transferred to the company's base in Wilmslow, Cheshire, following the closure. The decision comes after the Royal London Group's takeover of the organization in June. The iconic Royal Liver building, which recently celebrated its centenary on July 19th, will remain under Royal London Group ownership. The historic structure, adorned with Liverpool's famous Liver Birds emblem, is expected to be rented out to other companies for office space.

Three Arrested Following Serious Assault on Father and Son in Harlow Essex police have arrested three people in connection with a violent attack in Tunnmeade, Harlow, this March that left a father and son seriously injured. Officers executed search warrants at four properties across Harlow before detaining two men, aged 31 and 28, and a 31-year-old woman, all local residents. The trio face suspicion of attempted murder and aggravated burglary. The investigation is being treated as attempted murder by Essex police. All three suspects are currently being questioned at Harlow police station as the investigation continues.

Bradford boy charged over Drake Street incident A boy has been arrested and charged following an incident that took place on Drake Street in Bradford on 3 May. West Yorkshire Police confirmed the youth faces two charges: a racially-aggravated public order offence and assault of a police officer. He is scheduled to appear before a youth court on 12 June to answer the charges. The force has not released further details about the incident or the boy's age.

Powys Councillors Suspended Following Farming Prosecutions Two senior Powys councillors have begun suspensions for breaching the council's code of conduct following criminal convictions related to cattle regulations. Gwynfor Thomas, former chairman of the council's scrutiny committee who later resigned from that position, started a four-week suspension on Wednesday. He represents the Llansanffraid ward. Conservative group leader Aled Davies, representing Llanrhaeadr-ym-Mochnant and Llansilin, began a two-week suspension on 11 April. A third councillor, Gary Price, has appealed against his five-month suspension, with recommendations it be reduced to three months. This amendment requires approval from the council's standards committee after May's local elections. The suspensions follow prosecutions by Powys trading standards under the Cattle Identification (Wales) Regulations 2007 and Animal By-Products (Enforcement) (Wales) Regulations. The charges related to cattle tagging on farms, and all councillors were found guilty. The suspensions were imposed for bringing the council into disrepute. Powys council has arranged for neighbouring councillors to provide coverage during the suspension period.

Hereford FC Clinch Promotion with Emphatic Victory at Salisbury Hereford FC have secured promotion to the Southern League Premier Division in spectacular fashion, winning the Southern League Division One South & West title with six games remaining after a commanding 4-0 victory at Salisbury on Saturday. The phoenix club, which rose from the ashes of Hereford United following its demise in December 2014, will compete in English football's seventh tier next season, marking another significant milestone in their remarkable resurrection. Manager Peter Beadle was effusive in his praise for his players after the title-clinching performance. "To win 4-0 away is a great way to do it," he said. "And to do it against a decent side and to win the title with six games to go is a huge, spectacular effort by the players." The Bulls faced a stern examination at Steve Claridge's Salisbury, the same side they defeated in the FA Vase semi-finals before reaching Wembley in March 2016. The victory was made even sweeter as results elsewhere fell perfectly into place for Hereford's title aspirations. Second-placed Taunton Town suffered a 2-0 defeat at Evesham, while third-placed Tiverton Town lost 1-0 at Wimborne, meaning Hereford's goals from Mike Symons (2), Jamie Molyneux, and a stunning strike from Pablo Haysham sealed the championship. Beadle acknowledged the difficulty of the campaign, saying: "It was a real tough league for lots of different reasons. There were three or four really good sides in there and they've all raised their game when they've played us - their big day if you like." The club's support has been nothing short of extraordinary. Hereford have averaged 2,721 supporters at Edgar Street for their 18 Southern League Division One South & West home games this season - a figure that surpasses five League Two clubs and all but three National League sides: Tranmere Rovers (5,036), Lincoln City (4,346), and Wrexham (3,893). The travelling support has been equally impressive, with 1,807 fans making the journey to Salisbury - more than the combined attendance of all other Saturday fixtures in the division. "The fans have been spectacular," Beadle enthused. "You'd like to shake every one of them by the hand to thank them for all the effort they've put into getting across the south-west of the country to support us with the passion they do." BBC Hereford & Worcester sports editor Trevor Owens described it as "a phenomenal achievement by everyone connected with the club in only their second year in competitive league football." Looking ahead, Beadle remains ambitious: "This will keep evolving. It will keep getting bigger. That's our ambition - to make sure the club keeps moving forward."

V&A Launches £5m Campaign to Secure Cardinal Wolsey's Lost Angels The Victoria and Albert Museum is racing to raise £5 million to permanently acquire four bronze angel figurines originally designed for Cardinal Wolsey's tomb, with £2.5 million still needed. The rare 16th-century sculptures have caught the attention of acclaimed historical novelist Hilary Mantel, author of the Booker Prize-winning *Wolf Hall*, who described them as a tangible connection to "one of our liveliest eras of history." Cardinal Wolsey, who features prominently in Mantel's work, was the powerful advisor to King Henry VIII during the Tudor period. The bronze figures were commissioned in 1524 from Florentine sculptor Benedetto da Rovezzano to adorn the corners of Wolsey's elaborate tomb, intended to reflect his considerable stature and influence. However, the tomb was never completed, and the angels were sold off during the English Civil War, subsequently separated and lost to history. The pieces have only recently re-emerged through various sales and are now reunited at the V&A for the first time in centuries during the museum's fundraising campaign. The National Heritage Memorial Fund has committed £2 million toward the purchase, with the Art Fund contributing an additional £500,000. The museum is appealing to the public to donate the remaining funds online, via text message, or in person at the gallery. V&A director Martin Roth emphasized the angels' significance as "a vital part of our national history and artistic heritage," expressing his determination to acquire them for permanent preservation. Cardinal Wolsey fell from royal favour in his final years after failing to secure a Papal annulment for Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon. He died in 1530. Henry VIII later intended to appropriate the tomb for himself, but work remained incomplete at his death in 1547. The angels vanished from public view until 1994, when two surfaced at auction but went unrecognized as the Wolsey bronzes.

Rangers Fan Dies in Coach Crash on Way to Match A Rangers football supporter has died and 18 others were injured when a coach carrying fans to a match overturned in East Ayrshire on Saturday afternoon. The man has been named by family members as Ryan Baird, who was originally from Northern Ireland. His cousin, Louise Evanne Baird, said he was "amazing" and would be "sadly missed". Police Scotland said a further 18 people were taken to hospital, and three were seriously hurt. The crash happened at about 13:15 BST on Saturday on the A76 by the Crossroads Roundabout near Kilmarnock. The coach was taking the Nith Valley Loyal Rangers Supporters' Club to Ibrox Stadium, where Rangers were due to play Partick Thistle in the Scottish Premiership. Mr Baird's partner Sarah Hughes paid tribute to him, saying he had loved the club. The Nith Valley Loyal Rangers Supporters Club posted on its Facebook page: "The club would like to thank everyone for their good wishes & concern at this sad time." RangersLinfieldFC tweeted: "We have been informed that the man who sadly passed away was a Rangers and Linfield fan named Ryan Baird from Larne, Northern Ireland, RIP." In a club statement, Rangers said it was "deeply saddened" by the crash, adding: "Our profound condolences go to the gentleman who has died and our thoughts are with his family. We are also thinking of those who have been injured and taken to hospital." Rangers managing director Stewart Robertson said: "Everyone at the football club and every member of our Rangers family is thinking of all of those caught up in this terrible accident. Clearly this is a deeply distressing time and the board extend our deepest sympathies and concerns." Rangers assistant manager David Weir said he was sure the club "will be very supportive in regards to anything they can do to help the situation". Celtic also passed on their condolences in a club statement, saying: "In relation to news of today's accident involving Rangers supporters on their way to the match, everyone at Celtic sends our sincere condolences following the death of a supporter." One passenger said the bus, which had 37 people on board including the driver, had "swerved" before landing on its side on a grass verge. Police Scotland confirmed the 39-year-old man's death and said a report will be prepared for the Procurator Fiscal. The 18 people receiving hospital treatment include seven men under 20 years of age, three men and three women aged between 30 and 59, and five men over 60.

Brain Tumour Patient Emily Bennett Undergoes Surgery After Repeated Cancellations A 24-year-old woman from Fernhill Heath, near Worcester, has finally undergone brain surgery after experiencing multiple operation cancellations. Emily Bennett was originally scheduled to have the procedure at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham, at the beginning of December. The tumour had been causing her seizures and memory loss, creating significant health challenges. Her mother, Maxine Renton, confirmed that Emily was "awake and talking" following the three-hour operation. "They think they have removed the tumour but she's going to have an MRI tomorrow to make sure," she said. "She's just been moved into intensive care. She's very, very tired." Ms Renton added: "I am so relieved she is ok and conscious. Hopefully now the tumour has gone she might get back to normal." Emily's medical history is complex. She first had a malignant brain tumour removed when she was eight years old, which resulted in a slow-growing benign tumour. Although not life-threatening, the tumour was causing ongoing health problems. Emily described the repeated cancellations as "upsetting". A spokesperson for the hospital trust acknowledged the distress caused, stating: "We regret that any operation has to be cancelled and acknowledge the distress this can cause to both patients and their relatives."

Digwyddiadau yng Llanfyllin I gofio Ryan Davies Bydd cyfres o ddigwyddiadau'n cael eu cynnal yn Llanfyllin, Powys I gofio am y perfformiwr enwog Ryan Davies, 40 mlynedd ers ei farwolaeth. Er mai yng Nglanaman yn Sir Gaerfyrddin y cafodd ei eni, treuliodd Ryan Davies nifer o flynyddoedd o'i blentyndod yn Llanfyllin ar ôl I'w deulu symud yno pan oedd yn 10 oed. Cafodd ei rieni eu cyflogi I redeg wyrcws Y Dolydd wrth iddo gael ei drosglwyddo I fod yn gartref gofal. Roedd ei dad, W.T. Davies, wedi gweithio I nifer o awdurdodau lleol fel swyddog mewn cartrefi plant a chartrefi gofal. Yn ystod ei gyfnod yn Llanfyllin, bu Ryan yn canu yng Nghôr Plant Llanfyllin a dysgodd sut I ganu'r delyn dan gyfarwyddyd y delynores enwog Nansi Richards. Bu farw Ryan Davies ar 22 Ebrill 1977 yn Buffalo, talaith Efrog Newydd, yn 40 oed, ar ôl dioddef pwl difrifol o'r fogfa tra roedd ar ei wyliau yn yr Unol Daleithiau.

Police Launch Operation Respect to Keep Inverness Safe During Christmas Season Police Scotland has unveiled Operation Respect, a comprehensive safety initiative designed to protect residents and visitors in Inverness throughout the festive period. The operation will deploy additional police patrols during evening hours at licensed premises and taxi ranks, where revellers are most vulnerable. During daytime hours, plain clothes officers will focus on combating shoplifting in the city centre. Operation Respect represents a collaborative effort, involving Inverness Business Improvement District security workers, street pastors, and British Red Cross volunteers working alongside police officers. The initiative coincides with Police Scotland's national Campaign Against Violence, which takes place on Friday, 19 December. Inspector Anne Urquhart from Police Scotland's Inverness community beat unit said: "Christmas is a time to celebrate and have fun but for some it can provide opportunity to take advantage of those who are vulnerable and susceptible to crime. Police Scotland is once again delighted to work with our key partners to ensure that people gain maximum enjoyment from the city over the next few weeks and remain safe in doing so."

Sir Tom Jones Thanks Fans for Support After Wife's Death Sir Tom Jones has expressed his gratitude to fans for their messages of support following the death of his wife, Lady Melinda Rose Woodward, known as Linda, who passed away earlier this month after battling cancer. The couple, who hailed from Pontypridd in Rhondda Cynon Taff, shared 59 years of marriage. In a statement posted on his website under the heading "A little note from Tom," the legendary singer wrote: "So many beautiful and meaningful things were said and reading these genuine and lovely messages has lifted us all." Sir Tom and Linda's love story began when they were just 15 years old, meeting at a phone box at the end of his street in Treforest. They married at age 16 in 1957 and later had that very phone box relocated to their Los Angeles home as a sentimental keepsake. The couple had one son, Mark, who now serves as Sir Tom's manager. Lady Woodward died at Cedars Sinai Hospital in Los Angeles on 10 April. The singer cancelled several concerts when his wife fell ill. In his message, Sir Tom thanked fans for their "heartfelt" notes of sympathy and support, adding "See you soon." According to his website, the singer who achieved his first number one hit with "It's Not Unusual" in 1965, is scheduled to return to performing at the Hampton Court Palace Festival in London on 8 June, followed by concerts throughout the UK, Norway and Spain.

Two Welsh health boards are to receive £68.4m in emergency funding from the Welsh Government to address budget shortfalls. Betsi Cadwaladr in north Wales and Hywel Dda in west Wales are both projected to exceed their budgets for 2016-17. The money will be drawn from Welsh Government reserves. Health boards now operate on three-year budget cycles following criticism of repeated financial bail-outs. Last year, Hywel Dda overspent by £31.2m whilst Betsi Cadwaladr exceeded its budget by £19.5m, highlighting ongoing financial pressures within Welsh healthcare services.

Eden Hazard Completes Chelsea Move After Choosing Blues Over Manchester United The Belgium international, 21, has agreed personal terms and passed a medical with the Blues. Eden Hazard's journey to Stamford Bridge represents one of the summer's most sought-after transfers, with the talented winger ultimately choosing Chelsea's "project" over rival suitors. Born in La Louviere, Belgium in January 1991, Hazard has enjoyed a meteoric rise through European football. He made his first-team debut for Lille in November 2007 in a 2-0 defeat by Nancy, and within a year had earned his first Belgium cap against Luxembourg at just 18 years old. In September 2008, Hazard became Lille's youngest-ever goalscorer with a strike against Auxerre in a 3-2 victory. His precocious talent was further recognized when he won the Young Player of the Year award twice, in May 2010 becoming the first player to achieve this feat. The 2010-11 season proved particularly successful as Hazard helped Lille secure a league and cup double whilst claiming Player of the Year honors. He notched his first international goal for Belgium in October 2011 and won Player of the Year again in May 2012 after netting 17 league goals. "When they won the Champions League I told myself,'Why not Chelsea?'," said Hazard. "There was a struggle between Chelsea and [Manchester] United but, for me, Chelsea has the best project. It's a wonderful club." Chelsea are reportedly paying £32m for the youngster, who added: "The team is young and I have a better chance to play there. If I play well enough at Chelsea, I could win my place in the starting team." In his final season at Lille, Hazard scored 21 goals in 48 games, signing off with a hat-trick against Nancy last month. He joins Germany international Marko Marin as Chelsea's second major addition since January.

Cricket Commentator's Tip to Captain Under Investigation by Cricket Australia Cricket Australia has launched an investigation after a television commentator appeared to influence a captain's bowling decision during a Big Bash League match between Adelaide Strikers and Sydney Thunder. Adelaide Strikers captain Brad Hodge was told by Network Ten commentator Mark Howard that bowler Ben Laughlin had dismissed Sydney Thunder batsman Shane Watson twice in eight balls previously. Hodge, who was wearing a microphone and earpiece to communicate with the broadcast team between overs, responded by bringing Laughlin into the attack. During the exchange, Howard told Hodge: "Our master statistician Lawrie Colliver tells us that Laughlin has got Watson twice in the last eight balls he's bowled him in this competition." Hodge replied: "Really? I'll bring him on next over then. Let's get him into the game." The incident prompted former England batsman Kevin Pietersen, who was co-commentating but not involved in the exchange, to comment: "Very naughty. Very, very naughty, Howie." Cricket Australia issued a statement saying its integrity unit is investigating "to ensure the comments made during the broadcast did not jeopardise the integrity of last night's match." Network Ten subsequently apologised for Howard's remarks. Although Laughlin did not dismiss Watson, the Thunder batsman eventually scored 39 from 26 balls before being caught by Laughlin off Jake Lehmann's bowling. Thunder were dismissed for 101 chasing 178, leaving them bottom of the eight-team table and eliminated from knockout stage contention.

Massive Iceberg Breaks Away From Greenland's Jakobshavn Glacier A colossal section of ice measuring 12.4 square kilometres has broken away from Greenland's Jakobshavn Glacier in what scientists describe as one of the largest calving events ever recorded at this location. Satellite imagery from the European Space Agency indicates the dramatic break-up occurred between 13 and 19 August, pushing the glacier's calving front back several kilometres. Jakobshavn serves as a major drainage channel for the Greenland ice sheet, responsible for producing approximately 10% of all its icebergs. Once detached, these massive ice formations travel through a lengthy fjord before entering the Davis Strait and eventually making their way towards the Atlantic Ocean. The glacier holds historical significance, as it is widely believed to be the source of the iceberg that tragically sank the Titanic. Scientists have observed that Jakobshavn moves at tens of metres per day during summer months, establishing it as one of Greenland's fastest-flowing ice streams. The European Space Agency has been monitoring the situation using EU Sentinel satellites. The Sentinel-1a radar platform can penetrate cloud cover and map flow and elevation changes, whilst the Sentinel-2a optical spacecraft provides contextual imagery. According to ESA calculations, assuming the ice depth of approximately 1,400 metres, the calved volume would equal roughly 17.5 cubic kilometres—enough ice to blanket Manhattan Island with a layer 300 metres thick. Whilst substantial for Greenland, this calving event remains relatively modest compared to Antarctic ice sheet break-ups, where tabular bergs spanning thousands of square kilometres can separate from the southern polar region.

Temple Circus Roundabout to Be Replaced with Public Square Bristol's Temple Circus roundabout near Temple Meads station is set to be transformed into a public square with improved city access routes. A Bristol City Council spokesman said the new square would "give life to the area day and night." The redevelopment is part of a wider £21m investment in the Temple Quarter Enterprise Zone. Public consultation on the proposals will run until 18 February 2015, with an exhibition of the plans displayed at the Engine Shed from Tuesday, 13 January through Friday, 30 January. The council hopes the transformation will create a more vibrant and accessible gateway to the city centre.

Tall Ships Set Sail from Belfast as Thousands Line Coast Belfast served as the starting point for the prestigious Tall Ships Races, which commenced off the County Antrim coast on Monday. The magnificent fleet made its way towards Bangor in County Down before completing the ceremonial departure at Whitehead in County Antrim. Spectators were treated to a thrilling pre-race performance by the Red Arrows aerobatic display team before the vessels departed. The event showcased an impressive 50 ships representing 15 different nations. Police estimated that up to 300,000 people gathered along the Antrim and north Down coastlines to witness the spectacular send-off. This marked Belfast's second time hosting the event, having previously welcomed the Tall Ships in 2009. The official race began five miles off Portrush, County Antrim, at 10:00 BST on Monday. Following their departure from Northern Ireland, the international fleet will visit six ports across five countries, including stops in Aalesund and Kristiansand in Norway, before concluding in Aalborg, Denmark.

Brighton Refuse Workers Suspend Strike as Talks Continue A planned strike by refuse and recycling truck drivers in Brighton and Hove scheduled for Tuesday has been suspended, though industrial action remains scheduled for 3 October, the GMB union has confirmed. The drivers, who walked out earlier this month, are in dispute with the council over pay, staff grading and responsibility issues. The GMB union said a work-to-rule policy would continue during the negotiations. The union claims that some council employees are performing equivalent work to their members whilst receiving higher pay. GMB also alleges the authority has failed to "consult meaningfully" over new working practices and ongoing concerns about round allocation and distribution. GMB representative Mark Turner indicated further talks with the council are planned for next Tuesday. Brighton and Hove City Council welcomed the suspension of strike action and stated it is examining a "full service redesign to ensure we meet the needs of the city and to resolve work-to-rule". In a statement, the council said: "We cannot favour one group of workers over another and increasing allowances for one group of staff would require us to increase it for many others at great cost to the council's overall pay bill." The council noted that an agreement reached with trade unions last year aimed to ensure equal pay compliance. Last summer, similar industrial action resulted in waste accumulating on city streets.

Tiny Tail Cameras Reveal Secret Lives of Tool-Making New Caledonian Crows Ecologists have fitted wild New Caledonian crows with specially designed miniature tail cameras to observe their behavior beneath their bellies, capturing rare footage of these remarkable birds crafting and using sophisticated tools in their natural habitat. The groundbreaking study, led by Christian Rutz from the University of St Andrews in the UK, aimed to understand why New Caledonian crows are among the rare bird species that use tools while most others don't. "I think the answer lies in figuring out how important tool use is in their everyday lives," Dr Rutz explained. The research team analyzed nearly 12 hours of "crow cam" footage from 10 different birds, revealing surprising insights about their daily activities. Contrary to expectations, the crows spent remarkably little time making or using tools—only about 3% of their total observation time. Only four of the 10 birds even picked up a tool during the recording period. Instead, the crows dedicated most of their time to foraging for food using their beaks, particularly tearing strips from paperbark trees in search of grubs. Their sturdy beaks proved perfectly adequate for this task. "But every now and then, they suddenly switch to tool use - in the very same trees," Dr Rutz noted. "We don't understand what is happening there." Despite the limited tool use, the team captured extraordinary footage of two different crows not merely using sticks but actually manufacturing hooks—a sophisticated tool-making behavior. The birds snap off one branch from a forked twig, leaving a small portion of the main stem attached to create a hooked tool. "When we got that footage it was a proper high-five moment in the field camp," Dr Rutz said enthusiastically. While laboratory experiments and binocular observations had previously documented this hook-making behavior, this marked the first time researchers obtained video evidence of it occurring unprompted in the wild. Jolyon Troscianko from the University of Exeter emphasized the challenges of studying these birds: "New Caledonian crows are notoriously difficult to observe, not just because of the challenging terrain of their tropical habitats, but also because they can be quite sensitive to disturbance." The research team employed newly designed cameras that stored footage on micro SD cards rather than transmitting signals, eliminating the need for researchers to trek through difficult forest terrain with antennas. The devices record for approximately one week before automatically falling off the birds, and researchers locate them using tiny radio beacons. "We got much longer, uninterrupted video recordings," Dr Rutz said, highlighting how the improved technology has advanced their understanding of these intelligent birds.

Man Bailed in Murder Investigation of Wisbech Widow A 58-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder has been released on bail following the death of Una Crown in Wisbech. The widow was discovered in her Magazine Lane home on 13 January, having been stabbed and her body burned. Mrs Crown was last seen alive on the morning of 11 January but had spoken to a friend by telephone on 12 January afternoon. The man, arrested in Wisbech earlier this week, has been released pending further inquiries as police continue their investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death.

UN Chief Ban Ki-moon Hints at South Korean Presidential Bid UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon has strongly hinted he may run for South Korea's presidency, as political turmoil engulfs the country following the impeachment of President Park Geun-hye. Mr Ban's term as the world's top diplomat expires at the end of December. In his final press conference as UN chief, Mr Ban said that after some rest he will return to South Korea and consider how best to help his country. South Korea's next presidential election is scheduled to be held in December 2017. However, a poll could take place within two months after the country's parliament voted to impeach current President Park Geun-hye over an influence-peddling scandal. Ms Park is accused of allowing a close friend to profit from her connections with the presidency. If the country's constitutional court upholds last week's impeachment vote, she will become the first sitting South Korean president to be deposed in the country's democratic era - and a new presidential election will be held within 60 days. The constitutional court has 180 days to make a final ruling. Mr Ban's comments come amid ongoing protests in the South Korean capital, Seoul. Large crowds are expected to gather this weekend to demand that Ms Park resigns immediately, and to urge the constitutional court to formally remove her from office. This will be the eighth consecutive week of protests against Ms Park. While the rallies have been largely peaceful, there are fears that demonstrators could clash with thousands of the president's supporters who have planned their own protest near the court. Ms Park's lawyer, Lee Joong-hwan, has said the court should restore the president's powers because there is insufficient evidence to justify her removal. The case against Ms Park rests on her relationship with long-time friend Choi Soon-sil, who faces charges of coercion and abuse of power. It is alleged that after Ms Park became president in 2013, Ms Choi, 60, used their friendship to pressure powerful corporations into donating to foundations she controlled and then siphoned off funds for her personal use. Prosecutors say Ms Park had a "considerable" role in the alleged corruption. The president has denied that, but apologised for putting her trust in her jailed friend. Ms Choi's criminal trial will begin on 20 December.

Thieves Steal £550,000 Worth of Statues in Targeted Raid Three valuable statues worth approximately £550,000 have been stolen from a property in South Gloucestershire during a targeted break-in. The theft occurred at Bath Road, Cold Ashton, between 7 and 9 May. The most valuable item taken was a wishing well statue worth £500,000, along with two other statues depicting a horse and rider, each valued at around £25,000. Avon and Somerset Police described the raid as "targeted" and "well-planned". PC Simon McFall said the operation would have required multiple people due to the statues' significant weight and size. "It is more than likely that a van or other large vehicle was used to transport them," he added. Police are appealing for witnesses and anyone with information to contact the force.

Kobe Bryant Launches Investment Fund with Tech Entrepreneur Jeff Stibel Retired basketball legend Kobe Bryant has partnered with technology entrepreneur Jeff Stibel to launch a formal investment fund focused on technology, media, and data companies. Mr Bryant, the former captain of the Los Angeles Lakers, told the Wall Street Journal he felt he has a talent for identifying entrepreneurs. It is that talent and not his star power that the pair say they hope to bring to the companies they invest in. The "Bryant Stibel" fund will invest in tech, media and data companies. Mr Stibel is an entrepreneur and investor who founded several companies including Web.com. Mr Bryant, 37, retired from basketball earlier this year after a 20-year career. He has invested with Mr Stibel before, but this fund is the first formal partnership between them. The pair are financing the fund themselves. Since 2013, they have invested in 15 companies together including sports website The Players Tribune, videogame designer Scopely, and legal-services company LegalZoom. Mr Bryant who was known for his strong work ethic in basketball said, similar skills are needed for sport and growing a business. "It's the inner belief that a person has that he will endure no matter what the obstacle may be. It's that persistence, the entrepreneur doing what he or she truly believes in and truly loves to do," he said. The pair said the fund will last a few years and look to target companies where they feel they can add value through their business insight, and not through Mr Bryant's celebrity. Mr Stibel told the Wall Street Journal, "We don't want to be in the business of investing in companies so someone can use Kobe as an endorser. That's not interesting. The point is to add real value". Mr Bryant is not the first athlete to enter the investment world. An increasing number of sports starts and retired athletes are investing in venture capital funds and start-ups. Former basketball player Shaquille O'Neal has invested in several tech start-ups. Footballers David Beckham and Thierry Henry have both turned their attentions to investing since retiring.

Wakefield Trinity's Adam Walker Dropped from Scotland World Cup Squad After Positive Cocaine Test Wakefield Trinity forward Adam Walker has been removed from Scotland's Rugby League World Cup squad after testing positive for cocaine. The 26-year-old prop failed a drugs test following his team's Super League match at Widnes on 14 July. Both Wakefield Trinity and the Rugby Football League immediately suspended Walker pending further investigation. Scotland Rugby League chairman Keith Hogg announced the decision, stating: "We totally support the RFL anti-doping regulations and the action undertaken by Wakefield Trinity. We will be withdrawing Adam Walker from our extended World Cup squad." Scotland head coach Steve McCormack has moved quickly to replace Walker by adding two promising players to his 37-man squad for the World Cup in Australia later this year. New Zealand Warriors' James Bell and South Sydney Rabbitohs' Campbell Graham have been called up after both made their National Rugby League debuts last week. McCormack expressed his enthusiasm about the new additions: "We've known about them since last year and have been really pleased to see the progress that James and Campbell have been making. It was great to see them make their NRL debuts within a few days of each other."

Thousands join social media tribute to teenage rider Olivia Inglis The #rideforolivia tribute was launched following the death of Australian Olivia Inglis, 17, in a fall on Sunday. Hundreds of thousands of social media users from dozens of countries have been posting and sharing photos of their own horses using the hashtag. Olympic gold medallist Charlotte Dujardin is among the high-profile figures to have joined in the tributes. Fellow British dressage rider and gold medallist Carl Hester has also paid tribute. The movement echoes a similar social campaign to mark the death of Australian cricketer Phillip Hughes in 2014. The hashtags #putoutyourbats and #putyourbatsout were tweeted and shared across platforms such as Instagram and Facebook along with photos of cricket bats. As of 08:00 GMT on Thursday, more than 120,000 people had posted photographs and videos for #rideforolivia on Instagram alone. The images will be used to create a mosaic of Olivia for her family, following a call from the bloodstock company which her family runs. "We have been overwhelmed by the kindness and sympathy from family and friends throughout the school, equestrian and thoroughbred communities," parents Arthur and Charlotte said in a family statement. The global outpouring of support demonstrates the tight-knit nature of the international equestrian community and the profound impact of Olivia's tragic passing.

Man Admits Life-Threatening Assault on Islay After Pub Altercation A man has admitted assaulting another man to the danger of his life following a violent attack outside a pub on the Isle of Islay. Andrew MacGillivray, 33, punched Keith Cameron and stood on his chest, causing his ribs to crack, near the Ardview Inn in Port Ellen on 23 March last year. He pleaded guilty to assaulting the 41-year-old to the danger of his life at the High Court in Glasgow, where judges heard Mr Cameron was fortunate to be alive. The court was told that MacGillivray became involved in an argument with a woman inside the bar. Mr Cameron, known locally as "Cabana," attempted to intervene and calm the situation. MacGillivray was subsequently asked to leave the premises but waited outside for his victim to emerge. When Mr Cameron left the pub, MacGillivray knocked him to the ground with a single punch before launching a sustained attack on him as he lay defenceless. He then stood on Mr Cameron's ribs with such force that they cracked audibly. The severity of the injuries was such that when a passing couple who knew Mr Cameron discovered him, they were unable to recognise him due to the extent of his facial injuries. MacGillivray, a father-of-three, returned home and told his wife: "I think I've killed Cabana. I hope he's OK. I know I hurt his ribs." He later told police that he heard the ribs crack and that Mr Cameron's chest "went as flat as his stomach." Before his arrest, MacGillivray told his father-in-law: "I did it - I would do it again and worse. If you want to be hard, you have to act hard." Mr Cameron suffered facial injuries, damage to his eye, and significant chest fractures. He required treatment at the Southern General Hospital in Glasgow after being airlifted from Islay. Medical experts told the court that the chest injuries were more commonly associated with heavy objects falling on people and that Mr Cameron's life had been in danger. Sentence on MacGillivray was deferred.

Mother'Staged Baby's Death on London Bus', Court Hears A mother accused of murdering her 16-week-old daughter "staged" the infant's death on a London bus after the baby was already dead, a court has heard. Rosalin Baker, 25, and her partner Jeffrey Wiltshire, 52, deny murdering baby Imani and attempting to cover up her death by making it appear she died in public. The Old Bailey was told that Imani was already deceased when Ms Baker boarded the number 25 bus in Stratford, east London, with her daughter's body. Passenger Fjoralba Shmitz told jurors how Ms Baker gestured to her while on the phone, saying: "There's something wrong with my baby." Ms Shmitz described the harrowing scene: "I saw the baby's face. I touched her left cheek. It was cold. The baby was not breathing. I tried to help but I didn't manage to do so." The witness said she took the child and asked the bus driver to call emergency services. "I became distressed because the baby was not moving," she told the court. "I thought that the baby was dead." She described how she returned to the bus seat with the infant, where another passenger, believed to be Spanish, "started praying." When asked about Ms Baker's reaction, Ms Shmitz said the mother was notably calm. "She was not crying, she was not shouting, she was not speaking," the witness testified. Under cross-examination by Icah Peart QC, Ms Shmitz confirmed Ms Baker appeared "very relaxed" and seemed detached during the "distressing episode." Jurors have previously heard that Imani had suffered multiple attacks before her death, sustaining 40 rib fractures, a fractured wrist, and head injuries. Both Ms Baker and Mr Wiltshire, from Newham, east London, deny charges of murder and causing or allowing the death of a child. The trial continues.

Mad Men Star Jon Hamm Completes Rehabilitation Treatment Jon Hamm, the acclaimed actor best known for portraying the complex Don Draper in AMC's hit series Mad Men, has completed treatment for alcohol addiction at a rehabilitation facility, his representatives have confirmed. The actor, who has asked for "privacy and sensitivity" following the revelation, sought help with the support of his long-time partner, actress and film-maker Jennifer Westfeldt. The timing of his treatment comes as Hamm has been actively promoting the final season of the Emmy-winning drama series. According to celebrity website TMZ, which broke the story, the Golden Globe-winning actor underwent a 30-day treatment program at Silver Hill Hospital in New Canaan, Connecticut, a facility known for treating high-profile clients. Throughout Mad Men's eight-year run, Hamm has frequently been asked about similarities between himself and his hard-drinking character. In a 2012 interview with the Daily Mail, he noted, "I don't drink as much as Don Draper. I would be unconscious if I did." However, the actor has previously been candid about his struggles with alcohol, particularly following his father's death from diabetes complications in 1991. Hamm, who lost his mother a decade earlier, found himself orphaned at age 20. "It just changed everything," he told GQ magazine last year. "It was just a profound sense of being alone. I was at a crossroads. It really could have gone the wrong way." Despite the personal challenges, Hamm's career continues to flourish. Beyond Mad Men's conclusion, he has secured roles in two Netflix series: Tina Fey's critically-acclaimed Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt and the upcoming Wet Hot American Summer prequel series. The actor has also built an impressive film resume, appearing in The Town, Bridesmaids, and Kissing Jessica Stein, where he first met Westfeldt. Representatives for Hamm have requested that his privacy be respected during this time.

Cardiff Blues Reject WRU Takeover Option to Focus on Arms Park Redevelopment Cardiff Blues have unanimously decided not to pursue the option of a Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) takeover, the region's chief executive Richard Holland has confirmed. The announcement comes as the Blues continue negotiations with Cardiff Athletic Club over extending their lease at Cardiff Arms Park, which is set to expire in January 2022. In an open letter to supporters, Holland revealed that "amicable discussions" had taken place regarding potential WRU assistance during the possible redevelopment of the historic stadium. However, the region's board has chosen to maintain independence while exploring alternative paths forward. "We will continue to explore the best way forward for the future of our region," Holland stated. The decision follows earlier comments from WRU chief executive Martyn Phillips in May, when he described talks over a potential Blues takeover as "embryonic." The announcement also comes shortly after a vote that enabled the WRU to take over Blues' regional rivals, Newport Gwent Dragons. ## Lease Negotiations Progress The Blues' stadium redevelopment plans hinge on securing a new agreement with Cardiff Athletic Club (CAC), the body comprising Cardiff's tennis, bowls, hockey and cricket clubs that maintains a clubhouse at the Arms Park. A CAC spokesperson confirmed that negotiations are continuing, saying: "I can confirm that negotiations are ongoing and we hope to call an EGM [extraordinary general meeting] in the not too distant future." However, the spokesperson added that practical considerations, including the Champions League Final on 3 June, would likely delay any meeting for several weeks. ## Redevelopment Vision Holland emphasized the urgency of securing the Blues' long-term future at their traditional home, noting that only five years remain on the current lease while annual maintenance costs continue to rise. "The history and heritage of Cardiff Rugby at Cardiff Arms Park is of paramount importance to the board and it is essential to protect all elements of this great club and its iconic home," he said. The Blues are seeking a new 150-year lease with development rights from CAC. Holland expressed optimism about reaching an agreement with the CAC management board. Previously announced plans envision transforming the Arms Park into a modern 15,000-capacity stadium featuring a retractable pitch and sliding roof, enabling the venue to host concerts as well as rugby matches. Additional proposals include an exhibition centre, hotel and residential flats. Holland indicated he would soon present "concept ideas" for the redevelopment, ranging from replacing the North and South stands to a complete site redevelopment, while maintaining rugby as the priority use. "These concepts are purely an indication of what could be achieved," he explained.

Syrian Refugees Cast Votes in Presidential Election at Embassies in Beirut and Amman Polling stations at Syrian embassies in Beirut and Amman opened Wednesday for expatriate voting ahead of Syria's controversial presidential election, drawing massive crowds of Syrian refugees eager to cast their ballots. The voting comes as the United Nations reports that 2.8 million Syrian refugees have fled to neighbouring countries since the conflict began. President Bashar al-Assad is widely expected to secure a third seven-year term in the June 3 election, which Western nations have dismissed as a sham. ## Massive Turnout in Beirut Thousands of Syrians flocked to their embassy in the hills overlooking Beirut, creating unprecedented scenes. BBC correspondent Jim Muir, reporting from the scene, described the massive turnout as producing "scenes rarely observed at any embassy or polling station in the world." The event transformed at times into what appeared to be a rowdy support rally for President Assad, abandoning typical election decorum. As the only polling station available for all of Lebanon, where an estimated 1.5 million or more Syrians currently reside, the embassy was completely overwhelmed. The voting congestion brought much of Beirut to a standstill, demonstrating to many Lebanese residents how deeply the Syrian crisis has penetrated their country. Of the one million Syrian refugees registered in Lebanon, approximately half are believed to be of voting age. Embassy officials indicated they may extend voting hours if large numbers are unable to participate. ## Regional Diplomatic Tensions In Jordan's capital, Amman, voting proceeded just days after the kingdom expelled Syrian ambassador Bahjat Suleiman over what it termed "repeated insults" against the country. According to Syria's state-run Sana news agency, voting also commenced at embassies in Russia, Malaysia, Sudan, and several other countries. However, the agency reported that the United Arab Emirates banned Syrians from voting, following similar prohibitions by France, Germany, and Belgium. Many expatriates living in countries where Syrian embassies closed in 2011 remain unable to vote. ## Controversial Election The strength and assertiveness of the vote may reflect an underlying sentiment among many Syrians abroad that momentum favours the regime, observers suggest. The opposition coalition welcomed recent promises from President Obama for increased aid, though questions remain about whether such support can shift the balance given Western concerns about jihadi presence in rebel-controlled areas. This marks the first time in decades that Syria has held a presidential election featuring multiple candidates. However, the two challengers remain largely unknown and have been unable to campaign equally with the president. Previous presidential terms were determined through referendums with only Assad family members on the ballot. More than 160,000 people have died since the uprising against President Assad began in March 2011.

Australian Government Website Accidentally Exposes Politicians' Phone Numbers The mobile phone numbers of several former Australian prime ministers and hundreds of other politicians were inadvertently exposed on a government website for more than three months, Fairfax Media has reported. The security breach affected Opposition Leader Bill Shorten and former prime ministers Julia Gillard, John Howard, and Paul Keating. Current Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull and some senior government members were not impacted by the incident. The sensitive information was discovered on the Department of Parliamentary Services (DPS) website, where phone numbers appeared invisible but could be revealed when highlighted with a cursor or copied and pasted into another document. In a statement to the BBC, the DPS explained that the numbers were included in a report detailing parliamentary phone and data spending. The report was compiled by private contractor TELCO Management. "In the most recent report provided by the contractor, it became possible to view the official mobile phone number of parliamentarians and their staff even though they appeared redacted from the published files," a DPS spokesperson stated. The department removed the documents immediately after being alerted to the problem and is investigating the cause with the contractor. While the exact number of affected individuals wasn't disclosed, Fairfax reported it reached into the hundreds. The DPS has committed to addressing privacy concerns with affected MPs. TELCO Management has been contacted for comment.

Britain Boycotts Russian Biathlon Event Over Doping Scandal Britain has announced it will boycott a biathlon event in Tyumen, Russia, citing "brain-washed, deluded and dishonest comments" from Russian athletes following the damning McLaren report. The report alleges that over 1,000 Russian athletes benefited from state-sponsored doping between 2011 and 2015, with 31 suspicious cases specifically involving biathletes according to the International Biathlon Union. The IBU plans to announce sanctions on 22 December, following World Anti-Doping Agency guidelines. The investigation focused heavily on the Sochi Olympic Winter Games. Britain joins the Czech Republic in boycotting the March 9-12 competition in Tyumen, taking a firm stance against what they perceive as inadequate responses from Russian sporting authorities.

Ukraine Blocks Russian Websites and Services in Escalating Sanctions Row Ukraine has dramatically escalated sanctions against Russia by blocking access to the country's most popular social media platforms and internet services, in a move that could affect millions of Ukrainian users. President Petro Poroshenko has signed off on restrictions targeting major Russian digital platforms including the social networks VK.com and Odnoklassniki, search engine Yandex, and the Mail.ru email service. The decision represents a significant ramping up of sanctions on Ukraine's neighbour for its annexation of Crimea and the continuing conflict in eastern Ukraine. Ukrainian service providers have been ordered to block access to these sites, whilst the companies' offices in Ukraine will face asset freezes and other restrictions. However, it remains unclear how the ban will be technically implemented and whether Ukrainian authorities possess the means to enforce it effectively. The president's decision to implement recommendations from Ukraine's national security council could prove controversial domestically. VK (VKontakte) alone boasts an estimated 15 million users in Ukraine, whilst Odnoklassniki (translating as "Classmates") enjoys widespread popularity across the country. Public reaction has been mixed.
