Hart began this campaign as second choice behind Willy Caballero, a clear indication of Guardiola's doubts about his suitability for the role. The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager has been forthright about his requirements from a goalkeeper, explaining his tactical approach in detail on Tuesday. "From 15 years old, I grew up knowing every time we had a good build-up we created chances," Guardiola said. "When the goalkeeper, the full-backs and the centre-backs can do this, it is easier. The pitch is big and the space is always there." He added: "I would like to have the ball for 90 minutes. I know some managers prefer to play on the counter-attack. I am completely the opposite." Despite training with the first-team squad on Tuesday morning at the City Football Academy, Hart's long-term future at the club remains uncertain. While it was widely expected that he would leave before the transfer window closes on 31 August, an immediate departure now appears less certain. Hart has reportedly rejected potential moves to both Sevilla and Borussia Dortmund, who have expressed interest in signing him. Everton, who seemed a likely destination last week, have apparently cooled their interest due to Hart's substantial wages, which exceed their current salary structure, and the impressive early-season performances of their new signing Maarten Stekelenburg. England manager Sam Allardyce has expressed concern about Hart's situation but confirmed he would still select the goalkeeper for the World Cup qualifier against Slovakia on 4 September, provided his lack of club football doesn't continue. Hart wasn't the only high-profile player training away from the main group on Tuesday. Yaya Toure, Wilfried Bony, Samir Nasri, and Eliaquim Mangala, none of whom have featured for City this season, were among 33 players training across two pitches at the academy. With just over two weeks remaining in the transfer window, Hart faces a crucial decision about his future as Guardiola's revolution at Manchester City continues to gather pace.

Train Hits Conveyor Wagon at 102mph in Barrow upon Soar Incident An East Midlands Trains service travelling from Leicester to York struck part of a conveyor wagon at Barrow upon Soar earlier this month, prompting dual investigations by safety authorities. The collision occurred at 10:27 on 14 February when the train, travelling at 102mph, hit the boom of a conveyor wagon protruding over the line at Mountsorrel sidings. The Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) confirmed the train was within the 110mph speed limit for that section. The driver immediately applied emergency brakes, preventing derailment and passenger injuries, though the driver was reportedly "badly shaken" by the incident. A man working on the lorry was taken to hospital for treatment. Following the collision, the train proceeded at low speed to Loughborough, where passengers transferred to alternative services to complete their journeys. Both the RAIB and the Office of Road and Rail have launched investigations into the incident to determine the circumstances that led to the equipment obstructing the railway line.

Drug Dealer Sentenced for Supplying Hallucinogen That Led to Fatal Stabbing A drug dealer who supplied a dangerous hallucinogenic substance that led to a young man being stabbed to death has been sentenced to community service. Keiron Turley, 20, from Malden Road in Liverpool, was ordered to complete 200 hours of unpaid community work at York Crown Court after pleading guilty to being concerned in the supply of class A drugs. North Yorkshire Police confirmed Turley had supplied 25i-NBOMe, commonly known as N-bomb, to victim Liam Miller in June 2015. The hallucinogenic drug triggered a fatal chain of events culminating in Mr Miller's death the following month. Samuel Donley, then 19, stabbed his close friend 32 times during a psychotic episode at his home on Hamilton Drive, York, on the night of July 27 whilst his parents were away. During Donley's trial at Leeds Crown Court, jurors heard he believed he was trapped in a dream and thought Mr Miller was a skull that needed to be stabbed to return to reality. Donley, now 20, was jailed last November for six years and eight months after admitting manslaughter. He also received a concurrent 32-month sentence for wounding innocent passer-by Theophilos Theophilou during what detectives described as a "horrific and violent attack." Mr Miller was from Terrington, near Malton.

UK Services Sector Growth Slows as Business Confidence Weakens The UK services sector experienced a notable slowdown in December, according to the latest Markit/CIPS purchasing managers' index (PMI), though the economy continues to expand at a healthy rate. The services PMI fell to 55.5 from 59.9 in November, marking a significant drop but remaining comfortably above the 50-point threshold that separates growth from contraction. Despite the deceleration, Markit reported that UK growth had "stabilised at a solid pace" with continued strong increases in new business. Chris Williamson, chief economist at Markit, noted that "the services sector remained the key driver of the UK's economic upturn in December, helping to offset the recent weakness seen in manufacturing and putting the economy on the starting block for another year of 2 to 2.5% growth in 2016." The data suggests the economy grew by 0.5% in the fourth quarter, slightly down from Markit's previous estimate of 0.6%. This follows mixed signals from other sectors, with manufacturing growing at its slowest pace in three months whilst construction rebounded due to stronger commercial building activity. However, Mr Williamson warned of "significant downside risks" facing the UK economy in 2016, including the impact of the Living Wage, government spending cuts, potential interest rate increases, global economic concerns, and uncertainty over Brexit. Concerns are mounting as job creation in the services sector slowed to its weakest pace in five months during December. Long-term business expectations also fell to their lowest level since 2013, which Mr Williamson described as "a warning shot to those taking a complacent view of economic prospects for the coming year."

NHS 111 Service Rollout Should Be Halted, Says BMA Chief The troubled rollout of the NHS 111 helpline should be suspended immediately due to serious safety concerns, the British Medical Association has warned. The new telephone service, designed to replace NHS Direct, is being piloted across various regions of England but has encountered significant problems, with some callers reportedly left waiting on hold for hours before receiving medical advice. Dr Laurence Buckman, chair of the BMA's GP committee, has called for the wider implementation of the service to be stalled until the numerous technical and operational issues can be resolved. "The BMA is seriously concerned that these failures are not only having impact on other, already overstretched NHS services, but potentially putting patient safety at risk," he said. The association has received widespread reports of NHS 111 failures from multiple pilot areas. Several regions have struggled to cope with call volumes, while others have experienced catastrophic IT system failures. In Greater Manchester, the entire system crashed, leaving calls completely unanswered. One elderly patient was forced to wait 90 minutes for a callback from the service. These problems have triggered a surge in ambulance callouts and accident and emergency department visits, as frustrated callers resort to alternative measures to access healthcare professionals. This has placed additional strain on already stretched NHS resources. "Patients need to have their calls answered immediately and correctly and not be faced with any form of delay," Dr Buckman emphasized. "The Department of Health needs to reconsider immediately its launch of NHS 111 which clearly is not functioning properly. They must ensure that the system is safe for patients before it is rolled out any further." The Department of Health has acknowledged the difficulties and is providing some areas with additional time to prepare. It has already approved extensions of up to six months beyond the original 1 April 2013 deadline for regions struggling to establish the new service. Health Minister Lord Howe defended the rollout, stating: "NHS 111 will help patients access the whole of the NHS through just one simple number. To ensure that patients get the best care and treatment, we are giving some areas more time to go live with NHS 111 while we carry out thorough testing to ensure that those services are reliable." The existing NHS Direct 0845 4647 service will continue operating in areas where NHS 111 is not yet available, including North of Tyne and Tees, North Essex, Bedfordshire and Luton, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, Leicestershire and Rutland, Berkshire, Cornwall and Devon.

BMW Masters: Play Suspended as Slattery Leads in Shanghai Twenty-three players will return early on Monday to complete their rounds after play was suspended on Sunday because of bad light at the BMW Masters in Shanghai. England's Andrew Slattery and South Korea's Soomin Lee are 14-under after 13 completed holes, sharing the lead in difficult conditions. Co-leader Alexander Levy of France faces a birdie putt on the 13th green when play resumes. More than six and a half hours were lost to bad weather over the first two days, and more time was lost in the final round on Sunday because of an afternoon thunderstorm. Australian Scott Hend is the clubhouse leader at 13-under after a bogey-free 66, with South African Brandon Stone and Dutchman Joost Luiten also 13-under with five and three holes to complete respectively.

Northern Ireland Health Minister Issues New Abortion Guidelines Following Human Rights Ruling Northern Ireland's Health Minister Simon Hamilton has announced plans to introduce new guidelines on abortion following a landmark court ruling that declared the region's current legislation to be in breach of human rights law. The announcement comes after a judicial review on Monday found that the grounds for abortion should be extended in Northern Ireland. Currently, termination of pregnancy is only permitted if a woman's life is at risk or there is a permanent or serious risk to her mental or physical health. The Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission (NIHRC), which brought the case, is seeking to extend abortion access to cases of serious foetal malformation, rape or incest. Unlike the rest of the United Kingdom, the 1967 Abortion Act does not apply to Northern Ireland. Minister Hamilton confirmed that the new guidelines have been prepared in consultation with health professionals and would be made public after consideration by his Executive colleagues. "I think the guidelines offer an opportunity to clarify satisfactorily the law as it currently stands in Northern Ireland," he stated. In Monday's ruling, Mr Justice Horner determined that women who were victims of sexual crimes and cases of fatal foetal abnormality were entitled to exemptions in the law. He stated that given the Northern Ireland Executive's unlikely action on the matter, and that citizens were entitled to have their human rights protected, the current legislation violated their rights under the European Convention on Human Rights. The decision has been welcomed by Sarah Ewart, whose personal experience brought the issue to public attention in 2013. At 20 weeks pregnant, Ms Ewart was forced to travel to England for an abortion after her baby was diagnosed with anencephaly, a condition where the brain fails to develop. Speaking on Tuesday, Ms Ewart expressed relief that women could now "get medical attention in our hospitals in our own country." She added: "At the start we'll just take small steps and see where we go from here." However, Northern Ireland's Attorney General John Larkin said he was "profoundly disappointed" by the decision and was considering grounds for appeal. The Lord Chief Justice's Office has indicated that whilst the court cannot force legislation to be changed, the final decision rests with Parliament.

New Bus Station and Cycle Hub Planned for Cardiff's Central Square A major transport development could transform Cardiff's Central Square, with plans for a 14-stand bus station and a 502-space cycle hub on the site of Marland House and NCP car park. The proposal, scheduled for review by Cardiff council's planning committee on Wednesday, also includes retail units, a five-storey office block, a nine-storey apartment block, and a private car park. The development comes after the city's previous bus station was demolished to accommodate BBC Wales' new headquarters at Central Square.

Interpol Suspends €20 Million Fifa Partnership Over Corruption Scandal Interpol has frozen a €20 million (£14m) agreement with Fifa, suspending a major anti-corruption partnership as the football governing body faces mounting allegations of bribery and wrongdoing. The international police agency announced it would halt the 10-year "Integrity in Sport" programme, which was established in 2011 with Fifa funding to combat match-fixing and illegal gambling in football. Juergen Stock, Interpol's Secretary General, said the decision was made "in light of the current context surrounding Fifa," adding that the organisation remains committed to integrity in sport but cannot continue the partnership under present circumstances. "All external partners, whether public or private, must share the fundamental values and principles of the organisation, as well as those of the wider law enforcement community," Mr Stock stated. The original agreement stipulated that Fifa must be "compatible with the principles, aims and activities of Interpol" – a condition now apparently in question. Fifa expressed disappointment at the decision, with a spokesperson telling the BBC that the programme's "success and importance cannot be understated" and describing it as "a key part of addressing the transnational problem of match-fixing." The football body argued the programme is "unrelated to the current issues surrounding Fifa" and warned that Interpol's "unilateral decision will negatively impact the fight against criminal activity." Fifa said it would reach out to Interpol for further discussions. The suspension comes after US and Swiss authorities launched investigations into Fifa for alleged corruption. Last month, 14 current and former Fifa officials and sports marketing executives were charged following a years-long US-led investigation. The scandal has cast doubt over the legitimacy of bidding processes for the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, awarded to Russia and Qatar respectively, with ongoing questions about potential irregularities in the selection process.

Diageo to Move Scotch Whisky Bottling Jobs from Scotland to Italy Drinks giant Diageo has announced plans to transfer some Scotch whisky bottling operations from Scotland to Italy, putting more than 100 jobs at risk across two Scottish plants. Seventy jobs are expected to go at Shieldhall by the end of the year and 35 at Leven, unless new bottling contracts can be won. Diageo's bottling plant in Italy is running below capacity after it disposed of its wine business. Unions at the main distiller of Scotch whisky strongly criticised the move. Unite said it was a "shocking betrayal of Scottish workers" and the GMB said it was connected to the economic uncertainties arising from Brexit. But Diageo said it followed a review of its spirits bottling business to ensure the company delivered "leading performance" in domestic and export supply chains. A spokesman added: "Regrettably, these changes may impact some roles in our European bottling plants towards the end of the year and we will now enter a period of consultation with our employees and their representatives to discuss the proposals in more detail. "We are committed to our three spirits bottling sites in Europe - two in Scotland and one in Italy. The outcomes of this review will ensure we have the flexibility to respond to increased competition and external volatility, alongside testing and building the capability we need across our global supply chain to grow our brands." There are currently 500 workers at Shieldhall, in south-west Glasgow, and 800 at Leven in Fife. Cabinet Secretary for Finance Derek Mackay said Diageo's announcement was "deeply disappointing news". He said Scottish Enterprise is engaging with the company to explore all possible options for supporting those affected. "If any redundancies proceed, through our initiative for responding to redundancy situations, Partnership Action for Continuing Employment, we will provide skills development and employability support to minimise the time that individuals affected are out of work."

Shkreli to Invoke Fifth Amendment at Congressional Hearing on Drug Pricing Martin Shkreli, the controversial former pharmaceutical executive, will refuse to testify before Congress about dramatic drug price increases, his attorney has confirmed. Mr Shkreli's lawyer informed the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform that he would invoke his right against self-incrimination. The former hedge fund manager hit the headlines when his company raised the price of a life-saving drug by 5,000%. He also faces separate criminal charges that he defrauded investors. The committee sent a letter to Mr Shkreli requesting he testify about his former company Turing Pharmaceuticals' decision to raise the price of the drug Daraprim, used to treat life-threatening parasitic infections. In a statement, Congressman Elijah Cummings, a member of the committee said: "If he [Mr Shkreli] plans on trying to use his own intentional inaction as some kind of bogus excuse for not showing up at Tuesday's hearing, people will see right through such a juvenile tactic." On Wednesday, Mr Shkreli posted a picture of the subpoena letter on his Twitter account and wrote, "Found this letter. Looks important." In December, Mr Shkreli was arrested in New York on charges he defrauded investors at a drug company he previously ran, Retrophin, and a hedge fund, MSMB Capital Management, where he was a fund manager. He has denied the charges and was released on bail pending the trial. The FBI allege Mr Shkreli "engaged in multiple schemes to ensnare investors through a web of lies and deceit". Neither of those cases are connected to Daraprim's price increase or Turing Pharmaceuticals. Mr Shkreli stepped down as Turing's head after his December arrest.

Countryfile Success Leads to New BBC Daytime Spin-Off Series The BBC has announced a new daytime spin-off of its hit rural affairs programme Countryfile, following the show's impressive ratings performance in 2015. The Sunday night programme attracted an average of six million viewers throughout 2015, with a November episode reaching a peak audience of 7.8 million. In a significant achievement, Countryfile managed to beat The X Factor's Sunday results show in the ratings on two occasions last month. The new five-part series, titled Countryfile Diaries, will launch in spring on BBC One. Running across a week, the spin-off will showcase country life through the changing seasons and will be scheduled to coincide with Countryfile's seasonal specials. BBC daytime controller Dan McGolpin said the programme would allow viewers "to further enjoy the full splendour and sheer variety of life in the British countryside during key moments of the year". Countryfile, presented by Matt Baker, Anita Rani and others, achieved its highest audiences in autumn when scheduled before Strictly Come Dancing. Between 8 November and 13 December, more than 7.2 million households tuned in on average. Executive producer Bill Lyons attributed the "huge audience" to "the enduring love-affair between the British people and their countryside", making it the most popular weekly factual series on television. Details of locations and presenters for Countryfile Diaries are yet to be announced.

Yemen Peace Talks Announced as Conflict Intensifies with Rebel Attacks on Saudi Arabia UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon has called for peace negotiations in Yemen as violence escalated dramatically on Saturday, with Houthi rebels launching increasingly bold attacks against Saudi Arabian targets. The announcement of upcoming talks comes amid intensifying hostilities that have already claimed more than 2,000 lives over several months of warfare. Mr. Ban urged all parties to enter negotiations in good faith and without pre-conditions, though observers note this may prove challenging given the current climate. In a significant escalation on Saturday, Saudi Arabia intercepted a Scud missile fired by Houthi rebels and their allies using a Patriot missile battery near the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait. According to the state-run Saudi Press Agency, this marked one of the few missile attacks since the air campaign began ten weeks ago. A pro-Houthi military spokesman told Yemen's rebel-controlled Saba news agency that the missile targeted the Prince Khaled air base. The attack followed Friday's border clashes that left four Saudi soldiers and several Yemeni rebels dead. BBC Middle East Editor Sebastian Usher notes that both Yemen's government—now largely exiled in Saudi Arabia—and the rebel forces have confirmed their attendance at peace negotiations. However, each side appears to be positioning for advantage before talks commence. "The Houthis and their allies are launching ever bolder attacks inside Saudi Arabia to demonstrate they have withstood two months of air bombardment, while the Saudis only pound them more," Usher observed. Saudi officials characterized the rebel actions as attempts "to penetrate our borders," which were ultimately repelled. The kingdom's 10-week bombing campaign has prioritized destroying rebel missile capabilities, though officials acknowledge the difficulty of this task, as approximately 300 missiles are believed hidden in caves. The Saudi-led air campaign supports Yemeni President Abedrabbo Manour Hadi, who fled to Riyadh when Houthi forces advanced on his southern stronghold in Aden. Meanwhile, the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate dramatically. The UN has described the crisis as "catastrophic," with 20 million civilians—representing 80% of Yemen's population—requiring humanitarian assistance. Despite the escalating violence and mounting civilian toll, the scheduled peace talks represent a potential diplomatic breakthrough in the conflict.

Prison Lifer Convicted of Murdering Fellow Inmate with Kitchen Knife A prisoner already serving life for murder has been found guilty of killing a fellow inmate at Dartmoor Prison with a 10-inch kitchen knife. William Tolcher, 51, denied attacking Alex Cusworth, 37, with the 10in (23cm) knife at Dartmoor Prison last November. A jury at Plymouth Crown Court found him guilty of murder and he is due to be sentenced on Friday. Tolcher, from Liverpool, is serving a life sentence for the murder of a woman in Newquay, Cornwall, in 1996. Mr Cusworth suffered internal bleeding after the attack and died at Derriford Hospital in Plymouth. Judge James Dingemens said he was considering a minimum 30-year jail sentence. Tolcher was convicted of murdering a woman in Newquay, Cornwall, in 1996 and was already serving a life sentence.

Inmate Admits Attacking Soham Killer Ian Huntley's Attacker A prisoner has admitted attempting to murder the man who previously attacked Soham murderer Ian Huntley. Kevin McCarthy, 49, appeared at Cambridge Crown Court charged with the attempted murder of Damien Fowkes, 41, leaving him with life-threatening neck injuries on 2 October. Both men were inmates at HMP Whitemoor in Cambridgeshire at the time. McCarthy is due to be sentenced on Wednesday. Fowkes is serving a life sentence with a minimum term of 20 years for the attempted murder of Huntley at HMP Frankland in Durham in 2010. Fowkes went on to strangle paedophile and child-killer Colin Hatch in 2011 at Full Sutton high security prison near York.

Berlin Police Shut Down Dandy Diner Opening After Massive Crowd Forms The highly anticipated opening of the Dandy Diner in Berlin was abruptly shut down by police after drawing an unprecedented crowd on Saturday night. About 300 people packed inside the new restaurant while hundreds more waited outside, prompting police intervention. The Dandy Diary blog on Facebook confirmed the closure with a colourful expletive, acknowledging "police closed us down." The event, organized by entrepreneurs Jakob Haupt and David Roth, attracted exceptional attention. German newspaper Der Tagesspiegel noted that restaurant openings "have rarely drawn such a big crowd" in Berlin. The massive gathering extended far down Karl Marx Strasse in the Neukoelln district, creating significant buzz on social media.

Strictly Come Dancing Final: Four Couples Compete for Glitterball Trophy The stage is set for one of the most anticipated television events of the year as four remaining couples prepare to battle it out in the Strictly Come Dancing final this Saturday. Actresses Kellie Bright and Georgia May Foote, presenter Katie Derham, and pop star Jay McGuiness are all hoping to dance their way to glory alongside their professional partners, with the ultimate prize being the iconic Strictly glitterball trophy. In interviews with the BBC, all four finalists expressed a mixture of excitement and emotion as they prepare for their final performances. The pressure is mounting as they face the culmination of weeks of intensive training and live performances that have captivated audiences throughout the series. The final comes after last week's dramatic dance-off, which saw presenter Anita Rani and her partner Gleb Savchenko eliminated from the competition. The judges unanimously voted to save Katie Derham and her partner Anton Du Beke, sending them through to the final and making Strictly history in the process. Katie Derham spoke about the significance of taking Anton to the final for the first time in his 12-year tenure on the show. Despite this achievement, she maintained a realistic perspective about their chances of winning. "I don't know if anybody has really thought about the trophy much," she said. She revealed that a friend had given her a miniature glitterball necklace with the message: "Even if you don't win you have your own little one already." EastEnders star Kellie Bright admitted to feeling "slightly more emotional" ahead of the final show but said she was focusing on the opportunity to relax afterwards. "I'm quite looking forward to not having any make-up on, or brushing my hair, or even getting out of my pyjamas for a few days," she confessed. She emphasized that winning wasn't her primary focus, saying: "Our whole thing has always been to try and entertain everybody, so that's what we want to do on Saturday." Former Coronation Street actress Georgia May Foote said she was "more excited than nervous," though she acknowledged the added pressure of the final, describing it as "everything you have learnt put together." In a surprising revelation, pop star Jay McGuiness announced he would not be repeating his memorable jive in the final, despite fan expectations. "I think the jive was so fun and I think everyone loved it. I'm more than happy with what that was [but] I'd rather do something that I think will surprise people," he explained. McGuiness also expressed his newfound passion for the show, saying: "I'm in love with the show, I think it's awesome." The final will consist of two live shows on Saturday. One couple will be eliminated at the beginning of the second show, with the remaining three finalists performing their favourite dance of the series before the winner is crowned. All professional dancers and celebrity participants will reunite for the spectacular finale, with several posting excited messages and rehearsal photos on social media. Strictly Come Dancing airs on BBC One at 18:35 GMT and 21:00 GMT.

Storm Collapses Circus Tent in New Hampshire, Injuring Spectators A violent storm with winds reaching up to 60mph struck a circus tent in Lancaster, New Hampshire, on Monday evening, injuring multiple people as a performance was just beginning. Approximately 100 spectators were inside the tent when the storm hit, causing the structure to collapse. Although a thunderstorm warning was in effect for the region, it remains unclear whether attendees were aware of the storm's severity before entering the venue. Eyewitness Heidi Medeiros, attending with her three-year-old son, described the terrifying moments as the tent went dark and screams erupted. "I see these very large metal poles that are in the ground and go through the top of the tent, I see them starting to come out of the ground and fly up, into the air toward us," she told WMUR-TV. Medeiros and her son escaped injury, though the flying poles came within feet of their seats. The injured were transported to local hospitals for treatment. The incident comes just one day after a similar tragedy in Illinois, where a music festival tent collapsed during a storm, killing one person and injuring more than a dozen others.

**Mel Giedroyc on Strictly Come Dancing: "I'd Want to Be Ann Widdecombe"** Television presenter Mel Giedroyc has revealed why she's hesitant about appearing on Strictly Come Dancing, despite being a devoted fan of the BBC show. "I love watching it so much I almost didn't want to spoil the pleasure by being on it," she told Radio Times. The 48-year-old said it was tricky for a woman her age to be on the show. "You're not the comedy old bag yet, which would be the joy of going on Strictly," she said. "If I did it, I'd want to be Ann Widdecombe. I'd want to be out there getting the laughs, being dragged around." The presenter may not have strutted her stuff in a ball gown, but she can still be seen on a prime time Saturday night show - fronting BBC One's talent search Let It Shine. The gig comes after Giedroyc stepped down as co-host of the Great British Bake Off, along with Sue Perkins, when it was announced the hit show was moving to Channel 4. Giedroyc said the furore surrounding the move was "a pretty weird time". "The press were camped out on my doorstep. My eldest daughter actually saw a few of them off, which I was very, very proud of," she said. "I'm not the kind of person who would court that sort of attention. I have a very private existence and I had to slightly clench my buttocks during that." Follow us on Facebook, on Twitter @BBCNewsEnts, or on Instagram at bbcnewsents. If you have a story suggestion email entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

Islamic State: Syria Regime Buying Oil from IS, Says US Islamic State's primary customer for oil has been the Syrian government of President Bashar al-Assad, despite the regime's fight against the militant group, a senior US Treasury official has revealed. Adam Szubin told the BBC that the two sides were engaged in millions of dollars of trade while simultaneously trying to destroy each other. He estimated that IS was making up to $40 million monthly from oil sales, including to buyers in Turkey. The group has also looted approximately $1 billion from banks in territories under its control, Mr Szubin added. The US-led coalition has been conducting airstrikes against IS targets in Syria and Iraq for over a year, recently killing the group's finance chief. A new military campaign called Tidal Wave 2 has intensified strikes on oil infrastructure, including fields, refineries, and tankers. Mr Szubin emphasised that disrupting IS's cash flow was crucial to the coalition's strategy. Unlike other terrorist organisations, IS doesn't depend on foreign donations but generates revenue from its own operations. According to UK defence consultancy IHS, IS currently earns around $80 million monthly, primarily from oil revenues. Additional income sources include taxation, smuggling of drugs and antiquities, robbery, kidnapping, and electricity sales. The revelation highlights the complex and controversial economic relationships in the Syrian conflict, where sworn enemies continue trading despite their military confrontation. Cutting these financial lifelines remains a key objective for coalition forces fighting the militant group.

Man Charged with Murder of Woman Found Dead in Neath Home A 43-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a woman found dead at a property in South Wales. Andrea Lewis, 51, was discovered at a home on Fairyland Road in Tonna, Neath, at approximately 08:00 GMT on 30 January. Rhys Trevor Anthony Hobbs, 43, from Tonna, appeared at Swansea Crown Court on Friday charged with her murder. He was remanded in custody until his next court appearance on 24 March. A second man, aged 46, who was also arrested in connection with Ms Lewis's death, has been released on police bail.

Creepy Clown Sightings Spread Across Six States, Alarming Communities A wave of unsettling clown sightings has swept across at least six U.S. states, with reports of mysterious figures dressed as clowns attempting to lure children and lurking in wooded areas, prompting police warnings and community concern. The most recent incident occurred in Georgia, where two young boys fled in terror while waiting for their school bus. "We saw a man with all black on, clown mask, and a red wig," 12-year-old Cameron Frails told WRDW News, describing their frightening encounter. In nearby Aiken County, South Carolina, police responded to an equally disturbing report captured on radio dispatch: "Subject dressed in a red and yellow suit with a clown mask through the woods. He also had a green laser light shining it through windows." The phenomenon has now spread to Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, California, Wisconsin, and Georgia, with children claiming the clowns have tried to lure them into the woods using money. "The clowning around needs to stop," declared Greenville, South Carolina Police Chief Ken Miller at a press conference earlier this month. "It's illegal, it's dangerous, it's inappropriate, it's creating community concern." Law enforcement officials have warned that even if these incidents are pranks, criminal charges may still be filed against perpetrators. New Jersey State Police addressed the trend on Facebook with a creepy clown photo, writing: "For all of the coulrophobics out there, we apologise for the pic, but it was necessary. If all of the bad people out there stuck out as much as a person dressed as a clown, we wouldn't have write posts like this." The sightings have distressed legitimate clown performers, who already contend with negative depictions like Stephen King's character Pennywise from "IT" and serial killer John Wayne Gacy, who performed as an amateur clown. At least one Georgia performer has begun informing police of his movements whenever in costume to avoid causing public alarm.

Italian City Government Dissolved Over Mafia Links In an unprecedented move, Italian authorities have dismissed the entire city government of a provincial capital over suspected ties to the notorious'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, Interior Minister Annamaria Cancellieri announced. Mayor Demetrio Arena and all 30 city councillors were removed from office to prevent "mafia contagion" within the local administration. This marks the first time an entire provincial capital government has been dissolved due to suspected mafia connections, though smaller municipalities have faced similar action previously. Three government-appointed commissioners will oversee city operations for 18 months until new elections can be held. The dramatic intervention follows months of concern about'Ndrangheta influence over the city council. An investigation was triggered after one councillor was arrested last year on charges of association with the criminal organization. According to experts, the'Ndrangheta has surpassed Sicily's Cosa Nostra to become one of the world's largest criminal enterprises. The organization generates vast revenues primarily through cocaine trafficking, extortion, and money laundering operations. Italy's parliamentary anti-mafia commission considers the'Ndrangheta the country's most dangerous and wealthiest mafia group. The syndicate has successfully expanded its influence beyond its Calabrian stronghold by exploiting migration patterns of southern Italians moving northward and abroad. The dissolution demonstrates Italian authorities' determination to combat organized crime's infiltration of democratic institutions.

West Brom Fans Organize Collection for Chris Brunt After Coin-Throwing Incident West Bromwich Albion supporters are rallying to show their appreciation for defender Chris Brunt following an incident in which he was struck by a coin thrown by one of the club's own fans. The incident occurred after Brunt had gone to give his shirt to a visiting fan after Albion lost 3-1 in the FA Cup fifth round at Championship side Reading on Saturday. A group of fans will hold collections outside The Hawthorns before Saturday's league game against Crystal Palace. "We want to show Albion fans are not all like that," said fan Debbie Green. Brunt, 31, said he was "disgusted" and "ashamed" after being struck on the face by a coin thrown by a West Brom supporter. "I was angry with the result but no way would you throw anything," Green, 54, who was at Reading and is helping to organise the collection, told BBC Sport. "After the game, Chris was the only one who walked up to the fans and clapped them. "I was about 25 feet away from what happened. Most were clapping him back and then you get this one idiot. "Chris had given his shirt to a little girl. He didn't deserve that to happen to him. "I have supported Albion for 50 years but I was ashamed to be an Albion fan on Saturday." Up to 30 Albion fans have come forward so far to hold buckets outside the ground and go into pubs near The Hawthorns. All money raised will go to a charity of the Northern Ireland international's choice, added Green. A West Brom spokesman said: "It's a fan-led initiative and we are trying to co-ordinate it. It's got the club's blessing and it's got Chris's blessing." West Brom will feature an image of long-serving Brunt on the front cover of Saturday's programme above the word'loyalty'. Brunt, who can also play in midfield, joined West Brom from Sheffield Wednesday in 2007 and has played 313 games for the club.

Nigeria Deploys Female Police to Displacement Camps After Abuse Allegations Nigerian authorities have deployed female police officers to camps housing people displaced by Boko Haram violence, following allegations of sexual abuse by security personnel. State police commissioner Damian Chukwu said the female officers will ensure the protection of women in the camps. The deployment comes after a Human Rights Watch (HRW) report last week alleged that several women had been sexually abused by security officers. The officers, drawn from various divisions, are also tasked to "dig out true happenings" in the camps, Mr Chukwu told the Nigerian News Agency. President Muhammadu Buhari said he was "worried" and "shocked" about the HRW report and ordered an investigation into the alleged abuses. The report detailed how women and girls had been coerced into sex and abandoned when they became pregnant. "It is disgraceful and outrageous that people who should protect these women and girls are attacking and abusing them," said HRW's Mausi Segun. The group blamed the vulnerability of women - many of whom are widows and unaccompanied orphans - on irregular supplies of food, clothing, medicine and other essentials in internally displaced camps in Borno state capital, Maiduguri. Boko Haram's seven-year battle to create an Islamic state has forced thousands from their homes.

Security Review Recommended for Stormont After Unauthorised Flag Incident A comprehensive security review of Parliament Buildings has been recommended by police following an incident in which unauthorised nationalist flags were flown from the Stormont estate. The tricolour and another nationalist flag appeared on flagpoles at the Belfast site earlier in June, with a republican group called the 1916 Societies claiming responsibility for hoisting them. DUP assembly member Paula Bradley, who serves on the assembly commission, raised concerns in the assembly on Tuesday about potential security breaches. She questioned whether police had assessed the risk to Parliament Buildings and asked what measures were being implemented to ensure the building's safety had not been compromised. In a written response on behalf of Chief Constable George Hamilton, a PSNI officer stated that whilst a full investigation into the incident is ongoing, police would recommend "a full review of internal security be undertaken under the auspices of the assembly commission". The letter also revealed that Chief Superintendent Nigel Grimshaw has requested an immediate, updated threat assessment relating to Parliament Buildings and will review the findings once received. An internal assembly investigation into the unauthorised flags was launched but subsequently suspended pending the outcome of the police inquiry. Assembly authorities have requested a report from contractors currently working on site, who are renovating sections of the roof and fourth floor. The assembly confirmed that the flags were removed immediately upon discovery. The incident has raised serious questions about security protocols at one of Northern Ireland's most significant political buildings.

Aston Villa Boss Remi Garde Apologises After Humiliating Liverpool Defeat Aston Villa manager Remi Garde has apologised to supporters following his side's humiliating 6-0 home defeat to Liverpool, admitting his team "did not fight enough" in their battle against relegation. The crushing loss marked the first time the Midlands club had conceded six goals at home in a league fixture since October 1983, deepening the crisis at Villa Park. The result leaves Villa rooted to the bottom of the Premier League, a seemingly insurmountable eight points from safety. "I feel humiliated. I am sorry for the fans who came to Villa Park," said Garde after the match. "This is a bad feeling that we did not fight enough." The manner of the defeat proved particularly concerning for the Frenchman. After conceding two goals before half-time, Villa capitulated spectacularly after the break, shipping four goals in just 13 minutes. The home supporters began streaming towards the exits during the second half, while those who remained directed their frustration at American owner Randy Lerner with chants of'Lerner out'. "Before the game you could expect the level of the two teams was not on the same one but, after quite a good 15 minutes, I don't know what happened," Garde explained. "The first two goals were difficult to digest and then my team did not play anymore. We were always two or three metres away from the opponent. It was very easy for them." The Villa boss expressed particular disappointment at his side's lack of fighting spirit given their precarious position. "I was expecting fighting spirit, especially in the position we are in, but we were not able to deliver it." Despite the demoralising defeat, Garde refused to concede that relegation is inevitable. The former Lyon manager, appointed in November on a three-and-a-half-year contract, insisted he would maintain belief whilst any mathematical hope remains. "I was not expecting this kind of match and we have to go for the next one to win it," he said. "Until we have little hope, I will be the one who will still believe. After a game like this, it is very difficult but we won't play Liverpool every weekend." Garde also addressed the supporters' frustrations, acknowledging the difficult situation at the club. "I understand [the fans' frustration]. I don't know exactly who let down who in this football club. I am trying to concentrate on my job and try to do the best with the players who want to still fight." BBC Radio 5 live's Pat Murphy was scathing in his assessment, describing Villa as "an absolute shambles" and questioning what incentive Garde has to remain at the club given the lack of investment and the scale of the challenge facing him.

JCB Chairman Pledges £100,000 to Save Wedgwood Museum Collection JCB chairman Sir Anthony Bamford has donated £100,000 towards the appeal to save the historic Wedgwood Museum collection, citing the company's "deep roots and long links with manufacturing in Staffordshire". The Art Fund announced it has raised more than £2.3m following an "extraordinary tide" of recent donations. The organisation needs £2.74m by 30 November to purchase the collection before administrators sell it to the highest bidder. The collection is being sold to help pay off part of the ceramics firm's pension bill, inherited by the museum after Waterford Wedgwood Plc's collapse in 2009. The museum houses more than 80,000 historical pieces, works of art, photographs and archival material spanning Wedgwood's 250-year history, valued at £15m. Art Fund director Stephen Deuchar praised the "exceptional" public support, which complements a £13m pledge from the Heritage Lottery Fund. JCB's donation, made through the Bamford Charitable Foundation, has been match-funded by a private charitable trust, contributing £200,000 to the appeal. Approximately 8,000 former workers received payments from the Pension Protection Fund, and in 2011, a judge authorised the collection's sale to repay the remaining debt.

Derbyshire Pub Dazzles with 53 Christmas Trees A Victorian-era pub in Ripley, Derbyshire, has transformed into a festive wonderland with an impressive display of 53 Christmas trees adorning its premises. The Angel pub, aptly named for the season, features trees of varying sizes, with the showstopper being a 22-foot (6.7-meter) specimen that cost owner Peter Clay over £1,000, including decorations. Adding to the spectacle is a permanent 9-foot (2.7-meter) golden angel positioned above the entrance, which has an unusual claim to fame – it previously graced the set of soap opera Crossroads. Clay explained the tradition began three years ago during difficult economic times. "It started back in the middle of the recession. Everyone was depressed and saying it's doom and gloom," he said. "I'm a partly-sunny guy, not a partly-cloudy guy, so we thought we would do something to cheer everybody up." The display has grown more elaborate each year, with customers invited to participate by hanging baubles on the trees. The distinctive building, constructed in 1888 for Queen Victoria's jubilee, is often mistaken for a chapel due to its architectural style.

Welsh Government Takes "Formal Management Action" Over Failed Furniture Contract Legal proceedings were brought by Triumph Furniture after it challenged a contract awarded to a rival competitor in a procurement dispute. Top civil servant Sir Derek Jones has announced that "formal management action" has begun in relation to staff members involved in the controversial contract process. The contract in question was for furniture, fittings, planning and interior design services for three public bodies: the Welsh Government, the National Assembly, and the Higher Education Funding Council for Wales. Sir Derek, the Welsh Government's permanent secretary, made his comments in a letter to the assembly's Public Accounts Committee. In the letter, he acknowledged the failings "centre around poor information management and a lack of oversight which, ultimately, weakened the position of the Welsh Government not only in terms of public perception of the robustness and transparency of the procurement process, but at the point where the Welsh Government was required to defend itself in subsequent litigation proceedings". However, he stressed that "there is no evidence that anyone received personal gain from the procurement process". The Welsh Government was alleged by Triumph Furniture to have breached EU procurement rules. Sir Derek previously told Assembly Members that compensation was paid following an arbitration process.

Keith Pelley has been named as the new chief executive of the European Tour, replacing George O'Grady who has held the position for over a decade. The 51-year-old, president of Rogers Media in Canada for the last five years, will start his role this summer. An "honoured" Pelley said he wanted to ensure golf remained at the "forefront of the game" across the world. O'Grady, 65, had been chief executive of the Tour, which runs the three leading men's professional golf circuits in Europe, since 2005. David Williams, chairman of the European Tour, said: "Throughout the interview process, it was clear Keith has an unwavering passion for golf, as well as a strong grasp of the challenges and opportunities facing not only the European Tour, but the wider game of golf as a whole." O'Grady, who will now take up a presidential role to represent the Tour through the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro, said he would ensure a smooth transition. "I am certain Keith will bring a fresh and business-focused perspective to the Tour," he added.

Rome Faces Drastic Water Rationing as Drought Crisis Deepens Parts of Italy, including the Lazio region surrounding Rome, are grappling with a severe drought that has prompted emergency measures. Acea, the water utility serving the capital, has proposed implementing eight-hour daily water cuts that would affect approximately 1.5 million Rome residents. The water company blames regional officials for preventing it from extracting supplies from Lake Bracciano, a nearby water source. Lazio authorities defended their decision, stating that lake levels have dropped dangerously low due to the ongoing drought, raising fears of an environmental catastrophe. Health Minister Beatrice Lorenzin warned of serious consequences, stating: "An eventual suspension of the supply of water in Rome could seriously compromise the level of hygiene of all the accommodation structures, restaurants and public offices. But above all, it could seriously compromise the provision of essential health services." While Acea maintains it has no alternative but to introduce rationing, both the water company and regional authorities have committed to continuing negotiations for a solution. Italy is experiencing its third-driest spring in six decades, with two-thirds of farmland affected and agricultural losses estimated at €2 billion ($2.3 billion). Rome has endured two consecutive years of below-average rainfall. The crisis has even reached the Vatican, which began shutting off its famous fountains on Tuesday as a conservation measure.

Former Leeds Lord Mayor Neil Taggart Jailed for Child Sex Offences A former Lord Mayor of Leeds has been jailed after admitting to a series of child sex offences that spanned six years. Neil Taggart, 65, of Marlowe Court, Garforth, appeared at Leeds Crown Court where a judge declared his once high-standing reputation in the community now "lay in the gutter". He pleaded guilty in June to eight child sex offences committed between 2010 and 2016. Taggart served as Leeds Lord Mayor in 2003 and was a Labour councillor for more than 30 years. He also held the position of West Yorkshire Police Authority chairman before being deselected by the Labour Party in October 2013 ahead of the 2014 election. The former councillor was suspended by the party in October when allegations emerged and was subsequently dismissed after admitting to the offences. A spokesman for the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (NSPCC) described Taggart as "just one of the growing number of offenders caught using the internet to access child abuse images." "Every child in his sickening catalogue of images has suffered abuse in the real world," the spokesman said, calling for technology companies, government and law enforcement to commit resources to prevent such material being published. Detective Superintendent Pat Twiggs of West Yorkshire Police condemned Taggart's actions, stating: "Offenders like Taggart, who seek out and distribute abusive images of children for the sexual gratification of themselves and others, play a significant role in the continuation of the appalling real-life abuse that these images capture." Police confirmed the crimes involved a high volume of images, many of the most serious kind, accumulated over a significant period.

Aberdeen FC Pushes Forward with Controversial Kingsford Stadium Plans Aberdeen Football Club is pressing ahead with plans to build a new 20,000-capacity stadium and training facilities at Kingsford, near Westhill, close to the Aberdeen bypass. The club insists the relocation is essential for securing a sustainable future, following years of planning difficulties with a previous proposal at Loirston, south of Aberdeen. However, the development has sparked significant local opposition. The Say No To Kingsford Stadium campaign group is distributing information packs to residents, continuing their protest despite reporting online abuse last year. Aberdeen FC condemned any such harassment of campaigners. Club chairman Stewart Milne has defended the choice, calling Kingsford "an ideal location for supporters." The contentious project highlights the tension between the club's ambitions for modernisation and community concerns about the development's impact on the area.

Irish Director of Rugby Kennedy Eyes Premiership Challenge London Irish director of rugby Brian Kennedy is preparing his side for their return to the Premiership, starting with a season opener against Harlequins at Twickenham. The Exiles secured promotion from the Championship at the first attempt and are ready to face the challenges of top-flight rugby. "We're happy to be back, but we know it's a huge, huge challenge ahead of us," Kennedy told BBC Sport. Irish face a demanding opening month, with a trip to defending champions Exeter following the Harlequins match, plus Friday-night fixtures at Sale and Newcastle. "Every game's difficult," Kennedy acknowledged. "We won't think about them individually until they come around." Despite the tough schedule, Kennedy is delighted to be back in the Premiership. "We all love the Premiership. It's a league we thoroughly enjoy being in as a club," he said. "We missed it and we did enjoy our time in the Championship, we felt we learnt a lot and built a lot of strong foundations down there. But, this is ultimately where we want to be." Irish's squad will be strengthened by new signings including Samoa lock Teofilo Paulo and Fiji winger Napolioni Nalaga, who join for pre-season training. "They're going to add experience, strength in depth and we're going to get competition for a few places now," Kennedy added.

Hezbollah Vows Revenge After Samir Qantar Killed in Damascus Strike Hezbollah has vowed that Israel will "pay the price" for the death of Samir Qantar, a former prisoner and senior operative killed in an alleged Israeli air strike in Damascus. Speaking at Qantar's funeral in Beirut on Monday, Hezbollah executive council chief Hashem Safieddine issued a stark warning to Israel, declaring that the militant group would avenge the killing. Israel has welcomed Qantar's death but has not officially confirmed responsibility for the strike. Qantar, who spent almost 30 years in Israeli prison for murder before being released in a 2008 prisoner exchange with Hezbollah, was killed along with eight others when missiles fired by Israeli jets reportedly hit a residential building in Damascus's Jaramana district on Saturday night, according to Hezbollah sources. Thousands of mourners filled the streets of Ghobeiry, a southern Beirut suburb, on Monday, carrying Qantar's coffin draped in Hezbollah's distinctive yellow flag. Chants of "Death to Israel" echoed through the crowd as supporters paid their respects to the controversial figure. In his funeral address, Mr Safieddine delivered a defiant message to Israel. "If the Israelis imagine that by targeting Samir Qantar they have closed an account, they are very wrong because they know and will know that they have opened accounts that are not closed with a treacherous missile," he declared. Israeli cabinet minister Yuval Steinitz responded on Sunday by saying he was not sorry about Qantar's death, though he declined to comment on allegations of Israeli involvement in the strike. Qantar, a Lebanese Druze, was just 16 years old when he participated in a deadly 1979 attack in the Israeli coastal town of Nahariya alongside three other members of the Palestine Liberation Front. The raid resulted in the deaths of two policemen, a civilian man, and his four-year-old daughter. Tragically, a two-year-old girl also died when her mother accidentally smothered her while trying to keep her quiet as they hid in a cupboard. Nearly three decades later, Hezbollah secured Qantar's release in exchange for the bodies of two Israeli soldiers captured in 2006. Upon his return to Lebanon, he is believed to have joined Hezbollah's armed wing. While Hezbollah has not publicly disclosed Qantar's role in Syria, where thousands of its fighters support government forces, his brother wrote in the Lebanese newspaper al-Akhbar that Qantar had been involved in "resistance" activities against Israel's occupation of the Syrian Golan Heights since his release. He claimed Israel had attempted to assassinate him six times previously. The United States identified Qantar as one of Hezbollah's "most visible and popular spokesmen" who had "played an operational role, with the assistance of Iran and Syria, in building up Hezbollah's terrorist infrastructure in the Golan Heights." Israel has conducted several air strikes inside Syria since 2011. In January, a suspected Israeli strike in the Syrian Golan Heights killed six Hezbollah fighters, including the son of the group's late military chief Imad Mughniyeh, and an Iranian Revolutionary Guards general.

**Burton Albion Sign Leeds Midfielder on Permanent Deal** Burton Albion have completed the permanent signing of the 27-year-old midfielder who impressed during his loan spell last season. The Crewe academy graduate initially joined Albion in January, making 19 appearances and scoring once as the club secured their survival. Since joining Leeds in 2013, he has amassed over 100 appearances for the Yorkshire club. Manager Nigel Clough praised his new signing: "He's quiet and unassuming, he's maturing into his role, knows what he's good at, knows his limitations and plays accordingly."

Australia batter Meg Lanning has withdrawn from the inaugural Women's Cricket Super League due to injury concerns. The 24-year-old was scheduled to represent Surrey Stars but will instead remain in Australia to focus on her rehabilitation programme. "The tournament concept and growth of women's cricket across the globe is fantastic and I would have loved to have taken part," Lanning said. The Super League, featuring six teams competing in 15 Twenty20 matches in a round-robin format, begins on 30 July. Lanning's withdrawal follows England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor's decision not to play for Lancashire Thunder this year, as she takes an indefinite break from cricket to address anxiety issues.

Swansea Council Leader David Phillips Steps Down After Decade in Charge David Phillips has announced his resignation as leader of Swansea Council after 10 years at the helm of the Labour group. Mr Phillips said the decision was made to focus on building Swansea's regional and national profile, although details of his new role are not yet known. It comes a week after he was told to expect a leadership challenge after sacking two cabinet members in a reshuffle, but he would not comment on whether his departure was linked. The Labour group has been in power at the authority for the last two years. The selection process to find a new leader begins on Monday. Speaking about his decision, Mr Phillips said from the back benches he will continue to give his "complete support to the new cabinet and the group as we work to continue to deliver on our manifesto commitments for the good of the people of Swansea and the wider region". Labour group chairman Robert Francis Davies praised the outgoing leader, saying: "David Phillips has made an enormous contribution to Swansea and to Labour and will continue to do so in the future. We want to keep his talents working for our city."

Climber Dies from Natural Causes on Snowdonia Mountain A 52-year-old man from Nottingham has died from natural causes while climbing in Snowdonia. Neil Parnell fell from Bristley Ridge, between Tryfan and Glyder Fach, at approximately 15:00 GMT on Saturday. His body was airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd, where he was pronounced dead. A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from natural causes, and no inquest will be held.

Essex Cruise to Victory as Westley and Pettini Dominate Warwickshire Essex secured a comprehensive victory over Warwickshire in their One-Day Cup encounter, with Tom Westley and Mark Pettini delivering match-winning performances at Chelmsford. The pair put on 191 for the first wicket before Westley was trapped lbw by spinner Jeetan Patel for 108. Pettini struck 126, with 10 fours and two sixes, as Essex piled up 320-5. Warwickshire and former England batsman Jonathan Trott made 51, but he was removed by Westley (2-26) as the visitors were bowled out for 168. Left-armer Reece Topley also shone with the ball for the hosts claiming 4-29. Essex now top the early Group B table with two wins and a no result, while Warwickshire are bottom with two defeats and a washed out game. Essex opener Tom Westley reflected: "I wouldn't say it was a difficult wicket but we had to work hard for the runs so to put on 191 with Mark for the first wicket was very rewarding. That set the platform for others to come in and finish the job off." Warwickshire director of cricket Dougie Brown admitted: "Essex played very well but was still a disappointing result, more so because we failed to reach the standards we set ourselves."

**FA Cup Third Round: Team News and Fourth Round Draw** Ashley Eastham stands ready to deputise for Pond should fitness concerns prevent his participation, with new signing Joe Maguire poised for a potential debut following his transfer from Liverpool. Bristol City's defensive options improve as Hordur Magnusson nears recovery from hamstring problems. Midfielders Gary O'Neil and Callum O'Dowda are also pushing for returns to the starting lineup. However, the Robins remain without Korey Smith and Adam Matthews, sidelined with hamstring and calf injuries respectively. The victors will face either Burnley or Sunderland away in the fourth round, with both Premier League sides awaiting their own third-round outcome.

Wolves striker Nouha Dicko faces extended layoff after minor knee surgery Wolverhampton Wanderers striker Nouha Dicko will miss an additional three weeks of training after undergoing minor knee surgery, further delaying his return from a serious injury that has sidelined him for nearly an entire season. The France-born 24-year-old has been absent for almost the whole of the 2015-16 campaign after suffering an injury during Wolves' 2-1 home victory over Charlton in late August. The Championship club initially ruled Dicko out for nine months, but the recent surgical procedure will extend his rehabilitation period. Wolves had originally hoped the striker would be fit to start the new season, which begins with a trip to his former club Rotherham United on 6 August. However, those plans now appear in jeopardy following the latest setback. Wolves head of medical Phil Hayward explained the situation to the Express & Star: "He's undergone some minor surgery to have a staple taken from his knee. It's a very small, minor procedure. It's quite common with surgery. Probably half of people who have surgery have the staple taken out." Hayward emphasised the decision was made strategically: "We thought it best to do it now rather than delay it and potentially do it during the season. It'll be a case of easing him back in August. It's not a big issue." He added: "If he's going to be out for a few weeks we're better off doing it now and missing a bit of pre-season, rather than in September or October and missing four or five games." The news comes amid ongoing uncertainty about the club's ownership. Wolves could be in new hands by the start of next season, as talks progress to end Steve Morgan's ownership of the club. More than one interested party is currently in discussions with Morgan, who put Wolves up for sale last September. Sources indicate talks are proceeding constructively, with the club finishing 14th in the Championship and Morgan reportedly reluctant to spend additional money on new players. Wolves, along with West Midlands neighbours Aston Villa and West Bromwich Albion, have been the subject of reported Chinese ownership interest. The asking price is understood to be in the region of £50m. Morgan would take a substantial financial hit on the deal, having invested £30m initially and approximately another £75m on new players, upgrading the training facility to Category 1 Academy status and developing a new stand at Molineux. The club owns the Molineux stadium and all assets, leasing the ground from the council on a 999-year lease at a peppercorn rent, which should make any potential sale relatively straightforward once agreement is reached.

Wrexham vice-captain Michael Carrington has signed a new one-year contract with the National League club. The 29-year-old former Crewe and Bury player joined Wrexham in September 2013 and has been a key figure for the Welsh side. Manager Dean Keates confirmed the club has also reached an agreement with midfielder Paul Rutherford for next season. Keates revealed negotiations continue with top-scorer John Rooney, who scored twice as a substitute in Saturday's 3-1 victory over Guiseley. Rooney is just one start away from automatically triggering a new contract clause.

Welsh Boxing Champion Rachael Buckland Awakes from Coma Ahead of Schedule A Welsh boxing champion is showing remarkable signs of recovery after awakening from an induced coma two months earlier than doctors expected. Rachael Buckland, 25, suffered life-threatening injuries in October when she fell at her Cardiff home, fracturing her skull and causing a bleed on the brain. The mother of two, who is married to Celtic boxing champion Mitchell Buckland, required emergency surgery at Cardiff's University Hospital of Wales. During the operation, surgeons removed a piece of bone and a damaged section of her brain. Medical professionals initially predicted she would remain in a coma until the new year. However, her former coach Tony Borg announced the encouraging news that Mrs Buckland is now awake and able to recognise people around her. "This is a really positive sign and we are naturally delighted," he said. "She's definitely showing that fighting spirit." The former bantamweight champion, originally from Magor in Monmouthshire, still faces a lengthy recovery journey. Mr Borg, who also coaches Welsh world featherweight boxing champion Lee Selby, emphasized that whilst progress is encouraging, there remains considerable work ahead. The boxing community has rallied around the family, with friends organizing fundraising events. So far, approximately £6,500 has been raised to support Mrs Buckland's family during this difficult time. She works as a chef at a Newport pub when not training.

Rare 1962 Beatles Acetate Disc Sells for Record Price at Auction A rare 10-inch acetate disc featuring early Beatles recordings has sold for an undisclosed sum at a Warrington auction, with Omega Auctions expressing they were "nicely surprised" by the final price paid by a Manchester collector. The 78 RPM record, dating from 1962, contains recordings of "Till There Was You" and "Hello Little Girl" and has been described by Beatles historian Mark Lewisohn as "a Holy Grail item" and one of the "rarest and most collectable of all Beatles records." The disc was cut at the HMV store in Oxford Street, London, before the Beatles achieved national chart success. It bears handwriting from the band's manager, Brian Epstein, though contains notable misspellings – labelling the tracks as "'Til There Was You" and "Hullo Little Girl." The recordings were credited to "Paul McCartney & The Beatles" and "John Lennon & The Beatles" respectively. Created as part of Epstein's effort to secure a recording contract, the acetate was presented to George Martin, who would later become the Beatles' producer, at EMI record label. Martin, who died in March 2016, eventually returned the disc to Epstein. The record's owner, Les Maguire, 74, was keyboardist for fellow Liverpool band Gerry and the Pacemakers. He received the disc as a gift from Epstein in 1963 and stored it in his Formby loft for over 50 years, wrapped in paper. Maguire called it "a special piece" but decided to sell, giving the proceeds to his granddaughter to help purchase a house after completing her accountancy exams. "It's no good to me," he explained. The sale represents a significant moment in Beatles memorabilia collecting history.

Swan Shot with Pellet Gun Had to Be Put Down A swan discovered with severe injuries at Monks Pond, between Glasbury and Painscastle in Hay-on-Wye, has been put down after veterinary examination. The bird was found by a member of the public at approximately 11:00 GMT on Wednesday and immediately taken to veterinary care. However, the extent of its injuries was so severe that the swan had to be euthanized. Dyfed-Powys Police have confirmed the swan was shot with a pellet gun. Sergeant Craig Morgan condemned the incident as "absolutely appalling." Officers in Hay-on-Wye are conducting enquiries into the attack. Sgt Morgan has urged anyone with information about those responsible to come forward immediately.

Wrexham Captain Corry Evans Among Nine Players Released Wrexham have announced that captain Corry Evans will leave the club along with eight other players following the end of the season. Evans, 21, was appointed captain in November and has made over 100 appearances for his hometown club. Iffy Allen, Khaellem Bailey-Nichols, Anthony Barry, Shwan Jalal, Izale McLeod, Callum Powell, Martin Riley, and Jordan White will also depart the Racecourse Ground. Additionally, Curtis Tilt, Hamza Bencherif, and John Rooney have all requested transfers after spending time on loan elsewhere this season. Tilt joined Forest Green Rovers, Bencherif linked up with former manager Gary Mills at York City, while Rooney moved to Guiseley. "To the players leaving, we offer our thanks for their service this season and in previous years. We hope all are quickly fixed up with new clubs and that our paths cross again," the club said in a statement. The Dragons are hoping to extend defender James Jennings' stay after his loan from Cheltenham Town.

Young Zambian Footballer Vows to Return After Tragic Accident **Chingola, Zambia** - While his teammates competed in the Africa Cup of Nations in Equatorial Guinea, promising young Zambian midfielder Changwe Kalale lay in a hospital bed, battling injuries that doctors say may end his football career before it truly began. The 17-year-old was involved in a devastating road accident on December 14 while traveling to Lusaka to join Zambia's pre-Nations Cup training camp. Kalale, along with teammates Nyambe Mulenga and Satchmo Chakawa, was a passenger in a minibus that collided head-on with another vehicle. The accident claimed four lives and left eight others injured, with Kalale suffering the most severe consequences. A spinal injury has left him with limited movement from the waist down, and medical professionals have delivered a crushing prognosis: he may never walk again, let alone play professional football. Despite the grim outlook, Kalale remains defiant and determined. Speaking exclusively to BBC Sport from his bed at Nchanga South Hospital in Chingola, the young midfielder refused to accept that his career is over. "I can't give up on football just because of that accident," Kalale said. "After the accident, I wasn't able to move. All I could do is sleep on the bed. But I'll be back, I know I will play football again. It's a matter of time." The timing of the accident was particularly cruel for the talented teenager, who was on the verge of potentially representing his country at a major tournament. Having earned his first senior international cap in a friendly against Ivory Coast in October, Kalale was widely regarded as one of Zambia's brightest young prospects. "It has been a very painful experience for me especially because my career was on the rise," he reflected. "I'm sure I'd have played at the Africa Cup of Nations but the accident ruined all my plans." The incident has reignited discussions about the welfare of players injured while on national duty. Although the Football Association of Zambia has acknowledged the situation, they have indicated limited capacity to provide comprehensive support. However, Kalale's father, Bernard, has refused to assign blame for the tragedy. "I have three sons who play football and what happened to Changwe cannot make me tell them to stop playing football - it was an accident and it could have happened to anyone," he said. Bernard added that the family draws strength from their son's survival. "There was a period when my son was critical and we never thought he would come back to life in the manner he has. As a family, we are really grateful for all the support we are receiving and we take a lot of courage and confidence that our son will play football again." Kalale now faces months of intensive physiotherapy and rehabilitation, motivated by the realization that he "could be dead or completely paralysed." His determination to return to the sport he loves serves as an inspiration to many who face similar challenges.

Friends of Snibston Group Seeks Judicial Review Over Museum Closure A group campaigning to save Snibston Discovery Museum has applied for a judicial review of Leicestershire County Council's decision to close the attraction. The county council decided in January to replace the Snibston Discovery Museum with a smaller attraction to save money. A plan by the Friends of Snibston to run the current museum as a charitable trust was dismissed by the authority. The council said it followed proper processes. The group intends to take legal action on grounds including the council's consultation on the museum's future being "flawed". Brian Vollar, chair of Friends of Snibston, said: "We think we have a strong case, else we wouldn't have proceeded along with this plan. We have given plenty of indication of our intention to follow this plan and plenty of opportunity for the council to be more accommodating in following the people's wishes and not going ahead with the decision to close." He said they would be informed in six weeks whether permission will be given for a review. A spokesman for Leicestershire County Council said: "The council maintains that proper processes were followed to arrive at the conclusions reached by the cabinet. We will study the application in detail and assess the implications for the council." Snibston Discovery Museum is focused on industry and design but also has a theatre and large country park.

Cavendish to Support Boasson Hagen in Paris-Roubaix Return Mark Cavendish will make his return to Paris-Roubaix on Sunday, riding in support of Norwegian teammate Edvald Boasson Hagen in cycling's grueling one-day classic. The Manxman has attempted the'Queen of the Classics' only once, when he failed to finish in 2011. The sprinter, 30, said: "I hope to get a bit deeper into the race than last time and help Edvald later on." Cavendish has won 26 Tour de France stages and the Milan-San Remo'monument' in 2009. However, the 257.5km route across northern France, nicknamed the'Hell of the North', is famous for its cobbled sections that don't suit the British sprinter's strengths. Switzerland's Fabian Cancellara, who won Paris-Roubaix in 2006, 2010 and 2013, and Slovakian world champion Peter Sagan - winner of the Tour of Flanders last Sunday - are the favourites. Defending champion John Degenkolb, from Germany, is absent as he continues his recovery after being hit by a car while training in Spain in January. Britain's Luke Rowe, who finished fifth in the Tour of Flanders, and Ian Stannard will lead Team Sky's challenge. The 2011 world champion Cavendish said: "We've come to Roubaix and we've got no pressure. We're not the big favourites but definitely we can be in the mix at the end." Cavendish, who won the Tour of Qatar for the second time in February, is focusing on this year's Tour de France and the Rio Olympics.

Teenager Leah Kerry Dies After Taking New Psychoactive Substances A 15-year-old schoolgirl from Salisbury has died after taking new psychoactive substances (NPS), prompting her family to issue an urgent warning about the dangers of so-called "legal highs." Leah Kerry was found unconscious at an address in Newton Abbot, Devon, and died in hospital on 16 July. Her family described her as "a courageous and confident young woman" who was aware of the risks but "thought she was invincible." In a heartfelt statement released through Devon and Cornwall Police, the family said: "Leah lit up any room she walked into with her incredible personality, sense of humour, striking looks and demeanour. Those who know her will ache to hear the words'You allriiight' one last time." The family emphasized that despite knowing the dangers of drugs, Leah believed she was invulnerable. "Sadly, despite being well aware of the risks, she thought she was invincible and she rolled the dice and has paid the ultimate price," they said. Her relatives are calling on the government to prioritize the dangers of psychoactive substances following the 2017 Drugs Strategy, urging other young people to avoid dangerous NPS tablets. Jacob Khanlarian, 20, from Newton Abbot, has been charged with intent to supply drugs in connection with the incident and will appear before Exeter Crown Court on 10 August.

Mysterious Foam on Welsh Beaches Identified as Harmless Algae Natural Resources Wales has confirmed that mysterious foam appearing on several Pembrokeshire beaches is naturally occurring algae, not pollution. The algae species, Phaeocystis and Chaetocerus, commonly deceive beachgoers due to their oily appearance and seaweed-like odour. Thriving in warm weather conditions, the algae has been identified at Barafundle, Cwm-yr-Eglwys, Freshwater East, Lydstep, Newgale, and Tenby beaches. Officials anticipate additional sightings as temperatures remain elevated throughout the region.

Coldplay's New Album Misses Top Spot Despite Strong Sales Coldplay's latest album "A Head Full Of Dreams" has become the band's first studio album not to debut at number one in the UK charts, despite impressive sales of 236,000 copies in its opening week. The British rock band's previous releases had consistently topped the charts, with 2014's "Ghost Stories" debuting with 168,000 sales and 2011's "Mylo Xyloto" selling 208,000 copies in its first week. Adele maintained her stranglehold on the number one position, with her album "25" shifting another 354,000 copies. Elvis Presley's "If I Can Dream" held at three, while Justin Bieber's "Purpose" sat at four. Jess Glynne's "I Cry When I Laugh" logged its 16th consecutive week in the top 10 at number five.
