X Factor runner-up Fleur East made her chart debut, with "Love, Sax and Flashbacks" entering at 14. In the singles chart, Bieber secured a second consecutive week at number one with "Love Yourself," having replaced his own song the previous week. Sigala's "Sweet Lovin'" was the highest new entry at three, while Adele's "Hello" held fourth place. The festive season influenced both charts, with Mariah Carey's "All I Want For Christmas Is You" climbing to 13, The Pogues' "Fairytale Of New York" at 20, and Wham's "Last Christmas" reaching 27.

From Reality TV to Hampshire: Ian Holland's Unique Journey to County Cricket Ian Holland's path to professional cricket with Hampshire reads like something from a screenplay, beginning with an Australian reality television show and culminating in a promising county cricket career in England. The 26-year-old all-rounder, born in the United States but holding a British passport through his English father, credits former Australian Test captain Allan Border for launching his professional career. In 2012, Holland won Cricket Superstar, a Foxtel television series that saw him triumph over 14 other finalists selected through national trials. "It was one of those unique opportunities that popped up," Holland told BBC Radio Solent. "I went into it without any expectations and came out with an opportunity. It was a chance to fast-track myself at that point of my career and it got me a foot in the door of the Australian system." The prize was a rookie contract with Victoria, Australia's state side. The show featured Border as chief judge, with former wicket-keeper Graham Manou as mentor and guest appearances from cricket legends Matthew Hayden and Ricky Ponting. "It was a strange experience watching yourself back on television," Holland admitted. "There were a few challenges that looked good on camera, but it was Allan Border's involvement that gave it the credibility for me." However, despite his television success, opportunities at Victoria proved limited. Holland eventually looked to the Northern Hemisphere, spending two years playing for Fleetwood Cricket Club in the Northern League before his Hampshire connection materialised. "Dimitri Mascarenhas is the connection to Hampshire from the time he moved back to Melbourne," explained the right-hand batsman and medium-pace bowler. "I played some second-team cricket here last season and then the first XI chances have come this year." Holland's impressive figures of 4-16 and 2-23 against Somerset in the County Championship this week have built on earlier limited-overs and four-day appearances this campaign. "It's been a really great transition for me," Holland revealed. "I'm really enjoying my cricket here and it's just a great place to play. My goal is to play here for the rest of my career." Ian Holland was talking to BBC Radio Solent's Kevan James.

Brothers Jailed for Grooming and Sexually Assaulting Nine Teenage Girls Two brothers who exploited their positions working in convenience stores to groom and sexually assault nine vulnerable teenage girls have been jailed for a combined total of 41 years. Ilvarasan Rajenthiram, 26, of Wallasey Village, Wirral, was sentenced to 22 and a half years in prison, while his brother Vinothan Rajenthiram, 27, of Wigan, received 18 and a half years. The pair were found guilty of a total of 30 charges spanning more than five years. Sentencing them at Liverpool Crown Court, Judge Norman Wright said "both abused their position in the shops to target teenage girls". The grooming happened at convenience stores the brothers worked in at Birkenhead, Walton and Garston between 2010 and January 2016. ## Pattern of Grooming Judge Wright said they gave the 14 and 15-year-old girls free sweets and mobile phone top-ups, as well as serving them cigarettes, "to win their trust and confidence". The pair, known to victims as Ara and Vino, then invited them to go for drives, listen to music and "chill out". "The final step was to take them back to unoccupied flats and ply them with alcohol," the judge said. Judge Wright added that it was all about the brothers' "sexual gratification". Detective Superintendent Dave Brunskill described the pair as "calculating sexual predators who went to extraordinary lengths to groom their victims". He said: "In most cases, they gained the trust of the young girls then took the relationship further by coercing the girls to take part in sexual activity after plying them with alcohol. "Victims mistakenly believed that these men genuinely had feelings for them and they didn't realise that they were being groomed and sexually exploited." ## Impact on Victims In a statement to court, one of the victims said the experience had "ruined my life". She said she "trusted him to be a good person" and thought they had "something special". "I had not done anything wrong," she said. "I was just a vulnerable, naive child who should have been safe in his company." The mother of another victim said their sentences "will never justify the damage they have caused my daughter and all the others involved". "The fact that those men pleaded not guilty sickened me and proves that they feel no guilt, shame or remorse. They have no conscience in my eyes," she added. Ilvarasan was found guilty of 15 counts of sexual activity with a child, three counts of sexual assault and two counts of perverting the course of justice. Vinothan was convicted of four counts of sexual assault, one rape, four counts of sexual activity with a child and one count of perverting the course of justice. The pair were ordered to sign the Sex Offenders Register for life.

County Antrim Shield: Linfield Thrash Cliftonville 3-0 as Holders Ballymena Crash Out Linfield eased into the next round of the County Antrim Shield with a commanding 3-0 victory over Cliftonville at Windsor Park on Tuesday night. Matthew Clarke, Ross Gaynor and Andrew Waterworth were on target for the Blues, while their north Belfast rivals finished the match with 10 men following Caoimhin Bonner's dismissal. At Windsor Park, Cliftonville defender Bonner blocked early efforts by Mark Haughey and Waterworth, but clear-cut chances were at a premium in the opening stages. The breakthrough came on 41 minutes when hesitation by Tomas Cosgrove allowed Clarke to strike Linfield ahead. The hosts doubled their advantage on 61 minutes through fortunate circumstances when Aaron Donnelly's misdirected ball across his own penalty area gifted Gaynor an easy finish. Waterworth completed the scoring with a header 10 minutes from time as Cliftonville offered little attacking threat throughout. A miserable evening for the Reds was compounded when Bonner received his marching orders after collecting a second yellow card for a late challenge on Waterworth. **Ballymena Dumped Out by Ards** On a night when holders Ballymena United were beaten 2-1 at home by Ards, Joe McKinney emerged as the hero for the visitors at the Showgrounds. After their 5-0 Premiership hammering by Glenavon on Saturday, Ballymena suffered another disappointment as McKinney's two goals sealed a deserved success for the north Down club. McKinney had already tested home keeper Ross Glendinning early on before firing Ards ahead in the 28th minute. As Ballymena rarely threatened, a mix-up between keeper Glendinning and Caolan Loughran allowed McKinney to double the lead after the break. Ards held on despite Allan Jenkins' 89th-minute reply. **Crusaders Edge Glentoran in Extra-Time** Extra-time goals from David Cushley and Brandon Doyle helped Crusaders see off Glentoran 2-1 at the Oval. Cushley half-volleyed the Crues ahead in the fourth minute of extra-time, and after Ciaran Caldwell hit the underside of the crossbar, Doyle struck the visitors' second after being set up by Cushley. Steven Gordon replied in the final minute of extra-time. Elsewhere, PSNI beat Albert Foundry 3-0 at Seaview.

Wales Focus on Moldova Despite Hull City's Interest in Coleman The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has firmly rejected Hull City's approach to speak with manager Chris Coleman, as the national team remains concentrated on their upcoming World Cup qualifier against Moldova. FAW chief executive Jonathan Ford and the organization stood behind their 46-year-old manager, who recently led Wales to a historic semi-final appearance at Euro 2016. Coleman had signed a new two-year contract with the FAW just a month before the tournament. "We're fully focused on Moldova," said FAW operations manager Roberts to BBC Radio Wales Sport. "We've started our preparation and planning for the Moldova game and that will continue over the next three or four weeks." The former Fulham boss has emerged as a prime candidate for Hull City's managerial vacancy after Steve Bruce's resignation in July, following a breakdown in his relationship with vice-chairman Ehab Allam. However, Coleman, who took over as Wales manager in January 2012 after the tragic death of Gary Speed, has already indicated his long-term plans. "The plan is to try and get the team to Russia and as he's already stated, after that he will look at his options," Roberts explained. Coleman has confirmed the 2018 World Cup campaign will be his final spell as Wales manager. Roberts acknowledged that speculation surrounding Coleman's future is inevitable following Wales' remarkable Euro 2016 performance – their first major tournament appearance in 58 years. "There's always going to be speculation any time a major job becomes vacant," he said. "That's due to the great work Chris has achieved with the national team."

London Shooting: Gang-Related Murder Case of Mistaken Identity, Police Say A 27-year-old man, identified in reports as Oliver Tetlow, has been pronounced dead following a shooting in Harlesden on Wednesday night. Detective Chief Inspector Mark Lawson confirmed the killing is being investigated as gang-related, revealing the victim was shot multiple times with what appeared to be an automatic weapon. "At this very early stage in the investigation, we are exploring that the shooting was gang related, however I am satisfied the victim was not the intended target and this was a tragic case of mistaken identity," DCI Lawson stated. Police believe the gunman emerged from a dark hatchback car before fleeing in the same vehicle after the attack. DCI Lawson acknowledged that details of the murder are "circulating" on social media and urged anyone with information to contact authorities. The victim's family has been notified, though formal identification will only occur following a post-mortem examination. Investigators continue to appeal for witnesses to come forward as they work to piece together the circumstances of this fatal shooting.

**Murtagh Returns as Ireland Name Squad for England ODI** Tim Murtagh has been included in Ireland's 14-man squad for the one-day international against England at Malahide on 8 May after recovering from the foot injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. The Middlesex seamer is the only addition to the squad that represented Ireland at the tournament in Australia and New Zealand, with Peter Chase and Max Sorensen the players to miss out. The match will mark a significant milestone for captain William Porterfield, who will make his 200th appearance for Ireland in what is expected to be a sell-out crowd near Dublin. "It's a great honour for me to have played 200 times for my country," said Porterfield, who made his debut against Namibia in 2006. "It's a bit special for it to be against England in front of an expected sell-out crowd at Malahide." The fixture will be Porterfield's 80th ODI for Ireland, where he has scored seven centuries - more than any other Irish batsman. "I've happy memories personally from the last time we played them in Dublin, scoring a century, although the result didn't go our way," added the 30-year-old. "Hopefully in home conditions we can get the win that our fantastic supporters so richly deserve." Ireland are still searching for a replacement for Phil Simmons, who departed last month to take charge of West Indies, but hope to have a new coach appointed before the England match. **Squad:** William Porterfield (captain), Andrew Balbirnie, Alex Cusack, George Dockrell, Ed Joyce, Andrew McBrine, John Mooney, Tim Murtagh, Kevin O'Brien, Niall O'Brien, Paul Stirling, Stuart Thompson, Gary Wilson, Craig Young.

Brighton seafront pool plans spark concerns over impact on Saltdean Lido Plans for a new outdoor swimming pool on Brighton's seafront have drawn criticism from an MP and operators of a nearby historic lido, who warn the proximity of the two facilities could harm both businesses. The proposed 50-metre pool would be built on a derelict council-owned site on Madeira Drive, just 3.9 miles from Saltdean Lido, a 1930s facility currently undergoing restoration and scheduled to open next year. Brighton Kemptown MP Simon Kirby questioned the wisdom of having two outdoor pools so close together. "There is only a certain demand, and I'm not sure having two outdoor pools within three miles of each other is a very sensible way forward," he said. Rebecca Crook from Saltdean Lido echoed these concerns, stating that "two outdoor swimming pools within a four-mile radius is most unusual and certainly will impact on both businesses." She also criticised what she described as a "lack of joined-up thinking." However, developers behind the new pool insist the facilities would serve different purposes. Rod Hart from Swimmergy, one of three companies involved in the project, said the 50m pool would focus primarily on training rather than general swimming, targeting triathletes and swimming squads from around the world. Brighton and Hove Council defended the plans, saying the new pool would provide "excellence and broad appeal" and become a hub for swimming and sport-related businesses. The facility would be marketed for triathlons and offer escorted sea swims, lifeguard training, and leisure swimming. Councillor Geoffrey Bowden, chairman of the economic development and culture committee, emphasised that Saltdean Lido was "a very different facility" with its own unique offering. His committee will decide on Thursday whether to grant landlord's consent for the project.

Three People Injured in Bradford Shooting Incident Armed police responded to a shooting at a property on Parkway in Bradford during the early hours of Saturday morning at approximately 01:00 BST. Three people were injured in the incident – two men aged 22 and 41, and a 38-year-old woman. All three victims required hospital treatment but have since been discharged. Jordan Barrett, 22, from Chelwood Drive in Allerton, has been charged with attempted murder and firearms offences. He is scheduled to appear before Bradford Magistrates' Court.

Putin'Probably Approved' Litvinenko Murder, UK Inquiry Finds The assassination of former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko in London was probably approved by President Vladimir Putin himself, according to a landmark British public inquiry released today. "Taking full account of all the evidence and analysis available to me, I find that the FSB operation to kill Litvinenko was probably approved by Mr Patrushev and also by President Putin," wrote Sir Robert Owen, who led the inquiry. This is the most significant statement to come out of the report, says the BBC's Richard Galpin. Nikolai Patrushev was head of Russia's main intelligence agency, FSB, at the time of the murder and very close to Mr Putin. Mr Litvinenko died from acute radiation syndrome on 23 November 2006, three weeks after drinking tea containing polonium-210 in a hotel bar in central London's Mayfair, the inquiry found. The report identified two Russian men, Andrei Lugovoi and Dmitry Kovtun, as the perpetrators. For many years, they have been the two chief suspects. Mr Lugovoi had been in the FSB and the federal protection service, and continued to have strong links to the FSB. Sir Robert said there was a strong probability that Mr Lugovoi poisoned Mr Litvinenko under the direction of Moscow's FSB intelligence service. Mr Kovtun was also acting under FSB direction, possibly indirectly through Mr Lugovoi but probably to his knowledge. The Russian pair had tried to poison Mr Litvinenko almost a month earlier at a London office of multinational security company, Erinys, the report said. They knew they were using a deadly poison, but did not know precisely which chemical, it went on. Both deny killing Mr Litvinenko. They are wanted in the UK for questioning, but Russia has refused to extradite them. The use of polonium-210 was "at the very least a strong indicator of state involvement" as it had to be made in a nuclear reactor, the report said. Possible motives were Mr Litvinenko's work for British intelligence agencies, his criticism of Mr Putin and the FSB and his association with other Russian dissidents, the report said. There was "undoubtedly a personal dimension to the antagonism" between Mr Putin and Mr Litvinenko, Sir Robert said. The inquiry heard evidence that Mr Litvinenko may have been consigned to a slow death from radiation to "send a message".

Lewes Parking Meters Targeted in Latest Vandalism Attack Parking meters in Lewes have been targeted in the latest of a series of vandalism attacks that have plagued the Sussex town for nearly a decade. In the most recent incident, four meters were attacked with fireworks while paint was daubed on a fifth machine. A witness reported seeing a man running towards the town centre following an explosion heard in Friars Walk at 22:00 BST on Sunday, according to Sussex Police. The attacks caused approximately £4,500 worth of damage, affecting machines in Phoenix Causeway car park, Friars Walk, Garden Street and Southover Road. This continues a disturbing pattern of vandalism. A previous attack in October 2012 resulted in £2,900 of damage to two pay-and-display machines. The most serious spate occurred in 2011, when vandals carried out 15 attacks on 14 parking meters between September and November, causing over £20,000 in damage. Police say similar incidents have been reported annually since on-street parking charges were introduced in 2004.

Northern Ireland to Host Major Aviation Conference Routes Europe 2017 Belfast is set to welcome approximately 1,200 delegates when it hosts Routes Europe in early 2017, organisers have announced. The prestigious annual conference brings together airports and tourism authorities from across the continent. Northern Ireland Enterprise Minister Arlene Foster emphasized the significance of securing the event. "It is not just any old conference," she said. "Any city which has held it comes out the other side with more routes." The conference comes at a crucial time for Northern Ireland's three airports, which have struggled to open new markets while competing with the rapid growth of Dublin Airport. Airlines have cited air passenger duty (APD) as a barrier to establishing new routes, particularly to destinations like Germany. Mrs Foster currently opposes devolving complete APD control to Stormont, as any tax cut would require the executive to reimburse the Treasury for lost revenue—estimated at £55 million annually. However, she supports establishing an air route development fund to attract specific airlines and routes. "I am hoping that will come about soon," she stated. Both Belfast International and George Best Belfast City airports have welcomed the news. Following this year's event in Aberdeen and next year's conference in Krakow, the Belfast gathering will take place at the newly revamped Waterfront Hall.

Angolan Activists Face Trial for Discussing Book on Nonviolent Resistance A group of Angolan activists, including prominent rapper and activist Luaty Beirao, are facing trial after being arrested in June for participating in a book club discussion about nonviolent resistance. The activists, who belong to a youth movement critical of the government, were detained while preparing to discuss Gene Sharp's 1993 book "From Dictatorship to Democracy: A Conceptual Framework for Liberation." The book, which has become a handbook for democratic movements worldwide, outlines strategies for peaceful resistance against authoritarian regimes. Mr. Beirao, who performs under the stage name Ikonoklasta, has been a vocal critic of Angola's government, advocating for more equitable distribution of the country's substantial oil wealth. He recently ended a five-week hunger strike while in detention. The arrests have sparked international concern, with protests erupting in Portugal and widespread condemnation from human rights organizations. Zenaida Machado of Human Rights Watch called on Angolan judges to "show independence and not permit this trial to be used as an instrument to silence the government's critics." Angola's deputy state prosecutor defended the detentions, claiming the activists were planning an uprising among students and workers "with incalculable consequences." If convicted, the group faces up to 12 years in prison. The detained activists had previously organized demonstrations calling for the resignation of President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, who has ruled Angola for 36 years. Despite Angola being Africa's second-largest oil producer and experiencing significant economic growth since the civil war ended in 2002, critics argue that the nation's wealth has only enriched a small elite while the majority of citizens remain impoverished. The case highlights ongoing tensions between civil society and the government in Angola.

Trial Opens for Two Men Accused in Alan Kurdi's Death The trial has begun in Turkey for two Syrian nationals accused in connection with the death of three-year-old Alan Kurdi, whose photograph lying lifeless on a Turkish beach became a defining image of the 2015 refugee crisis. Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad are being tried in Bodrum, the same seaside city where Alan's body washed ashore. The men face up to 35 years in prison each if convicted on charges of human smuggling and causing deaths "through deliberate negligence." Both defendants pleaded not guilty at Thursday's hearing, which has reportedly concluded. Their next court appearance is scheduled for early March, and they will remain in custody until then. Alan, along with his five-year-old brother Galib and mother Rihan, drowned when their overcrowded boat capsized during an attempted crossing to the Greek island of Kos. Alan's father, Abdullah, was the sole family survivor and is believed to be living outside Turkey. The tragic photograph of Alan sparked global outrage and brought unprecedented attention to the Syrian refugee crisis.

Leicester Tigers Sign Wales Sevens Star Owen Jenkins and Australia's Nick Malouf Leicester Tigers have bolstered their backline with the signings of Wales Sevens international Owen Jenkins and Australia Sevens player Nick Malouf. Back Malouf, 24, made his international Sevens debut in 2012 and played every game of the 2013 and 2014 World Series, as well as last year's Olympic Games. Wales Sevens international Owen, 28, can also play at fly-half and full-back. He was released from his deal with Pro12 side Scarlets this month. The length of contracts for the two players has not been revealed. Tigers head coach Matt O'Connor said Owen's experience and Malouf's versatility would boost their backline options. "He (Owen) is a natural footballer in the midfield and works well with the players around him," O'Connor said. "Nick has the ability to play at centre or wing, and has good power and pace. He is now at a point in his career where he wants to focus on the full version of the game again and we'd like to see him develop with us."

WWI Hero's Bronze Statue Unveiled in Middlesbrough A bronze statue honoring Private Tom Dresser, a World War I hero from Middlesbrough, has been unveiled at the town's Dorman Museum following a remarkable fundraising effort by his family. Pte Dresser displayed exceptional courage during the 1917 Battle of Arras in Northern France, running through No Man's Land to deliver two crucial messages despite being shot. He survived his wounds and lived until 1982, reaching the age of 90. His family successfully raised over £50,000 to commission the memorial statue. His grandson Brian attended the unveiling ceremony and reflected on his grandfather's modest character: "It's the culmination of a lot of hard work of a lot of people. He would have been utterly embarrassed by [the unveiling] and would have shied away from it totally."

Row the Rock Challenge Postponed Due to Rough Seas A crew of 17 friends comprising the Row the Rock Challenge team has been forced to postpone their attempt to circumnavigate the Isle of Man due to adverse weather conditions. The team had planned to depart from Peel earlier but was prevented by strong winds creating waves too dangerous for their vessel to safely navigate during the 90-mile round trip. Team member Andy Mulhern explained: "We can cope with a sea state of two, but at the moment its three or four, which would make it impossible to challenge the record. It's a little disappointing, but that's the way it goes and we're all looking forward to getting on with the challenge next weekend." The crew has rescheduled their attempt for the following weekend, aiming to beat the 1995 record of 27 hours. They are raising funds for the RNLI, Sailing for the Disabled and the Hyperbaric Chamber.

Facebook Reports Soaring Mobile Ad Revenue as Zuckerberg Seeks New Share Structure Facebook has announced stellar first-quarter results that significantly exceeded Wall Street expectations, with advertising revenues climbing to $5.2 billion and mobile advertising now accounting for more than 80% of the company's total ad revenue. The social media giant reported total sales of $5.4 billion for the quarter, representing a substantial increase from $3.5 billion during the same period last year. Following the announcement, Facebook shares surged more than 9% in after-hours trading, demonstrating investor confidence in the company's continued growth trajectory. ## Mobile Strategy Pays Dividends Facebook's strategic emphasis on mobile advertising has proven remarkably successful, with mobile now generating 82% of the company's advertising revenues for the first quarter of 2016, up from 73% during the corresponding quarter in 2015. This growth comes despite earlier investor concerns about the company's ability to transition effectively to mobile platforms. The company's focus on live video has attracted new advertisers to the platform, while sales from existing services have also experienced robust growth. Total monthly active users (MAU) increased 15% year-over-year to reach 1.65 billion, surpassing analyst predictions. Perhaps more impressively, the average revenue per user climbed to $3.32, compared to $2.50 during the same period last year. ## New Share Class Proposed Alongside the financial results, Facebook announced that CEO Mark Zuckerberg has requested the creation of a new class of stock. This move would allow him to donate money from his shares to charitable causes while maintaining control of the company he founded. Facebook stated that the new structure would "encourage Mr Zuckerberg to remain in an active leadership role at Facebook." The announcement follows Zuckerberg's December 2015 commitment, made with his wife Priscilla Chan after the birth of their daughter Max, to give away 99% of their wealth over the course of their lives. The couple plans to direct these donations through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, which they established to "advance human potential and promote equality for all children in the next generation." Under Facebook's current shareholder structure, Zuckerberg cannot make such substantial donations without relinquishing control of the company. The proposed new share class would address this limitation. ## Future Investment Plans During a call with investors, Facebook indicated its intention to continue acquiring other companies, though it emphasized that it would focus only on those offering services that could become "ubiquitous." The company has a history of significant acquisitions, most notably purchasing photo-sharing platform Instagram for $1 billion in 2012. However, Facebook has not disclosed specific earnings figures from its acquired companies, making it challenging for investors to evaluate the success of these deals. The company also declined to share specific sales figures for the Oculus Rift virtual reality headset, which began shipping toward the end of the quarter. ## Tech Sector Leadership Facebook's impressive performance stands in stark contrast to recent struggles elsewhere in the technology sector, including disappointing results from Apple and ongoing challenges at Twitter. The company appears to have overcome obstacles that once concerned investors, particularly the transition to mobile advertising, which some had viewed as a potential weakness but has instead become a major strength.

UKIP Candidate Quits Party After Offensive Remarks Scandal A UKIP parliamentary candidate has resigned from the party following a turbulent week that saw multiple controversies plague the organization's election preparations. Kerry Smith, who was selected to contest the South Basildon and East Thurrock constituency, announced his departure from UKIP, citing frustration with "internal backstabbers who hold minor roles in the party." Mr Smith will continue to serve as an independent councillor on both Essex County Council and Basildon District Council. The resignation comes just four days after Mr Smith was re-adopted as the party's candidate for the seat, which UKIP views as a key target in the upcoming general election. His candidacy became untenable after the Mail On Sunday obtained a recording in which he made offensive remarks about gay people, fellow UKIP members, and the Essex town of Chigwell. In a statement explaining his decision, Mr Smith said: "I want the best for South Basildon and Thurrock and I want to see the real issues discussed that touch the lives of people. Therefore I have chosen to resign so that UKIP can win this seat next May." Despite leaving the party, Mr Smith expressed support for UKIP's "general goals" but said he needed to "walk away" and "get my life back." UKIP leader Nigel Farage confirmed that Mr Smith resigned "by mutual consent," describing his behavior as "loutish and wholly inappropriate." Mr Farage acknowledged that the party had experienced "great difficulty" with the Basildon selection process and emphasized the need to "grip this and sort it out, in short order." The party's national executive committee now has the power to impose a candidate if necessary, Mr Farage indicated. Mr Smith's departure caps a particularly challenging week for UKIP, which is seeking to win several seats and potentially hold the balance of power in Parliament. The South Basildon and East Thurrock seat has been at the center of multiple controversies, with former Conservative MP Neil Hamilton previously withdrawing from consideration amid questions about his expenses. Additionally, another candidate, Natasha Bolter, withdrew during an investigation into allegations she made against Roger Bird, UKIP's candidate vetting officer, who denies the claims. Mr Smith previously stood for UKIP in Basildon in 2010, finishing fourth. The selection process for the constituency is now expected to be reopened.

Bus Driver Traced After Hit-and-Run Leaves Woman Seriously Injured A 47-year-old woman remains in serious but stable condition after being struck by a bus in Islington early Saturday morning. Officers responded to Rosebery Avenue just before 01:00 GMT following the collision. The Metropolitan Police confirmed the bus driver fled the scene without stopping but has since been located. No arrests have been made at this time as investigations continue. The victim was transported to hospital for treatment of her injuries.

Bushcricket Breaks Records with Testicles 14% of Body Weight Scientists have discovered that a species of bushcricket possesses the largest testicles in relation to body weight ever recorded in the animal kingdom, according to a new study published in Biology Letters. The species Platycleis affinis has testicles that make up approximately 14% of its body weight – equivalent to a human male having testicles weighing five kilograms (11 pounds) each. This surpasses the previous record holder, a fruit fly species called Drosophila bifurca, whose testicle-to-body weight ratio was recorded at 10.6%. However, the research team led by Dr Karim Vahed of the University of Derby has uncovered a surprising twist that challenges long-held assumptions about the purpose of large testicles in the animal kingdom. ## Mating Strategy Over Sperm Competition When studying the mating strategies of these bushcrickets, also known as katydids, researchers found that males with bigger testicles actually release only small amounts of sperm at each mating encounter. This discovery suggests that the oversized reproductive organs are designed for mating with many different females rather than producing competitive volumes of sperm for individual encounters. "Males with bigger testicles are actually producing smaller amounts of ejaculate," Dr Vahed told BBC News. "This very much favours the alternative hypothesis: that it's about the number of different females the male can fertilise, rather than getting a greater success per female." ## Challenging Established Theory Significant research across the animal kingdom has previously shown that male testicle size correlates with the degree of promiscuity within a species. The more partners a female has, the larger the male's testicles tend to be. The traditional assumption has been that larger testicles produce more sperm for a "numbers game" within the female reproductive system, where the male providing the highest amount of sperm has a better chance of fathering offspring. Many experiments in vertebrate species, including our closest primate relatives, have supported this theory. However, the bushcricket research supports an alternative hypothesis: that larger testicles permit a higher total number of mates rather than a higher sperm allocation per mate. The study examined testicle sizes across 21 species of bushcrickets, finding wide variation in proportional testicle size before identifying Platycleis affinis as the record-breaker. Dr Vahed emphasised the importance of not applying findings from vertebrates universally: "One important message is that we shouldn't expect that exactly the same rules and situations apply across all species; it can be an either-or."

Ancient Egyptian Mummies Reveal Secrets Through Revolutionary CT Scanning Never before has anyone seen mummy hair, muscles and bone in such detail. In a groundbreaking study, researchers at the British Museum have used cutting-edge technology to peer beneath the wrappings of ancient Egyptian mummies, revealing unprecedented insights into the lives and deaths of people who lived thousands of years ago. Each mummy was put into a special CT scanner (an X-ray machine) to investigate the mummies layer by layer, building up a 3D picture of each one. The study's revealed many details about who these people were, how they lived and how they died. By peeling away each layer museum staff could see the face of the person underneath the bandages and for the first time to tell the age of the mummies, what they ate, and the kinds of diseases they suffered from. John Taylor, from the British Museum said he was "stunned" when he saw the images. "It's as if you switched a light on in a dark room and things jump out with a clarity where you are able to find out what the life experiences of these people really were," he said. The researchers were able to see muscles and even arteries in the ancient bodies. They even saw that some arteries seemed clogged with fatty deposits, which could mean that these particular people ate rich fatty foods and maybe died of heart disease. After peeling away the muscle, researchers were able to see the skeletons in amazing detail. They were able to guess the age of the individual mummies from their pelvis and their teeth. Many of them had bad teeth with signs of abscesses (infections), which would have been very painful to live with. One scan shows a spatula left inside the mummy's skull. The tool would have been used to pull the brain out through the nostrils during the embalming process. But in this case a large chunk of brain was left inside, along with the tool, possibly because the person carrying out the embalming did a bad job. Researchers also discovered that the mummies lived between 3,500BC and 700AD. All of them lived in the Nile Valley in Egypt.

Anthony McGill Wins First Ranking Title in Snooker Breakthrough Anthony McGill secured his maiden ranking title at 25, becoming Scotland's first new ranking event winner in ten years. The Glasgow native seized control in a tense final after the players were locked at 2-2 at the interval, resuming with an impressive break of 96. The decisive final frame proved nail-biting, with McGill clinching victory by clearing the table after potting the last red. The triumph propels him up the world rankings from 29th to 18th position. McGill's path to glory included notable victories over former world champions Stuart Bingham and Shaun Murphy, marking a significant breakthrough for the Scot who had never previously progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a ranking tournament.

West Brom's Berahino Rebuked by Pulis Over Unauthorised Transfer Interview West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has criticized striker Saido Berahino following an unauthorised interview in which the young forward discussed his ambitions to play for a top-four club. The 21-year-old made the comments in an interview with Sky Sports News that had not been authorised by the club, prompting a firm response from his manager. "For Saido, the most important thing is to go out there and perform, rather than talking about it. He's still got a long way to go," said Pulis. The manager emphasized that Berahino needs to let his performances do the talking before attracting interest from elite clubs. "If he gets to that stage, he'll have teams coming after him," Pulis added. "He's not had that yet, as there were no phone calls asking for him in this transfer window." The former Stoke City and Crystal Palace manager was keen to stress Berahino's long-standing connection to West Brom and the responsibility that comes with it. "The kid has been at this football club since he was 10. He has got real respect for the people who have helped him get to where he's got so far," Pulis said. "The question is, does he want to go on and play in a top four team? I've no doubt he does, but his responsibility is to work as hard as he can for us until that happens and to go out and score as many goals as he can until the end of the season." Despite the public rebuke, sources suggest the incident has been handled internally with good humour. "The lads got straight into him for the interview, but it was all in good fun. He is young, he said something and he will learn from it. I know from being in the dressing room he loves West Brom and he wants to do well here," said one teammate. West Brom face a crucial period as they look to distance themselves from relegation trouble. The Baggies, bolstered by new signing Darren Fletcher, travel to Burnley on Sunday sitting three points above the relegation zone, with Sean Dyche's side only a point clear of safety. Fletcher, discussing his move to The Hawthorns, praised Pulis's role in his decision: "The manager sold the place to me. It wasn't until I came down here and saw the great facilities and met some of the great people involved in the club that I truly made my decision."

Scotland's Income Gap Narrows Despite Regional Disparities Scotland's disposable income has grown faster than the UK average over the past 16 years, though significant regional variations remain, according to new research from the Scottish Parliament Information Centre. The study revealed that Scotland's average disposable income in 2013 stood at £17,039 per head after tax and benefits, slightly below the UK average of £17,599. However, in real terms, Scottish incomes have risen by 27% since 1997, outpacing the 23% growth across the UK as a whole. In cash terms, excluding inflation, Scottish income increased by 81% over the same period, compared with 75% for the entire UK. This demonstrates that the income gap between Scotland and the rest of the UK has narrowed considerably since 1997. **Regional Variations** The research highlighted stark differences across Scotland's regions. Only two areas – the north-east and Edinburgh – recorded disposable incomes exceeding £20,000 per head, placing them among the top 20% of UK regions. Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire enjoyed the highest incomes, at 35% above Glasgow levels. However, these figures predate the recent slump in oil prices, which has significantly impacted the north-east economy. At the other end of the scale, Glasgow recorded the lowest disposable income per head in Scotland. West central Scotland, West Lothian, and parts of Tayside also featured among the poorest areas, with Glasgow and North Lanarkshire falling into the bottom 25% for UK income. The disparity between Scotland's richest and poorest areas exceeded £5,000 per head, highlighting persistent regional inequality. **Benefits Dependency** The analysis also examined the role of social benefits, including pensions and welfare payments, in household income. Benefits accounted for 21% of Scottish disposable income, slightly higher than the UK figure of just below 20%. The west Highlands and Ayrshire emerged as Scotland's most benefit-dependent regions. The area encompassing Lochaber, Skye and Lochalsh, Arran and Cumbrae, along with Argyll and Bute, derived 28% of its income from benefits – placing it in the top 10% of UK regions for benefit reliance. Areas with high concentrations of older people or greater poverty levels showed the highest dependency on benefits as income sources. **Income Distribution** Additional analysis from the Budget for Fiscal Responsibility, using HMRC statistics from 2012-13, revealed that Scotland's income tax-paying population is slightly more weighted towards lower earning segments compared to the UK average. The most significant difference appeared among high earners, with Scotland having a notably smaller proportion of people earning more than £150,000 annually. However, Scotland's income distribution was much closer to the UK average than Wales's distribution.

Egyptair Flight Diverted to Scotland After Threatening Note Found on Board An Egyptair flight bound for New York was diverted to Prestwick Airport in Scotland on Saturday after a threatening note was discovered on board, prompting the RAF to scramble fighter jets to escort the aircraft. BBC producer Nada Tawfik, a passenger on board flight 985, said she saw a note written on a napkin with a pencil bearing the words "I'll set this plane on fire" along with a seat number. The Boeing 777, which was travelling from Cairo to JFK International Airport, touched down at Prestwick at around 14:30 BST. The Ministry of Defence confirmed that RAF Typhoon aircraft from RAF Leuchars were scrambled following "an incident on board" the plane. An eyewitness reported seeing the two fighter jets escort the aircraft into the Ayrshire airport. Ms Tawfik, who was travelling with her daughter under two years old, described the handwriting on the note as appearing childlike or sloppy. "It was very alarming especially these days when everyone is so concerned about safety on flights," she said. She added that the incident had been "very scary" and created a tense atmosphere, particularly for passengers travelling with babies. The aircraft, carrying 326 passengers, was moved to an isolated part of the airport away from the passenger terminal. Passengers were allowed to begin disembarking three hours after landing, and police commenced interviews with all those on board. Detective Superintendent Alan Crawford of Police Scotland said he would not speculate on whether the threat was credible, but confirmed that the plane's captain and crew made the decision to divert from their normal flight path after discovering the note. A Police Scotland spokeswoman stated: "At around 1420 hours today an Egyptair aircraft flying from Cairo to New York was diverted to Prestwick Airport after a suspicious note was discovered on the aircraft. There are no reports of anyone injured." The airport confirmed that there was no disruption to other flights, which continued to operate normally. The A79 road, which had been temporarily closed in both directions next to the airport, has since reopened. The investigation into the incident continues as authorities work to determine the source and credibility of the threat.

Harry Potter Actor Unveils Memorial to War Poet Wilfred Owen Actor Jason Isaacs has unveiled a memorial stone honouring war poet Wilfred Owen at Edinburgh Napier University's Craiglockhart campus, the site of the former war hospital where Owen received treatment during World War One. Owen was sent to the Craiglockhart War Hospital in Edinburgh, where he met fellow war poet Siegfried Sassoon in August 1917. The site is now part of Edinburgh Napier University's Craiglockhart campus. The university already has a permanent exhibition to mark war poets' work. Earlier a Caithness flagstone bearing a quote from the poet "My subject is war and the pity of war. The poetry is in the pity" was unveiled by Isaacs, who is in Scotland with Theatre of War company, which produces ancient Greek tragedies for service members, veterans and their families. Owen was killed in the final week of World War One, shot by German machine guns as British forces unsuccessfully tried to bridge a canal in northern France. Isaacs, who plays Lucius Malfoy in the Harry Potter films, said: "This flagstone and its quotation will remind everyone who sees it that though the poets to emerge from the Great War have come to represent something culturally significant and revered, their inspiration was what all wars still provide; tragedy, terror and death. These were dispatches from the front line." The flagstone was donated to the university by Glen-Art, a military charity supporting former members of the armed forces. It lies outside the old main entrance to the building as a permanent memorial to Owen and all those affected by the First World War and other conflicts. Catherine Walker, curator of the university's War Poets Collection, said: "It is a unique gift, which is a fitting tribute to all who have been affected by war, not only those officers treated at Craiglockhart War Hospital." Fiona MacDonald, founder and director of Glen-Art and a trustee of the Wilfred Owen Association, said: "We are delighted to be able to donate this beautiful stone as the first of many events and activities commemorating the centenary of the time Wilfred Owen spent at Craiglockhart, where he met Siegfried Sassoon."

Kenyan Tech Platform Ushahidi Monitors US Election Process A Kenyan technology platform originally developed to track post-election violence is being deployed to monitor the United States presidential election, according to Ushahidi's innovation manager Chris Mukuria. The platform, Ushahidi, is collecting and verifying information about the voting process, which is then shared with affiliated organizations for appropriate action. The initiative comes amid heightened concerns about election integrity, particularly after Republican candidate Donald Trump claimed the election would be "rigged" and called on his supporters to monitor polling stations—a move some fear could lead to voter intimidation. Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton has dismissed these voter fraud allegations as baseless. "The team is currently combing through social media and dealing with messages sent directly to its platform, verifying the content before escalating to the right people," Mr. Mukuria told the BBC. Ushahidi has partnered with several institutions, including the Election Protection Committee, which operates one of the largest non-partisan election monitoring organizations in the United States. The collaborative effort aims to ensure a smooth voting process as millions of Americans cast their ballots to elect not only a president but also federal and state leaders, as well as vote on various local ballot measures. "Our honest hope is that all of this is for naught, and that end of the day Tuesday we look at all the reports and that 99.9% of reports say:'Everything went great!'" said Nathaniel Manning, Ushahidi's chief operating officer. Originally launched in 2008 by activists and developers to monitor post-election violence in Kenya following a disputed election, Ushahidi has since been utilized globally. The platform has tracked sexual harassment in Egypt and coordinated disaster response during Haiti's 2012 earthquake. The specific application deployed for US election monitoring has also been used in Mexico and Nigeria, according to Mr. Mukuria. The team plans to continue monitoring activities until polling stations close across the country. Mrs. Clinton is seeking to make history as the first female president of the United States, while Mr. Trump, a real-estate billionaire and reality-TV personality, surprised many by defeating established politicians during the Republican primaries.

Museum Strike: National Museum Wales Chief Urges Staff to Accept'Best Offer' The director general of National Museum Wales (NMW), David Anderson, has spoken to BBC Wales after making an offer to staff involved in a long-running pay dispute over ending "premium payments" to weekend staff. Strikes by the Public and Commercial Services (PCS) union have hit museums across Wales, forcing closures at various times since the dispute began in 2014. Mr Anderson said public sector spending cuts had forced a review of NMW's staff costs and he urged workers to accept the museum's "best offer". "There's only a certain number of options we have and if we don't make the savings on the staff costs then we have to do it in terms of the galleries and the buildings and the sites, or not having any new exhibitions, or closing down our education services," he said. "Those are the things we spend the money on, so those are our choices. We wouldn't be doing our job if we didn't preserve our services as well as preserving staff." NMW runs seven sites across Wales: National Museum Cardiff, St Fagans National History Museum, National Waterfront Museum in Swansea, Big Pit in Blaenavon, Torfaen, National Roman Legion Museum in Newport, the National Wool Museum in Llandysul, Carmarthenshire, and the Welsh Slate Museum in Llanberis, Gwynedd. ## Union Response However, one union official said the proposals "attacked" the terms and conditions of workers who gave up their own weekends. Neil Harrison, the PCS union's branch chairman at National Museum Wales, said he did not believe "affordability" was a factor in the proposed changes to staff payments. "What lies at the heart of this is an attempt by management to remove weekend payments," he said. "It's an attack on the terms and conditions of those people who have to give up their weekends so that other people can come with their families to enjoy the national museums." ## The Offer The museum said its latest offer to workers involved in the dispute includes a 6% increase in basic pay, plus a further two years' worth of premium payments equivalent to an average payout of £3,600. It will also guarantee the lowest paid staff will not "lose out" through the process. Mr Anderson said he had returned £30,000 of bonuses he had been eligible for in recent years and staff on higher pay grades had been subject to a pay freeze. A spokesman said: "We feel that in the present economic circumstances where, like everybody else in the public sector in the UK, we've had a loss in real terms of about 25% of our budget in the last few years. "This is a very fair offer that we're making in the middle of an austerity storm." ## Next Steps PCS is conducting an indicative ballot to assess whether its members will accept the latest proposal. The result will be known by 2 October and it will then decide whether to hold a full vote on the issue.

Northern Ireland's Corporation Tax Plan Loses Edge as UK Rate Drops A senior business figure has warned that Northern Ireland's plans to attract investment through a lower corporation tax rate are being undermined by reductions in the UK-wide rate. Martin Fleetwood from PWC told the BBC's Inside Business show the UK-wide rate was reducing, meaning the proposed differential would not be as great. Corporation tax - the tax firms pay on their profits - is now 20% in the UK. The Northern Ireland Executive hoped to set its own lower rate but the plan has been held up by stalemate over welfare. Stormont's aim was to cut corporation tax by April 2017, in a bid to compete for business with the Republic of Ireland where the rate is 12.5%. In his July budget earlier this week, Chancellor George Osborne confirmed that the UK-wide rate will fall to 19% in 2017 and will be reduced again to 18% by 2020. Mr Fleetwood, a senior partner at the leading management consultancy firm, said Northern Ireland needs to rethink how it sells itself as a place to do business. "The game-changer that was hoped to come from corporation tax in Northern Ireland, the benefit from that is being eroded because the differential between us and the rest of the UK is reducing," he told Inside Business. "I think that what that means for Northern Ireland is that we have to be even clearer about enunciating what our compelling sales message is as a FDI [foreign direct investment] location." Under last December's Stormont House Agreement, the Westminster government agreed to legislate to devolve corporation tax setting powers to Northern Ireland ministers. However, the move is dependent on Stormont ministers' ability to balance their budget and implement welfare reform. There has been stalemate over welfare since March, when Sinn Féin withdrew its support for the Stormont House Agreement. Martin Fleetwood's interview will be broadcast on Inside Business on BBC Radio Ulster at 13:30 BST on Sunday, 12 July.

Castlereagh Council Seeks Approval for Dundonald Ice Bowl Replacement Castlereagh Council has formally submitted planning permission to demolish and replace the Dundonald Ice Bowl with a state-of-the-art leisure complex. The original Ice Bowl, which opened its doors in 1986, attracts approximately 600,000 visitors annually and has become a cherished community facility. According to planning documents, the proposed replacement will serve as a "flagship development" featuring modern amenities, including an Olympic-standard ice rink. The redevelopment will be carried out in phases to minimize disruption, with the completed complex also housing an NHS health and well-being centre. Council officials, who first announced the ambitious project earlier this year, anticipate completion by 2017, though final costs remain undisclosed. Planning documents emphasize the facility's status as "a regional facility of significant importance to Northern Ireland's economy."

Armed Police Debate Intensifies Following London Bridge Terror Attack A former Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) Special Branch officer has called for all police officers in the UK to carry firearms following Saturday's terror attack in London, which left seven people dead and 48 injured. William Matchett, who has also advised on policing matters in Iraq and Afghanistan and authored a book about Special Branch operations during the Northern Ireland Troubles, argues that the nature of modern terrorism requires a fundamentally different police response than what was needed during the Troubles. "When you look at this new threat and the way it's manifested in England, particularly looking at vehicles, looking at cars and knives to kill people - it's very quick, it's very dynamic and it happens within seconds," Mr Matchett explained. He drew a stark contrast between terrorist tactics in Northern Ireland and those employed in recent mainland UK attacks. "It's a totally different ball game to what I grew up with in Northern Ireland, where the terrorist essentially attacked someone. It was very short, it was sharp and then they looked to get away," he said. "In England, in the last three series of attacks, that's not been the case - they actually hang about and try to kill as many people as possible." Mr Matchett argued that the speed and brutality of these attacks necessitates immediate armed response. "So the quicker that it's stopped the better and, in that respect, it's very hard now to stand up against every police officer carrying a sidearm and that's through from your neighbourhood beat, your community officers, to plain clothes officers - that everyone on and off duty has a sidearm." Saturday night's attack saw three assailants drive into pedestrians on London Bridge before stabbing people in Borough Market. Armed response units shot the attackers dead within minutes of arriving on the scene. The incident highlighted both the bravery and vulnerability of unarmed officers. An off-duty policeman and amateur rugby player was stabbed after tackling one of the attackers and remains critically ill. A British Transport Police officer who confronted the terrorists armed only with his baton was seriously injured but is now in stable condition. All police officers in Northern Ireland currently carry firearms on duty and have access to personal protection weapons when off-duty, reflecting the province's unique security situation. However, Metropolitan Police Commissioner Cressida Dick firmly rejected calls for routine arming of all officers in the rest of the UK during an interview with BBC Five Live on Monday. "I personally do not support the routine arming of every single police officer on the streets," she stated. "What these terrorists want to do is completely change the nature of our society." Commissioner Dick emphasized that neither the public nor police officers themselves are comfortable with universal arming. She also challenged the assumption that armed officers provide better protection, citing examples from France where armed lone officers have proven vulnerable. "In other countries where you have someone armed with a sidearm who is going about his normal business as a community officer - they are also very, very vulnerable," she explained. "So to have people who can deal with this kind of very complex terrifying threat strikes me as the right way to go." The debate reflects the difficult balance Britain faces between maintaining its traditional policing model and responding to evolving terrorist threats.

Boris Johnson Condemns Attack on Cereal Cafe During Anti-Gentrification Protest London Mayor Boris Johnson has spoken out after a cereal cafe in east London was attacked during protests against gentrification, describing small businesses as the "lifeblood of London's economy." The Cereal Killer cafe on Brick Lane suffered damage on Sunday night when demonstrators targeted the business during a protest about gentrification in parts of east London. The mayor's office said he was "deeply concerned" about the "unacceptable" violent elements that marred the demonstration. Owner Alan Keery defended his business in an interview with the BBC's Victoria Derbyshire programme, saying it was "incredibly unfair to target a small business for a larger problem." "They're talking about gentrification but they've tagged us as the poster boys for it, and we're not the real problem here," Mr Keery said. The protest, which was advertised on Facebook, also saw a local estate agent's windows smashed. One man was arrested on suspicion of causing criminal damage but has since been released with no further action taken. The Cereal Killer cafe, which Mr Keery opened with his brother in December 2014, has previously attracted criticism for its pricing, with bowls of cereal costing up to £3.20. The protest organisers' Facebook post stated: "We don't want luxury flats that no-one can afford, we want genuinely affordable housing. We don't want pop-up gin bars or brioche buns - we want community." Labour's mayoral candidate Sadiq Khan also condemned the violence, saying: "There is no excuse for mindless violence and intimidation." A spokesman for the mayor emphasised that Mr Johnson "fully recognises the importance of Shoreditch's unique character" and continues working to "strike a balance between residential and commercial properties and strong day and night-time economies." Police in Tower Hamlets are reviewing CCTV footage and appealing for witnesses. Superintendent Pete Turner stated that anyone identified as being involved in the violence would be "actively sought, arrested and brought to justice."

Grey Seal Pups Spotted on Isle of Man: Public Urged to Keep Distance The Manx Wildlife Trust has issued a warning to the public following the arrival of this season's first grey seal pup on the Calf of Mann, reminding visitors that despite their adorable appearance, these animals can be aggressive when approached. Officials from the trust emphasized the importance of maintaining a safe distance from the newborn seals, as mother seals have been known to abandon their offspring if disturbed by human interaction. "It's important to keep dogs away from them too," a spokesman stated. The trust reassured concerned onlookers that it is normal behavior for mother seals to temporarily leave their pups alone on the beach. "There is no need to be alarmed if they appear to be on their own, their mum is probably not far away," the spokesman explained. The Wildlife Trust is currently conducting a monitoring programme to better understand the grey seal population along the Manx coastline. Members of the public who have concerns about a pup's welfare are encouraged to contact the Manx Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (MSPCA).

Brexit Negotiating Team Now 40% Women, Says David Davis Brexit Secretary David Davis has defended the gender balance of the UK's EU negotiating team after facing criticism from parliamentary committee members who described earlier photographs of the predominantly male delegation as "a disgrace." In a letter to the House of Lords EU Committee, Mr Davis revealed that 40% of his team in last month's round of talks were women, a significant increase from previous rounds. The committee had previously expressed concern about images showing a largely male line-up representing Britain in the crucial Brexit negotiations. Mr Davis emphasised that the government is committed to making the civil service "representative of modern-day Britain." He explained that personnel would "vary from round to round as we deploy the best available staff for each issue under negotiation." The Brexit Secretary also noted that 52% of all staff at his Department for Exiting the EU (DExEU) are women. "I will continue to work for the best possible deal for the UK during these negotiations, and that means using the best expertise we have available, regardless of gender or any other factor," he stated. The gender balance issue came to prominence last month when Labour's Baroness Kennedy questioned Mr Davis about female representation during a committee appearance. Subsequently, Labour MPs wrote to Prime Minister Theresa May, warning that the talks risked becoming "just another job for the boys." Meanwhile, controversy erupted when Mr Davis's former chief of staff, James Chapman, described Brexit as the "biggest calamity" facing Britain since World War Two. In a series of tweets, Chapman urged "sensible" MPs to reverse the Brexit process, possibly by forming a new party, warning that businesses would "flee" the UK. Former UKIP leader Nigel Farage questioned Chapman's loyalty, asking: "Which side was Mr Chapman really working for in the Brexit department?" Brexit negotiations continue, with the UK scheduled to leave the EU in March 2019.

Historic Crystal Palace Fireplace Returns to Cliffe Castle Museum A remarkable malachite fireplace that was once showcased at London's Crystal Palace Exhibition in 1851 has found its way home to Cliffe Castle Museum in Keighley. The ornate fire surround, crafted in St Petersburg from malachite—a distinctive green copper mineral—was purchased at auction in 1880 by Henry Isaac Butterfield, a wealthy textile manufacturer who built Cliffe Castle in the late 19th Century. The chimneypiece was relocated to another property in the 1950s when Cliffe Castle was converted into a museum. Following the recent death of its latest owner, the historic piece was bequeathed back to the museum. According to Cliffe Castle, only one similar malachite fireplace is known to survive, housed at the Kremlin Palace in Moscow, making this returned treasure extraordinarily rare.

**Swansea City Secure Premier League Survival as Hull City are Relegated** Swansea City manager Paul Clement has expressed his pride after his side secured their Premier League status for another season, avoiding relegation on a dramatic final day of fixtures. The Swans' 2-0 victory over Sunderland, combined with Hull City's 4-0 defeat at Crystal Palace on Sunday, confirmed Swansea's survival in the top flight. Hull needed just a point to keep their hopes alive, but Palace's comprehensive win sealed their fate and brought relief to the Liberty Stadium. "Credit to the players for showing the form they have over the last four games to pick up 10 points from a possible 12," Clement told Swansea's official website. "They deserve to be where they are - playing in the Premier League again." The turnaround has been remarkable for the Welsh club. When Clement arrived in January, Swansea were bottom of the table with a mere 12 points from 19 games, seemingly destined for the Championship. "I am very proud of what we have achieved in the second half of the season, especially when you put into context where we were when I arrived," Clement added. "It's been a collective effort from everyone connected to the club; so congratulations to the players, backroom staff, club staff and definitely our supporters." Clement admitted he expected the survival battle to go down to the wire. "I honestly thought it would go down to the last game of the season," he said. "I'm not complaining it hasn't gone to the last game as I predicted." Swansea will conclude their campaign at home to West Bromwich Albion on Sunday, 21 May, with Clement targeting 41 points to finish the season. "Our supporters have been amazing," Clement said. "I'm looking forward to enjoying the last game of the season with them at the Liberty on Sunday. It should be a fantastic atmosphere."

Prankster's Galaxy Note 7 Wi-Fi Name Causes Alarm on Virgin America Flight A passenger's attempt at humor nearly resulted in an emergency landing when they renamed their Wi-Fi hotspot to mimic the banned Samsung Galaxy Note 7 smartphone. Lucas Wojciechowski was aboard Virgin America flight 358 traveling from San Francisco to Boston when he noticed an unusual Wi-Fi network name on his laptop: "Samsung Galaxy Note 7_1097." What seemed like a harmless observation quickly escalated into a serious situation aboard the late-night flight. The Samsung Galaxy Note 7 had been banned from all U.S. aircraft by the Department of Transportation after several devices caught fire due to battery defects. The ban made any presence of the device on a flight a matter of significant safety concern. After Wojciechowski alerted the crew, flight attendants made an urgent announcement requesting any passenger with a Note 7 to press their call button. When no one responded, the situation intensified. "This isn't a joke. We're going to turn on the lights (it's 11pm) and search everyone's bag until we find it," the crew announced, according to Wojciechowski's tweets from the flight. The captain then warned passengers of potential consequences: "Apparently the plane is going to have to get diverted and searched if nobody fesses up soon." Eventually, the owner of the Wi-Fi hotspot came forward, confessing they had simply renamed their wireless device to "Samsung Galaxy Note 7_1097" as a prank. The flight crew announced the resolution: "Ladies and gentlemen, we found the device. Luckily only the name of the device was changed to'Galaxy Note 7'. It was not a GN7." The incident had wider repercussions. Serenity Caldwell, managing editor of iMore, was waiting to board a subsequent flight at the destination airport when she discovered a massive line at the gate counter. A 9am flight had been cancelled, and it took approximately two hours to sort out passenger itineraries. Caldwell later overheard crew members discussing the real reason for the cancellation: the Galaxy Note 7 scare from the previous flight. "The plane was mid-flight when an attendant noticed a wi-fi hotspot. A Galaxy Note 7 wi-fi hotspot," the crew member explained. According to Wojciechowski, no further action was taken against the passenger responsible for the prank. Virgin America responded to the incident, stating: "The U.S. Department of Transportation has banned the transport of the Samsung Galaxy Note 7 onboard all U.S. aircraft, and Virgin America actively informs guests that they should not bring these devices onboard. As such, when our InFlight Teammates see potential evidence of this device onboard, they take it seriously. In this case, there was no such device - and no flights were cancelled or delayed as a result." The airline's statement contradicted passenger accounts regarding flight cancellations.

England Euro 2016 Squad Announcement Delayed England manager Roy Hodgson has postponed the announcement of his 23-man squad for Euro 2016, which was originally scheduled for Thursday. The official deadline for the Football Association to submit the squad to Uefa is 31 May. England are preparing for the tournament with warm-up fixtures against Turkey, Australia and Portugal before the finals commence in France from 10 June to 10 July. Arsenal's Danny Welbeck faces exclusion after sustaining a right knee injury during Sunday's 2-2 draw with Manchester City. Fellow Gunner Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, 22, has already been ruled out. Midfielder Jack Wilshere's fitness remains uncertain despite returning to Arsenal's first team following a 10-month absence due to a broken leg. Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson, 25, is recovering from knee ligament damage sustained last month, though manager Jurgen Klopp has expressed confidence he will be fit for the tournament.

Business Leaders Urge Government Action on Heathrow Expansion The head of Britain's leading business lobby group has called on the government to stop delaying and move forward with building a third runway at Heathrow Airport. CBI president Paul Drechsler will deliver a strong message to ministers at the organization's annual conference on Monday, urging them to "get on" with the controversial infrastructure project. His intervention comes after the Airports Commission published a landmark report in July recommending Heathrow expansion. The commission's findings suggested that a third runway would deliver significant economic benefits, adding £147bn to the UK economy and creating 70,000 jobs by 2050. The government has promised to make a final decision on the matter by the end of the year, though the project has faced years of political disagreement and delays. **Infrastructure Investment Priority** Mr Drechsler will also praise Chancellor George Osborne's decision to establish the National Infrastructure Commission, which will oversee £100bn in infrastructure spending across the country. "The commission is a chance to end the cycle of politicisation and procrastination that has plagued British infrastructure for decades," he will tell the conference. However, he will stress that the commission cannot be used as an excuse to postpone urgent decisions. "On airport capacity, we need strong political leadership and decisive action from government. Britain needs that new runway, so let's get it built," he will say. **Political Opposition and Controversy** Heathrow expansion has remained politically divisive for years. Prime Minister David Cameron famously opposed it whilst in opposition in 2009, declaring "no ifs, no buts" against expansion. The proposal faces opposition from multiple quarters, including rival airport Gatwick, London Mayor Boris Johnson—who advocates for an entirely new airport—as well as environmental groups and local residents concerned about noise and pollution. Reports emerged earlier this month that Sir Jeremy Heywood, the UK's most senior civil servant, wrote to ministers before party conference season warning them against publicly discussing the issue. **European Union Membership** Addressing the 1,000 delegates in London, Mr Drechsler will also discuss Europe, expressing hope that Britain remains in a reformed EU, noting that most CBI members believe membership advantages outweigh disadvantages.

**Charlton striker Nicky Ajose rejoins Bury on loan** Charlton Athletic striker Nicky Ajose has returned to Bury on loan for a third spell with the League One club. The 25-year-old joined the Addicks from Swindon Town in June 2016 and scored seven goals in 28 appearances. Ex-Manchester United trainee Ajose has had two previous loan spells with his hometown club, in 2010-11 and 2013. "I sat down with him and he said this was something he wanted, so I told him I wasn't going to stand in his way," Charlton boss Karl Robinson said. Libyan Rights Activist Salwa Bughaighis Shot Dead After Voting **BENGHAZI, Libya** — Prominent Libyan human rights activist and lawyer Salwa Bughaighis was shot dead in her Benghazi home on Wednesday, just hours after she cast her vote in the country's parliamentary elections and urged others to do the same despite ongoing violence. Armed men fought their way into Ms. Bughaighis' house before shooting her in what witnesses described as a targeted assassination. A medical source at a Benghazi hospital confirmed she died from a gunshot wound to the head. An eyewitness reported that she was attacked by five armed men, four of whom wore masks. Her husband, Issam, has disappeared following the attack, and relatives believe he has been kidnapped. The couple's whereabouts during the assault and Issam's current location remain unknown. Ms. Bughaighis was an outspoken critic of many of the armed groups which still control much of Libya. The killing is the latest in a string of attacks on politicians, activists, and journalists who have spoken out against the actions of certain militias operating with impunity across the country. The BBC's Rana Jawad in Tripoli reflected on Ms. Bughaighis' significance to Libya's political landscape. "It is not just Salwa Bughaighis' family and friends who are mourning her but many across Libya," Jawad said. "In 2011, in the early days of the uprising against Col Gaddafi, she was one of the few who kept me up-to-date on the deadly crackdown on protestors." Ms. Bughaighis was heavily involved in recent moves to establish a National Dialogue to address Libya's numerous problems. As a civil and women's rights activist, she frequently spoke bluntly about the dangers posed by Islamist groups and the failures since Gaddafi was ousted. As a lawyer, she championed the urgent need for the rule of law in post-revolutionary Libya. In a chilling final act of civic duty, Ms. Bughaighis gave a live television interview just hours before being killed. Despite a battle raging outside her home and the audible crackle of gunfire during the interview, she urged Benghazi residents to participate in the elections. Ms. Bughaighis had also been a strong critic of Muammar Gaddafi and joined some of the first protests against him in 2011. She later became an adviser to Libya's National Transitional Council, which governed the country during and directly after the uprising. She leaves behind three sons. U.S. Ambassador to Libya Deborah Jones called the killing "heartbreaking," describing it as a "cowardly, despicable, shameful act against a courageous woman and true Libyan patriot." The assassination follows the killing of a parliamentary candidate in the southern city of Sabha earlier this week, according to local media reports. Libya has suffered from persistent instability and violence since the downfall of Gaddafi in 2011. The government has struggled to disarm the various armed groups that remained from the war, leading to a security vacuum that has enabled targeted killings and lawlessness to flourish.

Fatal Incident in Cork: Woman Found Dead, Man Arrested Police were called to a residence on Murmount Avenue in Montenotte, Cork city, at 08:00 GMT on Monday, where they discovered a woman's body. A man in his 60s was transported to Mercy University Hospital Cork with non-life-threatening injuries. A man in his mid-20s was arrested at the scene and is currently being detained at Mayfield Police Station. According to RTE reports, the woman had been stabbed. The scene has been preserved for technical examination as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Pussy Riot's Tolokonnikova'Disappears' During Prison Transfer The husband of jailed Pussy Riot member Nadezhda Tolokonnikova says he has lost contact with his wife, whose whereabouts remain unknown as she is being transferred between Russian prisons. Pyotr Verzilov told US news website Buzzfeed that he had received no information about her current location, which authorities are keeping secret. He last knew her precise whereabouts on 21 October, when prison guards placed her on a train bound for a different facility. Ms Tolokonnikova was briefly sighted by a fellow passenger on 24 October as the train arrived in Chelyabinsk, a city in the Ural Mountains. Since then, there has been no further news. The 24-year-old activist had been serving her sentence at a penal colony in Mordovia, a region approximately 445km (275 miles) east of Moscow, home to labour camps dating from Joseph Stalin's notorious Gulag system. She recently staged hunger strikes to protest alleged abuses by prison staff. "They want to cut her off from the outside world," Mr Verzilov said, claiming the transfer order came from Moscow authorities. He added that his wife remains weak from two hunger strikes and accused officials of punishing her for speaking out. Ms Tolokonnikova and another Pussy Riot member were sentenced to two years' imprisonment for performing a crude protest song in a Moscow cathedral in February 2012. Their prosecution sparked international condemnation, though many Russians considered the act blasphemous. A third band member was released on appeal.

England's James Vince Opts Out of IPL to Focus on County Cricket and Test Ambitions England batsman James Vince has decided not to enter the Indian Premier League auction as he prioritizes his Hampshire captaincy and Test cricket aspirations, according to county director of cricket Giles White. The 24-year-old, who has represented England in both one-day and Twenty20 formats, averaged 28.57 in the 2015 County Championship.
