Despite his limited-overs success, including topping the T20 Blast run charts and impressing during England's T20 series against Pakistan in the UAE last November, Vince is keeping his focus closer to home. "James is very much in the space that he wants to play Test cricket," White told BBC Radio Solent. "I think that if he were to go to the IPL auction, for him at the moment, it might narrow that opportunity." White praised Vince's mature approach: "His head's screwed on. James is looking at it broadly and can see what's ahead of him right now." The right-hander took over Hampshire's captaincy from Jimmy Adams last season and believes performing well in early-season county cricket will strengthen his Test credentials. Vince is currently featuring for Karachi Kings in the inaugural Pakistan Super League and awaits England's T20 World Cup squad announcement on Monday.

Kenyan Bus Attack Hero Salah Farah Dies from Injuries Salah Farah, hailed as a hero for protecting Christian passengers during an al-Shabab attack in Kenya, has died from his injuries nearly a month after the incident. Mr Farah was travelling on a bus through Mandera in December when militants from the Somalia-based extremist group al-Shabab ambushed the vehicle. The attackers ordered passengers to separate into Muslims and Christians, a tactic used in previous attacks where Christians were executed while Muslims were spared. However, Mr Farah and fellow Muslim passengers refused to comply with the gunmen's demands. "They told us if you are a Muslim, we are safe," Mr Farah told the BBC's Bashkas Jugsodaay shortly after the attack. "We asked them to kill all of us or leave us alone." The attackers opened fire, and a bullet struck Mr Farah. He was transported to hospital in Nairobi, where he fought for his life before succumbing to his injuries. In interviews following the attack, Mr Farah explained his courageous stance: "People should live peacefully together. We are brothers. It's only the religion that is the difference." Inspector General of Police Joseph Boinnet praised Mr Farah as "a true hero" following news of his death. His brother Rashid expressed hope that the tragedy would promote religious harmony in Kenya. Mr Farah's selfless act of solidarity has resonated across Kenya, symbolizing unity in the face of terrorism that seeks to divide communities along religious lines. His sacrifice serves as a powerful reminder of the bonds that transcend faith.

Thomson Closes Gap on Le Cleac'h in Vendee Globe Race **Media playback is not supported on this device** British sailor Alex Thomson is closing in on race leader Armel Le Cleac'h in the Vendee Globe round-the-world yacht race, narrowing the gap to just 77 miles with fewer than 3,000 miles remaining. The 42-year-old Thomson, who rounded Cape Horn on Christmas Day after 48 days at sea, is attempting to become the first Briton to win the prestigious solo sailing competition. The Welshman had commanded the lead for most of the race before equipment trouble struck. Thomson lost his advantage when he suffered damage to his foil, allowing French sailor Le Cleac'h to overtake. Despite the setback, Thomson previously broke two race records, including reaching the Cape of Good Hope in record time. He briefly regained the lead near the Kerguelen Islands in the Indian Ocean on November 30. Both skippers are now heading north across the Atlantic towards the finish line at Les Sables-d'Olonne in France, with completion expected in eight days. Their pace has increased after navigating through the challenging Doldrums over the weekend. The Vendee Globe, held every four years since 1989, is renowned as one of the world's most demanding sporting challenges. Of the 138 sailors who have attempted the voyage, only 71 have successfully completed it. **Find out how to get into sailing with our special guide.**

National Teaching Service Scrapped After Pilot Fails to Meet Targets The government has scrapped plans for a National Teaching Service that was meant to deploy 1,500 outstanding teachers to struggling schools across England by 2020, after a pilot scheme failed to attract sufficient applicants. The initiative was announced with fanfare by then Education Secretary Nicky Morgan in 2015, promising to send "the country's best teachers and leaders to underperforming schools that struggle to attract and retain the professionals they need." A Department for Education spokesman confirmed that "following a review of the outcomes, we can confirm that we will not be progressing" with the scheme beyond its initial pilot phase in the North West. The National Teaching Service was designed to tackle educational inequality by deploying elite teaching staff to areas where schools struggled to recruit quality educators. In a speech to the Policy Exchange think-tank in November 2015, Mrs Morgan outlined the vision as part of a broader government commitment "to give every child an excellent education." "Too many places are lagging behind, meaning young people in these areas are not being given a fair shot," the government stated at the time. Under the original plan, NTS staff would work with schools for up to three years to drive up standards. The pilot, launched in September 2016, aimed to recruit up to 100 teachers and leaders for primary and secondary schools in the North West. However, according to the Times Educational Supplement, just 54 teachers were recruited after only 116 applied – falling significantly short of expectations. Despite the disappointing figures, the Department for Education maintained a positive tone about the pilot, saying officials were "pleased with the level of interest in the pilot and the calibre of the successful candidates." The spokesman added: "We recognise that it is vitally important that schools, particularly in challenging areas, can recruit and retain excellent teachers, and we are determined to continue to support them to do this. We will use the lessons learnt from the pilot to secure a better understanding of to support schools in the future, and will set out future plans in due course." The announcement comes as Thursday's Ofsted annual report highlighted serious problems in recruiting teachers and school leaders, particularly in northern England. School heads reported an "auction" for teachers in some areas. Labour's shadow education secretary, Angela Rayner, described Ofsted's verdict as "damning," adding: "We now learn that they're scrapping the much lauded National Teaching Service after just a year. Last week, we learnt that the Tories have missed their recruitment target for the fifth year in a row. And last year, the highest number of teachers left the profession in a decade. "The chronic teacher shortage continues to threaten standards under the Tories, and they are completely failing to take this crisis seriously."

**Connacht Secure Fifth Consecutive Victory with Bonus-Point Win Over Treviso** Connacht achieved a significant milestone by securing their fifth consecutive league victory for the first time since 2002, defeating Benetton Treviso in an entertaining Pro12 encounter at the Sportsground. The Irish province showcased their attacking prowess with second-half tries from Robbie Henshaw, Tom McCartney, and Matt Healy, though they ultimately fell short of claiming the bonus point they desperately sought in the closing stages. Craig Ronaldson's boot kept Connacht in control during the first half, landing three penalties to give the hosts a 9-5 lead at the interval. The opening 40 minutes saw two Ronaldson penalties establish an early 6-0 advantage before Treviso responded through Jayden Hayward's opening try after 26 minutes, showcasing his pace with a clear sprint to the try line. The second half belonged predominantly to Connacht. World Cup star Henshaw, making his first appearance for the province since the tournament and operating at full-back, crossed in the corner just two minutes after the restart to extend the lead. Despite Hayward claiming his second try to keep Treviso in contention, replacement hooker Tom McCartney powered over following an effective line-out move in the 51st minute. Matt Healy added Connacht's third try with five minutes remaining, setting up a frantic finish. Desperately chasing the fourth try needed for a bonus point, Connacht pushed forward in the dying moments but lost possession. Italy scrum-half Edoardo Gori capitalized on the turnover to grab a late consolation try for the visitors. The victory maintains Connacht's impressive form and marks a historic achievement for the Galway-based side, matching their best winning streak in two decades. Referee Ian Davies oversaw the contest, which demonstrated both sides' commitment to attacking rugby.

Asda Reports Decline in Sales as Supermarket Struggles Continue UK supermarket chain Asda has reported a 2.8% fall in like-for-like sales for the three months ending in March, highlighting ongoing challenges for the country's third-largest grocer as it battles to regain market share from discount rivals. While the figures represent a sequential improvement from previous quarters, analysts have cautioned that significant work remains for the struggling retailer to return to growth. The results stand in stark contrast to parent company Walmart's performance in the United States, where the retail giant posted a 1.4% rise in comparable sales during the same period. Asda's latest decline, though concerning, marks a considerable improvement from the devastating 7.5% quarterly sales drop reported in August last year. The results also showed marginal progress compared to the 2.9% decline recorded in the final quarter of 2016. Chief Executive Sean Clarke acknowledged the challenges ahead while expressing cautious optimism. "We're pleased that the momentum of Q4 has continued into the New Year with a third consecutive quarter of improvement," he said. "Despite this progress we are in no way complacent and there is still much for us to do." The supermarket experienced a 2% decrease in customer footfall during the period, while the average transaction value also fell by 0.8%, indicating both declining visitor numbers and reduced basket sizes. Asda has been hit harder than its fellow Big Four competitors—Tesco, Sainsbury's, and Morrisons—all of which have shown signs of recovery over the past year. The primary challenge comes from German discount chains Aldi and Lidl, which have aggressively expanded their UK presence, though their rapid growth has recently moderated. Tom Berry, associate retail analyst at GlobalData, explained Asda's particular vulnerability: "Asda's position as the main UK discounter prior to Aldi and Lidl's arrival, means they will suffer greatest in terms of losses in market share." Meanwhile, Walmart reported what it called a "solid first quarter" in the US, with sales reaching $117.5bn, meeting analyst expectations. The American retail giant has been investing heavily in e-commerce acquisitions to compete with Amazon, particularly as the online behemoth expands its grocery delivery operations. Industry observers note that Asda, once considered Walmart's crown jewel, has suffered from a strategic emphasis on profit margins over sales volume, contributing to its recent market share losses.

Health Officials Consider Withdrawing Consultant-Led Maternity Care Amid Staffing Crisis Health officials have suggested withdrawing consultant-led care at one of the region's three district hospitals due to a staffing shortage, sparking growing concern across North Wales. A protest was held in Rhyl this week to defend the maternity unit at nearby Glan Clwyd Hospital, with support now growing for the service at Wrexham Maelor Hospital. The other service at risk is at Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor. Prestatyn GP Dr Eamonn Jessup, chairman of the North Wales Local Medical Committee, expressed strong opposition to any changes. "We have to have three fully staffed maternity and obstetric units in north Wales," he said. "Any change to that particular system is going to increase risk for mothers and babies." The health board, still consulting on various proposals including retaining all services, emphasized that the quality and safety of maternity services was hugely important and said it looked forward to hearing feedback from the meeting. A public meeting is being held at the Catrin Finch Centre at Glyndwr University from 19:00 BST.

Chinese Fishing Vessel Crew Face Charges in Galapagos Marine Reserve The crew of a Chinese fishing vessel intercepted in Ecuador's protected Galapagos waters are facing potential prison sentences after authorities discovered an illegal catch of endangered sharks. The Fu Yuan Yu Leng 999 was discovered on Sunday within the Galapagos archipelago, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and marine reserve, carrying approximately 300 tonnes of fish. Most significantly, the majority of the catch consisted of sharks, including protected species such as hammerheads. Ecuador's environment minister Tarsicio Granizo announced Tuesday that a judge on San Cristobal island had ordered around 20 crew members to remain in custody pending trial. If convicted of trafficking protected species, they could face up to three years in prison. "Not necessarily all of the catch came from the marine reserve, but the fact that it included young sharks, even baby sharks, indicates that they could have been caught inside the reserve," Granizo told AFP news agency. Walter Bustos, director of Galapagos National Park, confirmed the vessel was the largest ever captured operating illegally within the marine reserve. The incident highlights ongoing conservation challenges in the region. In 2015, Ecuadorian authorities seized approximately 200,000 shark fins destined for Asian markets, where shark fin soup remains a prized delicacy at banquets. Conservation groups warn that continued demand for shark fins is driving endangered species toward extinction while fuelling illegal wildlife trafficking networks.

Justice Secretary Defends Feltham Prison Regime Despite Rule Breaches The Justice Secretary has acknowledged that prison regulations were breached at Feltham Young Offenders Institution, but disputes claims that conditions amounted to inhuman and degrading treatment, the High Court has heard. Liz Truss is contesting legal action brought by the mother of a teenage boy with mental health problems, known as AB, who was confined to his cell for 23-and-a-half hours daily. Her lawyer, Tom Weisselberg QC, admitted the isolation regime was "unlawful" but argued it was necessary due to the boy's "challenging" behaviour. Mr Weisselberg told the court that AB had a "history of assaulting staff" and had directed "rude, racist and threatening language" towards prison officers and fellow inmates. The teenager's racist remarks to Muslim and black inmates had inflamed tensions at the facility, making him a target within the prison population. The court heard that AB's "removal from association" breached Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which protects the right to private and family life, and violated prison regulations. Additionally, the boy did not receive the statutory minimum of 15 hours' education per week, constituting another breach of prison rules. However, Mr Weisselberg insisted that AB's behaviour required "very careful management" and defended the prison's response. "The prison has not sat on its hands," he said, arguing that staff were actively managing a difficult situation. The hearing continues as judges consider whether the isolation regime crossed the threshold into inhuman or degrading treatment.

Carlton Cole on Trial at Celtic as Bhoys Seek Striking Options Carlton Cole is training with Celtic as manager Ronny Deila considers adding the experienced striker to his squad. The 31-year-old former England international became a free agent after departing West Ham United at the end of last season. Deila expressed cautious optimism about Cole's potential arrival at Parkhead. "We have a good squad but we are always looking to improve," the Celtic boss stated. "We are happy he is here." The Norwegian manager acknowledged Cole's qualities as a target man but stressed the need for patience. "He's been good in the two exercises I've seen him doing but he needs more time. He hasn't trained for a while," Deila explained. The Celtic manager remained non-committal about the duration of Cole's trial period, saying only "we will see how it comes." Cole brings substantial experience, having earned seven England caps and scored 85 goals across 380-plus senior appearances for Chelsea, Aston Villa, and West Ham United.

Song Byeong-hun Holds Off Jordan Spieth to Win Singapore Open South Korea's Song Byeong-hun held his nerve on Monday morning to claim his maiden professional title at the Singapore Open, finishing one shot ahead of three-time major champion Jordan Spieth. The duo were among 13 players who had to finish their final rounds on Monday after Sunday's play at Sentosa Golf Club was curtailed by thunderstorms. American Spieth sank a five-foot birdie putt on the last hole for a five-under-par 66 to finish 11 under. Song, resuming on 12 under, parred his remaining three holes for a one-under 70 and victory by one shot. The world number 204 began the day with a testing 12-foot putt at the 16th, but a simple tap-in at the last secured his first professional victory after two second-place finishes on the Japan Tour. Song, 24, led from the second round and was five in front of Spieth heading into the final round.

Bigg Boss Tamil Faces Backlash Over "Insensitive" Mental Health Task A popular Indian reality show has come under fire for making contestants imitate mental health patients in what experts have condemned as an offensive and stigmatizing segment. Bigg Boss Tamil, which airs in Tamil Nadu, told contestants to act as if they were in a mental health facility. The contestants, in what looked like green hospital scrubs, started clapping their hands wildly and jumping around. Their display has been criticised as exaggerated, inaccurate and insensitive by experts. Dr Achal Bhagat, a Delhi-based psychologist, told the BBC that the episode was "outrageous". "It sustains the stigma that already exists against mental health patients in Indian society," he said. "Widely held perceptions that people who suffer from mental illness have no capacity and are dangerous have to be challenged." Dr Bhagat said the episode was indicative of a problem not just in the entertainment industry but in society as a whole. The word "mental" was often used as an insult and assumptions that people with mental health issues were dangerous were widespread. "This urgently needs to change," he said. Adding to the controversy, one of the contestants, Helen "Oviya" Nelson, who also participated in the episode, left the show soon afterwards, citing mental health issues. Bigg Boss Tamil, which airs every Saturday and Sunday, is one of the most popular shows in the southern state. Tamil actor Kamal Haasan who hosts the show, criticised the task and threatened to resign, saying it was "not in good taste". "I'm actually angry about it," he said in the following episode. "If it happens again, this show is not important to me." The show's legal consultant, C Rajasekar, told BBC Tamil's Pramila Krishnan that Bigg Boss Tamil follows "norms prescribed by the Information and Broadcasting Ministry". Asked about the widely-criticised episode, S Shekher, a member of Tamil Nadu's censor board, told BBC Tamil that imitating and mocking those with mental health issues "should have been avoided". The state censor board however does not have the authority to review entertainment shows produced for television. However, the Broadcasting Content Complaints Council (BCCC) advises against the use of "humour", "undesirable depiction of persons with disabilities" and "derisive and disparaging" references to their disabilities.

Arthur Simpson-Kent Arrives in UK After Arrest in Ghana Arthur Simpson-Kent has been arrested at Heathrow Airport following his arrival in the United Kingdom on a flight from Ghana. He has been taken to a west London police station for questioning. The arrest comes after the bodies of former EastEnders actress Sian Blake and her two young sons were discovered buried in the garden of their London home in Erith on 5 January. Ms Blake, aged eight-year-old Zachery, and four-year-old Amon had disappeared on 13 December. Post-mortem examinations revealed that all three victims died from neck and head injuries. Ms Blake, who portrayed Frankie Pierre in 56 episodes of EastEnders during 1996-97, had been suffering from motor neurone disease. Mr Simpson-Kent, the children's father, was apprehended by police officers on a beach in Ghana four days after the bodies were found. He had left the UK shortly after Ms Blake and the boys were reported missing. Scotland Yard is currently under investigation by the police watchdog regarding its handling of the missing persons inquiry and the three-week delay in discovering the bodies.

Roger Moore Praises Sam Smith's Bond Theme as Twitter Divides Over "Writing's On the Wall" Former James Bond actor Sir Roger Moore has praised Sam Smith's new theme song for the upcoming 007 film Spectre, calling "Writing's On the Wall" "very haunting and wonderfully orchestrated". However, the track's release has sparked fierce debate among fans and critics on social media. While Moore offered his seal of approval, Twitter users have been sharply divided over the song, with one critic branding it the "worst Bond theme ever". BBC entertainment correspondent Colin Paterson offered a more measured assessment, describing it as "good enough, but not a classic". The full version of the track runs for 4 minutes and 38 seconds and opens with the lyrics: "I've been here before / But always hit the floor." It continues: "I've spent a lifetime running, and I always get away. But with you I'm feeling something, that makes we want to stay." Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Paterson suggested the song tells the story of "a man deciding to quit it all for love". He compared its melody to Michael Jackson's 1995 single "Earth Song" and noted it was vastly superior to Madonna's much-criticised "Die Another Day" from the 2002 Bond film. The reaction from celebrities has been equally mixed. Comedian David Schneider greeted the release with the quip: "The name is Bland. James Bland." However, fellow comic Omid Djalili, who appeared in 1999's "The World is Not Enough", was far more enthusiastic, tweeting that the song had left him "in a broken heap" and declaring: "If you're not moved by this song you don't have a pulse." Smith makes history as the first solo male British artist to perform a Bond theme since Tom Jones sang "Thunderball" in 1964. The previous Bond theme, Adele's "Skyfall" from 2012, reached number two in the UK singles chart. Remarkably, no Bond song has ever topped the UK chart, and opinion remains divided on whether Smith's track will break that streak. Currently, Canadian pop star Justin Bieber holds the number one position and is expected to retain it when this week's chart is announced on Friday. Smith and his songwriting partner Jimmy Napes have stated they aimed to create something "timelessly classic". In a promotional video, Smith emphasised: "This isn't about me, about my life. I just hope people listen to it and think,'That's Bond'." The song's title apparently references a scene in the Spectre trailer where James Bond's name appears scrawled on a wall.

Worker Killed in Crossrail Tunnel Accident Identified Rene Tkacik, a 43-year-old Slovakian national, has been identified as the worker killed in a Crossrail tunnel accident. He died while spraying concrete 32ft down in a Holborn tunnel in central London during early morning hours on 7 March. A post-mortem examination was conducted Monday, with police requesting additional tests. The Crossrail project, spanning from Maidenhead to Shenfield through central London, ranks among Europe's largest engineering undertakings.

Actor David Huddleston Dies at 85 David Huddleston, the veteran character actor best known for playing the title role in the 1985 comedy "Santa Claus: The Movie" alongside Dudley Moore, has died at age 85. Born in 1930, the former US Air Force mechanic played the millionaire whom Jeff Bridges' character was mistaken for in the Coen brothers' 1998 comedy "The Big Lebowski." He previously starred with Dudley Moore in the 1985 film about the Christmas gift-giver. His widow said he died on Tuesday of advanced heart and kidney disease. "He'd always make you laugh," Sarah Koeppe told the Santa Fe New Mexican, saying her late husband had been "so amazed as he looked back at what happened in his life." Huddleston's other roles included the mayor in Mel Brooks's "Blazing Saddles" and a Republican senator in "The West Wing." He was nominated for an Emmy in 1990 for his guest appearance as Granpa Arnold in "The Wonder Years." Fellow actor Wilford Brimley remembered him as "a wonderful human being" who was "honest and kind and loyal." Besides Koeppe, he is survived by a son, a daughter-in-law and a recently adopted dog named Dooley.

Belfast Royal Academy Institute powered into the Ulster Schools' Cup final with a commanding 43-5 victory over Ballymena Academy at Kingspan Stadium. Tries from Zak Davidson and Niall Armstrong helped the holders to a 12-0 advantage at the break. The Belfast team surged clear in the second with Armstrong adding two more tries while Yasser Omar, Michael Lowry and Callum Reid also touched down. Ballymena did manage to register a try through Azur Allison. RBAI will play the winners of the second semi-final between Methodist College Belfast and Belfast Royal Academy at the same venue on Tuesday. Belfast Royal Academy were awarded a walkover in the quarter-finals after opponent Friends' were unable to field a team, with 17 of the their squad on a skiing trip in Austria.

EU Launches Legal Action Against Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic Over Refugee Quotas The European Commission has initiated legal proceedings against Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic for refusing to accept refugees under the EU's mandatory relocation scheme. Migration Commissioner Dimitris Avramopoulos said the three countries had ignored "repeated calls" from the EU's executive to take their share. Only 20,869 of the 160,000 refugees have so far been relocated in the EU. The three states could be referred to the European Court of Justice (ECJ) and eventually face heavy fines. The relocation plan was conceived in response to the large influx of migrants and refugees in 2015, in an attempt to relieve pressure on frontline states, mainly Greece and Italy, where the vast majority of migrants were arriving. EU countries agreed to relocate 160,000 asylum-seekers between them - though Romania, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary voted against accepting mandatory quotas. Hungary and Slovakia challenged the quota last month in the ECJ. While the UK and Ireland were exempt from the original 2015 proposal, Poland's previous government backed the plan, although its current Eurosceptic administration has since rejected it. The Czech Republic has accepted only 12 of the 2,000 it had been designated, while Hungary and Poland have received none. "I regret to see that despite our repeated calls to pledge to relocate, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Poland have not yet taken the necessary action," Mr Avramopoulos told journalists. "For this reason, the Commission has decided to launch infringement procedures against these three member states. I sincerely hope that these member states can still reconsider their position and contribute fairly." But Poland has already signalled it will not fall into line with the quota. "Each decision to relocate groups of migrants encourages thousands or millions more at the borders of Europe, to come to Europe, to get on boats and pontoons and risk their lives to reach the European continent," said Polish government spokesman Rafal Bochenek. Czech Prime Minister Bohuslav Sobotka stressed that his country too would not take part either, "with regard to the worsened security situation in Europe and dysfunctionality of the quota system". The quotas were based on the size and wealth of each country, but Austria and Denmark have so far not taken in any refugees either. Despite the small number of refugees relocated from Italy and Greece, the European Commission says the pace has quickened since January.

Man Injured After Gunshots Fired in Birmingham Police were called to Hamstead Road in the Lozells area of Birmingham at 01:10 GMT following reports of gunshots and disorder. West Midlands Police discovered a man suffering from minor injuries at the scene. The area has been cordoned off while officers conduct their investigation into the incident. Authorities are appealing for witnesses and have urged anyone with information to come forward and contact them.

Three Arrested in Connection with Surrey Woman's Death Three people have been arrested following the death of Robyn Mercer, 50, whose body was discovered in Walton Road, West Molesey, Surrey, on 14 March. Two women, aged 20 and 44, were detained Thursday on suspicion of conspiracy to pervert the course of justice. A 26-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder and conspiracy to burgle. All three suspects have been released on bail until 28 June pending further investigation.

Wales Defense Coach Shaun Edwards Backs Under-Fire Rob Howley Wales defense coach Shaun Edwards has leapt to the defense of interim head coach Rob Howley, praising his "attention to detail" and coaching abilities amid growing criticism of Wales' autumn performances. Howley is leading Wales through the 2016-17 season while regular boss Warren Gatland prepares for next year's British and Irish Lions tour to New Zealand. However, Wales' recent results have attracted negative attention, with a heavy 32-8 defeat to Australia bookended by unconvincing narrow victories over Argentina and Japan. Edwards, the former Wigan and Great Britain rugby league star, was keen to highlight Howley's strengths during a press conference ahead of Saturday's clash with South Africa. "He's excellent," Edwards said, specifically praising Howley's meticulous preparation. "The way he addresses the players - he's a very good head coach." The defense coach appeared unaware of the extent of criticism directed at Howley, who is in his second spell deputising for Gatland. Edwards pointed to Howley's track record, reminding critics that during his first stint as interim coach, Wales claimed the 2013 Six Nations championship. "I don't know what people have been saying about him to be honest. I just do my job," Edwards explained. "Every person is entitled to their opinion, but when you are a national coach it's important that you block everything out of your mind. You just do your job. "Rob Howley has only been in one Six Nations and he won it. He is a very good head coach, believe me." Wales face selection dilemmas ahead of the South Africa match, with record-cap holder Gethin Jenkins potentially unavailable due to a shoulder problem. The prop, who has earned 128 caps for his country, is considered doubtful for Saturday's encounter. However, there is positive news regarding number eight Taulupe Faletau, who returned to action for Bath in their victory over Bristol on Friday after missing Wales' autumn internationals with a knee injury. Lock Bradley Davies has been released back to the Ospreys to continue his injury rehabilitation. "We are looking at a pretty healthy squad," Edwards said. "Obviously we are hoping that Gethin's shoulder recovers. He's one of the greatest players Wales has ever had." Edwards acknowledged that while Wales responded "exceptionally" to their Australia defeat by beating Argentina, their performance against Japan fell short of expectations. A recurring concern has been interceptions, with Wales suffering from poor decision-making in all three autumn Tests. "We just made the wrong decisions at the wrong time. We have to be more accurate," Edwards admitted. "The attack coaches are working damned hard to make sure we are more accurate in those areas and if we do that it will be a start." With Wales sixth in the World Rugby rankings and South Africa dropping to fifth following their shock defeat to Italy, Edwards described Saturday's encounter as "must-win" for Wales and a "cup final" atmosphere.

Ireland's Fitzgerald Ruled Out of South Africa Tour as Springboks Name New Captain Ireland's preparations for their challenging three-Test tour of South Africa have suffered a setback with the news that Luke Fitzgerald has been ruled out of the squad due to injury. The 28-year-old Leinster back had been named in coach Joe Schmidt's 32-man squad for the tour just last week, but will now miss the opportunity to face the Springboks in what promises to be a demanding series. Fitzgerald's withdrawal could provide an opportunity for uncapped Connacht wing Matt Healy, who has been in excellent form this season. Healy capped off a terrific campaign with an impressive display on Saturday, putting himself firmly in contention for a call-up. Connacht full-back Tiernan O'Halloran represents another option for Schmidt as he considers his replacement options. A decision on Fitzgerald's replacement is expected within the next few days, with Healy currently the favourite to receive the call. Ulster's Craig Gilroy, who has been in outstanding form, could also be in the running to join the touring party. The injury adds to Ireland's mounting casualty list for the tour, which already includes wings Simon Zebo and Tommy Bowe, along with several key forwards including Cian Healy, Denis Buckley, Nathan White, Sean O'Brien, Peter O'Mahony, Josh van der Flier and Andrew Conway. Meanwhile, South Africa have announced that hooker Adriaan Strauss will captain the side for the series under new coach Allister Coetzee. The 30-year-old, who has 54 international caps and previously served as vice-captain in 2012 and 2013, will become the 57th Springboks captain. "Adriaan's leadership qualities are impressive and well-established and he has the respect of his team mates on and off the field," Coetzee said in a statement from SA Rugby. Strauss takes over from Jean de Villiers, who retired following last year's Rugby World Cup. The three-match series begins in Cape Town on 11 June, with subsequent Tests in Johannesburg and Port Elizabeth over the following two weekends.

Google Reverses Ad Ban on 9to5Google After Trademark Dispute In a sudden move that left a popular tech news site scrambling, Google abruptly disabled advertising on 9to5Google on February 24, citing a trademark violation over the site's name. The decision came as a shock, given that 9to5Google has been operating for years and maintains a close relationship with the search giant. The site discovered the problem when advertisements simply stopped appearing. In a blogpost, 9to5Google revealed that advertising revenue is their "lifeblood," generating a six-figure sum monthly, making the ban a significant financial blow. According to an official email shared by the site, a Google employee acknowledged the decision was "shocking and frustrating" but explained that the company must act quickly once a trademark violation is identified, regardless of whether it's detected "early on or much later." The employee also stated there could be no appeal process. In response to the crisis, 9to5Google turned to its readers for help, asking them to suggest alternative names for the site. However, just as suddenly as the ban was implemented, Google reversed course. On February 25, the company sent a brief message announcing it had "taken another look" at the issue and decided to restore the ad feed. Google has declined to provide further comment on the matter, leaving questions about the abrupt reversal unanswered.

Record Number of Red-Necked Phalaropes Breed in Scottish Islands Red-necked phalaropes, which migrate to Scotland's Western Isles, Orkney and Shetland during summer, have achieved record breeding numbers this year. RSPB Scotland reported that thirty-six breeding males were counted at their Fetlar reserve in Shetland, matching the highest number ever recorded at the site. The success extends beyond Shetland, with a pair breeding at Balranald reserve in North Uist for the first time in 31 years. Argyll, representing the species' most southerly UK breeding location, experienced its best season on record with six males present. Malcie Smith, RSPB Scotland's species and habitats officer for Shetland, expressed excitement about the results: "It's very satisfying that our work here is paying off and that birds are now breeding in record numbers." Notably, red-necked phalaropes display unusual gender roles, with males responsible for incubating eggs and raising chicks whilst females depart after laying.

Brighton 1-0 Nottingham Forest: LuaLua strikes to secure opening-day victory Brighton & Hove Albion began their Championship campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Nottingham Forest at the Amex Stadium, with winger Kazenga LuaLua's second-half strike proving to be the difference between the two sides. The Seagulls secured their first opening-day win since the 2011-12 season, delivering a performance that manager Chris Hughton described as deserving of the three points in what was a "typical Championship game." LuaLua found the breakthrough five minutes after half-time, beating Forest goalkeeper Dorus de Vries with a well-placed low angled shot that the Dutchman could not keep out despite his best efforts. The match was an entertaining affair with both sides creating chances throughout. Brighton looked the more threatening team, particularly as the first half progressed, though Forest served early notice of their intentions when Henri Lansbury's 30-yard free-kick struck the post and went wide. Brighton's Beram Kayal also hit the woodwork with a 20-yard effort midway through the opening period as the hosts began to assert their dominance. Israel international striker Tomer Hemed, making his debut for the club, came agonisingly close to opening his account in first-half stoppage time, but de Vries produced a stunning one-handed save to deny the new signing's header. Forest's task became more difficult when they lost midfielder Robert Tesche to a broken foot during the first half, a blow that manager Dougie Freedman described as "the last thing we need right now." Despite falling behind, the visitors threatened an equaliser in the closing stages, particularly after the introduction of teenage substitute Tyler Walker. Their best opportunity came from a quickly-taken long throw that Brighton failed to deal with properly, but Walker was unable to convert during the resulting goalmouth scramble. "It is a nice way in which to start the season," said Hughton after the match. "Kazenga is a winner and had a good all-round game. You want to see that from your wide players." Freedman remained philosophical despite the defeat: "We went down to a sucker punch and it's important for us to stay focused now. On another night we would have got something out of the game." Bobby Zamora, who re-signed for Brighton earlier in the week after a 12-year absence, was not included in the matchday squad.

Bravery Denies Ryan Moore Historic Four-Timer at Doncaster Bravery stormed to victory in a thrilling finish at Doncaster, denying jockey Ryan Moore what would have been a remarkable fourth consecutive win on the opening day of the Flat racing season. The 20-1 outsider, ridden by Daniel Tudhope and trained by David O'Meara, prevailed in dramatic fashion after Moore had already secured an impressive 575-1 treble earlier in the day. Moore's winning streak included Ballet Concerto in the Spring Mile Handicap, Tupi in the Cammidge Trophy Stakes, and Kool Kompany in the Doncaster Mile Stakes. Donncha finished third with Gabrial in fourth place. "He was held up slightly on the far side of the field, so to get that win was a real result," O'Meara told ITV. "It means an awful lot. You like to hit the ground running - sometimes you come here and loads of bubbles are burst, but it's nice to win. It tells you you've probably done the right thing over the winter." BBC Sport horse racing correspondent Cornelius Lysaght noted the palpable relief from the betting industry, which avoided a massive pay-out on combination bets just a week before the Grand National's potential uncertainties. For O'Meara's team, the victory was particularly sweet after enduring near-misses in this competitive race previously. The trainer admitted to taking time adjusting after relocating stables within Yorkshire, but confirmed things are now "well on track again."

Teenage Boy Dies After Stabbing in Walthamstow A 17-year-old boy has died after being stabbed in Walthamstow, east London, becoming the ninth teenager to be fatally stabbed or shot in the capital this year. Paramedics discovered the teenager after being called to High Street, Walthamstow, shortly after 23:30 BST on Sunday. Despite being rushed to hospital, the victim succumbed to his injuries. According to the Metropolitan Police, the victim was walking along the street with friends when two men on bicycles approached them at the junction with Buxton Road. An altercation ensued, during which the teenager was stabbed. Detective Chief Inspector Matt Bonner is leading the investigation and appealing for witnesses. "At this stage we are investigating whether the two suspects left the area on bicycles. If you were in the area last night and saw anything that may help us, or you have information that will assist, please get in touch," he said. While officers are still awaiting formal identification, the victim's next of kin have been informed. No arrests have been made in connection with the incident. ## Rising Knife Crime Statistics This latest fatality is part of a disturbing trend in London. Of the nine teenage deaths this year, six have resulted from stab wounds, whilst three were shootings. BBC Home Affairs Correspondent Danny Shaw noted that there have been 29 fatal stabbings in London this year, including six teenagers, compared to 23 by this time in 2016. The incident marks the second fatal stabbing in London within 48 hours. A 23-year-old man was found unconscious by police on Waterloo Road in Uxbridge, west London, early Saturday morning and later died from stab wounds. Official statistics released last month revealed knife crime in London increased by 24% in the year to April, with 12,074 recorded offences. Knife crime resulting in injury also rose by 21% to 4,415 incidents. ## Police Response Last week, the Met Police launched the latest phase of Operation Sceptre, their campaign to combat knife crime. During the week, 393 arrests were made, including 73 for possession of an offensive weapon or knife and 144 following stop and search operations. The taskforce, comprising approximately 100 officers, has been deployed to knife crime hotspots across the capital. Mayor of London Sadiq Khan emphasized a zero-tolerance approach: "My message today is clear: if you carry a knife in London, we will catch you and arrest you."

**Gabrielle Giffords Launches Gun Control Initiative on Anniversary of Shooting** Former Arizona Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords has launched a new political action committee aimed at curbing gun violence, marking the second anniversary of the shooting that nearly claimed her life with a direct challenge to the powerful gun lobby. The initiative, Americans for Responsible Solutions, was unveiled Tuesday as Ms. Giffords and her husband, former astronaut Mark Kelly, pledged to match the financial and political muscle of pro-gun groups like the National Rifle Association. The announcement comes amid renewed national debate over gun control following last month's elementary school massacre in Newtown, Connecticut, that left 20 children and six adults dead. "In response to a horrific series of shootings, Congress has done something quite extraordinary - nothing at all," Ms. Giffords and Mr. Kelly wrote in an opinion piece published in USA Today. The couple, both gun owners themselves, criticized lawmakers for failing to act despite mounting gun violence across the nation. The new organization aims to counter the NRA's influence on Capitol Hill, where the gun rights group spent more on lobbying in 2011 than all gun control organizations combined. "Until now, the gun lobby's political contributions, advertising and lobbying have dwarfed spending from anti-gun violence groups. No longer," Ms. Giffords declared. The couple emphasized they do not seek to disarm responsible gun owners but rather to achieve "reforms to reduce gun violence and prevent mass shootings." This will require "matching gun lobbyists in their reach and resources," they wrote. In a television interview with ABC News, Mr. Kelly did most of the speaking as his wife continues her recovery from the January 8, 2011, shooting in Tucson, Arizona, where she was meeting with constituents. The gunman killed six people and wounded 13 others, including Ms. Giffords, who suffered a severe brain injury. The initiative's launch coincides with ongoing discussions at the White House about potential gun control measures. Vice President Joe Biden, leading the administration's gun violence task force, is scheduled to meet with gun safety organizations and victims' groups on Wednesday. He will also hold talks later this week with the NRA and other gun-owner representatives, as well as members of the entertainment and video game industries. President Barack Obama has called on Congress to reinstate a ban on assault weapons, limit high-capacity ammunition magazines, and close loopholes that allow some gun purchases to proceed without background checks. The White House has promised to present specific proposals by the end of January. Last Friday, Ms. Giffords visited Newtown to meet with families affected by the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting. The visit sparked controversy when Connecticut State Representative DebraLee Hovey, who represents Newtown, wrote on Facebook: "Gabby Gifford [sic] stay out of my towns!!" The politician later apologized for the comment. While some pro-gun lawmakers have indicated they are reconsidering their positions following the Newtown tragedy, political observers note that attention to gun control may have waned as Congress focused on reaching a fiscal cliff deal to avert automatic tax increases and spending cuts. Another round of budget deadlines looms at the end of March, potentially overshadowing the gun debate once again. Ms. Giffords and Mr. Kelly have also consulted with New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg, a prominent gun control advocate, as they develop their strategy to challenge what observers call one of America's most powerful special interest groups.

Jersey Care Inquiry Hears Testimony of Harsh Treatment in Post-War Years A former resident of Jersey's care system has told a public inquiry how his treatment deteriorated dramatically after World War Two, transforming his experience from relatively bearable to "hell." Giffard Aubin, 79, testified before the Independent Jersey Care Inquiry about his experiences between 1943 and 1951, describing severe punishments, psychological abuse, and rampant bullying. Speaking emotionally, Mr Aubin expressed bitterness and anger over his treatment, saying he hoped such abuse would never be repeated. The inquiry, which has cost £6.5 million, is examining abuse within Jersey's care system from 1945 to the present day. Mr Aubin's testimony revealed a stark contrast between wartime and post-war care. During the German occupation, he described conditions as austere but relatively stable. German soldiers even made Christmas presents for the boys and escorted them to beaches that were otherwise prohibited to islanders. However, following liberation, despite improvements in diet and clothing, recreational outings ceased and conditions worsened significantly. Mr Aubin said certain boys were targeted for mistreatment by the matron, while insufficient staffing allowed older boys to bully younger residents with impunity. "I remember having darts thrown at you - they were different to the darts you get today, much heavier - and if you moved you were hit with an armoury stick, which would cut you," Mr Aubin recalled. He also described being subjected to electric shocks from generator wires applied to his wet legs. Fear of reprisals prevented him from complaining. So profound was his trauma that Mr Aubin said he still refuses to celebrate Liberation Day because he "did not feel liberated." The panel also heard from Violet Renouf, who entered the Jersey Home for Girls in 1942 aged six. She described having stinging nettles placed in her bed as punishment for bed-wetting and being locked in isolation for three weeks after a false accusation of theft. Mrs Renouf said her care experience had lasting effects on her relationships with her own children.

Lagan Valley Election Poster Ban Agreement in Doubt After Parties Dispute Statement Confusion has emerged over an alleged agreement between political parties to ban election posters in Lagan Valley, after two parties denied finalising the deal. On Friday, UUP MLA Robbie Butler posted what he described as a'joint statement' from the DUP, UUP, SDLP and Alliance Party on Facebook, announcing a voluntary poster ban during their respective campaigns. The statement was also shared by the DUP's Paul Givan and SDLP councillor Pat Catney. However, by Friday evening, spokespersons for both the SDLP and Alliance Party clarified that no final agreement had been reached, casting doubt on the validity of the arrangement. The published statement read: "As political parties in Lagan Valley, we recognise the desire from the public to minimise disruption during this election campaign and believe this is the right step to take. Engagement with the electorate will be focused on the door step." According to the document, the agreement would remain in place until 18:00 GMT on 1 March, after which candidates could place limited posters outside polling stations. The statement specified that no posters would appear on main or arterial roads unless directly outside polling stations, and that the ban would not extend to billboard or mobile advertising. Current MLAs in the constituency include Paul Givan, Edwin Poots and Brenda Hale of the DUP, Jenny Palmer and Robbie Butler of the UUP, and Trevor Lunn of Alliance. The statement warned: "If this agreement is broken by one party, it is no longer valid." A Northern Ireland-wide poster ban was previously proposed by Ulster Unionist chair Lord Empey last year but was dismissed by the DUP as "a stunt".

Eastleigh 1-1 York City: Basement Boys Snatch Unlikely Point at Ten Acres York City pulled off a surprising result at the Silverlake Stadium, earning a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Eastleigh despite their lowly league position. The home side dominated proceedings in the opening period, with striker Michael Mandron proving a constant threat. Gary Mills's struggling York side had to work tirelessly to contain the forward, successfully keeping the Spitfires at bay until the interval with the score goalless. Eastleigh's pressure finally told shortly after the break. Mandron rose majestically to meet Andy Drury's inviting cross, glancing his header past the York goalkeeper to give the home fans something to celebrate. However, York City refused to accept defeat. Simon Heslop produced a moment of individual brilliance that defied his team's position at the foot of the table. The midfielder controlled a long ball over the top expertly on his chest before coolly sliding his shot underneath the advancing Ryan Clarke to restore parity. The match became increasingly fractious as both sides searched for a winner. Michael Green and James Constable both received yellow cards for Eastleigh, while York's Richard Brodie was also booked. Mills made tactical changes, introducing Richard Brodie, Shaun Rooney and Callum Rzonca, whilst Eastleigh countered with substitutions of their own, bringing on Jai Reason, Ryan Bird and Jamie Cureton. Despite late pressure from both teams, neither could find a decisive goal, leaving York to celebrate a valuable point in their battle against relegation. Report supplied by the Press Association.

Deloitte Under Investigation Over Mitie Accounts Audit Accounting firm Deloitte is facing a regulatory investigation over its auditing of outsourcing giant Mitie's accounts, the Financial Reporting Council has announced. The Financial Reporting Council (FRC) said its investigation related to Mitie's financial statements for the years ending 31 March 2015 and 2016. Deloitte said it took the investigation "very seriously" and would co-operate fully. Last month, Mitie reported a full-year loss after being hit by charges stemming from an accounting review. One-off costs of £88.3m meant the company - which provides pest control, cleaning, security and healthcare services - posted an operating loss of £42.9m for the year to March. The accounting review, which was carried out by KPMG, found the company's accounting was "less conservative" than its peers. In a statement, Deloitte said: "Audit quality is of critical importance to our firm and we are committed to maintaining the highest professional standards. We take this investigation very seriously and will co-operate fully with the Financial Reporting Council." At Mitie's annual general meeting last week, nearly 30% of the company's shareholders voted against Deloitte remaining as its auditor. Mitie said it was undertaking a tender process over the next three months and would "announce a new external auditor in due course". Last month, the FRC said it had begun an investigation into the auditing of BT's financial statements by PwC, covering the years 2015 to 2017. In January, BT wrote down the value of its Italian unit by £530m after what it called years of "inappropriate behaviour". PwC was replaced in June as BT's auditor by KPMG.

Dozens of Firefighters Battle Major Gorse Fire Near Homes in Northern Ireland More than 60 firefighters worked through the night to tackle a major gorse fire that came dangerously close to residential properties on a hill behind Barley Lane on Friday night, with flames reaching within yards of some homes. The blaze, which broke out near St Mary's High School, was reported at approximately 20:50 BST and required crews to battle the inferno for more than five hours before it was finally extinguished at 02:00 BST. The incident was among 161 emergency calls that fire crews responded to since 18:00 BST on Friday. Local residents gathered to watch the dramatic scene unfold, with some moved to tears as the flames advanced perilously close to their properties, located just a mile from the city centre. Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service (NIFRS) Group Commander Brian Stanfield confirmed that eight fire appliances were deployed to combat the blaze. Faye Broadway, a resident living nearby, described the distressing scenes to BBC News NI, stating that some neighbours had fled their homes in nightwear. She witnessed two elderly women "in tears" desperately searching for missing pets amid the chaos. Ms Broadway's partner, David Cadden, recounted the terrifying moment they spotted thick black smoke billowing over their house, followed by flames rising above tree level. "We decided to just take a walk up to make sure that there was no-one in danger, because it looked quite serious," he explained. Mr Cadden described harrowing scenes of residents evacuating: "I walked up to the back of their houses and the fire was literally a stone's throw away, with ash falling down and embers hitting the roof. They were all running out of the house in their pyjamas, with dogs in their hands, and running across the street." Firefighters were forced to move crowds back for safety as ash and embers fell on spectators. Some crews were deployed from as far away as Belfast on what proved to be an exceptionally busy night for the service. Earlier on Friday, firefighters revealed they had responded to 221 gorse fires over the previous five days, with 92% started deliberately. Officials warned that recent dry, sunny weather had "provided a tinderbox landscape" conducive to such fires.

Cuba Announces Ambitious Shark Conservation Plan Cuba has unveiled a comprehensive shark conservation strategy developed in partnership with a United States environmental organization, marking a significant step in marine protection efforts. The plan will require fishermen to systematically record and limit their shark catches while establishing new protected fishing zones. This initiative is particularly crucial given that approximately 20% of the world's 500 shark species inhabit Cuban waters. Shark populations globally have experienced dramatic declines due to overfishing, the lucrative shark fin trade, and unintentional bycatch. Cuba has previously prohibited the practice of harvesting sharks solely for their fins. The conservation plan emerged after two years of collaboration with the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF). Daniel Whittle, EDF's Cuba programme director, highlighted that Cuban waters support shark populations through relatively healthy coral reef systems. "Cuba is considered the crown jewel of the Caribbean, principally because of its incredible coral reef ecosystems, its mangroves, its seagrasses," Whittle explained. The EDF emphasizes that shark conservation also offers economic benefits, as ecotourism continues expanding and marine resources become increasingly valuable assets. Cuba is now developing a broader regional shark conservation initiative.

Fox-Sky Deal Decision Delayed Until After UK General Election The deadline for a decision on 21st Century Fox's proposed takeover of Sky has been extended until after the UK general election, Culture Secretary Karen Bradley announced. The decision, originally scheduled for 16 May, has been postponed until 20 June to avoid the deal becoming entangled in election politics. Ms Bradley said the extension followed discussions with all parties involved, including Ofcom, the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), and the Cabinet Office Propriety and Ethics team. Regulators are currently examining the £11.7bn deal on grounds of media plurality and broadcasting standards. Fox has offered to pay £10.75 per share for the 61% of Sky it doesn't already own, valuing the entire company at £18.5bn. The proposed acquisition has raised concerns due to media mogul Rupert Murdoch's extensive UK media holdings. Both Sky and Fox are controlled by Murdoch, who also owns The Times and The Sun newspapers. His sons Lachlan and James serve as joint chairmen and chief executive respectively of Fox. Part of Ofcom's investigation includes assessing whether Sky's potential new owners meet the "fit and proper" standard required of broadcast licence holders. European competition authorities have already approved the deal, but UK regulators continue their scrutiny of its implications for media concentration.

Harry Potter Fans Face Four-Hour Online Queue as New Cursed Child Tickets Sell Out Theatre fans spent hours online on Thursday attempting to secure some of the 250,000 new tickets released at 11:00 BST for Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, only to see them quickly appear on resale websites at inflated prices. "Failed to get #CursedChild tickets after queuing for four hours," wrote one frustrated Twitter user. "Now loads on sale for hundreds of pounds on StubHub." Tickets are currently being offered on the secondary marketplace for up to £1,000, despite official vendors Nimax and ATG selling admission to the two-part stage production for significantly less—between £15 and £70 per part. A spokesperson for the show confirmed that whilst the newly-released tickets had sold out, returned and other late release tickets would become available daily. Additionally, an online lottery held every Friday releases 40 tickets for each performance the following week. The production has warned customers purchasing from resale websites that they risk being refused admission. "Tickets purchased through either of our official ticketing platforms must not be sold or advertised for sale on the internet, in newspapers or elsewhere. Any ticket advertised for sale in this way will be automatically void," the spokesperson said. StubHub defended its marketplace, stating that sales are "driven by supply and demand" and that sellers "set the price for what they think the market will bear." Harry Potter and the Cursed Child became one of the UK's hottest tickets well before opening at London's Palace Theatre in June. Thursday's ticket release followed the publication of Jack Thorne's script, approved by Potter author JK Rowling, which became the fastest-selling book in the UK this decade. Follow us on Twitter @BBCNewsEnts, on Instagram, or email entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

Space Station Gets Window Clean 250 Miles Up Two Russian cosmonauts ventured outside the International Space Station on Wednesday to tackle an unusual cleaning job - washing a dirty porthole window whilst floating 250 miles above Earth. The window had become grimy over the years from exhaust fumes produced by visiting spacecraft docking at the station. During their six-hour spacewalk, the cosmonauts also installed new equipment and performed routine maintenance work on the exterior of the orbiting laboratory. This marked the fourth spacewalk at the ISS this year. For station commander Gennady Padalka, it was his tenth career spacewalk, adding to his record as the person who has spent more cumulative time in space than anyone else in history.

Taliban Attackers Killed After 26-Hour Siege at Kandahar Air Base **KANDAHAR, Afghanistan** - Afghan security forces killed the final Taliban attacker late Wednesday, ending a devastating 26-hour siege at Kandahar Air Base that left 38 civilians and two police officers dead, the defense ministry announced. The prolonged assault on one of Afghanistan's largest military installations highlighted significant security vulnerabilities as the last gunman held out alone for several hours before being neutralized. The attack also wounded at least 37 people, including 17 military personnel and four police officers, according to ministry statements. The Taliban assault began Tuesday when insurgents, described by the militant group as "martyrdom seekers," breached the compound's perimeter. The attackers wore military uniforms and carried light and heavy weapons, according to Tolo News TV. After penetrating the first gate, they occupied an old school building where they exchanged heavy fire with Afghan forces. During the siege, witnesses reported that militants seized families as hostages, using them as human shields during the firefight. The airport compound houses both Afghan military and civilian sections, as well as a NATO base. US Army Col. Michael Lawhorn confirmed that the attackers "never physically entered the airfield" and reported no coalition casualties. The brazen attack, which the Taliban characterized as "thunderous attacks on foreign and hireling personnel," coincided with a regional peace conference in Islamabad where Afghan President Ashraf Ghani appealed to Pakistan for assistance in brokering peace negotiations with the Taliban. Security analysts described the incident as a major intelligence failure, noting that attackers successfully smuggled weapons into an area supposedly secured by Afghan National Security Forces. The assault follows the Taliban's brief seizure of Kunduz in September, demonstrating the group's continued capability to conduct sophisticated operations.

London Bombing Victim Led Quiet Life Dedicated to Family Izabela Brandt, a 38-year-old Polish cleaner, was among the victims of the 7 July 2005 London bombings, killed in the Russell Square blast that claimed 26 lives, including the suicide bomber. On that fateful morning, Ms Brandt left her Wood Green home at 8:00 AM and boarded a Piccadilly Line train bound for her cleaning job in Gunnersbury. When she failed to arrive at work, her brother Pawel Iskrzynski launched an urgent search, spending days traversing London whilst clutching his sister's photograph. Police eventually confirmed her death through DNA samples, delivering the devastating news to the family. Mr Iskrzynski described his sister as an intensely private individual who eschewed smoking and alcohol, maintaining only two close friendships. "She would normally return home from her job and stay indoors and did not pursue leisure activities," he told police in a statement read at the inquest. Ms Brandt's life had been marked by entrepreneurship and sacrifice. After leaving school in 1981, she established her own restaurant business in Poland. She married Arek Brandt shortly thereafter, and the couple had two children: Hubert and Natalie. When the restaurant closed in 2002, Ms Brandt made the difficult decision to move to London, leaving her husband to care for their children. The couple separated a year before her death. In London, she shared accommodation with her brother and worked various jobs, including bar work, before settling into cleaning. She sent most of her wages to Poland to fund her children's education. Tragically, her daughter Natalie had arrived in the UK on 7 July specifically to visit her mother. Hubert was residing in Sweden at the time of the tragedy.

Samaritans Sees Record Contact Numbers After Free Helpline Launch The Samaritans charity has reported a significant surge in people seeking support, handling more than 5.7 million cases throughout 2016. The organisation attributed the increase of nearly 300,000 contacts compared to the previous year largely to the introduction of a free confidential helpline in autumn 2015. Previously, callers faced a charge of two pence per minute. The figures, released to mark the beginning of Volunteers' Week, showed total contacts reached 5,703,830 in 2016, up from 5,404,331 in 2015. These contacts included helpline calls, emails, text messages and face-to-face support sessions. Ruth Sutherland, Samaritans chief executive, emphasized that suicide is both complex and an inequality issue, with factors such as deprivation increasing risk. "Even two pence a minute was enough to deter some callers, which is why we were determined to make all calls to Samaritans free," she said. Ms Sutherland praised the volunteers for making a difference by supporting growing numbers of people in crisis, but stressed the organisation is "just one part of the equation." She added that suicide is preventable rather than inevitable, calling on everyone from politicians and health workers to employers and media to play their part. Volunteers' Week, organised by the National Council for Voluntary Organisations, runs from 1-7 June.

York's Rougier Street Becomes One-Way for All Vehicles A major traffic change has been implemented on York's Rougier Street, with all vehicles now required to travel in a westerly direction. Previously, cars and lorries were restricted to one-way traffic, but buses and taxis used a separate two-way section. The change now means all traffic will travel in a westerly direction. Safety barriers were introduced earlier this year after a second person was killed crossing the road in two years. Sgt Louise Lucas died after being hit by a bus in March, while Daniel Foss, 37, died in 2013. The changes were brought in after a review of the system and the withdrawal of the city's Ftr Metro bendy bus - which the layout was designed for. David Hopkins, cabinet member for environment and transportation, said: "The change to a one-way route for buses and cars will hopefully mean the route is safer for pedestrians."

Gareth Bale injury: Real Madrid boss Zinedine Zidane uncertain over return date Real Madrid manager Zinedine Zidane has expressed uncertainty over Gareth Bale's return from injury ahead of the Champions League final. The Wales international forward, 27, has not played since tearing a calf muscle against Barcelona on 23 April. La Liga title favourites Real face Juventus in the 3 June European final. "We have to take it day by day but for now he's not with us and I don't know when he will be, but I hope it's soon," said Real boss Zinedine Zidane. Real have three La Liga games remaining this season, starting with Sunday's home match with Sevilla (19:00 BST). They are second to Barcelona - who visit Las Palmas at the same time - on the head-to-head rule, but have a game in hand.

African Nations Cup Qualifiers: Djibouti and Madagascar Claim First-Leg Victories Djibouti celebrated a historic breakthrough in African Nations Cup qualifying, securing a commanding 2-0 home victory over South Sudan in their preliminary round first-leg encounter. The win marks a significant milestone for the East African nation as they seek a place in the main qualifying phase. Goals from Hamza Abdi Idelh and Med Salam ended Djibouti's prolonged goal drought and put them in pole position to advance to Group C, where they would face formidable opposition in Burundi, Gabon, and Mali in the race to Cameroon 2019. The victory proved an encouraging debut for Mauritanian coach Moussa Ghassoum, who was overseeing his first match in charge of the Djiboutian national team. Meanwhile, South Sudan's troubling away form continued, extending their winless record on the road with their fifteenth goal conceded in qualifiers while managing just one score. In Wednesday's other fixture, Madagascar edged Sao Tome e Principe 1-0, courtesy of an own goal from Jordao Diogo. The result marked a winning start for new French manager Nicolas Dupuis, who faced fellow debutant coach Gustavo Clemente on the opposing bench. Despite missing several key injured players, Madagascar fielded a competitive squad, flying Europe-based players directly to Sao Tome to minimize costs while supplementing them with domestic talent. The winners will advance to Group A alongside Equatorial Guinea, Senegal, and Sudan. The third preliminary tie featured an Indian Ocean derby, with Comoros defeating Mauritius 2-0 in Moroni on Friday. The result gives Comoros a substantial advantage ahead of Tuesday's return leg at Stade Anjalay in Pamplemousse on April 28. All three winning teams now hold commanding positions heading into their respective second legs.

Two Men Seriously Injured in Separate Attacks in Renfrewshire Two men have been seriously assaulted in separate incidents in Renfrewshire over the weekend. A 45-year-old man was attacked outside the Anchor Bar in Paisley at approximately 21:30 on Saturday. He was taken to the Royal Alexandra Hospital where his condition was described as stable. In an unrelated incident, a 30-year-old man sustained facial injuries and head lacerations following an assault on Graham Street in Johnstone at 00:40 on Sunday. He was also transported to the Royal Alexandra Hospital for treatment. Police Scotland confirmed the two incidents are not connected and have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

Hatton Garden Raider Used Fake Freedom Pass to Travel to Heist Brian Reader, the 76-year-old ringleader who admitted involvement in the notorious Hatton Garden heist, used a fraudulent Freedom Pass to travel to central London on the night of the audacious burglary, a court has heard. The elderly criminal used the counterfeit senior travel card to board the 96 bus from near his Dartford home before alighting at Waterloo East station at approximately 6:30 pm on April 2, prosecutors told Woolwich Crown Court. The raid, which took place over the Easter weekend, saw thieves make off with valuables worth up to £14 million from safety deposit boxes in London's diamond district. Detective Constable Matthew Hollands revealed that the Freedom Pass was discovered in Reader's wallet following his arrest. However, the card was not registered in Reader's name but rather in the name of "Mr T McCarthy" and did not bear Reader's photograph. The court previously heard that Reader withdrew from what has been described as England's "largest burglary" when the gang encountered difficulties accessing the vault on their first attempt. New evidence presented by Detective Constable Jamie Day, the first Flying Squad officer at the scene, suggested that the still-unidentified red-haired burglar known only as "Basil" appeared to have accessed the building using a key. CCTV footage, captured by the building's only functioning security camera, showed a white van driven by defendant John Collins arriving at approximately 8:30 pm. Two men wearing high-visibility vests were seen exiting the vehicle. Subsequent footage showed "Basil" granting access to the building via an internal fire escape, followed by other men carrying tools, wheelie bins, and equipment. In a dramatic courtroom demonstration, jurors were shown a full-size polystyrene replica of the 25cm by 45cm hole drilled through the vault wall. Prosecutor Philip Evans cautioned: "I must point out it says it's for visual purposes only, do not attempt to climb inside." Three defendants deny conspiracy to commit burglary, whilst a fourth denies conspiracy to conceal or transfer criminal property. Reader and three co-conspirators have already pleaded guilty and await sentencing. The trial continues.

Thailand Offers Naval Base for Stranded Migrants as Trafficking Camps Discovered Thailand has announced it will establish a "floating naval base" to assist thousands of migrants stranded at sea, though authorities insist only those requiring serious medical treatment will be brought ashore. The move comes as the region grapples with a humanitarian crisis involving migrants from Bangladesh and Myanmar, many of whom have been victims of human trafficking. The Thai Prime Minister, Prayuth Chan-ocha, revealed this week that the naval operation would involve seven ships, two surveillance aircraft, and two helicopters patrolling the Andaman Sea. However, the BBC's Jonathan Head in Bangkok suggests the initiative appears designed to keep migrant boats at a distance rather than demonstrate a genuine commitment to helping those in distress. "If anyone is injured or sick, they can be treated at hospitals in Thailand but will face illegal entry charges - it is up to them to decide," the Prime Minister stated, emphasizing that migrants brought ashore would still be considered illegal arrivals. The announcement follows the discovery of horrific trafficking camps in the Malaysian jungle near the Thai border. Malaysian police teams began investigating a series of camps on Tuesday, finding evidence that migrants had been held in makeshift prisons constructed from wood and barbed wire. Malaysian national police chief Khalid Abu Bakar described the scene as shocking, noting clear signs of torture at the facilities. "We were shocked by the cruelty," he told reporters, though he declined to provide specific details about the abuses uncovered. Authorities believe the camps were used by human trafficking gangs to hold migrants for ransom before only recently being abandoned. The discovery mirrors similar findings in Thailand at the beginning of May, when graves were uncovered on the Thai side of the border. Those earlier discoveries prompted Thailand to intensify its crackdown on trafficking routes used to transport Bangladeshi migrants and Rohingya Muslims from Myanmar through Thai territory toward Malaysia. This crackdown had the unintended consequence of forcing traffickers to send migrants by sea instead, leaving thousands stranded in boats that no country initially wanted to accept. The UN's refugee agency estimates that approximately 3,000 people have now reached land, but another 2,600 may still be adrift at sea. In Myanmar, authorities have charged 20 people with human trafficking-related offences. The suspects were arrested from a vessel carrying 200 migrants from Bangladesh that was rescued last week. Under international pressure, Malaysia and Indonesia agreed last week to stop rejecting migrant boats and provide temporary shelter. Thailand has also agreed to stop towing boats away from its territory and has permitted US Navy aircraft searching for migrants to operate from Thai military bases - but only under Thai military command, after initially refusing an American request last week. Thailand is scheduled to host a regional meeting on Friday to address the ongoing crisis and coordinate a regional response to the humanitarian emergency.

Deadly Bomb Attack Strikes Pakistani Refugee Camp **JALOZAI, Pakistan** - A devastating bomb attack has killed numerous people at a refugee camp in Pakistan, with reports indicating victims were queuing for food rations when the explosion occurred. The blast struck the Jalozai camp, which provides shelter for people fleeing violence in Pakistan's tribal districts along the Afghan border - an area known as a sanctuary for Taliban and al-Qaeda-affiliated militants. While the camp serves a humanitarian purpose, police officials say it has also been exploited as a hiding place by some militant groups. The explosion, for which no organization has yet claimed responsibility, left a crater at the scene. Police official Fuad Khan reported that the bomb detonated in a car parked near the administration office, where refugees were both collecting rations and registering as new arrivals. "I saw about 20 casualties around me as the smoke and dust cleared," Khan told AFP news agency. Live television footage captured ambulances rushing victims to nearby hospitals, while authorities worked through wreckage of mangled vehicles to gather evidence. Such attacks on refugee camps in Pakistan are exceptionally rare. However, the BBC's M Ilyas Khan notes that security forces last week detained individuals connected to the militant group Lashkar-e-Islam. Police suspect Thursday's bombing may have been retaliation for those arrests. The attack comes at a sensitive time for Pakistan, which on Wednesday announced national elections scheduled for May 11. This will mark the country's first democratic transition from one elected civilian government to another. Security concerns are overshadowing election preparations, though the outgoing government's reforms now permit political parties to campaign in tribal areas for the first time - part of efforts to combat militancy in these volatile regions.

Cardiff Blues Confident of Luring Leigh Halfpenny Back to Wales Cardiff Blues are positioning themselves as the ideal destination for Wales full-back Leigh Halfpenny, with head coach Danny Wilson emphasizing that player welfare and international performance would take precedence over financial considerations. The 26-year-old star is out of contract with French Top 14 side Toulon at the end of the current season and faces a crucial decision about his future. While the Blues acknowledge they cannot match the lucrative wages offered by wealthy European clubs, Wilson believes they can provide something potentially more valuable: optimal player management to keep Halfpenny in "peak" condition for international duty. "The best interests of the player internationally would be at the front of our minds," Wilson stated, highlighting a key differentiator in their recruitment pitch.
