Defra will continue to monitor the situation and take necessary precautions to prevent the spread of the disease. Bird keepers are advised to remain alert and report any suspicious symptoms to the authorities promptly.

Two former miners from Thoresby colliery in Nottinghamshire have been diagnosed with pneumoconiosis, a lung disease caused by inhaling dust, after undergoing CT scans paid for by the Union of Democratic Mineworkers (UDM). The diagnosis has sparked concerns that many more ex-miners may be suffering from the disease, which can be difficult to detect using traditional X-ray tests. Ray Nunn and Crawford Hunter, both 51, had previously been given the all-clear after undergoing X-rays at work, but the CT scans revealed that they had developed pneumoconiosis. The pair, who were made redundant when the colliery closed last summer, said they felt "let down" by their former employer, UK Coal, for not providing more comprehensive testing. The UDM had paid for five former miners to undergo CT scans, which provide a more detailed image of the lungs than traditional X-rays. Two of the five miners tested positive for pneumoconiosis, prompting union president Jeff Wood to accuse UK Coal of failing its workers by not offering the scans. Wood said that the company had claimed that the cost of CT scans was too high and that X-rays were sufficient, based on the advice of their medical advisers. Nunn and Hunter, who worked at the Thoresby pit for over 30 years, said that they had always been told that their X-rays were "satisfactory", but they had suspicions that the tests were not good enough. Nunn, who was a miner for 35 years, said that he had concerns about the quality of the X-ray tests, and Hunter described the day he received his diagnosis as "devastating". The UDM and a group of MPs, including Nottinghamshire's Alan Meale and Mark Spencer, are now calling on the government to fund CT scans for all living ex-miners. The MPs have sent a letter to the government, signed by 25 cross-party MPs, urging them to take action to detect and prevent pneumoconiosis. The government and UK Coal have yet to respond to the BBC's requests for comment. With an estimated 120,000 former miner workers still alive today, the UDM is warning that many more may be suffering from the disease, and that urgent action is needed to address the issue.

Unrest Continues in Burundi as Protester is Shot Dead A protester was shot dead by police in the capital city of Bujumbura, Burundi, amidst ongoing unrest in the country. The incident occurred in the opposition stronghold of Musaga, where a witness reported that the protester was shot in the back. This latest incident comes after a failed coup attempt against President Pierre Nkurunziza last week, in which senior officials from the army and police were accused of involvement. Despite the turmoil, President Nkurunziza was seen playing a game of football with friends in the capital, seemingly unaffected by the chaos. In a speech on state radio, he downplayed the unrest, stating that only a small part of the capital was affected, while the rest of the country remained peaceful. He urged those who have fled the country to return, but the UN refugee agency reports that over 105,000 people have already sought refuge in neighboring countries. In response to the growing tensions, President Nkurunziza has announced a 10-day delay in the parliamentary elections, which were originally scheduled for next Tuesday. The decision was made after a recommendation from the electoral commission, and comes after calls from the African Union and EU for a postponement to allow for dialogue and ease tensions. The presidential election is still set to take place in June, despite criticism from opponents who claim that Nkurunziza's bid for a third term is unconstitutional.

ANZ Bank to Refund Millions to Affected Customers Over Interest Payment Error ANZ Bank has announced that it will be refunding millions of dollars to its customers after a system error resulted in incorrect interest payments on some accounts. The error, which dated back to 2007, affected approximately 0.5% of savings accounts each month, with the majority of refunds being for amounts of A$35 or less. According to Emily Kinnear, ANZ's media spokesperson, the issue was first reported to the bank in 2013, and a thorough review has been conducted to resolve the problem. The bank has apologized to its customers and has begun the process of reimbursing those who were underpaid. However, the bank has stated that it will not be recouping the amounts that were overpaid to some customers. The Australian Securities and Investment Commission (ASIC) has been informed of the matter, and the regulator has praised ANZ for taking its breach reporting obligations seriously. ASIC's deputy chairman, Peter Kell, stated that the refund payment included an additional amount to recognize the time elapsed since the initial breach. The error is estimated to have affected around 100,000 customers, with many owed less than A$5. The bank expects to complete the reimbursement process by the end of this week. This move comes as ANZ posted a record annual cash profit of A$7.2 billion last month, marking a 1% rise on cash profits from the previous year. Despite this, the bank has faced criticism in the past over its fees and practices, including a landmark court ruling that some of its late payment fees were unfair.

British Airways has announced that it will be bringing work on the new Boeing 787 Dreamliner to its base near Cardiff Airport, starting from 2016. The news was confirmed by Chairman Keith Williams at the opening of a £3.3m extension to the University of South Wales' aerospace centre in Treforest. This significant development is expected to create new opportunities for the region and further solidify Wales' position as a key player in the aerospace industry. The Boeing 787 Dreamliner is a state-of-the-art aircraft that uses 20% less fuel than similarly sized planes, making it an attractive option for airlines looking to reduce their environmental impact. British Airways will be operating 24 of these aircraft by next year, and the maintenance work will be carried out at its base in the Vale of Glamorgan, where 738 employees are currently based. The announcement is a welcome boost to the local economy, and Mr. Williams emphasized the potential for growth and expansion in the region. "What you can see is opportunity as we expand for Wales to expand at the same time," he said. The aerospace industry is a significant contributor to the Welsh economy, with 160 companies employing over 23,000 people and generating a combined turnover of £5bn. The University of South Wales' aerospace centre, which opened four years ago, is playing a crucial role in developing the skills and expertise needed to support the industry. The new extension includes a second hangar, maintenance and repair workshops, and an aircraft simulator, providing students with hands-on experience and training on industry-ready equipment. The university has also partnered with British Airways to offer an aerospace engineering degree, which includes technical training with the airline on real aircraft. Professor Julie Lydon, Vice Chancellor of the University of South Wales, highlighted the importance of the industry and the demand for skilled engineers. "It's a really important industry, it produces around £60bn across the world, and we want to be part of it," she said. "The investment here enables our students to work with industry on industry-ready kit and then to go into the world and make their contribution." Despite the competitive nature of the industry, with countries like Lithuania and Poland vying for business, Professor Lydon noted that students are still able to secure jobs easily due to the high demand for aircraft engineers. The news is a significant vote of confidence in the Welsh aerospace industry, and it is expected to have a positive impact on the local economy. With six of the world's top 10 aerospace and defence firms having bases in Wales, the region is well-positioned to continue playing a major role in the industry. As the sector continues to grow and evolve, it is likely that Wales will remain a key player, driven by its highly skilled workforce and world-class facilities.

A 21-year-old man has lost his life in a tragic knife crime incident in the St Ann's area of Nottingham. Reuben Morris-Laing was found outside the Premier Express store on Robin Hood Street shortly before 21:30 GMT on Wednesday. Despite being rushed to the Queen's Medical Centre, he sadly died from his injuries. Nottinghamshire Police have confirmed that the incident is being treated as a knife crime and have increased patrols in the area to reassure the community. A cordon remains in place at the scene as investigators work to piece together the events surrounding the attack. A post-mortem examination is currently underway, and Mr. Morris-Laing's relatives have been informed. The incident has sparked calls for tougher penalties for knife crime, with Nottingham City Council's leader, Jon Collins, urging the government to introduce mandatory prison sentences for those found guilty of knife-related offenses. Collins expressed his sympathies to the victim's family and friends, stating that the community must work together to tackle the scourge of knife crime. The police are working closely with partners to catch the perpetrator and prevent similar tragedies from occurring in the future.

London Transport Museum is set to unveil its Hidden London project, offering exclusive tours of the city's secret underground sites. One of the main attractions is Down Street in Mayfair, a former station that operated from 1907 to 1932 and was converted into a bomb-proof bunker for the prime minister during World War Two. The site also served as the main hub for coordinating the country's railways. In addition to Down Street, tours will also be available at Euston Station's passageways and Clapham South's deep-level bomb shelter, which is located 180 steps beneath the surface. This shelter has a rich history, having been used as a refuge during the Blitz, a base for Caribbean migrants in 1948, and a hub for visitors to the Festival of Britain in 1951. Tickets for the tours will go on sale on April 20, with the first tours scheduled to begin next month.

Tiger Woods' Ranking Plummets to 104, Lowest in Over 20 Years Tiger Woods, the 14-time major winner, has dropped to 104 in the world rankings, his lowest position in over two decades. The 39-year-old American's ranking has suffered due to his indefinite break from the sport, which he announced after withdrawing from the Farmers Insurance Open on February 6. Woods has been struggling with back problems and has described his recent performances as "unacceptable for tournament play". The last time Woods was outside the top 100 was in September 1996, when he was ranked 221. However, he quickly turned his fortunes around, winning the Las Vegas Invitational the following week and beginning his ascent to the top. Woods is hopeful of returning to competitive golf at the Masters, starting on April 9, but has stated that he will not return until he can "compete at the highest level". With 79 PGA Tour victories under his belt, Woods will be looking to regain his form and climb back up the rankings. His fans will be eagerly waiting to see if he can make a successful comeback.

A recent survey conducted by RSPB Scotland has revealed that hedgehogs are still a common sight in many Scottish gardens, despite their drastically declining population. The survey, which involved nearly 15,000 wildlife enthusiasts, found that 57% of participants spotted hedgehogs in their gardens or outdoor spaces. This is a significant finding, given that the hedgehog population in the UK has dwindled from an estimated 30 million in the 1950s to less than one million today. In contrast, other wildlife species such as the great crested newt and moles remained elusive, with only 2% of participants catching a glimpse of the former and over half of gardens failing to spot the latter. Foxes, on the other hand, were the most common garden visitors, with 64% of participants spotting at least one throughout the year. According to James Silvey, species and habitat officer at RSPB Scotland, the decline of garden wildlife is a growing concern. "Unfortunately, such garden wildlife and the sounds and sights it creates are becoming less and less familiar for many people," he said. To combat this, RSPB Scotland is encouraging families to spend more time outdoors and reconnect with nature through their Wild Challenge initiative. By participating in activities such as mini-beast safaris and planting for wildlife, families can take their first steps towards a wild adventure and help preserve Scotland's precious wildlife.

Wales Looks to Make History Against England in Euro 2016 As Wales prepares to face off against England in their highly anticipated Euro 2016 match, manager Chris Coleman is staying focused on the ultimate goal: reaching the last 16. With a win, Wales would achieve this milestone, but Coleman is cautious not to get ahead of himself. "The big thing for us is getting through," he said. "It's not about beating England and not getting through." The match, which will be the 102nd between the two sides, has been surrounded by intense media hype, with players from both teams exchanging comments about their respective squads. England midfielder Jack Wilshere claimed his team was superior, while Wales forward Aaron Ramsey countered that his team was the best. Gareth Bale also weighed in, saying that he and his teammates are prouder and more passionate about representing their country. However, Coleman is not concerned about the mind games and verbal sparring. "We can't worry about upsetting the opposition, whoever they are," he said. "It's about what happens on the pitch. All that other stuff is irrelevant." Wales has a poor record against England, with only 14 wins in 101 matches, but this team has already made history by ending a 58-year absence from major tournaments and winning their opening game at the European Championship. Defender Neil Taylor points to last year's qualifying win over Belgium, then ranked second in the world, as a turning point for the team. "We got over that massive hurdle," he said. "That was the moment we realized we could be a threat against anybody." With this newfound confidence, Wales is ready to take on England and prove themselves as a force to be reckoned with. As Taylor said, "We know the threat we carry, and on our day, we feel we can beat anybody, whether it's England or anyone else." The stage is set for an exciting and intense match, and Wales is ready to give it their all.

Residents of Derby have been plagued by swarms of flies emanating from the Shows Waste Management site in Slack Lane, making everyday tasks such as cooking and cleaning a daunting challenge. The infestation, which has affected approximately 3,000 households and businesses, has been ongoing for weeks, prompting the Environment Agency to launch an investigation into the cause of the swarms. Despite efforts to alleviate the issue, a significant amount of waste remains at the site, with estimates suggesting between 700 to 1,000 tonnes still await removal. Shows Waste Management has removed 3,018 tonnes of waste, but unforeseen circumstances, including weather and transport issues, have hindered the completion of the process. The situation has had a profound impact on residents, who have been forced to take drastic measures to cope with the fly infestation. Amanda Cairns, a resident of the affected area, described the difficulties she faced, saying, "You couldn't cook without flies landing on your food, and you had to constantly sterilize your worktops." Another resident, Melissa Marriott, reported being unable to take a bath without flies getting into the water, and resorted to buying an electric fly killer to combat the problem. The Environment Agency has confirmed that the fly issue has been resolved since early June, but the situation remains a concern for residents, who are calling for compensation for the distress and disruption caused. However, the agency has stated that this is a civil matter, and not their responsibility. Shows Waste Management has assured residents that all efforts are being made to clear the site completely, but the incident highlights the need for effective waste management and regulation to prevent such situations from arising in the future.

A chair with a rich history has sold for a substantial amount, far exceeding the seller's expectations. The 1930s chair, which was once owned by renowned British author J.K. Rowling, was originally picked up for free in Edinburgh, Scotland. Before rising to fame, Rowling used the chair as her trusty writing companion, typing out the first two books of the Harry Potter series while seated in it. The chair, which features hand-painted phrases by Rowling, including "I wrote Harry Potter while sitting on this chair," was auctioned off to benefit her charity in 2002. It was later purchased by Gerald Gray from Salford in Greater Manchester in 2009, after his daughter, a Harry Potter fan, spotted it on eBay. Gray has announced plans to donate 10% of the winning bid to Rowling's charity, Lumos. The new owner of the chair has chosen to remain anonymous. The sale of the chair is a testament to the enduring popularity of the Harry Potter series and the significance of the chair's role in the author's writing process.

A 49-year-old man, Peter Gifford, has been sentenced to six years in prison for conspiring to launder $500,000 (£320,000) after being convicted in his absence at Truro Crown Court. Gifford, from Budock, Falmouth, and his partner Penelope Lawton, 52, have a history of fraudulent activities, having previously been convicted of mortgage fraud and sentenced to three years in jail. According to police, the couple is believed to be on the run with their two teenage children, and a European Arrest Warrant has been issued. They were last seen traveling to France via the Eurotunnel in January, just before a separate fraud trial. In their absence, they were found guilty of three counts of fraud and sentenced to three years for each charge, to run concurrently. The investigation into Gifford's activities began in 2011, when police discovered banking irregularities in his accounts and seized his computer. It was found that he had received $500,000 from a US account, which was linked to a fraudulent investment scheme in Germany. Gifford spent the money quickly on luxury items, including a new Range Rover and a holiday to the US. The five-year investigation involved collaboration between Devon and Cornwall Police, the FBI, and German authorities. Gifford's conviction and sentencing are a significant outcome, but the search for him and his partner continues. Police urge anyone with information on their whereabouts to come forward, as the couple remains at large with their children.

Ministers have announced a significant investment in flood protection measures for the city of St Asaph in Denbighshire, with £3m allocated for the 2016-17 financial year. An additional £3m will be spent on improving coastal defences in north Wales, bringing the total investment in flood protection to £6m. However, the total cost of the flood defence project in St Asaph is estimated to be £7m, leaving a funding shortfall of £1m. The ongoing work in St Asaph aims to protect over 400 homes that were affected by severe flooding in 2012. The project includes improvements to St Asaph old bridge and the restoration of a small stream along the River Elwy. Natural Resources minister Carl Sargeant emphasized the importance of minimizing the effects of flooding and keeping communities safe. Former mayor John Roberts expressed concerns about the timeline for the project's completion, stating that it may take up to six years to finish. This has left residents anxious and uncertain about their future. Roberts noted that the prolonged wait has caused significant distress, with many residents living in fear of future floods. Natural Resources Wales, which is overseeing the project, has confirmed that the funding will be allocated over two financial years, and they are working to secure the remaining funds needed to complete the scheme.

Ghana's Black Stars Receive Boost as Kwarasey Returns to the Fold The Ghana national football team, the Black Stars, have received a significant boost ahead of their upcoming matches against Mozambique. Goalkeeper Adam Kwarasey, who plays for MLS side Portland Timbers, has returned to the national set-up after a two-year absence. Kwarasey's last appearance for the Black Stars was at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. Ghana coach Avram Grant convinced the 28-year-old shot-stopper to make a comeback, and he will join the squad for their matches against Mozambique later this month. The Black Stars are currently top of Group H with six points from their opening two games. Captain Asamoah Gyan and midfielder Mubarak Wakaso are also included in the squad. However, Swansea forward Andre Ayew will miss out due to an ankle injury. The Black Stars will host Mozambique on March 24 in Accra before playing the return leg in Maputo four days later. With Kwarasey's return and a strong squad, Ghana will be looking to maintain their lead in the group and take a step closer to qualifying for the next stage. The team's coach, Avram Grant, will be hoping that Kwarasey's experience and skills will make a significant impact in the upcoming matches.

Protesters in the Chinese city of Ningbo have claimed a significant victory after the local government announced that it would scrap plans to expand a chemical plant. The decision came after days of violent clashes between protesters and police, with demonstrators opposing the project due to environmental concerns. On Friday, crowds attacked police, and on Saturday, over 1,000 protesters were dispersed, with reports of scuffles, arrests, and tear gas being used. Despite the government's announcement on Sunday that the project would not go ahead, protesters remain skeptical. "There is very little public confidence in the government," said protester Liu Li. "Who knows if they are saying this just to make us leave and then keep on doing the project?" The protests in Ningbo are part of a growing trend of environmental activism in China, as the country's rapid economic growth has taken a heavy toll on the environment. With a once-in-a-decade change of national leaders looming, protesters are seizing the opportunity to make their voices heard. The incident highlights the increasing awareness and concern among Chinese citizens about pollution and the need for sustainable development.

A 61-year-old man has been sentenced to a minimum of 30 years in prison for the brutal murder of a father-of-three who was found dead in the boot of his taxi. Colin Cheetham, from Ripley, was found guilty of murdering 43-year-old Stuart Ludlam, whose body was discovered at Cromford Station in Derbyshire on September 17 last year. During the trial at Nottingham Crown Court, prosecutors revealed that Cheetham had meticulously planned the killing, with no apparent motive other than a desire to shoot a "complete stranger". The court heard that Mr. Ludlam had been made to kneel in the boot of his taxi before being shot in the head. Cheetham, a former member of a gun club, had used a mobile phone purchased from a supermarket in Derby to lure Mr. Ludlam to the isolated location. Police investigations found that Cheetham had spent a significant amount of time researching train timetables and scouting out the location, including taking photographs of various train stations, including Cromford. Officers also discovered a camera and bottles of urine at Cheetham's house, which was described as chaotic despite his careful planning of the crime. Det Ch Supt Tony Blockley, from Derbyshire Police, described Cheetham as an "evil man" who had carried out a "despicable act" with no apparent motive. He speculated that Cheetham may have committed the crime simply to satisfy his fascination with firearms, leaving many unanswered questions for Mr. Ludlam's family and friends. Mr. Ludlam, from Darley Dale, Derbyshire, was a father of three whose body was discovered by a holidaymaker, Peter Noble, who dialed 999. The community was left shocked and saddened by the senseless murder, and many are still struggling to come to terms with the events that unfolded. In a related development, Andrew Brough, 57, from Heanor, Derbyshire, has pleaded guilty to firearms offenses in connection with the investigation and will be sentenced on July 22. As the case comes to a close, the family and friends of Mr. Ludlam are left to pick up the pieces and try to move on from the tragic loss of a loved one. The sentence handed down to Cheetham reflects the gravity of his crime, and it is hoped that he will one day be able to provide some explanation for his actions. However, for now, the community is left to mourn the loss of an innocent man who was brutally taken from his family and friends.

Violent Clashes Erupt in Baghdad as Protesters Demand Reforms A wave of protests swept through the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, as demonstrators, largely comprised of Shia Muslims, took to the streets to express their outrage over corruption and security failures. The protests turned violent when security forces fired tear gas and live bullets to disperse the crowds, resulting in at least 50 injuries. In response to the unrest, authorities imposed a curfew, which has since been lifted. The protesters, who managed to break into the city's government area for the second time this month, accused the government of neglecting much-needed reforms as it struggles to combat the Islamic State group (IS) and address declining oil revenues. The demonstrators also stormed the prime minister's office and parliament, which are located in the heavily fortified Green Zone. Prominent Shia cleric Moqtada Sadr condemned the use of force against the protesters, describing their movement as a "peaceful [and] spontaneous revolt." Sadr, who has a significant following in Iraq, has been a vocal critic of the government and has called for radical reforms to address the country's deep-seated problems. The protests come as Iraq's government, led by Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi, struggles to implement reforms and stamp out corruption. Despite promises to create a government of technocrats, al-Abadi has faced significant opposition from lawmakers, who are deeply divided along party and religious lines. The country's system of sharing government jobs has long been criticized for promoting unqualified candidates and encouraging corruption, with Iraq ranking 161st out of 168 countries on Transparency International's corruption perceptions index. As the situation in Baghdad remains volatile, concerns are growing about the ability of the government to address the grievances of its citizens and provide stability in a country that has been ravaged by conflict and sectarian violence. The protests are a stark reminder of the challenges facing Iraq as it seeks to rebuild and recover from years of turmoil. With the IS group still controlling large swaths of territory and the economy struggling, the government must find a way to respond to the demands of its citizens and provide a more stable and secure future for all Iraqis.

Dani Alves has completed a move to Paris Saint-Germain, signing a two-year deal with the French club. The 34-year-old right-back had been linked with a move to Manchester City, where he would have reunited with his former Barcelona coach Pep Guardiola. However, City were unwilling to match the £230,000 a week salary that PSG offered, and Alves has instead opted to join the Ligue 1 giants. Alves' arrival at PSG was announced with a video of the player printing his name and number on a shirt. The Brazilian defender expressed his excitement at joining the club, stating "Believe me, I am coming to Paris to win." He also acknowledged the club's growth into a European football powerhouse and is eager to be a part of the project. Manchester City, meanwhile, remain in the market for a right-back, with Tottenham's Kyle Walker their top target. The club has yet to agree a fee with Spurs, leaving them without a recognised right-back ahead of their pre-season tour of the United States. Despite this, City are said to be relaxed about the situation, and will continue to pursue their top targets in the coming weeks. Alves' move to PSG marks the latest high-profile transfer of the summer, and fans can keep up to date with all the latest news on our dedicated football transfers page.

Great Britain's boxing squad had a mixed day in Bulgaria, with two wins and two losses in the quarter-finals. World number two Whiteside secured a unanimous decision against Greece's Koutsogeorgopo in the 51kg class. Ryan also advanced with a split decision against Sweden's Alexiusson in the 60kg category. However, Chantelle Cameron lost a unanimous decision to Russia's Ordina in the 64kg quarter-final. Natasha Gale will box for a guaranteed medal in the 75kg category on Sunday. Other British and Irish boxers competing outside of the GB squad also saw action, with England's Resztan, Wales' Eccles, and Ireland's Browne all suffering quarter-final defeats.

A US district judge has rejected a request for a recount of presidential votes in Pennsylvania, citing a lack of evidence that the state's voting system was compromised. Green Party candidate Jill Stein had sought the recount, along with those in Michigan and Wisconsin, due to concerns that voting machines are vulnerable to hacking. Donald Trump narrowly beat Hillary Clinton in all three states, including Pennsylvania where he won by approximately 44,000 votes out of six million cast. Judge Paul Diamond stated that there is "no credible evidence" of a hack and "compelling evidence" that the voting system was not compromised. The ruling comes after a recount in Wisconsin reaffirmed Trump's victory, and a judge in Michigan halted a recount last week. Despite the efforts, correspondents say the recounts are unlikely to change the final result, with Clinton's campaign cooperating with Stein's efforts but remaining silent on the matter.

Actor Freddie Fox is set to voice the iconic character Dennis in the upcoming BBC series "Dennis and Gnasher Unleashed". The 27-year-old, who comes from an acting dynasty, expressed his excitement about taking on the role, saying "As a life-long fan of Dennis, I am honoured to voice him for a new generation." Fox, who has previously appeared in stage productions such as Romeo and Juliet, will make his debut as Dennis later this year. The 52-part series will feature Dennis and his dog Gnasher getting into mischief and mayhem, while trying to outsmart their arch-nemesis Walter. The show will utilize CGI 3D techniques, bringing the beloved characters to life in a new and innovative way. Dennis will still sport his signature red and black striped T-shirt and spiky hair, although his trusty catapult will not be making an appearance. Fox's casting marks a new era for the character, who has previously been portrayed in cartoon animation form. The actor's other credits include the 2014 film Pride and a current West End production of Sir Tom Stoppard's play Travesties, alongside Tom Hollander. With his energy and enthusiasm, Fox is sure to bring a fresh spin to the character, and fans of all ages can look forward to the new series.

UK's BMX Team to Gain Competitive Edge with Cutting-Edge Technology In a bid to improve their performance ahead of the Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro next year, the UK's BMX team has partnered with defence firm BAE Systems to utilize innovative technology. The partnership has resulted in the development of a system that uses miniature infrared lamps and sensors to track the cyclists' movements, providing valuable data to enhance their techniques and race strategies. The technology, originally designed as part of a "sense and avoidance" system for unmanned commercial aircraft, has been adapted to record the trajectory of the cyclists in the air after they make their jumps, as well as their movements on the ground. This data is then transmitted to an app, which provides real-time feedback and suggestions for improvement. The app displays its findings immediately after each lap, allowing the athletes to compare their performance to previous runs and make adjustments accordingly. According to Liam Phillips, a member of the BMX squad, this technology will revolutionize the way they train. "In an elite sport such as BMX, where riders are travelling around 40kph and spending more than 40% of the race in the air, every millisecond counts and one imperfection in form can put you at a disadvantage," he commented. "This will allow us to analyze our techniques with a new-found precision." The UK's BMX team was previously reliant on data from timing loops buried into test tracks for feedback. However, the additional data provided by the new system will offer deeper insights into how team members change speed as they handle jumps. Kelvin Davies from BAE Systems explained that the app will enable athletes to compare their performance to other runs, whether it's on the same day or a different day, and make adjustments to improve their techniques. The use of such cutting-edge technology in BMX racing is not common, according to Richard Moore, a former racing cyclist and journalist. While road-based champions often have access to advanced technology, BMX racing has traditionally been seen as a more laid-back sport. However, with its inclusion in the Olympic Games since 2008, the stakes have increased, and the UK's BMX squad is taking a proactive approach to gain a competitive edge. Moore noted that most countries do not place a strong emphasis on BMX racing, and it's unlikely that any other team is using similar technology. "By contrast, in road cycling, they have data for everything, and on the track, it's still getting there," he said. The UK's BMX team is taking a serious approach to the sport, and this partnership with BAE Systems demonstrates their commitment to excellence. As the Olympic Games approach, the UK's BMX team is poised to benefit from this innovative technology. With the ability to analyze their techniques in real-time and make data-driven adjustments, they may gain a significant advantage over their competitors. The partnership between the UK's BMX team and BAE Systems is a prime example of how technology can be leveraged to improve performance in elite sports, and it will be exciting to see the results in Rio next year.

Welsh Conservatives Pledge to Treble Free Childcare for Working Parents The Welsh Conservatives have announced plans to treble free childcare for working parents in a bid to help them return to work and boost the economy. The pledge, made by Shadow Education Minister Angela Burns, aims to increase the current provision of 10 hours of free childcare, which is often spread over five days, making it difficult for parents to take advantage of. According to Ms Burns, the current system is not supporting working parents, and the Welsh Conservatives are committed to changing this. "Welsh Conservatives will work towards trebling free childcare for working parents to help parents return to work so they can provide for their family and help deliver a stronger economy," she said. The Tories' pledge comes as Wales is at risk of falling behind England, where the UK government has promised to double free childcare for parents of three and four-year-olds from 15 to 30 hours a week. The UK government's plan, which was originally due to take effect in 2015, is now expected to be fully implemented by 2017. However, a report for the Welsh government in February suggested that increasing free childcare may not have a significant impact on reducing poverty or getting more women into work. Despite this, the Welsh Conservatives believe that their pledge will make a real difference to working parents and the economy. The Liberal Democrats have yet to reveal their childcare plan, but have announced that they will unveil their policies later in March. UKIP, on the other hand, has expressed support for extending free childcare, but has highlighted the need to increase the supply of childcare providers in Wales. A recent survey of childcare providers in Wales has highlighted the challenges facing the sector, with nearly a quarter of respondents expressing very little confidence about the future of their business. The survey, conducted by the National Day Nurseries Association (NDNA), found that increasing costs and fewer children taking up places are major concerns for providers. NDNA chief executive Purnima Tanuku warned that the new National Living Wage would increase staff costs by 13% this year and 35% by 2019, putting further pressure on already struggling providers. "This, coupled with chronic underfunding for free places and declining numbers of children attending, is causing real problems," she said. The Welsh Conservatives' pledge to treble free childcare for working parents is a welcome move, but it remains to be seen how the party plans to implement this policy and address the challenges facing the childcare sector in Wales. With the Liberal Democrats and UKIP yet to fully reveal their plans, the debate on childcare in Wales is set to continue in the coming weeks and months.

A woman was approached by a suspicious man on Damfield Road on June 8. Police are seeking a 50-year-old, 6ft tall man with grey hair and beard, last seen near Old Hilton Hospital flats. He wore a dark knee-length coat. The incident occurred at 14:10 while the woman walked towards Old Edinburgh Road. Authorities urge anyone with information to come forward.

Motherwell Football Club has launched an investigation into historic child abuse allegations, following the revelation that former physiotherapist John Hart was dismissed from Partick Thistle in 1992 due to claims of sexual abuse. Hart, who is now deceased, also worked for Motherwell, prompting the club to conduct an internal review to determine if any incidents of abuse may have occurred during his tenure. The investigation, which began in response to widespread media coverage of historic child abuse in football, has involved speaking to individuals connected to the club in the late 1970s and 1980s. As a result, Motherwell has decided to expand the investigation and has hired a forensic accountant to examine employment records and club documents from the relevant period. Both Police Scotland and the Scottish Football Association (SFA) have been informed of the investigation, and all information gathered to date has been passed to the authorities. The club has stated that it will refrain from commenting further until the investigation is complete. In a statement, Motherwell urged anyone who may have been affected by abuse in football to contact Police Scotland or the NSPCC helpline, which has been set up to support and advise victims of abuse. The helpline can be reached at 0800 0232642. Partick Thistle, where Hart was employed before his dismissal, has also confirmed that it is cooperating fully with the investigation. The club stated that it has contacted the SFA and Police Scotland to share its knowledge of the allegations and will comply with any investigation. The developments come as the football community continues to grapple with the issue of historic child abuse. Several high-profile cases have emerged in recent months, leading to a widespread reckoning with the sport's past. As the investigation into Motherwell and Partick Thistle continues, it remains to be seen what further revelations may come to light. For now, the clubs' commitment to cooperating with authorities and supporting victims of abuse is a crucial step towards addressing this dark chapter in football's history.

Lewis Hamilton Secures Pole Position in Australian GP Qualifying Mercedes dominated the qualifying session for the Australian Grand Prix, with Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg taking the top two spots. Hamilton secured pole position, while his teammate Rosberg came in second. Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel trailed behind, finishing 0.652 seconds off the pace. Despite the gap, Vettel remains optimistic about his chances in the race. "In the race, you can always try to create something," he said. Mercedes F1 boss Toto Wolff also acknowledged the threat posed by Ferrari, stating that they have the pace but have yet to translate it into lap time. Both Hamilton and Rosberg pointed out that Vettel had only completed one run in final qualifying, whereas they had done two. Hamilton estimated that Vettel would have been quicker by another 0.2 seconds if he had gone out again. The British world champion expects the gap to narrow in some races this year, but admits that predicting form for the season is "a big guess." The Australian GP gets underway on Sunday, with coverage starting from 03:30 GMT.

Warner Bros Television has announced the termination of Charlie Sheen's contract on the popular sitcom "Two and a Half Men", effective immediately. The decision comes after a tumultuous few weeks, during which Sheen's personal life has been under intense scrutiny by the US media. The 45-year-old actor, who is the highest paid on US television, has been at the center of a media frenzy following a series of provocative and often rambling interviews. Production on the show had been suspended since late January, after Sheen entered rehabilitation for reported drug and alcohol abuse. The suspension was made official in late February, following a public feud with the show's producer and co-creator, Chuck Lorre. Sheen had been insulting Lorre in several interviews, which ultimately led to the termination of his contract. In a statement, Warner Bros said that the decision to terminate Sheen's contract was made "after careful consideration". The studio has not made any decisions on the future of the show, which is the most popular series on the CBS television network. Sheen's contract with Warner Bros was set to run until the end of the 2012 television season, with a salary of $2 million per episode. However, Sheen had recently demanded a raise to $3 million per episode, claiming that he was being underpaid. Sheen has been using social media to comment on the dispute between himself and the show's producers. On Twitter, he posted a message early on Monday, searching for an intern to assist him in his work. The tweet, which was a paid-for endorsement from Internships.com, read: "I'm looking to hire a winning INTERN with TigerBlood". Sheen has been using the term "TigerBlood" to describe himself, and has gained a large following on Twitter, reaching 1 million followers in just 24 hours. When asked if he would sue Warner Bros over the termination of his contract, Sheen replied via text message with the word "big", hinting that his next move would be significant. In a statement obtained by celebrity website TMZ, Sheen said that the termination of his contract was "very good news". The actor has insisted that he is drug-free after undergoing rehabilitation in January, and has been taken to hospital in Los Angeles with severe abdominal pains. Sheen filed for divorce from his third wife, Brooke Mueller, in November, citing irreconcilable differences. The future of "Two and a Half Men" remains uncertain, but one thing is clear: Charlie Sheen's time on the show has come to an end.

A 48-year-old man, Dean Haverley, has died after sustaining fatal injuries in an assault at the George Inn in Burnham, near Slough. The incident occurred on Saturday morning, with police being called to the scene just after midnight. Described as a "well liked" and "family man" by friends, Haverley's death has sent shockwaves through the community. A police cordon is in operation and authorities are appealing for witnesses to come forward. Detective Chief Inspector Simon Steel urged anyone with information to contact police immediately. Friends have paid tribute to Haverley, with one describing him as a "happy-go-lucky top bloke" whose passing is still hard to believe.

A 42-year-old man, Ali Qazimaj, from Tilbury, Essex, has been arrested in connection with the murders of Peter and Sylvia Stuart. The couple, from Weybread, were last seen alive on May 29 at a farm shop in Norfolk. Mr. Stuart's body was found with multiple stab wounds near their home on June 3, while his wife remains missing, but is believed to have also been killed. Qazimaj was located in a Luxembourg City hostel after a staff member recognized him from internet photos. He is currently awaiting a Court of Appeal decision in Luxembourg, which has 20 days to review his case. If the decision to extradite him is upheld, Qazimaj will be surrendered to Suffolk Police within 10 days to face questioning over the murders. The investigation is ongoing, with updates available on the Suffolk Live page.

UK House Prices Predicted to Rise 5.6% This Year According to the Centre for Economics and Business Research (CEBR), house prices in the UK are expected to rise by 5.6% this year, exceeding its previous forecast of 4.7%. The main driver of this increase is the lack of properties being put on the market, which is pushing up prices. Despite a 14% rise in mortgage approvals for house purchases, the number of mortgage approvals in September was down 4.5% on the previous month. The British Bankers' Association (BBA) attributes the rise in mortgage approvals to first-time buyers finding "good deals". However, the CEBR warns that the widening price gaps between different property types are making it harder for people to climb the property ladder. For example, in London, moving from a flat to a terraced home would require an extra £176,000. The CEBR is calling on the government to extend its housebuilding programme to address the issue. Housing charity Shelter has also expressed concern, stating that further house price rises will make it even more difficult for people to become homeowners.

The UK government has rejected an amendment to the Referendum Bill that would have introduced a "quadruple lock" mechanism, requiring a majority vote in each of the four component nations of the UK - England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland - in order to leave the European Union. The amendment, proposed by the SNP's foreign affairs spokesman Alex Salmond, aimed to ensure that the outcome of the referendum would be respectful of the results in each nation. However, Foreign Office Minister David Lidington argued that the amendment "did not make sense" and that the referendum should be a UK-wide decision. He emphasized that the UK's membership in the EU is a matter for the entire country, and that a single, simple majority vote across the UK should be sufficient to determine the outcome. The government has confirmed that the referendum will be held before the end of 2017, but will not coincide with elections to devolved parliaments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland on May 5, 2016. Ministers have also announced plans to amend "purdah" rules, which limit government announcements in the run-up to polls, to ensure a "fair fight" in the referendum campaign. As the government begins renegotiating the terms of Britain's EU membership, Prime Minister David Cameron is set to lead the charge ahead of the historic vote.

Mansfield Town manager Nigel Murray is confident that his team can turn their fortunes around, despite a six-match winless streak in the league. The Stags had a strong start to the season but have struggled to find consistency, with their last victory coming several weeks ago. However, a morale-boosting win over League One side Port Vale in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday has given the team a much-needed boost. Murray believes that his team's performance levels have been high, but they have been unable to capitalize on their chances and have been caught out by sucker punches. Despite this, the team has remained focused and has been working hard to rectify their situation. Murray stated, "We've kept our head down and kept working hard. The boys are confident." He also acknowledged the frustrations of the fans, saying "This time last month I was nominated for manager of the month. I think this month some of our fans would probably chuck me out of a window, but that's the game." The win over Port Vale has given Mansfield a sense of renewed purpose, and Murray feels that it has helped to brush away some of the doubts that had crept in. He said, "We feel like we've brushed some things out the door and got some things back on track. All that's been missing over this last month is belief and confidence." The team is now looking forward to a crucial match against Notts County on Saturday, a team that will be seeking revenge for a 5-0 thrashing at Field Mill last season. Notts County manager John Sheridan is confident that his team can fare better this time around, and is looking forward to the challenge. He said, "It's one of those games that's about winning the game, no matter how you win. We'll try to play, but sometimes when it's an ugly game you've got to deal with that." Sheridan also acknowledged the intensity of the rivalry between the two teams, saying "With it being Mansfield there's a bit more of an edge to it, but we've just got to treat it like another game." The match promises to be a thrilling encounter, with both teams looking to gain the upper hand in the League Two standings.

A contest to design a flag for Caithness has garnered submissions from across Scotland, England, and even internationally. A judging panel recently shortlisted four ideas, which will be digitized for a public online vote later this month. The vote will run until July 31. Caithness Civic Leader Gail Ross expressed delight at the creative entries, including those from local schools, America, Brazil, Australia, and other parts of Scotland. The chosen flag will serve as a public symbol of Caithness, and the community is eagerly awaiting the opportunity to cast their votes and select the winning design.

A Surrey man has successfully reached the South Pole on the anniversary of Captain Scott's 1912 expedition, completing a gruelling 138-mile trek. Patrick McIntosh, a chartered financial adviser, was accompanied by polar explorer Conrad Dickinson from Hexham, who previously led Prince Harry's team on Walking With The Wounded in 2013. Mr McIntosh undertook the challenge after battling three types of cancer over a 13-month period in 2012-13. His goal was to raise awareness about the importance of monitoring one's health and reacting quickly to any symptoms, as well as to collect £222,000 for charities Bowel Cancer UK, Prostate Cancer UK, and the Voice Of The Listener And The Viewer. Upon reaching the pole, Mr McIntosh expressed his elation, stating he felt "like a million dollars." He was particularly pleased to have experienced no physical malfunctions during the 11-day journey. The pair achieved this feat unsupported, carrying all their supplies and equipment with them. Mr McIntosh's granddaughter, Gemma Barker, confirmed that the duo arrived safely at 7pm and were already enjoying a celebratory cup of tea. Mr McIntosh sounded "on cloud nine" and was thrilled with his accomplishment.

Wales Sees Significant Drop in Road Fatalities, Reaches Historic Low The number of road fatalities in Wales has plummeted to a historic low, with a 29% decrease in deaths last year. According to the Police Reported Road Traffic Fatalities, 2010 report, published by the Welsh Assembly Government, there were 89 deaths on Welsh roads in 2010, marking the first time the number has fallen below three figures. Transport Minister Ieuan Wyn Jones welcomed the news, stating that the decrease is a clear indication that the safe driving message and tougher enforcement are "paying off." Jones emphasized that while the figures are encouraging, more needs to be done to improve road safety, particularly among young drivers. The significant decline in road fatalities is a testament to the effectiveness of road safety interventions implemented in recent years. Steve Baker, head of accident prevention charity RoSPA Wales, praised the Welsh Assembly Government for its proactive approach to building a strong road safety culture. Baker noted that Wales is now one of the safest countries in the world in which to travel, with recent statistics suggesting that the country is on track to further improve its position. The report shows that road fatalities in Wales have been steadily declining since 1973, when a peak of 424 deaths was recorded. The numbers continued to fall, reaching 161 in 2007, and have now dropped to a record low of 89 in 2010. While the figures released are preliminary, with final numbers to be provided in June, the trend is clear: Wales is becoming a safer place to travel. The Welsh Assembly Government's commitment to road safety has been instrumental in achieving this milestone. The government's efforts to promote safe driving, improve road safety, and enforce tougher penalties have all contributed to the significant decline in road fatalities. As Jones noted, "this government is committed to making Wales' roads safer for all who use them," and the latest figures are a welcome indication that this commitment is yielding results.

Venezuelan Prosecutor Turned Whistleblower Alleges Sham Trial Against Opposition Leader A former Venezuelan prosecutor, Franklin Nieves, has come forward with explosive allegations that the trial of opposition leader Leopoldo Lopez was a sham. Nieves, who was one of the lead prosecutors in the case, claims that evidence against Lopez was fabricated and witnesses were coerced into giving false statements to ensure his conviction. Lopez was sentenced to nearly 14 years in prison for inciting violence during anti-government protests in 2014. Nieves' allegations have sparked a heated response from the Venezuelan government, with National Assembly head Diosdado Cabello accusing the former prosecutor of being bribed to make the claims. Cabello alleged that Nieves was offered $850,000 to speak out against the government and claimed that Lopez was guilty of murder, not just inciting violence. However, human rights activists have long argued that the trial against Lopez was politically motivated and unfair. Nieves, who has fled to the United States and is seeking asylum, says he can no longer live with the guilt of having sent an innocent man to prison. He claims that Cabello ordered the arrest of Lopez to remove him from the political scene. The former prosecutor's allegations have shed new light on the trial, which has been widely criticized by human rights groups. Venezuela's attorney-general, Luisa Ortega, has sacked Nieves, saying he acted contrary to his oath of office. However, Nieves' claims have sparked renewed calls for Lopez's release and have highlighted the need for greater transparency and accountability in Venezuela's justice system. Lopez has always maintained his innocence and is currently appealing against his sentence. The case has become a symbol of the ongoing struggle for democracy and human rights in Venezuela, and Nieves' allegations have added fuel to the fire. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen what impact Nieves' claims will have on the future of Venezuelan politics.

Venezuela's economic crisis has escalated, with General Motors (GM) announcing that its Venezolana plant in Valencia has been seized by public authorities. The US car giant condemned the unexpected move, stating it will take all legal actions to defend its interests. The plant, which employs 2,678 workers, has also had vehicles and other assets taken. GM warned that the seizure will cause irreparable damage to the company, its dealers, and suppliers. The incident highlights the deepening divisions in Venezuela, where protests against President Nicolas Maduro's government have turned violent, resulting in at least three deaths this week. The country's car industry has struggled due to currency controls and stagnant production, exacerbating the economic crisis. The Venezuelan government has yet to comment on the seizure.

Jamaican hurdler Omar McLeod has set his sights on breaking American Aries Merritt's 110m hurdles world record of 12.80. McLeod, 23, recently achieved a new Jamaican record of 12.90 at the national track and field championships, surpassing Hansle Parchment's 2014 record of 12.94. This impressive time has catapulted him to fifth place in the all-time fastest men's list. Although he narrowly missed his coach's target of 12.8, McLeod remains optimistic about his chances of breaking the world record before the London World Championships in August. With upcoming races in Paris and Budapest, McLeod is poised to make another attempt at the record. His achievement comes on the heels of strong performances by fellow Jamaican athletes Yohan Blake and Elaine Thompson at the national trials.

A serious incident occurred in Edinburgh yesterday morning when a 65-year-old man was struck by a number 41 Lothian bus. The accident happened at the junction of Princes Street and Frederick Street just before 10:45. Emergency services responded quickly, with the Scottish Ambulance Service arriving on the scene within three minutes. The man was taken to Edinburgh Royal Infirmary with serious injuries. Police are now appealing for witnesses to come forward. The incident resulted in partial road closures, with Princes Street and Frederick Street affected. Lothian Buses and Police Scotland are cooperating to investigate the incident. The public is advised to seek alternative routes to avoid the area.

Cardiff Councillor Neil McEvoy has announced that he will be pursuing a case against the council in a "political way" after a tribunal found him not guilty of bringing the council into disrepute. The Public Service Ombudsman for Wales had investigated a complaint against Mr. McEvoy, which led to a one-month suspension from his duties as a councillor. However, the tribunal ultimately cleared him of the more serious charge. Despite the outcome, the Ombudsman stated that the decision to investigate was vindicated, and a spokesman expressed satisfaction that the matter had come to a conclusion. Mr. McEvoy, who was re-elected as a councillor in May's local elections, claims that the results demonstrate he has been "found innocent in the court of public opinion." He has chosen to drop his appeal and instead focus on exposing what he describes as a "one-party state" in Wales. Meanwhile, a separate internal inquiry by Plaid Cymru into Mr. McEvoy's behavior has yet to formally begin, despite being launched almost four months ago. The party's executive committee is set to meet on Friday to discuss the way forward for the disciplinary panel, with a report expected to be published within six weeks. Mr. McEvoy's decision to pursue the case in a political manner is likely to lead to further controversy and debate in the coming weeks.

A man suffered shotgun injuries in a field near Hapsford Road in Bootle, Merseyside, on Friday at 22:00 GMT. He is being treated in hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Police are investigating, with a cordon in place and house-to-house inquiries underway. The motive is unclear, and witnesses are urged to come forward to assist with the investigation.

An inquest into the death of Australian cricketer Phillip Hughes has begun, examining the circumstances surrounding his tragic passing. Hughes, 25, died on November 27, 2014, two days after being struck on the neck by a ball during a domestic match in Sydney. The five-day hearing will investigate whether his death was avoidable, with a focus on the emergency response and the nature of play on the day. In her opening address, counsel assisting the coroner, Kristina Stern SC, stated that Hughes' death "appears to have been inevitable from the point of impact." Neurosurgeon Dr. Brian Owler's opinion is that no intervention, regardless of how early, could have prevented the fatal outcome. The inquest will hear testimony from several players who witnessed the incident, including Doug Bollinger, Brad Haddin, and Dave Warner. Before the inquest commenced, Hughes' former manager, James Henderson, appealed to the media to respect the family's privacy, stating that they had not been looking forward to this week. The family hopes that a positive outcome will emerge from the process, potentially leading to improved safety measures in cricket. NSW State Coroner Michael Barnes acknowledged that cricket carries inherent risks, but emphasized that the sport can still be made safer. A previous report commissioned by Cricket Australia recommended compulsory helmets for batsmen facing fast and medium-paced bowling, although it noted that even the newest safety standards would not have saved Hughes' life.

The United Lincolnshire Hospitals NHS Trust (ULHT) has introduced a new support system for international nurses joining their team. Following previous recruitment drives in countries such as Greece, Spain, and Portugal, the trust has appointed an international support nurse to help newcomers adjust to life in the UK. Russell Outen-Coe, Head of Nurse Education, stated that the trust has "learned many lessons" from past experiences and is now better equipped to support foreign nurses. The international support nurse will assist with tasks such as finding accommodation, making the transition to the UK smoother. Sheila Marriott, regional director for the Royal College of Nursing, welcomed this initiative, emphasizing the importance of making the transition easy for overseas nurses. However, she also highlighted the need to address the shortage of training places for home-grown nurses, citing evidence that locally trained nurses are more likely to stay in the area. The ULHT operates hospitals in Boston, Lincoln, and Grantham, and is working to fill the gaps in their nursing staff. By providing dedicated support, the trust hopes to attract and retain international talent while also addressing the underlying issues affecting nurse recruitment.

A devastating fire broke out in the Ajman One complex, a residential development in the Ajman emirate, north of Dubai, late on Monday. The blaze began in one tower and quickly spread to an adjacent block, prompting a swift evacuation of residents. Several people have been treated for breathing problems and minor injuries, according to reports. Dramatic videos posted by Ajman Police on Twitter showed flames engulfing a significant portion of one side of the tower, reaching several storeys high. The fire also sent burning debris crashing to the ground. Fortunately, Ajman civil defence teams were able to extinguish the fire by Tuesday morning and are currently waiting for the building to cool down. This incident comes just days after a large fire engulfed the luxury Address Hotel in central Dubai on New Year's Eve, injuring 16 people. Investigators found that the hotel blaze was caused by a short circuit in a spotlight and exacerbated by non-compliant cladding. The Ajman One complex, a 2.7bn dirham project, has a history of delays, having been completed years behind schedule. The repeated incidents of fires in the UAE's high-rise buildings have raised concerns about safety standards and the use of flammable materials in construction.

Astra, the Romanian champions, arrived in Glasgow three hours late due to payment issues with their flight. However, paperwork problems for Nigerian striker Fatai and Ghanaian midfielder Yahaya were resolved, and they arrived separately. Astra is set to play at Celtic Park on Thursday in their Europa League Group D game, currently bottom of the group after two defeats, while Celtic leads with four points.

Former Southampton Football Club Players Come Forward with Abuse Allegations Two former Southampton Football Club players, Dean Radford and Jamie Webb, have bravely spoken out about the abuse they suffered during their time at the club as teenagers. The allegations are part of a growing number of cases of abuse in football, with several other players also coming forward to share their experiences. Mr. Radford, who was part of the schoolboy development team, recalled how he would often stay with a club employee during weekends away from his home in Bristol. He described how he and another young player were made to "snuggle up" with the employee on a couch, which made him feel uncomfortable and odd. The employee had told them that they needed to trust him and that he needed to be like a second father to them in order to become professional footballers. Mr. Radford also alleged that he was sexually assaulted by the employee after suffering a back injury. He was asked to lie down for treatment, and it was during this time that the assault occurred. Jamie Webb, who joined the club at the age of 13, described how boys were "groomed" by the employee, who would ask them to write him "love" letters. Mr. Webb recalled a "definite attempt to abuse me" when the employee tried to touch him inappropriately. Both men have waived their anonymity to speak to the BBC about their experiences, and their allegations have sparked a wider investigation into abuse in football. Southampton Football Club has stated that it will fully cooperate with any police investigation, and Hampshire Constabulary is one of 15 police forces currently investigating allegations of abuse in the sport. The NSPCC has set up a hotline to offer support to victims of child sex abuse within football, and in its first week, it received an astonishing 860 calls. The charity is urging anyone who has been affected by abuse to come forward and seek help. Mr. Radford and Mr. Webb's bravery in speaking out has been praised, and their experiences have highlighted the need for greater protection and support for young players. Mr. Radford said that he holds the club "partly responsible" for the abuse, stating that they "must have known" about the rumors and allegations that were circulating at the time. The allegations of abuse at Southampton Football Club are a sobering reminder of the need for vigilance and action to prevent abuse in sport. As more players come forward to share their experiences, it is clear that this is a problem that affects many clubs and organizations. The football community must work together to ensure that young players are protected and supported, and that those responsible for abuse are held accountable. In the meantime, the NSPCC hotline remains available for anyone who has been affected by abuse in football. The charity is urging anyone who has been abused or has concerns about abuse to come forward and seek help. With the support of organizations like the NSPCC and the bravery of players like Mr. Radford and Mr. Webb, it is hoped that the sport can begin to heal and move forward.

An inquest into the death of Paul McGuigan, a 37-year-old former Royal Marine, has heard that he expressed concerns about his colleague Danny Fitzsimons, who would later shoot him dead. During a Skype call with his fiancée, McGuigan described Fitzsimons as "weird". Fitzsimons, a former paratrooper from Rochdale, is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence in Baghdad for the killings of McGuigan and Australian Darren Hoare in 2009. The inquest was told that McGuigan, who had previously worked as a bodyguard for ex-Beatle George Harrison, had been living in Tameside and was excited about the upcoming arrival of his baby with fiancée Nicola Prestage. All three men were working for British security firm ArmorGroup, part of G4S, in the Iraqi capital's Green Zone at the time of the incident. Fitzsimons claimed he acted in self-defence after a fight broke out, but his family has questioned whether he was fit to be employed by the security firm due to his struggles with post-traumatic stress. The inquest, being led by Deputy Coroner Joanne Kearsley, will seek evidence relating to G4S's employment policies. The hearing is set to resume on Thursday, with further investigation into the circumstances surrounding McGuigan's death.

A man in his 20s was hospitalized after a suspected corrosive substance attack in Salford. Officers responded to the incident at City Walk, near Silverdale Country Park, on Friday at 14:00 BST. The severity of his injuries is currently unknown. Greater Manchester Police are seeking information and urge witnesses to come forward. This incident comes as assaults involving corrosive substances have more than doubled in England since 2012, with most occurring in London. A similar attack occurred in Kent on Saturday, injuring a man at a fish and chip shop. Police are investigating both incidents.

Welsh Athlete Eilidh Bundy-Davies Named to Team GB for Rio Olympics Eilidh Bundy-Davies, a 21-year-old athlete from Wales, has been named to Team GB's 80-strong athletics team for the upcoming Rio Olympics. She will compete in the 400m individual race as well as the relay event, bringing hope to Welsh fans who are eager to see their country represented on the world stage. Bundy-Davies' selection comes as a welcome boost to Welsh athletics, which has seen a decline in representation at the Olympics in recent years. In fact, Wales will have just one athletics competitor at the Rio Games, the lowest number since the 1952 Helsinki Games. However, there is a glimmer of hope that this number could increase if hurdler Rhys Williams' appeal against his omission from the squad is successful. Despite the challenges faced by Welsh athletics, Bundy-Davies remains optimistic about the future of the sport in her country. "I think there are two sides to it," she explained. "A lot of people have been quite unlucky. Dai Greene, for example, has struggled with injury and everyone knows he's capable of massive things if he's fit." She also highlighted the talent of younger athletes coming through the ranks, saying, "There are a lot of younger people coming through that I'm sure will feature in the Commonwealth Games in a few years and the Olympics in 2020." Bundy-Davies' own career has been on the rise in recent years, with a string of impressive performances that have earned her a reputation as one of the UK's top young athletes. She helped Britain win 4x400m European relay gold in Amsterdam on Sunday, setting a world lead time of three minutes 25.05 seconds. She also won relay bronze at last year's World Championships and individual bronze at the 2015 European Indoor Championships. Legendary former 110m hurdler Colin Jackson has tipped Bundy-Davies as a medal contender in Brazil, and she feels that winning a relay medal is "really realistic." "Bringing home the bronze medal last year showed we can medal at a world level," she said. "I think we've got an even stronger relay squad this year. I think people are quicker and we want it just as much." While Bundy-Davies is confident about her chances in the relay event, she is more cautious about her individual prospects in the 400m. "There's a lot of experience I still need to gain," she said. "I think I will be peaking more four to eight years down the line." However, she is hopeful that she can bring home a medal from the 2018 Commonwealth Games and 2020 Olympics. As Bundy-Davies prepares to take on the world's best athletes in Rio, she is aware of the pressure and expectation that comes with representing her country. However, she is determined to make the most of the opportunity and do Wales proud. "It is what it is, and I'm still going to try and run to the best of my ability and hopefully bring home a medal for Wales," she said. With her talent, dedication, and determination, Bundy-Davies is certainly one to watch in the upcoming Olympics.

Global markets experienced a mixed day of trading amidst uncertainty over Greece's future in the European bloc. The euro initially fell to $1.09, but recovered to trade at $1.1134. Investors remained cautious ahead of trading in China, which has been recovering from significant losses since mid-June. In Asia, the Nikkei rose 0.8% to 19,929.56, while the S&P/ASX 200 index in Australia edged up 0.05% to 5,494.40. South Korea's Kospi index also gained 0.1% to 2,033.04, with Hotel Shilla's shares surging nearly 5% after winning a licence to operate duty-free stores in Seoul. The euro's initial decline against the Japanese yen was reversed, bouncing back to 136.35, on rumours of a potential delay in Greece's repayment to the European Central Bank. Overall, markets remained volatile, reflecting ongoing concerns about global economic stability.

Northern Ireland is grappling with a devastating drug epidemic, with several deaths linked to substance abuse in the past fortnight. The crisis has put immense pressure on the healthcare system, with General Practitioners (GPs) struggling to cope with the sheer volume of cases. Dr. Michael McKenna, a GP, expressed his concerns on BBC's Good Morning Ulster programme, stating that the services are "overwhelmed" and unable to provide adequate support. The alarming rise in drug-related deaths has surpassed the number of road fatalities in Northern Ireland. According to the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI), 88 opioid-related deaths were recorded in 2015, compared to 74 fatalities resulting from road crashes in the same year. The opioid-related deaths include cases involving heroin, morphine, methadone, and prescription drugs like tramadol. The human cost of this crisis is starkly evident in the story of Jamie Burns, who died last November after taking just one pill on a night out. His father, William Burns, is now campaigning to raise awareness about the dangers of drugs through the #onepillwillkill initiative. Mr. Burns recounted the heartbreaking moment he lost his son, describing the devastating scene in the hospital as "the ground opening and swallowing you up." The tragedy has driven Mr. Burns to warn others about the lethal consequences of drug use. He emphasized that even a single pill can be fatal, regardless of previous experiences with substances. "You could have taken 10 pills before it, over a period of weeks and been fine, and you could just take this one pill [which could kill you]," he cautioned. Dr. McKenna echoed Mr. Burns' concerns, highlighting the need for a comprehensive approach to address the drug epidemic. He stressed that the issue cannot be solely borne by GPs, who are already under tremendous pressure. The doctor revealed that he has lost several patients to drug addiction over the past decade, with the number "into double figures." As Northern Ireland struggles to combat the drug crisis, it is clear that a multi-faceted approach is required. This includes increasing funding, providing more resources, and raising awareness about the dangers of substance abuse. The #onepillwillkill campaign serves as a poignant reminder of the devastating consequences of drug use, and the need for collective action to prevent further tragedies.

Number eight Arno Bothma is joining Harlequins next summer. The 27-year-old has 13 caps and played in the 2015 Rugby World Cup. Bothma is moving from the Bulls and has also played for the Sharks and Toyota Verblitz. "I'm excited to move to England and positively impact Harlequins," he said, aiming to play a big role.

Derry City Football Club has announced the departure of manager Peter Hutton by mutual consent. Hutton, the former Candystripes captain, took over as Brandywell boss in May last year but has struggled to achieve success. The team is currently battling against relegation from the Premier Division, with only six wins in 27 league games. They also suffered a disappointing FAI Cup exit on Monday night, losing 3-0 to Cork City. City assistant boss Paul Hegarty will assume caretaker manager duties until the end of the season. Hutton led Derry to the FAI Cup final last season, but the team's poor performance this year ultimately led to his departure. The club has expressed gratitude for Hutton's service and wishes him well for the future.

A bizarre incident has left a Colorado office in disarray after a rogue goat smashed through the doors, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. The break-in occurred at the offices of Argonics Inc, where staff arrived on Monday morning to find the doors shattered and glass littering the floor. Initially, police were called to the scene to investigate what appeared to be a standard break-in. However, upon reviewing the CCTV footage, it became clear that the culprit was not a human, but a goat with distinctive long horns. The footage, which has been uploaded to the company's YouTube account, shows the goat approaching the doors and smashing through them with ease. The video has since gone viral, attracting close to half a million views. Despite the significant damage caused, it appears that the goat did not take anything from the office. The motives behind the goat's actions remain unclear, but social media users have been quick to speculate. Some have suggested that the goat may have seen its reflection in the glass and become aggressive, while others have joked about "peer pressure from a gang of goat looters." The whereabouts of the goat are currently unknown, but it can be seen trotting away from the scene of the crime at the end of the video. Staff at Argonics Inc have been left to clear up the mess and are likely to face an unusual insurance claim. The incident has brought a touch of humor to the office, with the company seemingly taking the incident in stride.

Drivers who received parking fines in Burrows Place near Swansea museum are set to be reimbursed after a councillor challenged the legality of the loading bay sign. Up to 320 tickets were issued since September, with fines totaling £70 each. Councillor Sybil Crouch, who represents the Castle ward, received one of these fines and disputed it, claiming the sign was inadequate. After her complaint, the council apologized and conceded that the sign was incorrect. The council has ceased enforcing parking restrictions in the area until a new sign is installed. Crouch has also requested that all 320 motorists who received fines be refunded, citing the sign's invalidity. The council has agreed to write to affected drivers to arrange reimbursement. The large number of fines issued in the small area suggests that many motorists were confused by the signage, highlighting the need for clear and accurate signs to avoid unnecessary penalties.

The historic theatre that hosted the World Figure Skating Championships in 1898 is set to welcome The Imperial Ice Stars for a spectacular production of The Nutcracker on Ice. The show, which begins on October 24, boasts an impressive cast of 26, including four-time figure skating world champion Evgeny Platov and ITV's Dancing on Ice stars Keith Chegwin and Olga Sharutenko. The production has already wowed audiences in South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, and Asia. Artistic Director Tony Mercer promises an action-packed performance, featuring gymnastics, flying, acrobatics, fire, and illusions. Set in St Petersburg, The Nutcracker tells the enchanting tale of Marie and her magical Nutcracker doll. After its London run, the show will move on to Cardiff and Southampton. Don't miss this thrilling ice skating extravaganza, a perfect treat for the whole family.
