Rennie argued that his party is the main challenger to the SNP in many marginal seats and that the Liberal Democrats can offer a fairer and more competent voice for the country. As the general election campaign gains momentum, it is clear that the debate in Scotland will be shaped by the interplay between nationalist and unionist sentiments. With the SNP, Labour, and the Conservatives all vying for dominance, the outcome of the election remains uncertain. One thing is certain, however: the issue of social justice and the need to address poverty will be a key battleground in the campaign ahead. As Brown's speech highlighted, the fate of thousands of children living in poverty in Scotland hangs in the balance, and it is up to voters to decide which party is best equipped to tackle this pressing issue.

Wales Forward Robson-Kanu Declares Fitness for Euro 2016 Opener After a string of leg and ankle injuries that kept him out of Wales' last four friendly matches, forward Hal Robson-Kanu has announced that he is ready to play a full 90 minutes in the team's Euro 2016 opener against Slovakia. The 27-year-old, who is currently unattached after leaving Reading in May, has resumed full training with the Wales squad in France and is confident in his ability to participate in the upcoming match. "I've trained, I'm feeling good, feeling fresh. Come Saturday, I'll be 100%," Robson-Kanu said, dispelling concerns about his fitness. Wales is set to face a demanding schedule, with three group games in 10 days against Slovakia, England, and Russia. Despite his recent injuries, Robson-Kanu believes he can cope with the physical demands of the tournament, citing his high levels of fitness and recent training sessions. Wales manager Chris Coleman has also expressed optimism about the availability of other injured players, including midfielders Joe Ledley and Joe Allen. However, midfielder David Vaughan missed training on Thursday, casting some uncertainty over his participation in the upcoming match. With the team's journey to Bordeaux set to begin on Friday, Robson-Kanu's declaration of fitness is a welcome boost to Wales' chances in their first major tournament appearance since the 1958 World Cup.

A crash on the A329 Oxford Road occurred at 05:30 GMT, involving a red Peugeot 206. Two of three occupants are being treated in hospital, while a fourth person is being sought by police. The road is closed as a structural engineer assesses two damaged buildings. Thames Valley Police are investigating, with no arrests made. Motorists are advised to find alternative routes due to lengthy delays, with a diversion in place. Inquiries are ongoing to establish the circumstances of the crash.

Christina Rees has been appointed as the Labour party's new spokesperson on Wales in Westminster, becoming the fifth person to hold the position since 2015. Speaking to BBC Wales for the first time since her appointment, Ms Rees expressed her hope that she will be the last to hold the role before the 2020 general election. Her predecessor, Jo Stevens, resigned over the party's stance on Brexit, specifically the vote to trigger Article 50. Ms Rees has pledged her support to Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, stating that he is the democratically elected leader and deserves the party's backing. She emphasized the importance of unity within the party and ruled out any involvement in attempts to unseat Mr. Corbyn. With a focus on unity, Ms Rees aims to bring stability to the role and serve out the remainder of the term until 2020. She hopes to be the last shadow Welsh secretary before the next election.

A Filipino national has been convicted of attempted murder and voyeurism after a brutal attack on his former partner in Cardiff. Arnel Martinez Raymundo, 48, was found guilty at Cardiff Crown Court on Thursday of stabbing Anna Caladiao, 43, in the back at their former home on June 12. The court heard that Miss Caladiao suffered life-threatening injuries, including stomach and lung wounds, and was forced to spend six days in intensive care on a ventilator. She would have died if not for the timely intervention of workmen who came to her aid when she stumbled into the street. Raymundo fled the scene and made his way to London, where he was arrested 13 days later in Croydon. During his trial, he denied the charges, claiming that Miss Caladiao had fed him crystal meth and that he had started stabbing randomly during a dream. However, the jury rejected his claims and found him guilty of both attempted murder and voyeurism. In a victim impact statement, Miss Caladiao described the devastating effects of the attack, saying she was left "badly scarred" and in need of a wheelchair for weeks. She also revealed that she was suffering from nightmares, stress, and panic attacks, and that she could still feel the knife going into her body. Judge Eleri Rees condemned Raymundo's actions, saying that he had shown "not the slightest remorse" for his crimes. She described the attack as "ferocious" and said that Raymundo's behavior had demonstrated a disregard for Miss Caladiao's life. Raymundo was jailed for his crimes, bringing an end to a traumatic ordeal for Miss Caladiao and her family.

Foxconn, the world's largest contract electronics manufacturer, has announced a historic deal to acquire a 66% stake in Sharp, a Japanese electronics firm, for approximately $3.5 billion. The deal, set to be signed on April 2, marks the first foreign takeover of a major Japanese electronics company. Foxconn, which assembles the majority of the world's iPhones, had initially attempted to invest in Sharp in 2012, but talks collapsed. Sharp, founded in 1912, has struggled with heavy debts and has undergone two major bailouts in the last four years. Despite its financial woes, the company remains a leader in liquid display technology, a key asset for Foxconn. The acquisition will form a "historic strategic alliance" between the two companies, with Foxconn seeking to leverage Sharp's innovative technologies. Japanese officials had previously been hesitant to allow Sharp to fall under foreign ownership due to its distinctive display panel technology. The deal surpasses a rival offer from a government-backed consortium of Japanese investors, securing Foxconn's position as a major player in the global electronics industry.

Cardiff council's new penalty scheme has seen a significant impact in its first month. A total of 3,544 penalty notices were handed out in December 2014, with 370 offenders already paying the £35 charge, totaling £12,950. The scheme, which currently focuses on bus lanes, will expand to yellow box junctions and illegal parking around schools. Drivers are warned that unpaid fines can double to £70 if not paid within 21 days. A council spokesman emphasized that the goal is to encourage drivers to follow the Highway Code, stating "if you don't want to be fined, don't breach it." The revenue generated will fund the project and other traffic-related initiatives. The council's message is clear: comply with the rules to avoid penalties.

Oculus Rift has made a significant reversal in its policy regarding the use of its games on rival headsets. A recent software update has removed the checks that prevented Oculus games from being played on the HTC Vive using the Revive software. The move comes as a surprise, given the company's previous efforts to lock down its content and prevent it from being used on other devices. The Revive software, released in April, allowed users to play Oculus games on the HTC Vive, much to the dismay of Oculus. The company had updated its software to include a headset check, ensuring that only Oculus Rift headsets could play the games. However, the developers behind Revive found ways to work around this check, allowing users to continue playing Oculus games on the Vive. The removal of the headset check has been confirmed by Oculus, which stated that it would not use such checks in the future. The company emphasized the importance of protecting developer content, citing it as crucial to the long-term success of the VR industry. The move has been met with surprise and relief from the VR community, with many criticizing Oculus's initial decision to lock down its content. The Revive developers expressed their surprise and disbelief at the change, posting a message on their Github page. The decision is seen as a significant shift in Oculus's approach to content protection and compatibility. By removing the headset check, Oculus is effectively allowing its games to be played on other devices, including the HTC Vive. The move is likely to be welcomed by VR enthusiasts, who value the ability to play a wide range of games across different platforms.

MPs Demand Action in 31-Year-Old Disappearance Case of Katrice Lee A debate was held in the House of Commons to discuss the handling of the investigation into the disappearance of Katrice Lee, who vanished 31 years ago from a shop at a German military base. Katrice's family, including her mother Sharon Lee, sister Natasha, and father Richard Lee, have been waiting for answers for far too long. The family believes that Katrice, who disappeared on her second birthday, is still alive and was abducted. Hartlepool Labour MP Iain Wright expressed his frustration, stating that the family has waited "far too long" and "action must be taken." Conservative MP Caroline Dinenage also criticized former Prime Minister David Cameron for refusing to meet with the family. Defence Minister Mark Francois assured the family that he would try to meet with them before Christmas and that the Royal Military Police are using modern investigative techniques to get to the bottom of the case. Katrice's disappearance occurred when her mother left her at the checkout with her aunt for a moment to get crisps. When she returned, Katrice was gone. The family is still holding out hope that Katrice will be found, and they are seeking justice and closure. The debate has brought renewed attention to the case, and the family is hoping that it will lead to a breakthrough in the investigation.

Ireland Names 14-Man Panel for Round-Robin Competition The Irish cricket team has announced a 14-man squad for the upcoming round-robin competition, featuring eight associate countries. The team will face off against Afghanistan, Scotland, Hong Kong, Oman, Namibia, and the UAE in the tournament. Notably, the squad includes the return of several key players who missed most of Ireland's 2016 campaign due to injury or personal issues. Boyd Rankin, Andrew Balbirnie, and Greg Thompson are all back in the fold, bringing valuable experience and skills to the team. Rankin's height and pace are expected to add an extra dimension to Ireland's attack, while Balbirnie and Thompson will provide stability and depth to the batting lineup. Head coach John Bracewell expressed his delight at having the trio back in the squad, citing the benefits of their experience and expertise. The selectors have opted to take Gary Wilson as the sole wicket-keeper, omitting Niall O'Brien from the squad. Middlesex seamer Tim Murtagh has also been left out. Meanwhile, young players Jacob Mulder and Josh Little have retained their places in the T20 squad, following impressive debuts against Hong Kong. The Ireland squad will be led by captain William Porterfield, and will look to make a strong impression in the round-robin competition.

A devastating attack occurred in el-Arish as a bomber rammed a lorry filled with explosives into a building. Militants then opened fire on the station, causing chaos. Although no group has claimed responsibility, the area is frequently targeted by Islamists linked to the Islamic State group. The North Sinai region has seen over 400 attacks between 2012 and 2015, with the Sinai Province jihadist group being the most active insurgents. This group, formerly known as Ansar Beit al-Maqdis, has around 1,000 to 1,500 members and swore loyalty to IS in 2014, posing a significant threat to the region.

A damning report has revealed the shocking conditions faced by thousands of migrants who arrived in the UK over the summer, with many being held in squalid and inhumane facilities. The prisons watchdog, led by chief inspector Peter Clarke, investigated conditions at Channel facilities in Folkestone and Dover, and found that officials were unable to cope with the influx of arrivals. The report found that over 3,500 people, including 370 children who had arrived without adults, were held in facilities that lacked basic decency. Many were forced to sleep on concrete floors in unhygienic conditions, with no access to clean or dry clothes, food, or hot drinks. Inspectors found that many migrants had not eaten for long periods and were dehydrated, while others suffered from scabies, headaches, and diarrhoea. The Longport Freight Shed in Folkestone, which was used as a temporary holding facility, was found to be particularly unsuitable. Inspectors described the conditions as "fundamentally lacking in decency", with migrants forced to endure cramped and unsanitary conditions. Another facility, Frontier House in Folkestone, had nowhere suitable for migrants to sleep, while a third facility at Dover Seaport was "crowded, poorly ventilated, and smelled badly". Mr Clarke said that it was "unacceptable" that officials did not work out more quickly how to manage the crisis, and that arrangements were still not in place to process detainees quickly and efficiently. He welcomed plans to refurbish the Dover Seaport holding room and praised a project that helped charities and other organisations support detained migrants. Immigration minister James Brokenshire acknowledged that the conditions were "not acceptable" and said that the Home Office had already accepted most of Mr Clarke's recommendations. He confirmed that the Longport Freight Shed would not be used again as a holding facility, saying that it was only used temporarily to ease exceptional pressures on existing screening centres. The report highlights the need for urgent action to address the crisis in migrant detention facilities. The number of detentions in the first nine months of 2015 more than doubled to 4,785, compared to 2,118 in the same period the previous year. Many of the arrivals were from Eritrea, Sudan, and Syria, and were fleeing conflict and persecution in their home countries. The government has faced criticism for its handling of the migrant crisis, with many arguing that more needs to be done to provide safe and humane accommodation for those seeking to enter the UK. The report's findings are a stark reminder of the need for a more compassionate and effective approach to managing migration, and for ensuring that the basic human rights of all individuals are respected and protected.

A romantic gesture by a Southampton university student has gone viral on social media, earning him admiration and date offers from around the world. Alfonso, a 25-year-old student from Mexico City, mustered up the courage to ask his crush, Naomi Lucking, out on a coffee date in a rather unconventional way. While studying in the university library, he penned a creative note that read: "Sorry to disturb your studies, but I really need to ask..... would you like to have a coffee with me someday?" The note even provided two possible replies, including a humorous option that mentioned a 7ft tall boyfriend. Although Naomi politely declined the offer, she was impressed by Alfonso's inventiveness and took to Twitter to share a photo of the note. Her tweet, which has been shared over 30,000 times, described the encounter as the "most awkward experience of my life," but also gave Alfonso "10/10 for creativity." In a follow-up tweet, Naomi revealed that she had told Alfonso that her boyfriend was actually 6ft 3", leaving him "crushed." The reaction to Alfonso's note has been overwhelming, with people from all over the world reaching out to him with date offers. Despite being turned down by Naomi, who is already in a relationship, Alfonso has described the experience as "really great." He explained that he wanted to approach Naomi in a unique way, as they were in a quiet room and he didn't want to disturb her. Alfonso's creative effort has not only earned him admiration but also taught him a valuable lesson about the power of social media. Naomi, on the other hand, has been left "completely bewildered" by the response to her tweet, saying she had no idea it would garner so much attention. While she appreciated Alfonso's effort, she has no plans to reconsider his offer, citing her existing relationship. Nevertheless, Alfonso's romantic gesture has clearly made an impact, and he can take comfort in knowing that his creativity has been recognized and appreciated by thousands of people around the world.

The Royal Regiment has been bestowed with the prestigious Freedom of the Borough award, recognizing its strong ties to the East Midlands region. A ceremony was held on Saturday to grant the honour, with Commanding Officer Lt Col Richard Slack expressing his gratitude. "It's a great honour," he said, acknowledging the support of the borough council and local community. The regiment, currently based in Germany, has a long history of recruiting from Northamptonshire and has seen action in various conflict zones, including Bosnia, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Council leader David Mackintosh praised the regiment's vital role in defending the country, noting the sacrifices made by its members. The council has invited the regiment to parade through Northampton's streets upon its return from deployment, a tradition that drew over 1,000 spectators last year. The regiment is set to be redeployed to Afghanistan in 2013.

Ronnie O'Sullivan Edges Out Liang Wenbo in Thrilling Masters Opener The 2023 Masters tournament got off to a thrilling start as England's Ronnie O'Sullivan battled back from the brink of defeat to overcome China's Liang Wenbo in a nail-biting 6-5 victory. O'Sullivan, seeking a record seventh Masters title, was pushed to the limit by the Chinese world number 11, who fought from 4-2 down to lead 5-4 before missing a crucial black in the 10th frame. Despite struggling with illness and fatigue, O'Sullivan showed his trademark resilience to hang in the match and eventually seal the win with a stunning 121 break in the deciding frame. The 41-year-old, who has been ranked as high as world number one, was relieved to have advanced to the quarterfinals, where he will face either Neil Robertson or Ali Carter. In the post-match interview, O'Sullivan admitted that he didn't deserve to win and felt for his opponent, Liang, who had come so close to pulling off a major upset. "I didn't feel well today, and I was tired," O'Sullivan said. "I've had it for about a month, but I just tried to stay professional and hang in there." The five-time world champion also expressed his admiration for Liang's skill and dedication, acknowledging that the Chinese player had given him a run for his money. Meanwhile, 2011 winner Ding Junhui made a successful return to the Masters, defeating English world number 16 Kyren Wilson 6-3 in the day's other first-round match. The Chinese world number six, who had not won a Masters match in five years, produced a break of 50 in the ninth frame to seal the win. Ding will now face either former world champion Stuart Bingham or Joe Perry in the quarterfinals. O'Sullivan's victory sets up an intriguing quarterfinal match against either Robertson or Carter, and the Englishman will be looking to build on his momentum as he bids to break the record for the most Masters titles. However, the 41-year-old seems unconcerned about the pressure to win, stating that he can play until he's 50 and that he doesn't see much grassroots talent emerging to challenge him. With his experience and skill, O'Sullivan remains a force to be reckoned with in the world of snooker, and his fans will be eagerly anticipating his next match at Alexandra Palace in London.

A Southeastern train travelling from Victoria to Dartford was evacuated at Denmark Hill Station in south London after flames were spotted underneath the train. The incident occurred at approximately 18:45 GMT, and the station was shut down as a precautionary measure. Passengers on board filmed sparks visible above the track, and one witness, Cosmin Suttu, described seeing "big flames" from the train window. The London Fire Brigade reported that the fire affected eight carriages and damaged one electrical box, but fortunately, there were no reports of injuries. The station has since reopened, and an investigation into the cause of the fire is underway. This is the second fire involving a Southeastern train in just 10 days, following a track fire at Charing Cross Station on November 23 that closed the station for about two hours. A spokesman for Southeastern confirmed that the driver took the decision to evacuate the train and the station, and the company is working to determine the cause of the incident.

Wales manager Chris Coleman has expressed optimism over the recovery of star player Gareth Bale, who underwent surgery in November after suffering an injury while playing for Real Madrid in the Champions League. With Wales' next 2018 World Cup qualifier against Republic of Ireland in Dublin on March 24, Coleman believes Bale is on track to regain full fitness. "So far, so good," Coleman told BBC Wales Sport. "There are no problems, no alarm bells ringing." Coleman plans to visit Bale in Madrid, a trip that was already scheduled, to check on his progress. The manager is confident that the changes to the World Cup format, which will expand from 32 to 48 teams, will benefit smaller nations like Wales. "It gives us a better chance to compete," Coleman said. Bale played a crucial role in Wales' run to the semi-finals of the 2016 European Championship, and his return to fitness will be a significant boost to the team's World Cup qualifying campaign.

Ofsted Inspections Deemed "Ineffective" in Detecting Child Abuse in Rotherham A scathing report by the Communities and Local Government Committee has deemed Ofsted inspections "ineffective" in detecting the widespread abuse of children in Rotherham. The committee's investigation into the abuse of over 1,400 children in the town between 1997 and 2013 found that Ofsted's inspections failed to expose the extent of the problem and the council's inability to combat it. According to the report, Ofsted's inquiries relied too heavily on what council staff said, rather than verifying that policies were being implemented and were effective. The inspections were also criticized for being "too short and narrowly focused," failing to probe beyond the information provided by council officials. This led to a failure to detect the "professional jealousy and incompetence" that hindered the operation of Children's Social Care in Rotherham. The committee's chair, Labour MP Clive Betts, stated that while the perpetrators of the abuse bear ultimate responsibility, Ofsted's ineffectiveness contributed to the failure to expose the problem. He expressed concerns that similar shortcomings in inspection arrangements may have allowed child sexual exploitation to go undetected in other areas. The report highlighted the need for Ofsted to re-inspect all local authorities in England as soon as possible to ensure that councils are identifying and tackling child sexual exploitation in their communities. Betts emphasized that Ofsted needs to "get under the skin of what is happening in local authorities" and not just focus on paperwork and procedures. Ofsted has welcomed the report and acknowledged that its inspection methods have changed since 2012. A spokesman apologized for the agency's historical mistakes in Rotherham, stating that the changes made since then strengthen its ability to uncover where children are at risk. The report's findings serve as a stark reminder of the need for effective inspection and oversight to protect vulnerable children and prevent such atrocities from happening again.

Stephen Board, 66, of Bognor, is charged with multiple sexual assaults at two hospitals. The incidents allegedly occurred at St Richard's Hospital and Worthing Hospital between 2006 and 2015. He will appear at Worthing Magistrates' Court on November 29. The charges include assaults on women aged 19, 34, and 78 at the time of the incidents, according to Sussex Police.

Melania Trump Marks World Reading Day with Hospital Visit In celebration of World Reading Day, US First Lady Melania Trump made a solo appearance at the Manhattan paediatrics ward of New York Presbyterian Hospital. The visit was a rare public outing for the first lady, who has kept a relatively low profile since her husband's inauguration. Accompanied by a small entourage, including two cameramen, Mrs Trump brought a special gift for the young patients - a collection of Dr Seuss books, including one of her personal favorites, "Oh, The Places You'll Go!" As she sat down to read to the children, Mrs Trump encouraged them to develop a love for reading and to think about their aspirations in life. "We will read some books today," she said with a smile. "So do you know what is today? It's a reading day." The children listened intently as she read from the iconic book, holding up the colorful illustrations and emphasizing the inspiring words. The first lady's visit was a heartwarming gesture, and the children seemed to enjoy her company. As she read, she wore a elegant outfit, complete with black stilettos and a large diamond ring. The Dr Seuss books she brought were beautifully presented in a white box, tied with a golden ribbon. After the reading, Mrs Trump was asked about her visit, but was briefly pulled away to pose for photos before she could respond. Despite her reserved nature, Mrs Trump's hospital visit suggested that she may be ready to take on a more public role. As she told the children, "You'll be as famous as famous can be, with the whole wide world watching you win on TV." Her message of encouragement and empowerment was a positive note, and it will be interesting to see how she chooses to use her platform as first lady in the future.

Researchers at the University of Warwick have utilized advanced scanning technology to create a 3D image of the Megalosaurus, a dinosaur discovered in Stonesfield, Oxfordshire, and named in 1824. The team, led by Professor Mark Williams, took over 3,000 X-ray images of the dinosaur's jawbone, revealing previously unseen teeth and allowing for a detailed examination of the fossil. The scans showed the roots of teeth, the extent of repairs, and even tiny newly-growing teeth that were hidden deep within the jaw. This groundbreaking research will aid in future restoration work on the specimen, which is owned by the Oxford University Museum of Natural History. The university plans to use the scans to make informed decisions about any upcoming restoration projects. Professor Williams expressed his excitement about the opportunity to use state-of-the-art technology on such an iconic specimen. The discovery of the hidden teeth has provided new insights into the life and biology of the Megalosaurus, shedding more light on this ancient creature. The scans have opened up new possibilities for the study and preservation of this historic fossil.

West Brom striker Saido Berahino has taken a step towards regaining his fitness after playing for the club's U-23 team against Brighton on Monday. The 23-year-old was sent to a conditioning camp in France to help him lose weight and improve his overall fitness. Berahino's last appearance for the first team was on September 10, and he has not scored since February 27 against Chelsea. With his contract set to expire at the end of the season, Berahino's future at the club remains uncertain. He is eligible to sign a pre-contract agreement with an overseas club from January 1, which would allow him to leave for free. If he chooses to join another English club, his transfer fee would be determined by a tribunal, similar to the situation with Danny Ings when he left Burnley for Liverpool in 2015. Despite interest from Stoke and Crystal Palace, who both made £20m offers last summer, Berahino's future remains up in the air. His return to fitness is a positive step, but it remains to be seen what the future holds for the Burundi-born player.

Tensions in the South China Sea have escalated after a US warship sailed near the disputed Fiery Cross Reef, which is controlled by China. The move was deemed "illegal" by Chinese authorities, who claim it has "damaged regional peace". The reef, which has been transformed into an artificial island through a massive dredging operation, is at the center of a longstanding territorial dispute between China and several of its neighbors, including Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei. According to US Defense Department spokesman Bill Urban, the naval operation was designed to "challenge excessive maritime claims" in the region and ensure access to key shipping and air routes. The US has maintained a policy of not taking sides in the territorial disputes, but has conducted regular "freedom of navigation" patrols to assert its presence in the area. China, however, has strongly objected to the US move, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Lu Kang stating that the warship had "threatened China's sovereignty and security interests" and endangered the staff and facilities on the reef. The incident has raised concerns among neighboring countries, who are wary of China's military ambitions in the region. The latest tensions come as the Philippines, a US ally, has elected a new president, Rodrigo Duterte, who has vowed to take a tough stance on the country's territorial dispute with China.

Nicky Hayden, the 2006 MotoGP World Champion, has passed away at the age of 35, following a tragic accident on the Rimini coastline in Italy. The American motorcycle racer suffered "serious cerebral damage" after colliding with a car on Wednesday, May 17, and had been in the intensive care unit of Cesena's Maurizio Bufalini Hospital. Hayden's family released a statement, saying, "We would like everyone to remember Nicky at his happiest - riding a motorcycle." His brother, Tommy, a former motorcycle racer himself, fondly remembered Nicky's passion for the sport, saying, "He dreamed as a kid of being a pro-rider and not only achieved that but also managed to reach the pinnacle of his chosen sport. We are all so proud of that. We will all miss him terribly." Nicky's sister, Kathleen, added, "Today I not only lost my big brother, but I lost a best friend." The outpouring of tributes from the racing community has been immense, with Red Bull Honda World Superbike saying, "The racing world has said goodbye to one of its dearest sons. The'Kentucky Kid' will be sorely missed by all that ever had the pleasure of meeting him or the privilege to see him race a motorcycle around a track, be it dirt or asphalt." Born in Kentucky, Hayden began competing in MotoGP in 2003 and quickly made a name for himself in the sport. He finished third in the standings in 2005 and went on to win the championship in 2006, ending Valentino Rossi's five-year winning streak in a dramatic final race in Valencia. Hayden's third-place finish allowed him to take the title by five points, and he remains the last American to win the premier class of motorcycle road racing. Hayden's achievement was hailed as one of the greatest moments in MotoGP history, with BBC commentator Steve Parrish describing the 2006 season as "the most entertaining I have ever seen." Nicky's family was instrumental in his success, with his parents and siblings all involved in the sport. His Twitter handle, "bikes and family," reflected the importance of his loved ones in his life. BBC's Azi Farni remembered Nicky as "a real gentleman" who came from a "wonderful family, a big racing family." He added, "His family were such a huge part of who he was. This is going to be such a great loss for them." The motorcycle racing community will deeply miss Nicky Hayden, a talented and beloved rider who left an indelible mark on the sport. His legacy will live on, inspiring future generations of riders and fans alike.

A recent study published in the journal Thorax has suggested a potential link between consuming large amounts of processed meat and worsening asthma symptoms. The research, which involved nearly 1,000 French people, found that those who ate more than four portions of processed meat per week experienced a significant deterioration in their lung symptoms. The study, which spanned a decade from 2003 to 2013, looked specifically at the intake of cured meat, such as sausages, salami, and ham, and its impact on asthma symptoms like breathlessness, wheeze, and chest tightness. The participants, around half of whom were asthma patients, were asked to report their consumption of processed meat, with a single portion defined as two slices of ham, one sausage, or two slices of salami. The results showed that among the people with asthma, higher meat consumption was linked with a worsening of their lung symptoms. Those who consumed more than four portions a week, equivalent to eight slices of ham or four sausages, experienced the biggest deterioration of their asthma by the end of the study. The researchers believe that a preservative called nitrite, used in meats like sausages and ham, may be to blame for aggravating the airways. However, experts are cautioning that the link between processed meat and worsening asthma has not been proven and more investigations are needed. Dr. Erika Kennington, Head of Research at Asthma UK, noted that while certain foods can trigger allergies in some people, there is no specific dietary advice for managing asthma symptoms. Instead, she recommended that people with asthma follow the same healthy eating advice as everyone else, which includes a balanced diet with plenty of fresh and unprocessed food, low in sugar, salt, and saturated fat. Catherine Collins of the British Dietetic Association also emphasized the importance of a varied and Mediterranean-style diet, rich in fresh produce, for overall health, whether or not one has asthma. The experts agree that rather than focusing on a single type of food, people should prioritize eating a healthy and varied diet. This is particularly important given the existing link between processed meat and cancer, with experts advising that people consume no more than 70g of red and processed meat per day, equivalent to one sausage plus a rasher of bacon. By adopting a balanced and healthy diet, individuals can reduce their risk of chronic diseases and promote overall well-being.

Guernsey's Environment Department has requested a delay in the debate on the proposed'width tax' and related charges until January. The discussion was initially scheduled for the December States sitting, but Environment Minister Yvonne Burford has indicated that the proposals may undergo changes. This decision comes after a massive 2,000-strong protest last month, organized by the campaign group Enough is Enough, which opposed the'width tax' as well as other plans, including a goods and services tax, increased parking charges, and a refuse tax. The Guernsey Motor Trades Association has also voiced its criticism, arguing that the charges would be too costly and pose a threat to jobs in the motor industry. K'han Holden, one of the protest organizers, expressed pride in the impact of the demonstration, stating that it has prompted the department to re-examine the proposals. Holden emphasized the need for the department to "throw it out and start afresh." The proposed charges are part of an island transport strategy introduced in March, and Deputy Burford has assured that the States remain committed to introducing this key element, but wants to address "various concerns" raised by the community. Deputy Al Brouard, who opposed the strategy, has called for a new transport strategy that is "fit for purpose."

Sinn Féin's Corporation Tax Stance Under Scrutiny After Conflicting Comments The devolution of corporation tax to Northern Ireland has sparked controversy, with Sinn Féin's comments on the issue coming under fire. Under the Fresh Start Agreement, the executive committed to introducing a new corporation tax rate from April 2018. However, the cost of implementing this change remains unclear. On the Nolan Show, Sinn Féin's Conor Murphy failed to clarify whether the cost would be £150m per year or £150m over four years. Murphy stated that the cost would "incrementally drop over the course of the years," but admitted that a final figure had not been determined. The SDLP has criticized Sinn Féin for their lack of clarity on the issue, with finance spokesperson Claire Hanna accusing the party of "muddling numbers." Later, Sinn Féin clarified that the £150m figure referred to a one-year cost. The proposed reduction in corporation tax to 12.5% would bring Northern Ireland in line with the Republic of Ireland, but the parties remain at odds over the issue. The SDLP is calling on Sinn Féin to "come clean" on their stance on corporation tax devolution.

Waste management workers in the city have voted overwhelmingly in favor of taking industrial action, with over 90% of GMB members employed at five sites backing the move. The first strike is set to take place on October 1, with a further five days of action planned for later in the month. The dispute centers around issues such as reduced hours and lack of extra pay for weekend work. According to Pete Davies from the GMB union, staff are frustrated with the current situation and are calling on decision-makers to resolve the issue. "I wish that we didn't have to do this," he said. "I wish that the decision-makers in this city would get round the table and resolve this." The union has been seeking a resolution to the dispute, but so far, no agreement has been reached. Veolia, the French firm contracted to run the city's waste services, has stated that it wants to "sort any issues out speedily." The company has assured that discussions between the union and the Green Company, which employs the workforce, are still ongoing. If the strike action goes ahead, Veolia has pledged to minimize disruption and keep as many sites open as possible. The Green Company has referred all comments to Veolia's statement. The industrial action is set to continue on October 6, with a further four days starting on October 10.

Tragedy on the Slopes: Trial Looms for Ski Resort and Supervisor A trial is set to take place this year for a French ski resort and its supervisor, following the death of a 14-year-old British boy in 2011. Kieran Brookes, from Devon, died after his backpack became entangled in a ski lift in Chatel, France. The incident occurred when Kieran attempted to climb off the six-seat lift at the top of the slope, causing him to become suspended by his clothing for approximately four minutes. Lawyers for SAEM Sports et Tourisme a Chatel have confirmed that the company, along with supervisor Richard Cettour, 50, will face trial for their alleged role in Kieran's death. The prosecution accuses SAEM of failing to enforce safety rules, including a ban on skiers wearing backpacks on the lift, and not conducting daily equipment checks. Mr. Cettour is also accused of several failings, including not being present at his post during the accident and failing to respond to emergency calls from other skiers. Kieran's family, including his father Nick, are still seeking answers about the circumstances surrounding his death. "Not knowing the events that led to his death holds back the healing process," said Nick Brookes. The trial is expected to shed light on the tragic events and provide some closure for the Brookes family. SAEM and Mr. Cettour will face trial later this year, with the outcome potentially bringing justice to Kieran's loved ones.

Northern Ireland's Power-Sharing Government Teeters on the Brink as Parties Engage in Procedural Game-Playing The power-sharing government in Northern Ireland is facing an uncertain future as the parties engage in a complex game of procedural maneuvering. The crisis deepened after the arrest and release of Sinn Féin's northern chair, who was being investigated in connection with the murder of Kevin McGuigan Sr. The incident sparked a chain reaction of events, with the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) ministerial team resigning or standing aside, except for Finance Minister Arlene Foster, who has taken on the role of Acting First Minister. According to the Northern Ireland Act, Foster can only occupy the acting role for a continuous period of six weeks. However, a senior DUP source has suggested that this period can be interrupted if the party's leader, Peter Robinson, were to return to office for a brief period, allowing Foster to step back into the breach. This "cunning plan" has raised concerns that the parties may engage in a series of tactical maneuvers to maintain control and influence. Meanwhile, Robinson has stated that he has no intention of allowing Sinn Féin and Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) ministers to take over the health, enterprise, and social development departments vacated by his colleagues. Instead, he may nominate DUP politicians to fill the vacant positions, only to have them step down again almost immediately. This game of musical chairs is likely to continue in parallel with renewed Stormont House talks, which aim to address the underlying issues threatening the power-sharing agreement. The public may view these procedural games as "too clever by half," and the parties are aware that they will eventually have to face the voters. With the next election scheduled to take place within the next eight months, the parties are under pressure to resolve their differences and find a way forward. However, the issues on the table, including welfare reform, the budget, corporation tax, paramilitary activity, parades, the past, and the weakness of the current Stormont system, are complex and deeply entrenched. The absence of a regional development minister has already begun to have practical negative impacts, with common sense measures such as speed restrictions near rural primary schools being delayed. If the current impasse continues, it is likely that similar problems will arise in the health and housing sectors, highlighting the need for a swift resolution to the crisis. As the parties engage in their procedural game-playing, they must also be mindful of the need to find a lasting solution to the challenges facing Northern Ireland, lest they face the wrath of the voters in the upcoming election.

The town of Beverley is set to host the start of a major cycling event, bringing a significant boost to the local economy. The announcement has been welcomed by Stephen Parnaby, Conservative leader of East Riding of Yorkshire Council, who described it as "great news for the town and the wider East Riding". The council is investing around £100,000 to host the event, which is expected to attract thousands of spectators. Last year's inaugural race brought in an estimated £50m to the region's economy, and organizers are hoping to replicate this success. The three-day event was launched by Welcome to Yorkshire after the county hosted the Tour de France Grand Depart in 2014, which drew in over 1.2m spectators. Local residents and business owners are excited about the opportunity, with amateur cyclist Ed Neilson hoping it will encourage more cyclists to visit the town. Garry Payne, owner of a cycling cafe, described the news as "fantastic" for fans, who will have the chance to get up close to the riders and get autographs. The event is expected to provide a significant boost to local traders, with the council believing the investment will be "money well spent". With the start of the race taking place in Beverley, the town is likely to receive increased recognition and attention, making it a great opportunity for the local community to showcase its charm and hospitality.

The north coast of Northern Ireland is set to host a star-studded field of golfers as the Dubai Duty Free Irish Open gets underway from July 6 to 9. The tournament, which boasts a prize pot of £5.3 million, will feature ten of the world's top 40 golfers, including defending champion Rory McIlroy and world number two Hideki Matsuyama. BBC Northern Ireland will provide extensive coverage of the event, with Stephen Watson presenting hour-long highlights on BBC One NI every night from Thursday to Sunday. A special 30-minute preview programme will air on Wednesday, July 5, at 22:40, featuring contributions from Major champions Rory McIlroy, Graeme McDowell, and Darren Clarke. BBC Radio Ulster will also have live coverage, starting with a preview from the course on Wednesday at 18:30 BST, followed by half-hour programmes on Thursday and Friday. The Summer Club will air on Saturday, with a final day round-up on Sunday at 18:00. Joel Taggart will present the Radio Ulster programmes, joined by Michael McNamee for The Summer Club live from Portstewart on Saturday. Notable entries in the tournament include Jon Rahm, Justin Rose, Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, and Danny Willett. The event forms part of a new Rolex Series, and fans can keep up with all the action on the BBC Sport NI website, BBC iPlayer, and social media outlets. Grant Cameron will provide updates on the action throughout the week on BBC Radio Ulster, while the BBC Sport NI website will feature leaderboard, reports, and interviews. With its strong field and extensive coverage, the Dubai Duty Free Irish Open is set to be an exciting event for golf fans.

Local Authority Under Fire for Insufficient Housing Plans The Cheshire East Council has come under scrutiny for its inadequate plans to build new homes, with a government inspector deeming their target of 27,000 new homes by 2030 to be insufficient. The inspector has suggested that the figure needs to be closer to 40,000 to meet the area's growing housing needs. This criticism has sparked concerns among local leaders, with Council leader Michael Jones expressing his worry about the findings. Jones attributed the council's shortcomings to outdated policies and guidelines, stating that the starting point for the plan was based on 2009 data. He acknowledged that the council had failed to adapt to changing circumstances and pledged to re-examine their analysis and methodology to ensure accuracy. Meanwhile, Cheadle MP Mark Hunter has been vocal in his criticism of the council's plans, describing them as a demonstration of "ineptitude". Hunter's comments come after he spoke out against the council's proposal to build 2,000 new homes at Handforth, near Wilmslow. The independent inspector's report highlighted significant flaws in the council's process, particularly with regards to the release of land from the green belt. The report's findings have been seen as a victory for objectors, with Hunter claiming it as "round one" in their favor. The council must now revisit its plans and strive to meet the inspector's recommended target to address the area's housing needs.

A bizarre incident involving bagels brought a train to a halt in Hertfordshire on Sunday. The train, operated by Great Northern, was stopped at Potters Bar station at 01:00 GMT after a disturbance broke out on board. A video posted on Twitter showed a group of women placing bagels on a man's head, before he threw them out of the window. The footage also captured brawls in the carriage and on the platform, although it is unclear if these were related to the bagel incident. The train was held for 18 minutes while police took statements from passengers. British Transport Police (BTP) responded to the incident, tweeting about "BagelGate" and condemning the intimidating behaviour. The video of the incident has gone viral, with over 17,000 likes and 10,000 retweets. Despite the commotion, no arrests have been made. Great Northern has encouraged passengers to report any incidents of intimidating behaviour to the BTP, taking all such incidents seriously. The unusual incident has left many puzzled, with the BTP reminding passengers that "no bagel should be treated so cruelly" and that everyone deserves to feel safe on public transport.

Gabon Unveils 23-Man Squad for Africa Cup of Nations The Gabonese Football Federation has announced its final 23-man squad for the upcoming Africa Cup of Nations, which kicks off on January 14 in Libreville. The hosts, led by team captain and Borussia Dortmund star Pierre Emerick Aubameyang, will face debutants Guinea-Bissau in the opening game of the tournament. Aubameyang, who is also the team's star player, will lead the Panthers out onto the pitch, and fans are expecting great things from the talented striker. Joining him in the squad is Sunderland midfielder Didier Ndong, who was surprisingly included despite being left out of November's World Cup qualifier in Mali. Ndong had failed to turn up for international duty ahead of the Mali game, but after holding clear-the-air talks with the Gabonese Football Federation, he has been given a second chance. Other notable names in the squad include Juventus midfielder Mario Lemina, Cardiff City defender Bruno Ecuélé Manga, and China-based striker Malick Evouna. Gabon coach José Antonio Camacho has also included three domestic-based stars in the squad, as well as three players on standby. Gabon is hosting the continental tournament for the second time, having previously co-organized the competition with Equatorial Guinea in 2012. The Panthers will face a tough challenge in Group A, where they will also face four-time winners Cameroon and Burkina Faso, runners-up in 2013. The squad announcement makes Gabon the first of the 16 participants to unveil its final squad for the tournament. Fans are eagerly awaiting the start of the competition, which runs from January 14 to February 5. With a strong squad and home advantage, Gabon will be looking to make a deep run in the tournament and bring glory to their country. The full Gabon squad is as follows: Goalkeepers: Didier Ovono, Yves Stéphane Bitséki Moto, and Anthony Mfa Mezui. Defenders: Lloyd Palun, André Biyogho Poko, Aaron Appindangoye, Franck Perrin Obambou, Bruno Ecuélé Manga, Yoann Wachter, Johann Serge Obiang, and Benjamin Zé Ondo. Midfielders: Mario René Junior Lemina, Junior Serge Martinsson Ngouali, Levy Clément Madinda, Guélor Kanga Kaku, Merlin Tandjigora, Didier Ibrahim Ndong, and Samson Mbingui. Forwards: Pierre Emerick Aubameyang, Malick Evouna, Denis Athanase Bouanga, Serge Kevyn Aboue Angoue, and Cedric Ondo Biyoghe. The three players on standby are Axel Meyé, Johan Lengoualama, and Donald Nzé.

England's Early World Cup Exit Sparks Review and Debate The English rugby team's disappointing performance in the World Cup has led to a comprehensive review, with a five-man panel tasked with examining the factors that contributed to their early exit from the tournament. The review, which will include input from players, coaches, and management staff, is being led by RFU chief executive Ian Ritchie and will also feature former Football Association chief executive Ian Watmore and Professional Game Board chairman Ian Metcalfe. England's elimination at the group stage, following losses to Wales and Australia, marks the first time a World Cup host nation has failed to progress to the knockout stages. The RFU has emphasized that the review will be thorough and that all feedback will remain confidential, with recommendations to be made to the RFU board at a later date. The performance of head coach Stuart Lancaster and his assistants, Andy Farrell, Graham Rowntree, and Mike Catt, will be under scrutiny as part of the review. Lancaster, who has a contract until 2020, has stated that he would find it "hard to walk away" from the job, despite the team's disappointing performance. The review panel does not include RFU professional rugby director Rob Andrew or 2003 World Cup-winning coach Sir Clive Woodward, a decision that has been questioned by some. Former England player Will Greenwood, who was part of Woodward's squad in 2003, believes that his former coach should have been involved in the review, saying "he's a giant spectre that gets thrown into the pot the whole time." Others, including BBC Sport pundit Jeremy Guscott, have argued that players and coaches should not be involved in the review, as their feedback may not be impartial. Sir Clive Woodward has also expressed concerns that player input could be "very divisive." In contrast, former Scotland coach Ian McGeechan has defended Lancaster and his coaching team, saying that he "cannot see anything better" than the current set-up. McGeechan, who was part of the group that approved Lancaster's appointment in 2012, has urged the RFU not to make "any rash decisions," pointing out that England would have qualified from any other pool and that defeat to two strong teams was "no disgrace." The review is expected to take some time, with no date set for its completion. The next RFU board meeting will take place on November 17, and it is likely that the review will be discussed further at that time. As the English rugby team looks to rebuild and move forward, the outcome of the review will be eagerly anticipated by fans and pundits alike.

US President Barack Obama has criticized the National Rifle Association (NRA) for misrepresenting his proposed gun control legislation, sparking a heated debate on the highly contentious issue. In a speech at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, Mr. Obama accused the NRA of spreading false information, claiming that his administration was seeking to seize all firearms. He emphasized that his goal was to strengthen background checks, not take away guns from law-abiding citizens. The NRA declined to participate in the discussion, labeling it a "public relations spectacle" orchestrated by the White House. In a statement, NRA spokesman Andrew Arulanandam said the group saw "no reason to participate" in the event. This move has been seen as a reflection of the deep divide between the NRA and the Obama administration on the issue of gun control. Meanwhile, US Republican presidential hopeful Donald Trump weighed in on the issue, promising to eliminate gun-free zones in schools on his first day in office, if elected. Speaking at a rally in Vermont, Trump described gun-free zones as "bait" for potential shooters, echoing a long-held NRA stance. His comments have sparked controversy, with many arguing that such a move would put more lives at risk. The debate comes as Mr. Obama unveiled a package of executive actions aimed at keeping guns from people who should not have access to them. The measures, which bypass Congress, have been met with fierce resistance from leading Republicans, including House of Representatives Speaker Paul Ryan. Ryan denounced the move, saying it "undermined liberty" and would be challenged in court. In an article published in the New York Times, Mr. Obama called gun violence a national crisis, urging gun owners and manufacturers to play their part in ending it. He also announced that he would not campaign for Democrats who do not back gun reforms, saying he wanted leaders brave enough to stand up to the gun lobby's lies. The NRA, founded in 1871, has become one of the most powerful special interest groups in the US, with a budget of around $250 million per year. The group boasts of nearly 5 million members, although analysts estimate the figure is likely closer to 3 million. Famous members have included Charlton Heston, Whoopi Goldberg, and former president George Bush Snr. The NRA has been widely criticized for its statements on mass shootings, including a claim that a lack of armed guards at schools was to blame for the Sandy Hook massacre. The group's stance on gun control has been seen as a major obstacle to reform, with many arguing that its influence has prevented meaningful action from being taken. As the debate continues, it remains to be seen whether Mr. Obama's efforts will lead to meaningful change. With the NRA and other gun rights groups firmly opposed to reform, it is likely that the issue will remain a contentious one for years to come. Nevertheless, the president's efforts have sparked a national conversation on the issue, and it is clear that something needs to be done to address the scourge of gun violence in the US.

A 42-year-old man was found with significant injuries in Greenend Avenue, Johnstone, on Saturday at approximately 10:45. Police believe the victim, identified as Mr. Quail, was killed following a disturbance at his home in the early hours of the morning. Detectives are urging anyone with information or who may have witnessed something suspicious to come forward. According to Detective Chief Inspector Raymond Brown, the disturbance occurred around 00:50 on Saturday. He emphasized that the key to solving the murder inquiry lies within the local community. Brown appealed to residents, stating that even seemingly insignificant information could be vital to the investigation. The area where the incident occurred is a busy residential neighborhood, increasing the likelihood that someone may have seen or heard something suspicious. The police are encouraging anyone with information to contact the inquiry team at Helen Street Police Office through 101. By working together, the community can help bring justice to the victim and his family. The investigation is ongoing, with extensive inquiries underway to establish the circumstances surrounding Mr. Quail's death.

Nottingham's Tram Extension Nears Completion, Despite Delays The long-awaited tram extension to Chilwell and Clifton is nearing completion, according to Phil Hewitt, executive chair of Tramlink Nottingham. The project, which began in 2012, was initially scheduled to open in December 2014. However, due to unforeseen problems, the opening has been delayed. Hewitt attributed the delays to a lack of "risk time" factored into the construction timeline, which has resulted in a significant extension to the planned completion date. Despite the setbacks, Hewitt remains optimistic, stating that the opening is "tantalisingly close." Further driver training and timetable testing are currently underway to ensure a smooth launch. The extension will significantly expand Nottingham's tram network, adding approximately 10 miles of new track and 28 tram stops. This will more than double the size of the existing network. Hewitt also addressed rumors surrounding the delays, dismissing claims that the wrong type of concrete was used and that tram lines were incorrectly installed. He explained that some localized concrete cracking issues have arisen, but these are being addressed. With the completion of the project imminent, residents and commuters can look forward to improved transportation links and a more efficient tram network. Although a specific opening date has not been confirmed, it is expected to be announced soon.

Yorkshire spinner Adil Rashid has announced that he will not be playing in the crucial match against Middlesex at Lord's, citing mental and physical exhaustion. The 28-year-old initially stated that he needed rest, but has since revealed that he is not in the right mental frame of mind to perform at his best. Rashid expressed his concerns on social media, stating that he would be letting his teammates down if he played. This news comes as a blow to Yorkshire, who are currently second in Division One and trailing Middlesex by nine points. The team is also missing Jonny Bairstow, as the ECB has refused their request to field the wicketkeeper-batsman. Despite his absence, Rashid has expressed his support for the team and is hoping they can secure their third consecutive Championship title. Rashid has had a busy schedule recently, playing for both Yorkshire and England, and has been included in the squad for England's tour of Bangladesh in October. He emphasized the importance of family and his upcoming England duties, wishing his teammates the best of luck for the match. Yorkshire will now have to rely on their remaining players to secure a win and keep their title hopes alive.

Gillingham Manager Andy Hessenthaler has announced that two of the club's players, a 37-year-old and striker Dennis Oli, 28, are free to leave the team. The 37-year-old, who has made 73 appearances for the Gills since joining in 2010, and Oli, who has started only one game this season, have been informed that their contracts will not be renewed. Hessenthaler stated that the decision is part of his plan to reduce the wage bill, which will give him more flexibility to sign new players, including former Charlton defender Jonathan Fortune and ex-Wolves midfielder Rohan Ricketts, who have both been training with the club. The manager is keen to bring in fresh talent, but this may require him to loan out some of his current players. Despite the team's recent struggles, including six consecutive defeats, Hessenthaler has received a vote of confidence from chairman Paul Scally. In a text message, Scally expressed his support for the manager, stating that he will back him until the end of the season as long as the team continues to show desire, commitment, and effort. Hessenthaler remains focused on turning the team's fortunes around and is not dwelling on the possibility of being sacked. With the chairman's backing, he is looking to make the necessary changes to get the team back on track.

A recent report compiled by the Higher Education Funding Council for Wales (Hefcw) has shed light on the significant disparities in pay among university staff in Wales. The research, which was released to BBC Wales under the Freedom of Information Act, reveals that senior staff at Welsh universities are earning substantial salaries, with some vice-chancellors taking home over £200,000 per year, including pension contributions. According to the report, Cardiff University has the largest number of higher-paid staff in Wales, with 136 employees receiving more than £100,000 between 2014-15. The university's Vice Chancellor, Colin Riordan, is the highest-paid head of a Welsh university, earning £288,000 after pension contributions. The report also notes that seven of Wales' eight vice-chancellors were paid more than £200,000 last year. While the report acknowledges that pay in Welsh universities is comparable to other institutions of the same size and stature in the UK, the University and College Union (UCU) has expressed concerns about the pay gaps at universities. The union argues that the high pay of senior staff is in stark contrast to the average salaries of other university teaching staff, many of whom are on insecure contracts and struggle to make ends meet. The UCU spokesman stated, "Our main concern is the inequality between the average salary of VCs in Wales, compared to the average salary of other staff in our universities, particularly when taking into account that undergraduates are likely to be taught by a member of staff on an insecure, fixed-term contract." The union believes that staff on insecure contracts are underpaid, vulnerable, and constantly facing the prospect of unemployment, which can negatively impact their ability to deliver high-quality teaching and services. The Higher Education Funding Council for Wales argues that Welsh universities need to compete to attract the best staff, and that pay needs to be comparable to other UK universities in order to recruit top talent. However, the UCU counters that this argument does not justify the significant pay disparities between senior staff and other university employees. In response to the report, a Cardiff University spokesman pointed out that the university is distinct from other Welsh universities in having large medical and dental schools, as well as the Postgraduate Deanery for Wales. The spokesman noted that clinical staff salaries are set by the NHS, and that the university offers competitive salaries to attract and retain the best staff. The issue of university pay has sparked a wider debate about the funding and management of higher education in Wales. The previous Welsh education minister, Huw Lewis, warned that higher education could not expect to avoid cuts forever, and the current report highlights the need for a more nuanced discussion about university funding and resource allocation. As the debate continues, it is clear that the pay disparities at Welsh universities are a complex issue that requires careful consideration. While the Higher Education Funding Council for Wales argues that competitive pay is necessary to attract top talent, the UCU believes that the current pay gaps are unsustainable and unfair. Ultimately, finding a solution that balances the need to recruit and retain top staff with the need to address pay inequality and support all university employees will be crucial to ensuring the long-term sustainability and success of Welsh universities.

A French court has fined Robert Menard, the mayor of the southern town of Beziers, 2,000 euros for inciting hatred and discrimination against Muslims. Menard, an ally of the anti-immigrant National Front party, sparked controversy with his comments on the first day of school in 2016, tweeting about the "great replacement" of France's white Christian population by migrants. In a subsequent television interview, Menard claimed that 91% of children in a class in his town's city center were Muslims, calling it a "problem" that exceeded the limits of tolerance. French law prohibits collecting data based on people's religious beliefs or ethnicity, and Menard's comments were widely criticized. The court ruled that Menard's statements were a "clear infringement" of the law and awarded 1,000 euros in court costs to anti-racist groups that brought the case. The fine was higher than the 1,800 euros requested by the public prosecutor, who argued that Menard had unfairly targeted children. Menard has defended his comments, saying they were simply a description of the situation in his town, but has announced plans to appeal the ruling. The case has drawn attention to the divisive rhetoric surrounding immigration in France, ahead of the presidential election on May 7.

Mohammad Amir, the 22-year-old left-arm bowler, has been given a second chance in cricket after being cleared to play domestic cricket in Pakistan. Amir was jailed for six months and banned from all cricket for his role in a spot-fixing scam during Pakistan's tour of England in 2010. However, with the approval of the International Cricket Council (ICC), the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), and Sir Ronnie Flanagan, the head of the ICC's Anti-Corruption and Security Unit, Amir's ban has been lifted early. Amir expressed his gratitude and stated, "It's a new life for me and you will see not only Mohammad Amir as a better cricketer but also a better human being." The ICC stated that Sir Ronnie Flanagan was satisfied that Amir had shown remorse and cooperated with the authorities, which led to the decision to allow him to return to domestic cricket. Before his suspension, Amir had taken 51 wickets in 14 Test matches and 25 wickets in 15 one-day internationals, showcasing his talent and potential. Unlike his co-conspirators, Mohammad Asif and Salman Butt, Amir admitted his guilt and showed remorse, which likely contributed to his early return to the sport. Asif and Butt were also jailed and banned from cricket, with Asif receiving a seven-year ban and Butt a 10-year ban. Amir's return to domestic cricket is seen as a fresh start for the young bowler, and fans will be eager to see him back in action.

A fire broke out at the Mill O'Mains Community Pavilion on Sunday evening. Firefighters responded quickly, bringing the blaze under control by 23:00. A joint investigation is underway to determine the cause. The pavilion, which provided meals for deprived children, suffered significant damage in the fire that was finally extinguished by 01:00.

A 34-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the brutal murder of David Clarke, a 26-year-old with learning difficulties, in 2001. Clarke's body was found in his flat on Forthriver Road in north Belfast after friends raised concerns for his welfare. The killing was described by police as one of the most savage and brutal they had ever dealt with. The arrested man was detained in north Belfast on Monday morning and has been bailed pending further inquiries. The arrest comes after police re-opened the murder investigation following new information. It has emerged that Clarke was bullied in the weeks leading up to his murder. Former Assistant Chief Constable Allan McQuillan, who was involved in the original inquiry, described Clarke's death as a "mystery" and said it was not related to the Troubles. Detective Chief Inspector Alan Dickson paid tribute to Clarke, describing him as an "inoffensive and vulnerable" man who died after an "increasingly frenzied" assault. The case has been re-examined, and police are hopeful that justice may finally be served for Clarke and his family. The investigation is ongoing, and police are urging anyone with information to come forward.

Borussia Dortmund defender Mats Hummels is facing a crucial decision regarding his future. The 27-year-old has one year left on his contract, but has been linked to several top clubs, including Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Manchester United, and Liverpool. Hummels has admitted that the uncertainty is affecting his sleep, taking him an extra 30 minutes to fall asleep each night. His father and agent, Hermann Hummels, says a return to Bayern Munich is a possibility, citing the club as one of the few top-tier teams his son would consider joining. With two Bundesliga titles and a World Cup win under his belt, Hummels' next move will be closely watched. As he weighs his options, Hummels must consider what's best for his career and life, with his father guiding him through the decision-making process. A decision is expected soon, with several clubs eagerly awaiting his choice.

A cannabis factory with approximately 200 plants was discovered in a Smethwick flat after a fire broke out. The fire service was alerted by a nearby resident who saw smoke billowing from a fourth-floor window of the five-story block on Beakes Road. Upon arrival, crews made a forced entry into the empty flat and found a fire in the back bedroom. According to West Midlands Fire Service, the fire is believed to have been caused by an electrical fault, possibly due to overloaded equipment used for the cannabis grow. West Midlands Police are working to locate the owner of the property, with enquiries still ongoing. The discovery was made at around 9:10 am, and police are investigating the incident. The flat was unoccupied at the time of the fire, and no injuries were reported. An investigation into the cannabis factory is underway.

A dramatic incident occurred at Cleghorn level crossing in Lanark on Saturday evening, when a car was struck by a Virgin train traveling from Preston to Glasgow. Fortunately, the occupants of the vehicle managed to escape before the collision, which happened just before 19:00. The train, carrying around 60 passengers, was able to continue on its journey without reported injuries. British Transport Police (BTP) and Police Scotland are currently investigating the incident, with support from the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service. The BTP stated that their priority is to ensure the safety of everyone involved and to understand how the car came to be on the tracks. The Rail Accident Investigation Branch and Office of Rail and Road have also been notified. The incident caused significant disruption to train services, with routes being re-routed as a result of the collision. An investigation is ongoing to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The fact that the occupants of the vehicle were able to escape unharmed is a relief, and authorities are now focused on preventing such incidents in the future.

Bouygues Telecom has made a bid to acquire Vivendi-owned SFR, a move that would create the largest mobile phone service provider in France. If successful, the merger would leave only three mobile phone companies in the country, with Bouygues and SFR overtaking current leader Orange. The combined entity would be a significant player in the French market, with Bouygues Telecom and SFR currently ranking as the second and third largest mobile phone companies. However, the deal is not without competition, as rival firm Altice, owner of French cable TV operator Numericable, has also made an offer for SFR. Although the details of Altice's offer have not been disclosed, industry analysts believe that Bouygues' bid is likely to be viewed as the most appealing by Vivendi. According to Dario Talmesia, principal analyst at Informa Telecomes and Media, "Vivendi would view the offer from Bouygues as the most appealing one." The proposed merger is part of a broader trend of consolidation among mobile phone operators in Europe, where there are currently 150 companies, compared to just four in the United States. If approved, the deal would require significant investment in infrastructure, which Bouygues claims would help protect jobs and boost the ailing French economy. Kester Mann, an analyst at CCS Insight, noted that Bouygues is positioning the deal as a way to bring economic benefits and job security. However, market analysts have warned that the merger could lead to an end to price cuts, which have benefited French mobile phone customers since the arrival of Free Mobile seven years ago. This could prompt the government to reconsider allowing the deal to go through. Before the merger can proceed, it must be approved by competition regulators in both France and the European Union. The European Union's response to a similar deal in Germany, where Telefonica is seeking to acquire E-Plus, may provide an indication of how the Bouygues-SFR merger will be received. As Talmesia noted, "What's happening in Germany can be a good indicator of what can be happening in France and the rest of Europe."

Great Britain's Cycling Team Gears Up for World Championships The Great Britain cycling team has announced its 20-rider squad for the upcoming World Championships, featuring a mix of experienced Olympians and debutants. Olympic champions Katie Archibald, Elinor Barker, Steven Burke, and Callum Skinner are among the notable names on the roster, which includes 10 riders making their World Championship debut. The team will be looking to replicate its success from last year's event in London, where they topped the medal table with five gold medals. However, they will be without several star names, including six-time Olympic champion Jason Kenny and his wife Laura, who are expecting their first child. Bradley Wiggins has retired, and Mark Cavendish is focusing on road racing. The women's endurance team features a strong lineup, with Archibald and Barker joined by Ellie Dickinson, Neah Evans, Emily Kay, Manon Lloyd, and Emily Nelson. The men's endurance team includes Matt Bostock, Steven Burke, Kian Emadi, Chris Latham, Mark Stewart, Andy Tennant, and Oliver Wood. The sprint team is led by Jack Carlin, Katy Marchant, Lewis Oliva, Ryan Owens, Callum Skinner, and Joe Truman. The team will be competing in a range of events, including the team pursuit, individual pursuit, sprint, and keirin. The World Championships will be broadcast on the BBC, with coverage starting on Wednesday, April 12, and running through to Sunday, April 16. Fans can watch live on BBC Two and Connected TV, with repeat broadcasts available on the Red Button. The BBC Sport website and app will also provide live streams, text commentaries, news, and reports. With a strong squad and a packed schedule of events, Great Britain's cycling team will be looking to make a big impact at the World Championships. Can they match their success from last year and bring home a haul of medals? Tune in to the BBC's coverage to find out.

Bristol Rovers have contacted the EFL's legal department amid claims that Bristol City knew about a confidential release clause in striker Matthew Taylor's contract. The clause's details are supposed to remain private under EFL rules. Bristol City confirmed making an offer for Taylor, which was accepted, but declined further comment. Taylor, 26, scored 61 goals in 118 league appearances for Rovers. His transfer to City marks the first time a player has moved directly from Rovers to City since Trevor Morgan in 1987. The situation has sparked controversy, with Rovers seeking clarification from the EFL.

Disney Parks Introduce Blanket Ban on Selfie Sticks In a move to enhance safety for its visitors, Disney has announced a complete ban on selfie sticks in its theme parks. The ban, which comes into effect in the US on Tuesday and in Paris and Hong Kong on Wednesday, prohibits guests from bringing the handheld extension poles into the parks altogether. previously, they were only banned on rides. According to a Disney spokeswoman, the decision was made due to growing safety concerns for both guests and staff. The long arms of selfie sticks pose a risk of injury if accidentally used to strike someone, and they can also interfere with ride mechanisms. Visitors will now be required to leave their selfie sticks in lockers at the park entrances and collect them later. Disney is not the first institution to ban selfie sticks. Several football clubs, the National Gallery, and the All England Lawn Tennis & Croquet Club have already implemented similar bans due to concerns over safety and nuisance. Apple also prohibited the use of selfie sticks at its recent WWDC developers conference in the US. While St John Ambulance has not reported a significant increase in selfie stick-related injuries, the charity has offered advice on how to treat head injuries caused by the devices. If someone is hit on the head with a selfie stick, they should sit down, apply a cold compress, and seek medical help if symptoms such as dizziness, nausea, or confusion occur. With the ban in place, Disney hopes to create a safer and more enjoyable experience for its visitors.

An art exhibit, "Suspended Forest," features discarded Christmas trees from Brooklyn. Artist Michael Neff created the display, hanging trees in a grid formation. The pine-scented installation took a day and a half to set up and will be on show for a month, showcasing a unique reuse of festive foliage.

A devastating arson attack on a family home in Meadow Drive has left a mother and her two young children "distraught" and shaken the local community. The incident, which occurred at approximately 06:20 GMT on Friday, is being treated as a hate crime by police. Subi Philip, a cardiac nurse, was at home with her ten and eight-year-old daughters when the attack happened. Her husband was not present, having returned to India for his father's funeral. The family, originally from India, has been living in the area for several years and is well-integrated into the local community. According to Mrs. Philip, the family was alerted to the attack by a loud noise outside. She described the scene as "chaotic" and said she was initially unsure of what was happening. "I just heard a big bang and got out of my bed and saw a big fire. When I came downstairs and saw it, I started screaming. My girls didn't know why I was screaming and they were screaming too.
